summary: Gross and Zagier prove that for a newform f of weight 2 on Γ₀(N), an imaginary quadratic field K of odd discriminant D prime to N in which every prime dividing N splits, and a class-group character χ, L′(f,χ,1) = 8π²(f,f)ĥ(c_{χ,f})/(h u²√|D|) (Theorem I.6.3), where c_{χ,f} is the (f,χ)-component of the Heegner divisor class in J₀(N)(H) and ĥ the Néron–Tate height; equivalently (Theorem I.6.1) the generating series of the heights ⟨c, T_m c^σ⟩ is a cusp form g_𝒜 whose Petersson product with f is u²√|D|/(8π²)·L′_𝒜(f,1). The proof computes the archimedean local heights through Green's functions and Legendre functions (Chapter II), the finite local heights through intersection theory on the integral model of X₀(N), Deuring's reduction theory and explicit Eichler orders (Chapter III), and the Fourier coefficients of a Rankin kernel θ_𝒜·E_s followed by holomorphic projection (Chapter IV), and matches them (Chapter V). Consequences: for E/ℚ modular with L′(E,1) ≠ 0 the Heegner point has infinite order and BSD holds up to a rational factor (Theorem I.7.3); an elliptic curve of analytic rank 3 (Proposition I.7.4), which with Goldfeld's theorem gives the effective lower bound h(D) > κ(ε)(log|D|)^{1−ε} (Theorem I.8.1). Chapter V §4 states the higher-weight analogue and the algebraicity conjecture (4.4) for higher Green's functions at Heegner points. After review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86), of 335 items 24 are in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (class groups, genus theory and the genus character, newforms and the Petersson product, the Atkin–Lehner lemma, Dedekind eta, digamma and ζ constants, the trace and U_n operators, Legendre polynomials, L(E,s)) and 149 are planned, mostly by GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights, HeegnerPointEulerSystems, RankZeroOneBSD, ModularCurvesPartII and the Tau Ceti modular-curve and modular-form roadmaps. 162 are missing: above all the paper's own classical proof, whose roadmap GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights follows Yuan–Zhang–Zhang but names 'Gross–Zagier, Chapters II–IV' as a primary source. They are routed as sources of GZ.0–GZ.3 and GZ.5–GZ.8; of the existing owners of the classical inputs (AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0–AS.2 for Legendre functions and non-holomorphic Eisenstein series, AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0 for K-Bessel integrals, QSeries QM.3 for Poincaré series and E₂*, MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.5–MP.6 for the theta series, AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4 for partial zeta functions, Gauss sums and the genus factorization); of CM.1/CM.5 (Deuring), ModularCurvesPartII (the integral model, Atkin–Lehner involutions, the modular polynomial, the Hecke algebra) and BSD.5. The class number application is a Part II of AnalyticNumberTheory (EffectiveClassNumberProblem), and the higher-weight material of Chapters IV §5 and V §4 joins the proposed Part II HigherGreenFunctionCMValues of GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights. 76 mistakes are recorded (59 by the extraction, 17 more by the review, all confirmed); none changes a main theorem, but several constants and signs in Chapters II–V must be corrected before formalisation, and Proposition III.(1.4) and the fourth line of Corollary V.(1.3) are not right as printed.

items.name: The modular curve X₀(N) over ℚ
items.statement: For an integer N ≥ 1, X = X₀(N) is the (coarse) compactified moduli space over ℚ of elliptic curves with a cyclic subgroup of order N: over a field k of characteristic 0 its points x are the diagrams (1.1) φ: E → E′, where E, E′ are (generalized) elliptic curves over k and φ is an isogeny over k whose kernel A is isomorphic to ℤ/Nℤ over k̄. X is a complete, non-singular, geometrically connected curve over ℚ.
items.locator: Chapter I, §1, (1.1), p. 226 (facts quoted as known, no proof in the paper)
items.note: No scheme X₀(N) exists in Mathlib 082e2d3 or Tau Ceti f790474 (grep for X₀/Y₀/ModularCurve/modularCurve in both trees: only unrelated hits; Mathlib has only the group CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0, Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups.lean:79, i.e. the analytic side). Plans: ModularCurvesPartII R13.2 'Construct compactified full and Γ₁ level problems, and the correct Γ₀(n) problem at general n ... Prove algebraicity/representability in the precise ranges, properness and normality'; R13.4a 'Construct coarse compactified curves from R13.2's actual stack presentations ... Prove properness, normality and the allowed base-change statements'; R12.6 'State the precise fields of definition of components and of the canonical cusp. Supply a named theorem to replace #81's conditional geometric-connectedness supplier'. Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 8D identifies [Γ₀(N)] with the cyclicity locus of [N-Isog] (the moduli description), and Layer 10 defines X_H (including X₀(N)) as the normalisation of ℙ¹_j in Y_H over ℤ[1/N], but only for N ≥ 5 prime ('N ≥ 5 prime is a standing hypothesis of the whole layer') and with 'no connectedness or irreducibility assertion'. The last sentence of §1's first paragraph (the function field ℚ(j, j′) and the modular equation Φ_N(j, j′) = 0) is split off as its own item, placed after this one, because no stage plans it (atlas, packet and decomposition search for 'modular polynomial', 'modular equation', 'Φ_N', 'function field of X': nothing relevant). The planned coverage of the curve itself is partial: general-level X₀(N) only through R13.2/R13.4a, since the Tau Ceti construction is for prime N ≥ 5.

items.name: The classical modular polynomial Φ_N and the function field of X₀(N) over ℚ
items.statement: For N ≥ 1 let Φ_N(X, Y) ∈ ℤ[X, Y] be the classical modular polynomial of level N, characterised by Φ_N(X, j(τ)) = ∏_{γ ∈ Γ₀(N)\SL₂(ℤ)} (X − j(Nγτ)) for τ in the upper half-plane (it has degree [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ₀(N)] = N∏_{p | N}(1 + 1/p) in X). The function field of X = X₀(N) over ℚ is generated by the modular invariants j(x) = j(E) and j′(x) = j(E′) of a point x = (φ: E → E′), and these satisfy the classical modular equation of level N: Φ_N(j, j′) = 0.
items.locator: Chapter I, §1, p. 226 ('The function field of X over ℚ is generated by the modular invariants j(x)=j(E) and j′(x)=j(E′); these satisfy the classical modular equation of level N: φ_N(j, j′)=0 [2]', quoted from Birch [2]); used again in Chapter III, §1, p. 255 (Kronecker's congruence, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/122)
items.note: Split off from PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/1. The paper gives no definition of φ_N beyond 'the classical modular equation' with a reference to Birch [2]; the characterisation by the product over Γ₀(N)\SL₂(ℤ) is the standard one and is what Kronecker's congruence (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/122) is about. Searched declarations.tsv (Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474) for modularPolynomial/ModularPolynomial and modular equation: nothing. Searched atlas stage descriptions, packets and decompositions for 'modular polynomial', 'modular equation', 'Φ_N': the only hits are unrelated (cyclotomic Φ_N in Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 5 and EllipticCurves Layer 1; a q-series mention in QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms). The irreducibility of Φ_N over ℂ(Y) is also the classical proof that X₀(N) is geometrically connected, which R12.6 is asked to supply. Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: The cusps ∞ and 0 of X₀(N)
items.statement: The cusps of X = X₀(N) are the points where j(x) = j′(x) = ∞; they correspond to diagrams (1.1) between degenerate elliptic curves in which A = ker φ meets every geometric component of E [7, 173ff.]. There is a unique cusp at which E has 1 component, denoted ∞, and a unique cusp at which E has N components, denoted 0; both are rational over ℚ (they are distinct iff N > 1).
items.note: Plans: R12.3 'Construct the local parameter at each cusp ... identify the scheme-theoretic cusp locus'; R13.2 (Γ₀(n) compactification 'include the extra boundary data'); packet node ModularCurvesPartII:R14.6/rational-cusp-abel-jacobi 'The cusp ∞ ∈ X₀(N)(ℚ) ... give Abel–Jacobi morphisms AJ_∞ : X₀(N) → J₀(N), x ↦ [x − ∞]'. Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 10 item 2 plans, for N prime only, 'D₀ := (Cusps₀(N))_red ≅ Spec ℤ[1/N] ⊔ Spec ℤ[1/N], giving the two disjoint cusp sections 0 and ∞', with ramification index 1 along ∞ and N along 0. The 1-gon/N-gon moduli description of the two cusps (generalized elliptic curves) is planned only through R13.1–R13.2 (generalised elliptic curves, Česnavičius's refined Γ₀(n)).

items.name: Atkin–Lehner involutions w_N, w_d and the group W
items.statement: (2.1) The canonical involution w_N of X sends x = (φ: E → E′) to w_N(x) = (φ′: E′ → E), φ′ the dual isogeny; it interchanges the cusps ∞ and 0. (2.2) For each positive divisor d of N with (d, N/d) = 1, let D ⊂ ker φ and D′ ⊂ ker φ′ be the unique subgroups of order d, and put w_d(x) = (E/D → E/ker φ ≅ E′ → E′/D′). These involutions form a group W ⊆ Aut_ℚ(X) isomorphic to (ℤ/2ℤ)^s, s the number of distinct prime factors of N, with group law w_d w_{d′} = w_{d″}, d″ = d d′ / gcd(d, d′)².
items.note: Curve-level statement; no stage plans it. Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 10 plans only w_N and only for N ≥ 5 prime ('N ≥ 5 prime is a standing hypothesis of the whole layer'; 'the extension of the Atkin–Lehner involution w_N from Y₀(N) (Layer 8's [N-Isog]-transposition) to X₀(N), a separate normalisation-functoriality theorem ... compute that it interchanges the two reduced cusp sections'). The packet node ModularCurvesPartII:R14.1/atkin-lehner-involution plans w_ζ on X₁(N), (E, P) ↦ (E/⟨P⟩, P′) over ℤ[1/N, ζ_N], not w_d on X₀(N). Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 6 plans only the action on forms ('𝒲_Q 𝒲_R = 𝒲_{QR/gcd(Q,R)²} — an action, possibly with kernel'); its library analogue is tauceti:TauCeti.Nat.IsExactDivisor.normalizedAtkinLehnerOperator_normalizedAtkinLehnerOperator (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/AtkinLehner/Normalized.lean:325) with TauCeti.Nat.ExactDivisor.normalizedAtkinLehnerRepresentation (line 392). No stage plans w_N for composite N, w_d (d ∥ N, 1 < d < N) on X₀(N), or the embedding W ≅ (ℤ/2ℤ)^s ⊆ Aut_ℚ(X₀(N)). Routed (source) to ModularCurvesPartII:R14.1, whose stage owns the algebraic correspondences of modular curves and whose packet already owns the Atkin–Lehner involution of X₁(N); the curve X₀(N) at general level comes from R13.2/R13.4a. Checked: the composite in (2.2) has kernel (A + E[d])/D ≅ ℤ/(N/d) × ℤ/d, cyclic of order N because (d, N/d) = 1, so w_d(x) is a point of X; and W acts faithfully, since w_d sends the cusp ∞ to a cusp whose denominator has greatest common divisor N/d with N, so distinct d give distinct automorphisms.

items.name: Hecke correspondences T_m on X₀(N)
items.statement: (2.3) For m ≥ 1, T_m(x) = Σ_C (x_C), the sum over all subgroups C ⊂ E of order m with C ∩ ker φ = 0, where x_C is the point (E/C → E′/φ(C)). T_m is an endomorphism of the divisor group of X induced by an algebraic correspondence on X × X rational over ℚ; when (m, N) = 1, T_m is self-dual of bidegree σ₁(m) = Σ_{d|m} d.
items.note: R14.1 'Construct the isogeny correspondences at good and bad primes, degeneracy maps and diamond operators from the moduli interpretation. Extend them to compactifications ... Prove composition, double-coset and adjoint formulas, and compare their q-expansion action with ModularForms'. Its packet node ModularCurvesPartII:R14.1/degeneracy-maps-and-hecke-correspondence is stated for X₁(N), N ≥ 5, p prime ('The Hecke correspondence T_p is the pair (π₁^{(p)}, π₂^{(p)})'); T_m for composite m on X₀(N) (all subgroups of order m, not only cyclic) follows from the composition formulas. Library analogue on forms only: tauceti:HeckeRing.GL2.heckeTCuspNat (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/HeckeSlash/Operators.lean:89), T_n on S_k(Γ₁(N)) as a double-coset operator.

items.name: The Jacobian J = J₀(N) and the Hecke algebra 𝕋
items.statement: J is the Jacobian of X: for a field k of characteristic 0, J(k) is the group of divisor classes of degree zero on X rational over k. The correspondences T_m induce endomorphisms of J over ℚ; 𝕋 ⊆ End_ℚ(J) is the commutative subalgebra they generate.
items.note: Packet node ModularCurvesPartII:R14.2/jacobian-and-functoriality: 'J₁(N) := Pic⁰_{X₁(N)/ℤ[1/N]} is an abelian scheme over ℤ[1/N] ... The same applies to J₀(N) = Pic⁰ of the coarse curve X₀(N) over ℤ[1/N]'; R14.2 'Construct the induced maps on Picard/Jacobian objects by pullback and norm. Prove the Hecke relations ... Define the integral Hecke algebra through its faithful action on an actual finite module'. The Jacobian itself: JacobianChallenge Layer D (relative Picard functor, Pic⁰, representability). Not in either library.

items.name: Imaginary quadratic data K, D, O, h, u (D odd)
items.statement: K is an imaginary quadratic field whose discriminant D is prime to N; O is its ring of integers, h = #Pic(O) its class number, and u = #(O^×/{±1}). Throughout the paper D is assumed odd, hence squarefree and D ≡ 1 (mod 4); ε: (ℤ/Dℤ)^× → {±1} is the quadratic character of K/ℚ.
items.locator: Chapter I, §3, p. 227 (and §5, p. 229 for ε)
items.note: h: mathlib:NumberField.classNumber (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/ClassNumber.lean:64, the cardinality of ClassGroup (𝓞 K)). u = torsionOrder K / 2 with mathlib:NumberField.Units.torsionOrder (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/Basic.lean:175, Nat.card of the torsion of (𝓞 K)ˣ); the identification u = torsionOrder/2 is the GZ.0 packet node GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.0/heegner-unit-index. D: mathlib:NumberField.discr (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Defs.lean:36); for K = ℚ(√d) with d squarefree and d ≡ 1 (mod 4), Tau Ceti's NumberField.discr_eq_of_squarefree_of_mod_four_eq_one (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Quadratic/RingOfIntegers.lean:302) gives D = d. ε: Mathlib has no Kronecker symbol, but Tau Ceti builds the character. tauceti:TauCeti.Multiquadratic.genusCharFun (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Quadratic/GenusCharacter/Basic.lean:212) is the product of the prime-discriminant characters primeDiscriminantCharFun P (at an odd prime discriminant p* this is the Legendre symbol (·/p), written as a Jacobi symbol; for odd D only odd prime discriminants occur). Indexed by the prime-discriminant factorization of D (IsFundamentalDiscriminant.exists_finset_primeDiscriminant) it is ε: completely multiplicative (genusCharFun_mul_right), a function modulo |D| (genusCharFun_mod_right'), equal to ±1 exactly on the integers prime to D (genusCharFun_eq_zero_iff, genusCharFun_eq_one_or_eq_neg_one), and tauceti:TauCeti.Multiquadratic.genusCharFun_natCast_eq_legendreSym (same file, line 308) identifies its value at an odd prime q with legendreSym q d, the splitting symbol of K = ℚ(√d). It is an unbundled function ℤ → ℤ, not a DirichletCharacter; for odd D one may equally use n ↦ jacobiSym n |D| (mathlib:jacobiSym). These are definitions; the value of u is item 7. 'D odd' is a standing hypothesis of the whole paper (it excludes D = −4 and all even D; together with (D, N) = 1 it gives (D, 2N) = 1).

items.name: The unit index u
items.statement: u = #(O_K^×/{±1}) equals 1 unless D = −3 or D = −4, where u = 3, resp. 2. (Under the standing hypothesis D odd: u = 1 unless D = −3, u = 3; and u = 1 when |D| > 4, p. 230.)
items.note: GZ.0 packet node GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.0/heegner-unit-index: 'For an imaginary quadratic field K, u(K) = [O_K^× : ℤ^×] = #μ(K)/2 ... In Mathlib terms, u(K) = NumberField.Units.torsionOrder K / 2. So u(K) = 1 except u(ℚ(√−1)) = 2 and u(ℚ(√−3)) = 3.' No declaration computes torsionOrder of an imaginary quadratic field (grep for torsionOrder in Tau Ceti: no theorem; Mathlib has only IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.torsionOrder_eq for cyclotomic fields, which covers ℚ(ζ₃), ℚ(ζ₄) but not the other fields).

items.name: Heegner point of discriminant D
items.statement: A point x = (φ: E → E′) of X is a Heegner point of discriminant D if the elliptic curves E and E′ both have complex multiplication by O = O_K (End E ≅ End E′ ≅ O). (Heegner points with non-fundamental discriminants or with discriminant not prime to N exist [13] but are not considered.)
items.note: HE.1 'Construct CM elliptic curves and cyclic-isogeny pairs over ℂ, identify them with the existing X₀(N) moduli objects, and prove descent to ring class fields by the main theorem of complex multiplication'; CM.1 'Construct the elliptic curve associated to a complex ideal lattice and its order action. Identify isomorphism classes through proper ideal classes'. Not in either library (grep 'Heegner' in Tau Ceti: 0 files).

items.name: Existence, number, field of rationality and Galois/Atkin–Lehner action of Heegner points
items.statement: Let K, D be as above ((D, N) = 1). Heegner points of discriminant D on X₀(N) exist if and only if D is congruent to a square modulo 4N. In that case there are exactly 2^s·h Heegner points (s = number of distinct prime factors of N), all rational over the Hilbert class field H = K(j(E)) of K, and they are permuted simply transitively by the abelian group W × Gal(H/K).
items.locator: Chapter I, §3, p. 227 (stated without proof; see Gross [13])
items.note: HE.1 plans 'descent to ring class fields by the main theorem of complex multiplication and the canonical-model reciprocity law' and 'Construct a compatible family of points P_c and show its dependence on choices is given by the specified Galois/Hecke actions'; HE.0 'Derive ring class fields and Artin maps from existing class field theory'; CM.3 'identify the associated ring class field' (H = K(j) for the maximal order). The exact count 2^s·h and the simple transitivity of W × Gal(H/K) are not stated in any stage: partial. Checked: the points correspond to (O, 𝔫, [𝔞]) with 𝔫 | N, O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N (2^s choices of β mod 2N with β² ≡ D mod 4N when (D, N) = 1, D odd) and [𝔞] ∈ Pic(O) (h choices).

items.name: The Heegner hypothesis in local form
items.statement: Assume D odd and (D, N) = 1. Then D ≡ β² (mod 4N) for some β ∈ ℤ if and only if every prime p dividing N splits in K (ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; for p = 2 this means D ≡ 1 mod 8). In particular ε(N) = 1, which is the condition to which Chapter IV relaxes it (so that the sign −ε(N) of the functional equation of L_𝒜(f, s) is −1).
items.locator: Implicit in Chapter I, §3, p. 227 and §9, p. 233 ('the condition D ≡ square (mod 4N) is relaxed to ε(N) = 1'); stated in Chapter IV, introduction, pp. 267–268 ('ε(p) = 1 for all primes p dividing N (i.e. D a square modulo 4N)') and Chapter V, §1, p. 306
items.note: Elementary; not stated in the paper as a numbered result but used to pass between the two formulations. Partial library input: tauceti:NumberField.ncard_primesOver_quadratic_iff (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Quadratic/Splitting.lean:169): for K = ℚ(θ), θ² = d, an odd prime p ∤ d splits iff legendreSym p d = 1. The 2-adic case and the packaging mod 4N are not in the library. HE.1 'Prove the local embedding conditions'; BSD.3 'choose K with the classical/generalized Heegner conditions and L(E^K,1)≠0'. My check: for odd p^a ∥ N, D ≡ β² mod p^a iff (D/p) = 1; for 2^a ∥ N, a ≥ 1, D ≡ β² mod 2^{a+2} iff D ≡ 1 mod 8; for N odd the condition mod 4 is automatic (D ≡ 1 mod 4).

items.name: The Heegner divisor class c = (x) − (∞) (and d = (x) − (0))
items.statement: For a Heegner point x of discriminant D, c is the class of the divisor (x) − (∞) in J(H). Birch's question [3]: determine the cyclic module spanned by c over the ring 𝕋[Gal(H/K)] acting on J(H). In §9, d = (x) − (0); since (0) − (∞) has finite order in J(ℚ), c and d have the same image in J(H) ⊗ ℚ.
items.note: HE.1 'Map CM points to degree-zero Jacobian classes using a cusp or the normalized rational Hodge class, then to A or E through the existing modular quotient'; packet node ModularCurvesPartII:R14.6/rational-cusp-abel-jacobi 'AJ_∞ : X₀(N) → J₀(N), x ↦ [x − ∞] ... over ℚ; ... Hecke-compatible on divisors'. The torsion statement for (0) − (∞) is item PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/46.

items.name: Normalized absolute values of H and the product formula
items.statement: For each place v of H with completion H_v: |α|_v = α ᾱ = |α|² if H_v ≅ ℂ, and |α|_v = q_v^{−v(α)} if H_v is non-archimedean with uniformizer π, v(π) = 1, residue field of order q_v. For every α ∈ H^×, ∏_v |α|_v = 1.
items.note: mathlib:NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/ProductFormula.lean:98): '(∏ w : InfinitePlace K, w x ^ w.mult) * ∏ᶠ w : FinitePlace K, w x = 1' for x ≠ 0. H is totally imaginary, so every infinite place has mult = 2 and w x ^ 2 = αᾱ = GZ's |α|_v; the finite places are normalized by the norm of the prime (file header: '|x|ᵥ is equal to the norm of the corresponding maximal ideal raised to the power of the v-adic valuation'), i.e. q_v^{−v(α)}. Same statement. GlobalNumberFields Layer 0 plans a uniform API over all places ('the real and squared-complex formulas at infinite places ... the global product formula as a transport of NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one').

items.name: Néron's local height symbol (existence, uniqueness, characterization)
items.statement: Let v be a place of H and X/H_v the curve. There is a unique real-valued symbol ⟨a, b⟩_v on pairs of relatively prime divisors a, b of degree zero on X over H_v which is bi-additive, symmetric, continuous, and satisfies (4.1) ⟨a, b⟩_v = log|f(a)|_v = Σ_x m_x log|f(x)|_v whenever a = Σ m_x (x) and b = div(f). It can be computed by potential theory (Green's functions on X(ℂ)) at archimedean v and by intersection theory on a regular model at non-archimedean v [14].
items.locator: Chapter I, §4, (4.1), p. 228 (quoted from Néron [27] and Gross [14]; computed in Chapter II (archimedean) and Chapter III (non-archimedean))
items.note: GZ.2 'construct the arithmetic intersection pairing from finite-place intersection lengths and archimedean Green functions. Include regular models, vertical correction divisors ... At infinite places prove existence and normalization of the Green kernel ... Export local height decomposition'; RP.0 'compare Néron–Tate and local heights on abelian varieties'. This plans the constructive (Gross [14]) description that Chapters II–III use; Néron's axiomatic uniqueness theorem is not stated as a target. Sign convention implied by (4.1): at non-archimedean v, ⟨a, b⟩_v = −(A·B) log q_v with A extended orthogonally to the vertical components (so that the global pairing is positive, see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/15). Not in either library.

items.name: The global height pairing ⟨a, b⟩ = Σ_v ⟨a, b⟩_v
items.statement: (4.2) If a and b are relatively prime divisors of degree zero on X defined over H, then ⟨a, b⟩_v = 0 for almost all v and ⟨a, b⟩ = Σ_v ⟨a, b⟩_v depends only on the images of a and b in J(H) (by (4.1) and the product formula). ⟨ , ⟩ is the global height pairing on J × J over H.
items.note: GZ.2 'Prove the Faltings–Hriljac comparison for degree-zero divisors with the canonical Jacobian pairing, including the sign and scalar fixed in GZ.0 ... Export local height decomposition, base-change and correspondence-adjunction APIs'; GZ.1 'Construct the bilinear height A(F̄)×A∨(F̄)→ℝ from the Poincaré biextension'. Not in either library for Jacobians of curves of genus > 1.

items.name: (4.3) The pairing is the Néron–Tate height and is positive definite
items.statement: (4.3) ĥ(a) = ⟨a, a⟩ is the canonical Néron–Tate height on J over H associated to the class of the divisor 2(Θ), Θ a symmetric theta divisor on J. Since 2Θ is ample, ĥ is a positive definite quadratic form on the real vector space J(H) ⊗ ℝ [24]; it extends to a Hermitian form on J(H) ⊗ ℂ.
items.note: GZ.1 'Construct Weil heights for the line bundles used on projective abelian varieties ... the canonical limit for symmetric bundles ... Prove positivity for ample symmetric bundles and characterize the zero locus as torsion over a number field using Northcott and finite generation'; GZ.2 (Faltings–Hriljac: equality of the local-symbol pairing with the canonical Jacobian pairing); GZ.0 'Never infer a regulator factor merely from the name “Néron–Tate”'. Library special case (dimension one only): tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.canonicalHeight (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/CanonicalHeight.lean:124) is the (O)-normalised height (1/2)·lim h_x(2ⁿP)/4ⁿ, so for an elliptic curve (Θ = (O)) GZ's ĥ = ĥ_{2(O)} = 2·canonicalHeight (GZ.0 packet node x-height-canonical-height), and Point.canonicalHeight_eq_zero_iff_isOfFinAddOrder (line 338, assuming a Northcott instance) gives definiteness mod torsion. J₀(N) is not an elliptic curve in general, so this is not the statement.

items.name: Newforms of weight 2 on Γ₀(N)
items.statement: The space of new forms of weight 2 on Γ₀(N) [1, 34] consists of the cusp forms f(z) = Σ_{n≥1} a_n e^{2πinz} of weight 2 and level N which are Petersson-orthogonal to every cusp form g(z) = g₀(dz) with g₀ of level N₀ properly dividing N and d a positive divisor of N/N₀.
items.note: tauceti:TauCeti.cuspFormsNew (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/Basic.lean:200) := CuspForm.peterssonOrthogonal (cuspFormsOld N k), with tauceti:TauCeti.cuspFormsOld (line 103) the span of the images of the level-raising operators V_d : S_k(Γ₁(M)) → S_k(Γ₁(N)) over d·M | N, M ≠ N. This is the Γ₁(N) new space; GZ's space is its trivial-nebentypus part (a more general statement). Normalized newforms: tauceti:HeckeRing.GL2.Newform (Newforms/Newform.lean:102), 'a good Hecke eigenform lying in the new subspace and normalised by a₁ = 1'.

items.name: The Petersson inner product (5.1)
items.statement: (5.1) For forms f, g of weight 2 on Γ₀(N): (f, g) = ∬_{Γ₀(N)\ℌ} f(z) \overline{g(z)} dx dy (z = x + iy), the integral over any fundamental domain for Γ₀(N) on the upper half plane ℌ (not normalized by the volume; linear in f, conjugate-linear in g).
items.note: tauceti:CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Petersson/FiniteIndex.lean:94) = Σ_{q ∈ SL₂(ℤ)/Γ·{±I}} ∫_𝒟 conj((f∣[k]q⁻¹)(τ))·(g∣[k]q⁻¹)(τ)·(Im τ)^k dμ with dμ = dx dy/y², un-normalized: for k = 2, Γ = Γ₀(N) this is ∬ \bar f g dx dy over a Γ₀(N)-domain. Convention difference: it is conjugate-linear in the FIRST argument, so GZ's (f, g) = peterssonInnerCosets g f. Positive definiteness: tauceti:CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets_definite (line 191).

items.name: Artin reciprocity for the Hilbert class field
items.statement: Gal(H/K) is canonically isomorphic to the class group Cl_K by the Artin map of global class field theory; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to an ideal class 𝒜.
items.locator: Chapter I, §5, p. 229 (quoted); convention fixed in §6, p. 230
items.note: ClassFieldTheory Layer 13 plans 'hilbertClassField is rayClassField at GlobalNumberFields.Modulus.one ... The Galois/class-group isomorphisms (gal_rayClassField_equiv_rayClassGroup, gal_hilbertClassField_equiv_classGroup)'; HE.0 'Derive ring class fields and Artin maps from existing class field theory'; GZ.0 packet node GZ.0/artin-map-convention 'The Gross–Zagier and Conrad convention sends uniformisers to arithmetic Frobenius elements'. Library partial: TauCeti.NumberFieldArithmetic.artinHomAway (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Ideal/ArtinMap.lean:175) is the ideal-theoretic Artin map for an abelian extension; its docstring says 'Nothing about the kernel, the image, or a factorization through ray class groups is proved here'.

items.name: The theta series θ_𝒜 of an ideal class
items.statement: (5.2) θ_𝒜(z) = 1/(2u) + Σ_{𝔞 ∈ 𝒜, 𝔞 integral} e^{2πi N𝔞 z} = Σ_{n≥0} r_𝒜(n) e^{2πinz}, where r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u) and, for n ≥ 1, r_𝒜(n) is the number of integral ideals 𝔞 in the class 𝒜 with norm n. θ_𝒜 is a modular form of weight 1 on Γ₁(|D|) with character ε [19] (Chapter IV §1: θ_𝒜 ∈ M₁(Γ₀(|D|), ε)).
items.locator: Chapter I, §5, (5.2), p. 229 (modularity quoted from Hecke [19]); Chapter IV, §1, (1.1), p. 270
items.note: Searched: 'theta'/'thetaSeries' in Tau Ceti (no theta series of quadratic forms) and Mathlib (only mathlib:jacobiTheta, Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/JacobiTheta/OneVariable.lean:29, θ(τ) = Σ_n e^{πin²τ}, a unary theta, not a binary form); no Tau Ceti roadmap document mentions theta series of quadratic forms. Atlas: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.5 defines the theta series of a 'rational quadratic/symplectic datum' adelically and MP.6 exports 'the quadratic-character and quaternionic-norm-form instances' to GZ.5; GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3's description names 'theta-series interfaces', but the GN blueprint assigns theta to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms (packet coverage of GN.3 and research/blueprint/readmes/GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic.md line 2100: 'MetaplecticAutomorphicForms owns theta'), and the accepted route 2 of PAPER-LI-23 imports 'the ordinary theta carrier' from MP.5; QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.1 has unary theta and eta functions only. No stage plans the classical weight-one form θ_𝒜 ∈ M₁(Γ₀(|D|), ε) of the norm form of an ideal class (MP.7 compares with classical forms only in half-integral weight). Routed (source) to MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.5. PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/177 (Chapter IV, (1.1)) is the same definition.

items.name: The Rankin-type L-series L_𝒜(f, s)
items.statement: (5.3) For f = Σ a_n qⁿ in the new space and 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K: L_𝒜(f, s) = Σ_{n≥1, (n, DN)=1} ε(n) n^{1−2s} · Σ_{n≥1} a_n r_𝒜(n) n^{−s}. The first factor is L(2s − 1, ε) with the Euler factors at all p | N removed (not removed in the announcement [17], which is in error; there it was denoted L_σ(f, s)). For weight 2k (§9, Chapter IV (0.1)): n^{1−2s} is replaced by n^{2k−1−2s}.
items.note: No stage plans the ideal-class partial series L_𝒜(f, s) (atlas search 'Rankin', 'ideal class', 'L_𝒜': only the general Rankin–Selberg AL.3 and YZZ GZ.6/GZ.8, which work with characters). L_𝒜 = h⁻¹ Σ_χ \bar χ(𝒜) L(f, χ, s), so it is recovered from the character L-functions of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/21 (planned) by finite Fourier inversion, but that reduction is not stated in any stage. Library ingredients only: Mathlib's LSeries and DirichletCharacter L-functions; Tau Ceti's TauCeti.normCoeff (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/NormCoeff.lean:101) regroups any ideal arithmetic function by absolute norm, so r_𝒜 = normCoeff (indicator of the integral ideals in 𝒜) is constructible, but no declaration defines r_𝒜, θ_𝒜 or L_𝒜. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: The L-function L(f, χ, s)
items.statement: (5.4) For f a Hecke eigenform in the new space of weight 2 on Γ₀(N), normalized by a₁ = 1, and χ a complex character of Cl_K: L(f, χ, s) = Σ_{𝒜 ∈ Cl_K} χ(𝒜) L_𝒜(f, s).
items.note: L(f, χ, s) is the Rankin–Selberg L-function of f and the weight-one form θ_χ = Σ_𝒜 χ(𝒜)θ_𝒜 (the base-change L-function of f to K twisted by χ), with centre s = 1. Plans: GZ.8 'Specialize to X₀(N) ... and finite ring-class characters'; AL.3 'Construct the GL_n×GL_m local zeta integrals ... Prove unramified calculations and the global unfolding for cuspidal data'; GZ.0 packet node GZ.0/unitary-and-motivic-centres (s = 1 vs s = 1/2); BSD.0 for χ = 1: 'the factorization L(E/K,s)=L(E,s)L(E^K,s)'. The identification of the classical Dirichlet series (5.4) with the automorphic L-function at the bad primes is not stated in any stage.

items.name: Euler product of L(f, χ, s)
items.statement: L(f, χ, s) has a formal Euler product in which the factor at p has degree 4 for p ∤ ND, degree 2 for p | D or p ∥ N, and degree 0 (i.e. is 1) for p² | N [13].
items.note: Checked: at p ∥ N (p splits since D ≡ □ mod 4N, a_p = ±1) the p-part of Σ a_n r_χ(n) n^{−s} is 1/((1 − a_p χ(𝔭)p^{−s})(1 − a_p χ(\bar𝔭)p^{−s})) and the ζ-factor at p is removed: degree 2; at p | D (𝔭² = (p)) it is 1/(1 − a_p χ(𝔭)p^{−s} + χ(𝔭)² p^{1−2s}) and ε(p) = 0: degree 2; at p² | N, a_{p^j} = 0 for j ≥ 1: degree 0. Plan: AL.3 'Prove unramified calculations' covers the degree-4 good factors; the explicit bad-prime degrees for this classical Dirichlet series are not stated in any stage: partial.

items.name: Absolute convergence of L_𝒜(f, s) and of the Euler product for Re(s) > 3/2
items.statement: The series defining L_𝒜(f, s) and the Euler product of L(f, χ, s) converge absolutely in the half-plane Re(s) > 3/2.
items.locator: Chapter I, §5, p. 229 ('It is not difficult to show'; no proof given)
items.note: Needs Σ |a_n| r_𝒜(n) n^{−σ} < ∞ for σ > 3/2, e.g. from a_n ≪ n^{1/2+ε} (Ramanujan–Petersson in weight 2, Eichler–Shimura) or from Rankin's mean-square bound Σ_{n≤X} |a_n|² ≪ X² plus Cauchy–Schwarz. Nearest library: tauceti:CuspForm.abscissaOfAbsConv_qExpansion_coeff_le (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/LFunction.lean:108), abscissa ≤ k/2 + 1 = 2 for f alone (Hecke's bound), which gives only Re(s) > 2. ModularForms Layer 9: 'Proving Ramanujan–Deligne is **not a target**'. No stage plans the Rankin mean-square estimate (atlas search 'mean square', 'Ramanujan'). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Proposition (5.5): continuation, functional equation and central vanishing
items.statement: Under the standing hypotheses (in particular D ≡ □ mod 4N, so ε(N) = 1), for f in the new space of weight 2 on Γ₀(N) (normalized eigenform for L(f, χ, s)), the functions L_𝒜(f, s) and L(f, χ, s) have analytic continuations to the entire s-plane, satisfy functional equations under s ↦ 2 − s, and vanish at s = 1. Precisely (Chapter IV (0.2) with k = 1): L*_𝒜(f, s) := (2π)^{−2s} N^s |D|^s Γ(s)² L_𝒜(f, s) = −ε(N) L*_𝒜(f, 2 − s), and −ε(N) = −1.
items.locator: Chapter I, §5, (5.5) Proposition, p. 229; proved in Chapter IV: continuation via Rankin's method (§1, Proposition (1.2)), functional equation (0.2) proved in §4, pp. 282–283 ('This completes the proof of the functional equation')
items.note: AL.3 'Prove holomorphic-multiple, vertical-strip, gamma-factor and functional-equation statements ... the global unfolding for cuspidal data'; GZ.6 'Prove the functional-equation vanishing that permits differentiation'; GZ.8 'For matching local signs deduce the global sign −1'. These plan the character form (L(f, χ, s)) in the automorphic normalization; the classical statement for L_𝒜 with the completed factor (2π)^{−2s}(N|D|)^sΓ(s)² is not stated. Library: nothing for Rankin–Selberg (Mathlib's ModularForm.L / CuspForm.differentiable_L, Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/LFunction.lean:134, 190, is the Hecke L-function of one form).

items.name: Theorem (6.1), first part: g_𝒜 is a cusp form
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter I: N ≥ 1 an integer (N > 1 is assumed in the proof, §9; N = 1 is treated in [18]); X = X₀(N) over ℚ, J = Jac(X); K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with discriminant D, (D, N) = 1, and D odd (hence D ≡ 1 mod 4 and squarefree, so (D, 2N) = 1; D = −3 is allowed, D = −4 is excluded); O = O_K; h = #Pic(O); u = #(O^×/{±1}) (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3); ε = (D/·) the quadratic character of K/ℚ; H = K(j(E)) the Hilbert class field; the Heegner hypothesis D ≡ β² (mod 4N) for some β ∈ ℤ (equivalently, every prime p | N splits in K); x a Heegner point of discriminant D on X; c = class of (x) − (∞) in J(H); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to the ideal class 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; ⟨ , ⟩ the global (Néron–Tate) height pairing over H extended Hermitian to J(H) ⊗ ℂ; ( , ) the Petersson product (5.1). Then the series g_𝒜(z) = Σ_{m≥1} ⟨c, T_m c^σ⟩ e^{2πimz} is a cusp form of weight 2 on Γ₀(N).
items.locator: Chapter I, §6, (6.1) Theorem, p. 230; proved in Chapter V, §1, p. 306 (formal argument: for any ℚ-linear α: 𝕋 → ℂ, Σ α(T_m) qᵐ ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)), via the perfect pairing 𝕋 × S₂(Γ₀(N), ℚ) → ℚ, (T, f) ↦ a₁(Tf); here α(T) = ⟨c, T c^σ⟩)
items.note: GZ.6 'Establish modularity of the curve-level Chow-valued series through the relevant product formula and theta construction' (the YZZ analogue: modularity of the generating series of Hecke correspondences, of which g_𝒜 is a height specialization); GZ.8 'Specialize to X₀(N)'; R14.2 'Define the integral Hecke algebra through its faithful action on an actual finite module'. GZ's own Hecke-duality argument (V §1) is not planned as such (atlas search 'perfect pairing', 'a₁(Tf)': nothing for modular forms). Library ingredient: a₁(T_p f) = a_p(f), tauceti:HeckeRing.GL2.qExpansion_coeff_one_heckeSlashGamma1CuspFormEnd_diagCosetGamma1 (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/HeckeSlash/Recurrence.lean:235, p prime). Hypotheses: the proof of modularity needs neither the Heegner hypothesis nor Heegner points ('if y and z are any two points of J₀(N)(H), then Σ ⟨y, T_m z⟩ qᵐ is a cusp form', p. 306). g_𝒜 depends on x only up to oldforms (p. 307).

items.name: Theorem (6.1)/(6.2): (f, g_𝒜) = u²|D|^{1/2}/(8π²) · L′_𝒜(f, 1)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter I: N ≥ 1 an integer (N > 1 is assumed in the proof, §9; N = 1 is treated in [18]); X = X₀(N) over ℚ, J = Jac(X); K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with discriminant D, (D, N) = 1, and D odd (hence D ≡ 1 mod 4 and squarefree, so (D, 2N) = 1; D = −3 is allowed, D = −4 is excluded); O = O_K; h = #Pic(O); u = #(O^×/{±1}) (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3); ε = (D/·) the quadratic character of K/ℚ; H = K(j(E)) the Hilbert class field; the Heegner hypothesis D ≡ β² (mod 4N) for some β ∈ ℤ (equivalently, every prime p | N splits in K); x a Heegner point of discriminant D on X; c = class of (x) − (∞) in J(H); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to the ideal class 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; ⟨ , ⟩ the global (Néron–Tate) height pairing over H extended Hermitian to J(H) ⊗ ℂ; ( , ) the Petersson product (5.1). Then for every f in the space of newforms of weight 2 on Γ₀(N): (6.2) (f, g_𝒜) = (u² |D|^{1/2} / (8π²)) · L′_𝒜(f, 1).
items.locator: Chapter I, §6, (6.1)–(6.2) Theorem, p. 230; proved in Chapter V, §1, pp. 306–307: ⟨c, T_m c^σ⟩ = u² a_{m,𝒜} for (m, N) = 1 (A/52), where Σ a_{m,𝒜} qᵐ = Φ_𝒜 is the cusp form of Chapter IV Theorem (6.9) with L′_𝒜(f, 1) = (8π²/√|D|)(f, Φ_𝒜); so g_𝒜 − u²Φ_𝒜 is old (A/53) and (f, g_𝒜) = u²(f, Φ_𝒜)
items.note: Plan is the YZZ generalization with explicit specialization: GZ.8 'Prove YZZ's corrected height identity ... Specialize to X₀(N), a rational elliptic modular quotient, generalized-Heegner quaternionic curves and finite ring-class characters. Prove the explicit formulas of Cai–Shu–Tian under their stated conductor conditions, keeping unit-group factors, discriminants, degrees and Manin constants'. (6.2) for all 𝒜 is equivalent, by Fourier inversion over Cl_K and the old/new decomposition, to the character formulas (6.3) for all χ and all newforms f, so the specialization in GZ.8 covers it; the ideal-class form itself is not stated. Constant check: (9.2) at k = 1 gives (f, φ_𝒜) = |D|^{1/2}/(8π²) L′_𝒜(f, 1), and g_𝒜 = u²φ_𝒜 + old gives (6.2).

items.name: The eigencomponents c_χ and c_{χ,f}
items.statement: Identify a character χ of Cl_K with a character of Gal(H/K). c_χ = Σ_{σ ∈ Gal(H/K)} χ^{−1}(σ) c^σ lies in the χ-eigenspace of J(H) ⊗ ℂ (it is h times the standard eigencomponent). For f a normalized newform, c_{χ,f} is the projection of c_χ to the f-isotypical component of J(H) ⊗ ℂ under the action of 𝕋 [13]. (Written c_{f,χ} on p. 228.)
items.note: Checked: (c_χ)^τ = Σ_σ χ^{−1}(σ) c^{στ} = χ(τ) c_χ, and c_χ = h·e_χ c with e_χ = h⁻¹ Σ χ^{−1}(σ)σ. GZ.8 'Identify the L-linear pairing of the χ- and χ⁻¹-Heegner points with the central derivative'; GZ.0 packet node GZ.0/trace-versus-average ('A formula written with averages and one written with traces differ by h² in every height' — relevant because c_χ is h times the eigencomponent); R14.5 'construct its Hecke ideal and the quotient A_f of ... J₀(N) for trivial character' (the f-isotypic part).

items.name: Theorem (6.3): the Gross–Zagier formula L′(f, χ, 1) = 8π²(f, f)/(h u² |D|^{1/2}) · ĥ(c_{χ,f})
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter I: N ≥ 1 an integer (N > 1 is assumed in the proof, §9; N = 1 is treated in [18]); X = X₀(N) over ℚ, J = Jac(X); K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with discriminant D, (D, N) = 1, and D odd (hence D ≡ 1 mod 4 and squarefree, so (D, 2N) = 1; D = −3 is allowed, D = −4 is excluded); O = O_K; h = #Pic(O); u = #(O^×/{±1}) (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3); ε = (D/·) the quadratic character of K/ℚ; H = K(j(E)) the Hilbert class field; the Heegner hypothesis D ≡ β² (mod 4N) for some β ∈ ℤ (equivalently, every prime p | N splits in K); x a Heegner point of discriminant D on X; c = class of (x) − (∞) in J(H); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to the ideal class 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; ⟨ , ⟩ the global (Néron–Tate) height pairing over H extended Hermitian to J(H) ⊗ ℂ; ( , ) the Petersson product (5.1). Let f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) be a normalized newform (Hecke eigenform in the new space, a₁ = 1) and χ a complex character of Cl_K ≅ Gal(H/K). Then (6.3) L′(f, χ, 1) = (8π² (f, f) / (h u² |D|^{1/2})) · ĥ(c_{χ,f}), where ĥ is the canonical height on J over H (4.3), extended Hermitian. In particular c_{χ,f} ≠ 0 in J(H) ⊗ ℂ if and only if L′(f, χ, 1) ≠ 0 (p. 228).
items.locator: Chapter I, §6, (6.3) Theorem, p. 230 (announced p. 228); proved in Chapter V, §1, p. 308 from (6.2)
items.note: Derivation checked: g_𝒜 = Σ_{f′} ⟨c_{f′}, c^σ_{f′}⟩ f′ + old, so (f, g_𝒜) = ⟨c_f, c_f^σ⟩ (f, f); ĥ(c_{χ,f}) = Σ_{σ,τ} χ^{−1}(σ)χ(τ)⟨c_f^σ, c_f^τ⟩ = h Σ_ρ χ(ρ)⟨c_f, c_f^ρ⟩; summing (6.2) against χ(𝒜) gives (6.3). Plan: GZ.8 (YZZ identity specialized to X₀(N) and ring-class characters, 'keeping unit-group factors, discriminants'); BSD.3 consumes it ('Apply GZ.8 with a suitable nonzero test vector and its explicit positive height comparison'). Conrad 2004 (§1) re-proves only Chapter III and remarks that, provided the analytic results were proved for even discriminants, the main results 'would be valid without parity restriction on the discriminant' — so, after Conrad's treatment of Chapter III, the oddness of D is needed only by the analytic part of the proof (Chapter IV). Hypotheses: N ≥ 1 with N > 1 in the proof; (D, N) = 1; D odd (so (D, 2N) = 1; D = −3 allowed with u = 3); every prime dividing N split in K; χ arbitrary (trivial and genus characters included).

items.name: (6.4) Heights over H, K and ℚ
items.statement: (6.4) ⟨a, b⟩_H = h ⟨a, b⟩_K = 2h ⟨a, b⟩_ℚ, the global heights on J over H, K and ℚ ([H:K] = h, [K:ℚ] = 2); the constants of (6.2), (6.3) differ from those of the announcement [17] because [17] used the height over ℚ.
items.note: GZ.1 'independence under finite extension with the specified arithmetic-degree normalization'; GZ.0 packet gap 'The [K:ℚ] normalisation of heights over number fields' (neither library has a number-field height instance: 'Mathlib's Height/Basic.lean lists it as a TODO'). Convention: for classes defined only over H, ⟨ , ⟩_K is defined as [H:K]⁻¹⟨ , ⟩_H.

items.name: 8π²(f, f) equals the period integral ‖ω_f‖²
items.statement: For ω_f = 2πi f(z) dz the eigendifferential of f on X(ℂ): ‖ω_f‖² = ∬_{X(ℂ)} ω_f ∧ i \bar{ω_f} = 8π²(f, f).
items.note: Checked: ω_f ∧ i\bar ω_f = (2πi)(−2πi)·i·|f|² dz∧d\bar z and i dz∧d\bar z = 2 dx∧dy, so the integrand is 8π²|f|² dx dy. GZ.0 'Construct explicit comparison maps for the choices of volume, differential ...'; GZ.3 'compare with the Petersson pairing'; packet node ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3/cup-product-petersson (the analogous cup-product/Petersson comparison). Only a normalization identity; no stage states it.

items.name: (6.5) The formula with heights over K
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter I: N ≥ 1 an integer (N > 1 is assumed in the proof, §9; N = 1 is treated in [18]); X = X₀(N) over ℚ, J = Jac(X); K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with discriminant D, (D, N) = 1, and D odd (hence D ≡ 1 mod 4 and squarefree, so (D, 2N) = 1; D = −3 is allowed, D = −4 is excluded); O = O_K; h = #Pic(O); u = #(O^×/{±1}) (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3); ε = (D/·) the quadratic character of K/ℚ; H = K(j(E)) the Hilbert class field; the Heegner hypothesis D ≡ β² (mod 4N) for some β ∈ ℤ (equivalently, every prime p | N splits in K); x a Heegner point of discriminant D on X; c = class of (x) − (∞) in J(H); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to the ideal class 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; ⟨ , ⟩ the global (Néron–Tate) height pairing over H extended Hermitian to J(H) ⊗ ℂ; ( , ) the Petersson product (5.1). For a normalized newform f and a character χ of Cl_K: (6.5) L′(f, χ, 1) = (‖ω_f‖² / (u² |D|^{1/2})) · ĥ_K(c_{χ,f}), with ĥ_K = h⁻¹ ĥ_H the height over K; u = 1 when |D| > 4.
items.note: Checked from (6.3) and (6.4). Planned with (6.3) in GZ.8.

items.name: The Hasse–Weil L-function L(E, s) of an elliptic curve over ℚ
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E over ℚ, L(E, s) = Σ_{n≥1} a_n n^{−s} is the Dirichlet series given by the Euler product over all primes p whose factor at p is determined by the reduction of a minimal model of E modulo p: (1 − a_p p^{−s} + p^{1−2s})^{−1} with a_p = p + 1 − #E(𝔽_p) when E has good reduction at p, and (1 − a_p p^{−s})^{−1} with a_p = 1, −1 or 0 when the reduction is split multiplicative, non-split multiplicative or additive.
items.locator: Chapter I, §7, pp. 230–231 ('The L-function L(E, s) is a Dirichlet series Σ a_n n^{−s} defined by an Euler product which determines the number of points on E (mod p) for all primes p [35]')
items.note: Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/LFunction.lean: WeierstrassCurve.LFunction (line 79) is the formal Dirichlet series eulerProduct over the height-one primes of 𝓞 K of the local Euler factors 1/f_p(‖p‖^{−s}), with f_p = 1 − a_p T + ‖p‖T² at good reduction (a_p = ‖p‖ + 1 − |W(κ_p)|, computed on the minimal model W.minimal), 1 − T at split multiplicative, 1 + T at non-split multiplicative and 1 at additive reduction; WeierstrassCurve.LSeries (line 84) is the complex L-series of its coefficients. For K = ℚ this is the paper's L(E, s). The paper's next sentence, absolute convergence of the product for Re(s) > 3/2 (from Hasse's bound, planned in Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 3), is part of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/32 and is not in either library; its analytic continuation is RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0 and EllipticCurveModularity:R29.6. Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: Modularity of E/ℚ and the functional equation (7.1) (assumed in §7)
items.statement: Let E/ℚ be an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = Σ_{n≥1} a_n n^{−s} (Euler product, convergent for Re(s) > 3/2). Assumed (then conjectured [35, 38]; 'verified for a given curve by a finite computation'): f(z) = Σ a_n e^{2πinz} is a newform of weight 2 and level N equal to the conductor of E. In that case L*(E, s) = ∫_0^∞ f(iy/√N) y^s dy/y = N^{s/2}(2π)^{−s}Γ(s)L(E, s) is entire and (7.1) L*(E, s) = ±L*(E, 2 − s).
items.locator: Chapter I, §7, (7.1), pp. 230–231 (hypothesis of all of §7 and of Chapter V §2)
items.note: Packet node EllipticCurveModularity:R29.6/modularity-theorem: 'Every elliptic curve E/ℚ of conductor N is modular: equivalently (i) there is a normalised newform F ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) with rational integer coefficients and A_p(F) = a_p(E) for all primes p ... (iii) there is a nonconstant morphism X₀(N) → E over ℚ'; R29.6 'Transfer the analytic continuation and functional equation from ModularForms after proving equality of every local factor'; BSD.0 'Build the interface from the Euler product/Dirichlet series of E to its modular entire continuation and completed functional equation'; ModularForms Layer 7 (Hecke's functional equation with the Fricke companion, sign i^k ε_N). Checked the Mellin identity ∫ f(iy/√N) y^s dy/y = N^{s/2}(2π)^{−s}Γ(s)L(E, s). Library partial: Mathlib's ModularForm.Λ / CuspForm.differentiable_L (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/LFunction.lean) use the S-transform, not W_N; no level-N functional equation in Tau Ceti (grep 'functional_equation' in TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms: none).

items.name: The Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture (7.2) (as used)
items.statement: Conjecture: r = ord_{s=1} L(E, s) equals rank E(ℚ), and (7.2) L^{(r)}(E, 1) = α · Ω · R, where Ω is the real period of a regular differential on E over ℚ, R = det(⟨P_i, P_j⟩) is the regulator of the global height pairing on a basis P_1, …, P_r of E(ℚ) ⊗ ℚ, and α is a non-zero rational number (with a conjectural arithmetic description [35]).
items.note: A conjecture, recorded as the definition of the predicted formula. BSD.5 'Define the rational BSD defect as the analytic leading term divided by the arithmetic expression'; EllipticCurves Layer 7 'the BSD quotient Ω(E) · Reg(E/K) · #Ш(E/K) · ∏_p c_p / #E(K)_tors²'; GZ.0 packet node GZ.0/bsd-regulator: 'Reg_BSD ... equals 2^r · regulator W'. Library partial: tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.regulator (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MordellWeil/Regulator.lean:91), |det| of the Gram matrix of the halved pairing neronTatePairing. Since (7.2) only asserts α ∈ ℚ^× and R is taken on a basis of E(ℚ) ⊗ ℚ, the factor 2^r and the choice of basis are absorbed into α.

items.name: Waldspurger's non-vanishing theorem for quadratic twists (as used)
items.statement: (Waldspurger [36, Th. 2.3], [37, Th. 4], as applied in Chapter V §§1–2.) Let f be a normalized newform of weight 2 on Γ₀(N) whose L-function has sign −1 in its functional equation (f|w_N = f). Then there is an imaginary quadratic field K = ℚ(√D) 'as in this paper' (D odd, (D, N) = 1, D ≡ □ mod 4N) such that the twist L_ε(f, s) = Σ ε(n) a_n n^{−s}, ε = (D/·), satisfies L_ε(f, 1) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Chapter I, §7, p. 231 ('a theorem of Waldspurger'); precise use in Chapter V, §1, p. 309 and §2, p. 312
items.note: BSD.2 'Prove the quadratic-twist nonvanishing theorem needed to choose a Heegner field, including finitely many prescribed splitting/local character conditions compatible with the functional equation. For a weight-two newform, construct twists with nonzero central value in the sign + branch ... Specify the permitted discriminants, coprimality, negative sign at infinity' — planned by a different route (Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein / Friedberg–Hoffstein double Dirichlet series), not Waldspurger's. GZ.5 'Establish the Waldspurger period formula' is a different theorem (toric periods). Note [36] in the bibliography is Vignéras's exposé and [37] Waldspurger's preprint.

items.name: Theorem (7.3): L′(E, 1) is a rational multiple of Ω·⟨P, P⟩
items.statement: Let E/ℚ be an elliptic curve of conductor N which is modular (its L-series is that of a weight-2 newform on Γ₀(N); assumption of §7). Assume L(E, 1) = 0. Then there is a rational point P ∈ E(ℚ) such that L′(E, 1) = α · Ω · ⟨P, P⟩ with α ∈ ℚ^×, Ω the real period of a regular differential on E over ℚ.
items.locator: Chapter I, §7, (7.3) Theorem, p. 231; proved in Chapter V, §2, pp. 310–312 (trivial with P = 0 if L′(E, 1) = 0; otherwise sign −1, choose K by Waldspurger with L(E′, 1) ≠ 0 for the twist E′, apply Theorem V.(2.1) and take P = P_K + \bar P_K)
items.note: BSD.5 'Prove the rationality and positivity of L*(E,1)/(Ω_E Reg_E) in analytic ranks 0 and 1: use modular-symbol rationality at rank zero and the Gross–Zagier/period/index comparison at rank one. Relate the height of a non-torsion Heegner point to the squared index of its class in the rank-one lattice'; BSD.3 (non-torsion Heegner point from GZ.8). The planned route produces the rank-one statement for all E/ℚ (modularity from R29.6), which contains (7.3).

items.name: Theorem (7.3) 1): L′(E, 1) ≠ 0 ⟹ E(ℚ) has a point of infinite order
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of (7.3) (E/ℚ modular, L(E, 1) = 0): if L′(E, 1) ≠ 0 then E(ℚ) contains elements of infinite order.
items.locator: Chapter I, §7, (7.3) 1), p. 231; proved in Chapter V, §2, p. 310/312
items.note: BSD.3 'Given analytic rank one over ℚ, use BSD.2 to choose K ... Apply GZ.8 with a suitable nonzero test vector and its explicit positive height comparison to obtain a non-torsion Heegner point in E(K) ... Show that the rational trace/eigenspace selected by the functional equation gives the rank-one part for E and not its twist'. BSD.3 plans the stronger rank = 1 (with Kolyvagin, HE.7).

items.name: Theorem (7.3) 2): BSD formula up to ℚ^× in rank one
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of (7.3) (E/ℚ modular, L(E, 1) = 0): if L′(E, 1) ≠ 0 and rank E(ℚ) = 1, then formula (7.2) holds (with r = 1) for some non-zero rational number α.
items.locator: Chapter I, §7, (7.3) 2), p. 231; proved in Chapter V, §2, pp. 310–312
items.note: BSD.5 (rationality of L*(E,1)/(Ω_E Reg_E) in analytic rank 1). Deduction: P = n P₁ + torsion for a generator P₁, so ⟨P, P⟩ = n² R.

items.name: Sign −1 and trivial Heegner point force ord_{s=1} L(E, s) ≥ 3
items.statement: Let E/ℚ be modular. If the sign in (7.1) is −1 and the point P of Theorem (7.3) is trivial in E(ℚ) ⊗ ℚ, then r = ord_{s=1} L(E, s) ≥ 3.
items.note: Sign −1 gives odd order (BSD.0 'Prove the root-number parity relation for the analytic order'), and L′(E, 1) = αΩ⟨P, P⟩ = 0. Planned only through the components (BSD.0 parity + the GZ/BSD.5 formula).

items.name: Proposition (7.4): an elliptic curve of analytic rank 3
items.statement: The elliptic curve E: −139y² = x³ + 10x² − 20x + 8 (conductor 714877 = 37·139²) has ord_{s=1} L(E, s) = rank E(ℚ) = 3.
items.locator: Chapter I, §7, (7.4) Proposition, p. 231 (the triviality of P is proved in [17] or [39]; not proved in this paper); conductor stated on p. 232
items.note: Checked the data: y² = x³ + 10x² − 20x + 8 has c₄ = 2560, c₆ = −128512, Δ = 2¹²·37; scaling by u = 2 gives c₄ = 160, c₆ = −2008, Δ = 37, the invariants of y² + y = x³ + x² − 3x + 1, a curve of conductor 37 with j = 4096000/37 (so not 37a, j = 110592/37; the rank-0 isogeny class 37b); E is its quadratic twist by −139 (≡ 1 mod 4, prime to 2·37), of conductor 37·139² = 714877, as printed. Proving ord = 3 needs the sign −1, GZ with P torsion (ord ≥ 3) and a certified L‴(E, 1) ≠ 0; rank = 3 needs three independent points and a descent bound. No stage plans this example (atlas search 'rank 3', 'order three', '139', '714877': nothing; BSD.9 plans only rank-0/1 test curves). Routed (new) to the proposed roadmap EffectiveClassNumberProblem.

items.name: Goldfeld's theorem (quoted, [12])
items.statement: Goldfeld's theorem [12], in the form used here: the existence of a modular elliptic curve E/ℚ whose L-function has a zero of order 3 at s = 1 (as in (7.4)) yields an effective lower bound for the class number h(D) of imaginary quadratic fields, of the shape (8.1)/(8.2).
items.locator: Chapter I, §8, p. 231–232 (quoted; 'For the analytic details of Goldfeld's method, see Oesterlé [28]')
items.note: The paper does not restate Goldfeld's hypotheses (sign, (D, N_E) conditions, twist conditions); they must be taken from Goldfeld 1976 or Oesterlé's Bourbaki exposé [28]. No stage plans it (atlas: 'Goldfeld' occurs only in BSD.2/MP.7 as 'no Goldfeld density assertion is assumed', a different conjecture; 'class number' + 'lower bound': only upper bounds in Completed/EffectiveBounds). Routed (new) to the proposed roadmap EffectiveClassNumberProblem.

items.name: Theorem (8.1): effective lower bound h(D) > κ(ε)(log|D|)^{1−ε}
items.statement: For every ε > 0 there is an effectively computable constant κ(ε) > 0 such that h(D) > κ(ε)(log|D|)^{1−ε} for the class number h(D) of every imaginary quadratic field of discriminant D.
items.locator: Chapter I, §8, (8.1) Theorem, p. 232 (from Goldfeld's theorem [12] and Proposition (7.4); details in Oesterlé [28])
items.note: No stage plans effective lower bounds for class numbers (atlas searches 'class number' with 'lower'/'effective', 'Siegel', 'class number one', 'Montgomery': only Tau Ceti's EffectiveBounds upper bound h_F ≤ |d_F|·4ⁿ and ArithmeticStatistics ST.3 class-group statistics). The hypothesis on D here is only that K is imaginary quadratic (the standing 'D odd' of the paper is not used). Routed (new) to the proposed roadmap EffectiveClassNumberProblem.

items.name: Oesterlé's explicit inequality (8.2)
items.statement: (Oesterlé [28], slightly simplified.) C(t) h(D) ≥ log|D|, where C(t) is an explicitly given function of t = the number of prime divisors of D, with log C(t) ~ 4√(t / log t) as t → ∞. Using Mestre's curve of conductor 5077 instead of (7.4), (8.2) holds for D prime to 5077 with C(1) = 55, i.e. h(D) > (1/55) log|D| for |D| prime.
items.note: Consistency check: Oesterlé's factor ∏_{p | D} (1 − ⌊2√p⌋/(p+1)) is worst for the first t primes, where −log ∏ ~ Σ_{p ≤ t log t} 2/√p ~ 4√(t log t)/log t = 4√(t/log t), matching the printed asymptotic. 'D prime' means |D| prime. Not planned (as for PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/41). Routed (new) to the proposed roadmap EffectiveClassNumberProblem.

items.name: Genus theory: 2^{t−1} divides h(D)
items.statement: For an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant D with t distinct prime divisors of D, 2^{t−1} divides h(D).
items.locator: Chapter I, §8, p. 232 (used to deduce (8.1) from (8.2): log C(t) ≪ (log h(D))^{1/2})
items.note: tauceti:TauCeti.Multiquadratic.twoRank_eq_ncard_ramifiedPrimes_sub_one (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Quadratic/TwoRank.lean:155): for K = ℚ(θ), minpoly ℤ θ = X² − C d, d squarefree, d < 0, TauCeti.ClassGroup.twoRank (𝓞 K) = (ramifiedPrimes K).ncard − 1; tauceti:NumberField.two_pow_classGroupTwoRank_dvd_classNumber (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/ClassGroupElementaryTwoQuotient.lean:59): 2 ^ twoRank (𝓞 K) ∣ classNumber K. Composing gives 2^{t−1} | h(D) with t = #ramified primes = #prime divisors of D. Library, as a two-step composition (no single declaration).

items.name: Mestre's curve of conductor 5077 (quoted, [26])
items.statement: Proposition (7.4) also holds for the elliptic curve y² − y = x³ − 7x + 6 of conductor 5077: its L-function has a zero of order 3 at s = 1 and its rank is 3 [26].
items.note: y² − y = x³ − 7x + 6 is ℚ-isomorphic to the tabulated y² + y = x³ − 7x + 6 (5077a1) by y ↦ −y. Not planned (no stage mentions 5077 or rank-3 curves). Routed (new) to the proposed roadmap EffectiveClassNumberProblem.

items.name: The largest |D| with h(D) = 3 is 907
items.statement: Combining (8.2) (with Mestre's curve) with earlier results of Montgomery and Weinberger, the largest value of |D| with h(D) = 3 is 907.
items.note: Not planned; no class-number tables for class number 3 in the library or the atlas. Routed (new) to the proposed roadmap EffectiveClassNumberProblem.

items.name: Manin–Drinfeld: the cuspidal class (0) − (∞) is torsion
items.statement: The cuspidal divisor (0) − (∞) has finite order in J(ℚ). Hence, with d = (x) − (0), ⟨c, T_m c^σ⟩ = ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩ for all m.
items.locator: Chapter I, §9, p. 232 (used without reference; Chapter V §1, p. 306 cites 'the Manin-Drinfeld theorem ([4], Cor. 3.6)')
items.note: Planned in the general setting of X₁(N): packet node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/manin-drinfeld states 'For N ≥ 1 the divisor map div ⊗ ℚ : O*(Y₁(N)(ℂ)) ⊗ ℚ → Div⁰(P_N) ⊗ ℚ is surjective ... equivalently every degree-zero divisor supported on the cusps has finite order in Pic⁰(X₁(N)(ℂ))', and the modular-units node of the same packet adds that 'no modular-curves roadmap plans it'. The X₀(N) statement is a consequence: for π : X₁(N) → X₀(N), π*((0) − (∞)) is a degree-zero cuspidal divisor, hence of finite order, and π_*π* is multiplication by deg π, so (0) − (∞) has finite order in J₀(N)(ℂ), hence in J₀(N)(ℚ) because the divisor is rational. The ModularCurvesPartII packet node R14.6/rational-cusp-abel-jacobi uses the fact in a test ('AJ_0 and AJ_∞ differ by the class of 0 − ∞ (torsion by Manin–Drinfeld)'). ⟨c, T_m c^σ⟩ = ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩ follows because the height pairing vanishes on torsion. Same statement as PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/279. Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 10 uses no Jacobian.

items.name: Proposition (9.1): when c and T_m d^σ are relatively prime
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter I: N ≥ 1 an integer (N > 1 is assumed in the proof, §9; N = 1 is treated in [18]); X = X₀(N) over ℚ, J = Jac(X); K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with discriminant D, (D, N) = 1, and D odd (hence D ≡ 1 mod 4 and squarefree, so (D, 2N) = 1; D = −3 is allowed, D = −4 is excluded); O = O_K; h = #Pic(O); u = #(O^×/{±1}) (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3); ε = (D/·) the quadratic character of K/ℚ; H = K(j(E)) the Hilbert class field; the Heegner hypothesis D ≡ β² (mod 4N) for some β ∈ ℤ (equivalently, every prime p | N splits in K); x a Heegner point of discriminant D on X; c = class of (x) − (∞) in J(H); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to the ideal class 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; ⟨ , ⟩ the global (Néron–Tate) height pairing over H extended Hermitian to J(H) ⊗ ℂ; ( , ) the Petersson product (5.1). Let m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1. The divisors c = (x) − (∞) and T_m d^σ = T_m(x^σ) − T_m(0) are relatively prime if and only if N > 1 and r_𝒜(m) = 0.
items.locator: Chapter I, §9, (9.1) Proposition, p. 232 ('it is easy to show'); refined in Chapter III, (4.3) Proposition, p. 258 (the multiplicity of x in T_m x^σ is r_𝒜(m), m prime to N) and Chapter II §5, p. 249
items.note: Checked: the supports are {x, ∞} and supp T_m(x^σ) ∪ supp T_m(0); for (m, N) = 1, T_m(0) = σ₁(m)·(0) (T_m preserves the cusp class of 0, which has one element), 0 ≠ ∞ iff N > 1, and x occurs in T_m(x^σ) with multiplicity r_𝒜(m) (III (4.3)). The hypothesis (m, N) = 1 is the standing one of §9 ('for those m which are prime to N'). Plans: HE.2 'Compute Hecke correspondences on CM points by classifying the local cyclic subgroups/optimal embeddings'; GZ.6 'Prove pullback/push-forward, Hecke and diagonal identities'. Partial: the multiplicity formula r_𝒜(m) is not stated.

items.name: Local symbols for non-coprime divisors (r_𝒜(m) ≠ 0)
items.statement: When r_𝒜(m) ≠ 0, the global pairing ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩ is still defined by (4.2), and it is decomposed into local terms by a mild extension of Néron's local theory [14]: the local symbols are defined after choosing a tangent vector at x (Chapter II §5 archimedean, Chapter III §8 non-archimedean); the sum over all places does not depend on the choice.
items.locator: Chapter I, §9, p. 232; constructed in Chapter II, §5, pp. 249–252 and Chapter III, §8, pp. 262–264
items.note: GZ.2 'Handle rational degree-one Hodge classes and self-intersections by a genuine regularization/intersection construction'. The tangent-vector (adjunction) normalization of GZ is not named; details belong to the chunks for Chapters II §5 and III §8.

items.name: (9.2) for k = 1: the holomorphic form φ_𝒜 representing L′_𝒜(f, 1)
items.statement: Let N ≥ 1, K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with (D, N) = 1 and ε(N) = 1 (the Heegner hypothesis is not needed), 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K. There is a cusp form φ_𝒜(z) = Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,𝒜} e^{2πimz} of weight 2 on Γ₀(N) with (f, φ_𝒜) = (|D|^{1/2} / (8π²)) · L′_𝒜(f, 1) for all f in the space of newforms of weight 2 and level N; φ_𝒜 is unique up to oldforms, and its coefficients a_{m,𝒜} for (m, N) = 1 are given explicitly in Chapter IV.
items.locator: Chapter I, §9, (9.2) with k = 1, p. 233; proved in Chapter IV, Theorem (6.9), p. 305 (via Rankin's method §§1–3, the functional equation §4 and holomorphic projection with Hecke's trick §6)
items.note: GZ.6 'Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels and their central derivatives, normalized local Whittaker terms, holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection. Prove the functional-equation vanishing that permits differentiation ... Compare the arithmetic height kernel with the analytic derivative'. This is the YZZ adelic analogue; the classical theta×Eisenstein kernel, the trace to Γ₀(N) and Sturm's holomorphic projection of Chapter IV are not planned as such, and the explicit a_{m,𝒜} only through GZ.8's specialization. Constant check: (2k−2)!/(2^{4k−1}π^{2k}) at k = 1 is 1/(8π²), matching Theorem IV.(6.9) L′_𝒜(f,1) = (8π²/√|D|)(f, Φ_𝒜) (printed '√δ' on p. 305, see notes).

items.name: (9.2) for k > 1: the holomorphic form φ_𝒜 of weight 2k
items.statement: Let k > 1, N ≥ 1, (D, N) = 1, ε(N) = 1, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K. Define L_𝒜(f, s) for f of weight 2k as in (5.3) with n^{1−2s} replaced by n^{2k−1−2s}; it satisfies a functional equation under s ↦ 2k − s and vanishes at s = k. There is a cusp form φ_𝒜 = Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,𝒜} e^{2πimz} of weight 2k on Γ₀(N) with (9.2) (f, φ_𝒜) = ((2k−2)! / (2^{4k−1} π^{2k})) |D|^{1/2} L′_𝒜(f, k) for all f in the space of newforms of weight 2k and level N; φ_𝒜 is unique up to oldforms.
items.locator: Chapter I, §9, (9.2), p. 233; proved in Chapter IV, Theorem (5.8), p. 294 (L′_𝒜(f, k) = 2^{4k−1}π^{2k}/((2k−2)!√|D|) · (f, Σ a_{m,𝒜} qᵐ))
items.note: Constants checked against Theorem IV.(5.8) (page image p. 294). The Petersson product in weight 2k is implicitly ∬ f \bar g y^{2k−2} dx dy ((5.1) is stated only for weight 2). No stage plans higher-weight Gross–Zagier/Rankin derivative formulas (atlas search 'higher weight' with 'Gross'/'height'/'Heegner', 'Zhang': nothing; GeneralizedHeegnerCycles GH.0–GH.8 concern p-adic Abel–Jacobi images, not this identity). Nearest: GZ.6 (weight 2 only). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 8: HigherGreenFunctionCMValues (Part II).

items.name: Existence and uniqueness of φ_𝒜 from non-degeneracy of the Petersson product
items.statement: Since the Petersson product is non-degenerate on the (finite-dimensional) space of newforms of weight 2k and level N, for every linear functional ℓ on it (here ℓ(f) = const · L′_𝒜(f, k)) there is a cusp form φ with (f, φ) = ℓ(f) for all newforms f, and φ is determined up to the addition of an oldform.
items.note: A composition of library statements, not a single declaration: mathlib:InnerProductSpace.toDual (Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Dual.lean:137, Fréchet–Riesz 'any ℓ in the dual of a Hilbert space E is of the form fun u => ⟪y, u⟫'); tauceti:CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosetsCore (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Petersson/FiniteIndex.lean:296, the Petersson product as an InnerProductSpace.Core — a def, 'no InnerProductSpace instance is derived from it', so an instance must be built from the core); tauceti:TauCeti.isCompl_cuspFormsOld_cuspFormsNew (Newforms/Basic.lean:247, old ⊕ new = S_k(Γ₁(N))). Tau Ceti's product is conjugate-linear in the first slot, matching Riesz's ⟪y, u⟫ with y = φ.

items.name: (9.3) ⟨c, T_m c^σ⟩ = u² a_{m,𝒜} for (m, N) = 1
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter I: N ≥ 1 an integer (N > 1 is assumed in the proof, §9; N = 1 is treated in [18]); X = X₀(N) over ℚ, J = Jac(X); K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with discriminant D, (D, N) = 1, and D odd (hence D ≡ 1 mod 4 and squarefree, so (D, 2N) = 1; D = −3 is allowed, D = −4 is excluded); O = O_K; h = #Pic(O); u = #(O^×/{±1}) (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3); ε = (D/·) the quadratic character of K/ℚ; H = K(j(E)) the Hilbert class field; the Heegner hypothesis D ≡ β² (mod 4N) for some β ∈ ℤ (equivalently, every prime p | N splits in K); x a Heegner point of discriminant D on X; c = class of (x) − (∞) in J(H); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to the ideal class 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; ⟨ , ⟩ the global (Néron–Tate) height pairing over H extended Hermitian to J(H) ⊗ ℂ; ( , ) the Petersson product (5.1). For every m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1: (9.3) ⟨c, T_m c^σ⟩ = u² a_{m,𝒜}, where a_{m,𝒜} are the coefficients of φ_𝒜 (k = 1): the explicit formula of Chapter IV for a_{m,𝒜} coincides, up to the factor u², with the sum over all places v of H of the local height contributions ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v.
items.locator: Chapter I, §9, (9.3), p. 233; proved in Chapter V, §1, pp. 306–307 (archimedean part: II Propositions (4.2), (5.8) with IV Proposition (4.6); non-archimedean part: III Propositions (9.2), (9.7), (9.11); compared with IV Theorem (6.9))
items.note: GZ.7 'Prove the finite-place identities between CM intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local representation densities/Whittaker functions ... Prove the archimedean Green-function identity ... Assemble local formulas into the global kernel comparison of GZ.6'; GZ.6 'Compare the arithmetic height kernel with the analytic derivative modulo the explicitly identified constant/Eisenstein/old components'. The YZZ kernel identity is the analogue; the coefficient-by-coefficient classical identity on X₀(N) is planned only via GZ.8's specialization.

items.name: Atkin–Lehner main lemma (a form with a_m = 0 for all (m, N) = 1 is old)
items.statement: If g ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) has Fourier coefficients a_m(g) = 0 for all m prime to N, then g lies in the old space. (Used to conclude from (9.3) that g_𝒜 − u²φ_𝒜 is an old form, so (f, g_𝒜) = u²(f, φ_𝒜) for newforms f.)
items.locator: Chapter I, §9, p. 233; Chapter V, §1, p. 307 (used implicitly; Atkin–Lehner [1])
items.note: tauceti:TauCeti.mem_cuspFormsOld_of_forall_coprime_qExpansion_coeff_eq_zero (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/MainLemma.lean:178): 'a cusp form in S_k(Γ₁(N), χ) whose Fourier coefficients vanish at every index coprime to N lies in the old subspace' (hf : f ∈ cuspFormCharSpace k χ, hvan : ∀ n, Nat.Coprime n N → (qExpansion 1 f).coeff n = 0 ⊢ f ∈ cuspFormsOld N k). GZ's case is χ trivial, weight 2 (a special case of the library statement).

items.name: Complex uniformization of X₀(N)
items.statement: An elliptic curve E/ℂ is ℂ/L, L determined up to homothety. A non-cuspidal point x = (E →φ E′) of X = X₀(N) can be normalised to E(ℂ) = ℂ/L, E′(ℂ) = ℂ/L′ with L ⊂ L′, φ = identity, L′/L ≅ ℤ/Nℤ; choose an oriented basis ⟨ω₁, ω₂⟩ of L (Im(ω₁ω̄₂) > 0) such that ⟨ω₁, ω₂/N⟩ is a basis of L′. Then z = ω₁/ω₂ ∈ 𝔥 is determined by x up to Γ = Γ₀(N) = {(a b; c d) ∈ PSL₂(ℤ) : c ≡ 0 (mod N)}; conversely z ∈ Γ\𝔥 gives x = (ℂ/⟨z,1⟩ →id ℂ/⟨z,1/N⟩). Hence (X ∖ {cusps})(ℂ) ≅ Γ₀(N)\𝔥 and X(ℂ) ≅ Γ₀(N)\𝔥*, 𝔥* = 𝔥 ∪ ℙ¹(ℚ) with the usual topology.
items.note: Library: only the group. Mathlib .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups.lean:79 `def Gamma0 : Subgroup SL(2, ℤ)` (carrier {g | (g 1 0 : ZMod N) = 0}); no quotient Γ₀(N)\𝔥 as a Riemann surface and no moduli comparison in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (Tau Ceti has only Analysis/Complex/Fuchsian/{ProperAction,Stabilizer}.lean). Planned: R12.2 "Classify full, Γ₁ and Γ₀ level structures under uniformisation, and derive the corresponding analytic quotient with its functorial action ... Prove that the resulting analytic map is an isomorphism, not just a bijection of complex points."; ModularForms 10A "Consume X(Γ) and its ordinary, elliptic, and cusp charts from the Fuchsian-orbifolds roadmap. For congruence subgroups, prove cofiniteness, identify its cusp-orbit subtype with Γ\ℙ¹(ℚ)". The §1 dictionary z ↦ (ℂ/⟨z,1⟩ → ℂ/⟨z,1/N⟩) is the one against which issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E3 is measured.

items.name: Cusps of X₀(N) and their number
items.statement: ({cusps})(ℂ) = Γ₀(N)\ℙ¹(ℚ) ≅ ∐_{d|N, d>0} (ℤ/f_dℤ)^×, f_d = (d, N/d), via m/n (m, n ∈ ℤ, (m, n) = 1) ↦ (n/d)·m (mod f_d) in the component d = (n, N) [corrected; printed (n/d)⁻¹m, see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E1]; n/d is prime to f_d. In particular the number of cusps is Σ_{d|N} φ(f_d) = ∏_{p^ν‖N, ν>0} (p^{[ν/2]} + p^{[(ν−1)/2]}).
items.note: Library: Mathlib .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps.lean:168 `abbrev CuspOrbits (𝒢 : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ))` (orbits of 𝒢 on its cusps) with a Finite instance for arithmetic subgroups (:204); no Γ₀(N) cusp parametrisation or count in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched Cusps/*, Norm/Cusps.lean, HeckeSlash/Cusps.lean for totient/card). Planned: ModularForms 10A "identify its cusp-orbit subtype with Γ\ℙ¹(ℚ), and compute the cusp count ε∞" for congruence subgroups. Checked: the count formula holds (ν = 1..4 by hand); the printed invariant is not Γ₀(N)-invariant (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E1), the corrected one is (brute force, SCR/t_cusp.py).

items.name: Complex conjugation on X₀(N)(ℂ)
items.statement: c ∈ Gal(ℂ/ℝ) acts on X(ℂ) by c(z) = −z̄ (z ∈ 𝔥*): for a lattice L with oriented basis ⟨ω₁, ω₂⟩ the conjugate lattice c(L) has oriented basis ⟨−ω̄₁, ω̄₂⟩; compatible with 𝔥 → Γ\𝔥 because (−1 0; 0 1) normalizes Γ₀(N).
items.note: Planned: R12.6 "Prove compatibility of the comparison with changes of level, diamond operators, complex conjugation and the chosen rational cusp." No library statement (no analytic X₀(N)).

items.name: Fricke and Atkin–Lehner involutions over ℂ (1.1)
items.statement: The canonical involution w_N of X (Chap. I (2.1), dual isogeny) is induced by w_N(z) = −1/(Nz) on 𝔥*. For d | N, d > 0, (d, N/d) = 1, the involution w_d ∈ W (Chap. I (2.2)) is induced by the action on 𝔥* of any matrix w_d ∈ (dℤ ℤ; Nℤ dℤ) with det w_d = d. These agree with the modular definitions; W ≅ (ℤ/2ℤ)^s.
items.note: Library (the matrices only, not the curve involution): Tau Ceti NumberTheory/ModularForms/AtkinLehner/Matrix.lean:93 `structure IsAtkinLehnerMatrix (N Q : ℕ) (M : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ)` (Q | M 0 0, N | M 1 0, Q | M 1 1, det M = Q) — exactly the set in (1.1); :175 `isAtkinLehnerMatrix_fricke : IsAtkinLehnerMatrix N N !![0, -1; N, 0]`; :279 `IsAtkinLehnerMatrix.exists_mem_Gamma0_mul_eq_mul_left` (W γ = δ W with δ ∈ Γ₀(N), i.e. W normalizes Γ₀(N)). These are used for slash operators on forms, not for X₀(N)(ℂ). Planned: ModularCurvesPartII packet node ModularCurvesPartII:R14.1/atkin-lehner-involution: "Over ℂ, with ζ = e^{2πi/N}, it is w_N : z ↦ −1/(Nz)" (for X₁(N); partial: only w_N, only X₁(N)); ModularForms Layer 6 plans W_Q (Q ‖ N) on forms. No stage plans general w_d on X₀(N)(ℂ) explicitly. Review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86): changed to missing, with item 3. ModularCurvesPartII R14.1 constructs Hecke correspondences, degeneracy maps and diamond operators but does not mention Atkin–Lehner or Fricke involutions, Tau Ceti ModularForms layer 6 acts on forms only, and Tau Ceti ModularCurves layer 10 has w_N for prime N ≥ 5 only. Routed with item 3 to ModularCurvesPartII R14.1 (route 5).

items.name: Hecke correspondence T_m over ℂ (1.2)
items.statement: For m ∈ ℕ, (m, N) = 1, the Hecke correspondence T_m of Chap. I (2.3) acts on Γ\𝔥 by T_m(z) = Σ_{γ ∈ Γ\R_N, det γ = m} γz, R_N = (ℤ ℤ; Nℤ ℤ), and #{γ ∈ Γ\R_N : det γ = m} = σ₁(m) = Σ_{d|m, d>0} d (p. 242). On the two cusps used in the paper it acts by T_m((∞)) = σ₁(m)(∞) and T_m((0)) = σ₁(m)(0). [Corrected: p. 241 says 'T_m maps each cusp to itself', which is false for the other cusps as soon as some f_d = (d, N/d) is at least 3 (for example N = 9, m = 2: T₂ sends the cusp 1/3 to 3·(2/3)); see the new issue of reviewer R2. Only ∞ and 0 are used.]
items.locator: Chapter II, §1, (1.2), p. 235; count on p. 242
items.note: Library partial: Tau Ceti NumberTheory/HeckeRing/GL2/Basic.lean:124 `heckeT (m : ℕ+) : IntegralHeckeRing 2` and GL2/Degree.lean:146 `deg_heckeT (m : ℕ+) : deg (posDetInt 2) (SLnZ 2) ℤ (heckeT m) = (σ 1) (m : ℕ)` — the coset count σ₁(m) at level ONE (N = 1 special case); Gamma0/CosetMap.lean `toLevelOneCoset_injOn` compares Γ₀(N)- and level-one double cosets for coprime determinant but surjectivity/coset counts at level N are not proved there. No action on points of X₀(N)(ℂ).
