items.name: Heegner points over ℂ as pairs (𝒜, 𝔫)
items.statement: Standing notation (Chap. I §3, restated p. 233): K imaginary quadratic, discriminant D, 𝒪 = 𝒪_K, (D, N) = 1, D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), D ≡ square (mod 4N) (all p | N split in K); H = Hilbert class field, Cl_K ≅ Gal(H/K); u = #𝒪^×/2; t = number of prime factors of D; s = number of prime factors of N; Γ = Γ₀(N) ⊂ PSL₂(ℤ); 𝔥 = upper half-plane; R_N = (ℤ ℤ; Nℤ ℤ); m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; √D = i√|D|. A Heegner point x = (E → E′) (E, E′ with CM by 𝒪) has E(ℂ) = ℂ/𝔞, E′(ℂ) = ℂ/𝔞𝔫⁻¹ with 𝔞 a fractional ideal and 𝔫 = LL′⁻¹ ⊂ 𝒪 a primitive ideal of norm N (𝒪/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/Nℤ); this gives a bijection {Heegner points x ∈ X(ℂ) of discriminant D} ↔ {(𝒜, 𝔫) : 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, 𝔫 ⊂ 𝒪 primitive of norm N}, (ℂ/𝔞 →id ℂ/𝔞𝔫⁻¹) ↔ ([𝔞], 𝔫). Heegner points exist iff every p_i | N splits in K; then (N = ∏ p_i^{r_i}) there are exactly 2^s primitive 𝔫 of norm N, namely ∏ 𝔭_i^{r_i} with 𝔭_i one of the two primes over p_i, so 2^s·h_K Heegner points.
items.note: No Heegner/CM-point declarations in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep 'Heegner', 'complex multiplication', lattice/Weierstrass: only Mathlib Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Elliptic/Weierstrass.lean). Planned: HE.1 "Construct CM elliptic curves and cyclic-isogeny pairs over ℂ, identify them with the existing X₀(N) moduli objects, and prove descent to ring class fields"; CM.1 "Construct the elliptic curve associated to a complex ideal lattice and its order action. Identify isomorphism classes through proper ideal classes".

items.name: Actions of c, Gal(H/K) and W on Heegner points
items.statement: In the parametrisation of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/59: (a) complex conjugation acts by (𝒜, 𝔫) ↦ (𝒜̄, 𝔫̄) = (𝒜⁻¹, N𝔫⁻¹); (b) Gal(H/K) ≅ Cl_K acts on 𝒜 and trivially on 𝔫: with σ = σ_𝒜 the Artin image of 𝒜 (arithmetic Frobenius convention), σ_𝒜 : (𝒜₁, 𝔫) ↦ (𝒜₁𝒜⁻¹, 𝔫) (p. 243); (c) for d ‖ N, w_d maps (𝒜, 𝔫) to (𝒜[𝔡]⁻¹, 𝔫𝔡⁻¹𝔡̄), 𝔡 = (d, 𝔫) (i.e. the opposite prime is chosen above every p_i | d); in particular w_N : (𝒜, 𝔫) ↦ (𝒜[𝔫]⁻¹, 𝔫̄) = (𝒜[𝔫̄], 𝔫̄) [corrected; printed 𝒜[𝔡] on p. 235 and (𝒜[𝔫], 𝔫̄) on p. 236, see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E2; p. 243 prints the correct rule]; (d) Gal(H/K) × W (W ≅ (ℤ/2ℤ)^s) acts freely and transitively on the Heegner points of discriminant D.
items.note: Planned: packet node GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.0/artin-map-convention: "Under the arithmetic convention [a] ∈ Cl_K acts on the Heegner point ([b], n) by ([b][a]⁻¹, n)" (its library pointer TauCeti.GrossZagier.artinConvention does not exist at f790474; implementationStatus unchecked) — this is (b). HE.0 "Derive ring class fields and Artin maps from existing class field theory, including ... complex conjugation"; HE.1 "show its dependence on choices is given by the specified Galois/Hecke actions" (generic; the w_d rule (c) is not named by any stage). Rule (c) checked three ways (Chap. I (2.2) moduli definition; quadratic forms under z ↦ −1/(Nz); numerics D = −23, −47, −71; SCR/t_wN.py).

items.name: Heegner points in coordinates (1.3)–(1.5)
items.statement: Primitive ideals 𝔫 of norm N ↔ β ∈ ℤ/2Nℤ with β² ≡ D (mod 4N), 𝔫 = (N, (β+√D)/2) = ℤN + ℤ(β+√D)/2 (1.3). For the pair (𝒜, 𝔫) let τ = τ_{𝒜,𝔫} ∈ 𝔥 be the root of Aτ² + Bτ + C = 0 with A > 0, B² − 4AC = D, A ≡ 0 (mod N), B ≡ β (mod 2N) (1.4), where (1.5) 𝔞 = ℤA + ℤ(B+√D)/2 ∈ 𝒜, 𝔞𝔫⁻¹ = ℤ·AN⁻¹ + ℤ(B+√D)/2, N_{K/ℚ}(𝔞) = A; the class of B (mod 2N) is a Γ₀(N)-invariant. Correction (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E3): with √D = i√|D| (the branch §3 uses), this τ = (−B+√D)/(2A) represents, under the §1 dictionary, the complex-conjugate point c(ℂ/𝔞 → ℂ/𝔞𝔫⁻¹) = (ℂ/𝔞̄ → ℂ/𝔞̄𝔫̄⁻¹), i.e. the pair (𝒜⁻¹, 𝔫̄); the point (ℂ/𝔞 → ℂ/𝔞𝔫⁻¹) itself is −τ̄ = (B+√D)/(2A). §3 uses the algebraic relations (1.4)–(1.5) (Aτ ∈ 𝔞̄, so τ ∈ A⁻¹𝔞̄ = 𝔞⁻¹, and 𝔫 | 𝔞).
items.note: No library (no Heegner points, no ideal↔binary-form dictionary: Tau Ceti LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Binary.lean is about diagonal forms ⟨a, b⟩ only). Planned only generically by HE.1 ("cyclic-isogeny pairs over ℂ ... prove the comparison with the complex description"); the explicit (β, A, B, C) coordinates are not named. Checked numerically (SCR/nt.py, t_rho2.py): Aτ ∈ 𝔞̄ and Aτ ∉ 𝔞 for D = −7, −23.

items.name: CM points of 𝔥, positive-definite forms of discriminant D and ideal classes (quoted, classical)
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic of discriminant D (fundamental) and √D = i√|D|. For τ ∈ 𝔥, the elliptic curve ℂ/(ℤτ + ℤ) has complex multiplication by 𝒪_K if and only if τ is a root of Aτ² + Bτ + C = 0 with A, B, C ∈ ℤ, A > 0 and B² − 4AC = D (such a form is automatically primitive since D is fundamental). For such τ = (−B + √D)/(2A), A(ℤτ + ℤ) = ℤA + ℤ(−B + √D)/2 is an integral ideal of norm A, and [A, B, C] ↦ the class of ℤA + ℤ(−B + √D)/2 induces a bijection from SL₂(ℤ)-classes of positive-definite binary quadratic forms of discriminant D onto Cl_K.
items.locator: Chapter II, §1, p. 236 ('Indeed, a point τ ∈ 𝔥 gives rise to an elliptic curve ℂ/ℤτ + ℤ with complex multiplication by 𝒪 iff τ is the root of a quadratic equation Aτ² + Bτ + C = 0 with integral coefficients and discriminant D'); §4, p. 248 ('τ_𝒜 is any point in 𝔥 satisfying a quadratic equation of discriminant D corresponding to the ideal class 𝒜'); used in the proof of p. 248's identity E(τ_𝒜, s) = 2^{−s}|D|^{s/2}uζ(2s)^{−1}ζ_K(𝒜, s)
items.note: The Gauss–Dedekind dictionary between forms and ideal classes, stated at level 1; PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/61 is its level-N refinement and its orientation question is PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E3 (with the convention above, ℤτ + ℤ is homothetic to 𝔞̄ for the 𝔞 = ℤA + ℤ(B + √D)/2 of (1.5)). CM.1 plans 'Identify isomorphism classes through proper ideal classes' for lattices, not the forms. Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: Archimedean height symbol on a compact Riemann surface (2.1)
items.statement: For a compact Riemann surface S, a height symbol is a real function ⟨a, b⟩ = ⟨a, b⟩_ℂ on pairs of degree-0 divisors with disjoint support such that (a) it is additive in a and in b; (b) ⟨a, Σ m_j(y_j)⟩ is continuous on S ∖ |a| in each y_j; (c) ⟨Σ n_i(x_i), (f)⟩ = Σ n_i log|f(x_i)|² for a principal divisor (f). Such a symbol is unique if it exists (the difference of two symbols b ↦ ⟨a, b⟩ is a continuous homomorphism from the compact group Jac(S) to ℝ, hence 0).
items.note: No library (Mathlib/Tau Ceti have harmonic functions on ℂ — Mathlib Analysis/Complex/Harmonic — but no Riemann-surface height/Green-function theory). Planned: GZ.2 plans: "For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a number field, construct the arithmetic intersection pairing from finite-place intersection lengths and archimedean Green functions ... At infinite places prove existence and normalization of the Green kernel and the required analytic estimates ... Export local height decomposition".

items.name: Green's-function description of the height symbol (2.2), (2.3)
items.statement: Fix x₀ ≠ y₀ in S and put G(x, y) = ⟨(x) − (x₀), (y) − (y₀)⟩ (x ≠ y₀, y ≠ x₀, x ≠ y). Then ⟨a, b⟩ = Σ_{i,j} n_i m_j G(x_i, y_j) for a = Σ n_i(x_i), b = Σ m_j(y_j) (at least if y₀ ∉ |a|, x₀ ∉ |b|). Conversely any G such that for fixed x the function y ↦ G(x, y) is continuous and harmonic on S ∖ {x, x₀} with logarithmic singularities of residue +1 at y = x and −1 at y = x₀ (g − C log|ρ|² continuous near the point, ρ a local parameter), and symmetrically in x, defines by (2.2) a symbol satisfying (2.1); G is determined up to an additive constant, fixed e.g. by G(x₀, y) = 0 for one y. For S = X₀(N)(ℂ), N > 1, x₀ = ∞, y₀ = 0 this means a function G on 𝔥 × 𝔥 with (2.3a) G(γz, γ′z′) = G(z, z′) for γ, γ′ ∈ Γ₀(N); (b) G continuous and harmonic for z ∉ Γ₀(N)z′; (c) G = e_z log|z − z′|² + O(1) as z′ → z, e_z the order of the stabilizer of z in Γ₀(N); (d) G = 4πy′ + O(1) as z′ = x′ + iy′ → ∞ and O(1) as z′ → any other cusp; G = 4πy/(N|z|²) + O(1) as z → 0 and O(1) as z → any other cusp (local parameters (z′ − z)^{e_z}(1 + O(z′ − z)), e^{2πiz}, e^{−2πi/Nz}).
items.note: Planned: GZ.2 plans: "For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a number field, construct the arithmetic intersection pairing from finite-place intersection lengths and archimedean Green functions ... At infinite places prove existence and normalization of the Green kernel and the required analytic estimates ... Export local height decomposition". The X₀(N) conditions (2.3) are planned only through the general statement. Checked: the residues in (2.3d) follow from the stated local parameters (log|e^{−2πi/Nz}|² = −4πy/(N|z|²)).

items.name: Hyperbolic Laplace operator Δ on 𝔥
items.statement: For a C² function f on 𝔥, Δf = y²(∂²f/∂x² + ∂²f/∂y²) (z = x + iy). Δ commutes with the action of PSL₂(ℝ): Δ(f ∘ γ) = (Δf) ∘ γ. For a function of two variables, Δ_z and Δ_{z′} denote Δ in the first and in the second variable. With this sign convention Δ(y^s) = s(s − 1)y^s, and the eigenvalue equation Δg = εg (ε = s(s − 1), s > 1) is the one imposed on g_s, G_{N,s} and E_N.
items.locator: Chapter II, §2, p. 238 ('where Δ = y²(∂²/∂x² + ∂²/∂y²) denotes the Laplace operator on 𝔥'); used in (2.11) and in 'Δ(lim_{s→1}[G_{N,s}(z, z′) − κ_N/(s − 1)]) = κ_N', p. 239
items.note: QM.3's stage text: 'Define the weight Laplacian, growth conditions, holomorphic/nonholomorphic Fourier parts and the xi operator'. Its packet nodes QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3/weight-k-hyperbolic-laplacian ('Δ_k f(τ) := −v²(∂²_u + ∂²_v)f(τ) + ikv(∂_u + i∂_v)f(τ)') and QM.3/laplacian-slash-equivariance ('Δ_k(f|_kγ) = (Δ_k f)|_kγ' for det γ = 1) give the operator and its invariance at k = 0, with the opposite sign: Δ_0 = −Δ. The QM packet has no review file in research/blueprint/reviews, so only the stage text is certainly accepted. The reduction of Δg = εg, for g a function of t = 1 + |z − z′|²/(2yy′), to the Legendre equation ((1 − t²)d²/dt² − 2t d/dt + ε)Q = 0 is part of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/64 (reviewer R2 checked y²|∇t|² = t² − 1 and y²Δ_eucl t = 2t, so Δ_z Q(t) = (t² − 1)Q″ + 2tQ′). Libraries: only Euclidean Laplacians (Mathlib Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Laplacian.lean; Tau Ceti Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Laplacian/*); declarations.tsv has no hyperbolic Laplacian on ℍ. Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: Legendre function of the second kind Q_{s−1} (2.5), (2.6)
items.statement: For t > 1: Q_{s−1}(t) = ∫₀^∞ (t + √(t²−1) cosh u)^{−s} du (s > 0) (2.5) = Γ(s)²/(2Γ(2s)) · (2/(1+t))^s · F(s, s; 2s; 2/(1+t)) (2.6), F the hypergeometric function. It is the solution, unique up to a scalar, which is small at infinity of the Legendre equation ((1 − t²) d²/dt² − 2t d/dt + s(s−1)) Q(t) = 0 of index s − 1; this ODE is the equation Δg = s(s−1)g (Δ = y²(∂²/∂x² + ∂²/∂y²)) for g(z, z′) = Q(t), t = 1 + |z − z′|²/(2yy′) = cosh of the hyperbolic distance.
items.note: Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti for Legendre functions (only Legendre symbols and Mathlib RingTheory/Polynomial/ShiftedLegendre.lean exist). Nearest: Mathlib .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/OrdinaryHypergeometric.lean:81 `ordinaryHypergeometric (x : 𝔸) : 𝔸` (₂F₁ a b c, the series; junk 0 outside the radius), which could express (2.6). No atlas stage names Legendre functions (the 12 'Legendre' hits are Legendre symbols); GZ.7's archimedean Green function would use it but does not say so. Checked numerically (SCR/t_leg.py): (2.5) = (2.6) for s ∈ {1, 1.5, 2, 3}, t ∈ {1.1, 2, 5}; Q₀, Q₁ closed forms; ODE residual ~3e−8. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6, the single owner of the Legendre function of the second kind Q_{s−1} (for complex s with Re s > 0), shared with PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/258 (Q_{k−1} of Chapter IV (5.7)) and /273, which the extraction already routes to GZ.6; GZ.7, which depends on GZ.6, imports it for the Green function. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Point-pair invariants g and g_s (2.4), (2.9)
items.statement: g(z, z′) = log(|z − z′|²/|z̄ − z′|²) satisfies a′) g(γz, γz′) = g(z, z′) for γ ∈ PSL₂(ℝ); b′) continuous and harmonic in each variable on 𝔥 × 𝔥 ∖ diagonal; c′) g = log|z − z′|² + O(1) as z′ → z; but Σ_{γ ∈ Γ₀(N)} g(z, γz′) diverges (barely). For s > 1, g_s(z, z′) = −2Q_{s−1}(1 + |z − z′|²/(2yy′)) (z ≠ z′) (2.9) satisfies a′), c′) (by (2.7)) and Δg_s = s(s−1)g_s in each variable; g₁ = g.
items.note: Library partial: Mathlib .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/UpperHalfPlane/Metric.lean:67 `cosh_dist (z w : ℍ) : cosh (dist z w) = 1 + dist (z : ℂ) w ^ 2 / (2 * z.im * w.im)` and :58 `tanh_half_dist (z w : ℍ) : tanh (dist z w / 2) = dist (z : ℂ) w / dist (z : ℂ) (conj ↑w)`, with the instance `IsIsometricSMul SL(2, ℝ) ℍ` (:328): together they give a′) for g = 2 log tanh(d/2) and for any function of cosh d. Harmonicity and the Legendre kernel are absent. No stage (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/64). Checked: g₁ = g numerically and via Q₀(t) = ½ log((t+1)/(t−1)). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Resolvent kernel G_{N,s} (2.10)–(2.12)
items.statement: For z, z′ ∈ 𝔥, z′ ∉ Γ₀(N)z: G_{N,s}(z, z′) = Σ_{γ ∈ Γ₀(N)} g_s(z, γz′) (2.10). It converges absolutely (locally uniformly for Re s > 1, holomorphic in s), Δ_z G_{N,s} = Δ_{z′} G_{N,s} = s(s−1) G_{N,s} (2.11), and G_{N,s}(γz, γ′z′) = G_{N,s}(z, z′) for γ, γ′ ∈ Γ₀(N) (2.12). It is the resolvent kernel of Γ₀(N) (Hejhal [20, Chaps. 6–7]; Hejhal's normalisation is 1/(4π) times this).
items.note: No library (no hyperbolic Laplacian on 𝔥, no automorphic kernels). Planned: GZ.7 plans: "Prove the archimedean Green-function identity with convergent spectral expansion and matching normalization. ... prove the noncompact modular-curve boundary/cusp corrections rather than applying a compact formula unchanged." The stage is written in YZZ's quaternionic/adelic setting (X_U, which includes the split = modular-curve case); it does not name Γ₀(N), the Legendre-function kernel, κ_N or λ_N, and no stage plans specialising the LOCAL archimedean identity to X₀(N) (GZ.8's "Specialize to X₀(N)" concerns the global pairing).

items.name: Meromorphic continuation of G_{N,s}; residue κ_N (2.13)
items.statement: (Quoted from Hejhal [20].) G_{N,s}(z, z′) extends meromorphically in s to a neighbourhood of s = 1 with a simple pole at s = 1 of residue κ_N = −12/[SL₂(ℤ) : Γ₀(N)] = −12 N⁻¹ ∏_{p|N} (1 + 1/p)⁻¹, independent of z, z′. Consequently lim_{s→1}[G_{N,s} − κ_N/(s−1)] is not harmonic: its Laplacian is κ_N ≠ 0.
items.note: Planned: GZ.7 plans: "Prove the archimedean Green-function identity with convergent spectral expansion and matching normalization. ... prove the noncompact modular-curve boundary/cusp corrections rather than applying a compact formula unchanged." AS.4 "Construct discrete cuspidal and residual subspaces, Eisenstein wave packets ... for GL_2/Q recover the continuous Eisenstein contribution" (the constant-eigenfunction residue). The stage is written in YZZ's quaternionic/adelic setting (X_U, which includes the split = modular-curve case); it does not name Γ₀(N), the Legendre-function kernel, κ_N or λ_N, and no stage plans specialising the LOCAL archimedean identity to X₀(N) (GZ.8's "Specialize to X₀(N)" concerns the global pairing). Checked: residue −4π/vol(Γ₀(N)\𝔥) with vol = (π/3)[SL₂(ℤ):Γ₀(N)], consistent with the constant term (2.19) and the residue 3/(π·index) of E_N. Reviewer R2 re-derived the residue: by the Legendre equation ∫₁^∞ Q_{s−1}(t) dt = −[(1 − t²)Q′(t)]₁^∞/(s(s−1)) = 1/(s(s−1)), so ∫_𝔥 g_s(z, z′) dμ(z′) = −4π/(s(s−1)), and unfolding gives residue −4π/vol(Γ₀(N)\𝔥) = −12/[PSL₂(ℤ) : Γ₀(N)]. The index formula [SL₂(ℤ) : Γ₀(N)] = N ∏_{p|N}(1 + 1/p) used in (2.13) is in Tau Ceti only for prime powers: TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups/Basic.lean:574 `Gamma0_prime_power_index (p : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) : (Gamma0 (p ^ k)).index = p ^ (k - 1) * (p + 1)`; the product over the primes of N (multiplicativity by the Chinese remainder theorem) is not stated.

items.name: Weight-0 Eisenstein series E_N(z, s) at ∞ (2.14)
items.statement: E_N(z, s) = Σ_{γ ∈ (∗ ∗; 0 ∗)\Γ₀(N)} Im(γz)^s (z ∈ 𝔥, Re s > 1), the Eisenstein series of weight 0 for the cusp ∞ of Γ₀(N); ΔE_N = s(s−1)E_N, and −4πE_N(z, s) has the same pole κ_N/(s−1) at s = 1 as G_{N,s}.
items.note: No library: Mathlib's EisensteinSeries (NumberTheory/ModularForms/EisensteinSeries/*) are holomorphic weight-k series; no Im(γz)^s series in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep 'im .. ^ s', 'Epstein'). Planned (adelic generality): AS.1 "prove absolute convergence of the Eisenstein sum over P(F)\G(F) in a specified positive chamber ... Derive its constant term"; AS.2 "Prove meromorphic continuation of operators and Eisenstein series". The classical Γ₀(N) series is not named. Also planned classically at level N (accepted packet, REV-EllipticRegulators): node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series defines E_x(z, s) = Σ′_{(m,n) ≡ (u,v) mod N} y^s/|mz + n|^{2s} for x = (u, v) ∈ (ℤ/Nℤ)², with meromorphic continuation and a simple pole at s = 1 of residue π/N². E_N is the combination E_N(z, s) = [2ζ(2s) ∏_{p|N}(1 − p^{−2s})]^{−1} Σ_{v ∈ (ℤ/Nℤ)^×} E_{(0,v)}(z, s) (the pairs (m, n) with N | m and (n, N) = 1 are the g·(c, d) with (g, N) = 1, (c, d) = 1, N | c; checked numerically by reviewer R2 for N = 5, 6 at s = 3), which the node does not state.

items.name: E_N via the SL₂(ℤ) series (2.16)
items.statement: For N ≥ 1: E_N(z, s) = N^{−s} ∏_{p|N} (1 − p^{−2s})⁻¹ Σ_{d|N} μ(d) d^{−s} E((N/d)z, s), E = E₁ the SL₂(ℤ) series; consequently E_N(w_N z, s) = N^{−s} ∏_{p|N}(1 − p^{−2s})⁻¹ Σ_{d|N} μ(d) d^{−s} E(dz, s) (p. 241).
items.note: No library or stage (no non-holomorphic Eisenstein series; no stage names the Möbius identity). Checked numerically (SCR/t_eis.py, lattice sums at s = 3, N = 4, 5, 6): both identities agree to ~1e−10. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Constant term of E(z, s) for SL₂(ℤ) (2.17), (2.18)
items.statement: (Well known.) E(z, s) = y^s + φ(s) y^{1−s} + O(e^{−y}) as y = Im z → ∞, φ(s) = Γ(½)Γ(s − ½)ζ(2s − 1)/(Γ(s)ζ(2s)); here O(e^{−y}) is O(e^{−cy}) for every c < 2π for fixed s > 1, holomorphic in s at s = 1 and O(e^{−y}) uniformly near s = 1.
items.note: No library. Planned in adelic generality: AS.1 "Derive its constant term as a finite Weyl sum of intertwining operators"; AS.2 meromorphic continuation; AS.4 "for GL_2/Q recover the continuous Eisenstein contribution". The explicit φ(s) for SL₂(ℤ) is not named (a specialisation step, not separately planned).

items.name: Expansion of G_{N,s} at the cusps (2.19)
items.statement: (Quoted from Hejhal [20], (6.5); Fourier development in z.) G_{N,s}(z, z′) = −(4π/(2s − 1)) E_N(z′, s) y^{1−s} + O(e^{−y}) as y = Im z → ∞; at any other cusp G_{N,s}(z, z′) = α(s) Y^{1−s} + O(e^{−Y}), Y = Im(γz) for γ ∈ SL₂(ℝ) carrying the cusp to ∞.
items.note: Planned: GZ.7 plans: "Prove the archimedean Green-function identity with convergent spectral expansion and matching normalization. ... prove the noncompact modular-curve boundary/cusp corrections rather than applying a compact formula unchanged." The stage is written in YZZ's quaternionic/adelic setting (X_U, which includes the split = modular-curve case); it does not name Γ₀(N), the Legendre-function kernel, κ_N or λ_N, and no stage plans specialising the LOCAL archimedean identity to X₀(N) (GZ.8's "Specialize to X₀(N)" concerns the global pairing). Checked (SCR/t_leg.py): ∫_ℝ −2Q_{s−1}(1 + (x² + (y−v)²)/(2yv)) dx = −(4π/(2s−1)) v^s y^{1−s} (y > v) for s = 1.5, 2, 3, which with unfolding over Γ_∞\Γ₀(N) gives the coefficient in (2.19).

items.name: The Green's function G(z, z′) of X₀(N) (2.15), (2.20)
items.statement: Let N > 1. G(z, z′) = lim_{s→1}[G_{N,s}(z, z′) + 4πE_N(w_N z, s) + 4πE_N(z′, s) + κ_N/(s − 1)] + C with C = 2κ_N − λ_N (λ_N as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/74). It satisfies (2.3a)–(2.3d) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/63), tends to 0 as z → ∞, and G(z, z′) = G(w_N z′, w_N z) (2.20); the pole cancels since the residues are κ_N − κ_N − κ_N + κ_N.
items.note: Planned: GZ.7 plans: "Prove the archimedean Green-function identity with convergent spectral expansion and matching normalization. ... prove the noncompact modular-curve boundary/cusp corrections rather than applying a compact formula unchanged." and GZ.2 plans: "For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a number field, construct the arithmetic intersection pairing from finite-place intersection lengths and archimedean Green functions ... At infinite places prove existence and normalization of the Green kernel and the required analytic estimates ... Export local height decomposition". The stage is written in YZZ's quaternionic/adelic setting (X_U, which includes the split = modular-curve case); it does not name Γ₀(N), the Legendre-function kernel, κ_N or λ_N, and no stage plans specialising the LOCAL archimedean identity to X₀(N) (GZ.8's "Specialize to X₀(N)" concerns the global pairing). The subtraction of Eisenstein series at the two cusps is the 'cusp correction' GZ.7 names. Proof steps checked (harmonicity: Δ_z of the bracket → 0; log y terms cancel at ∞; C from G → 0 as z → ∞).

items.name: The constant λ_N (2.21)
items.statement: For N > 1: lim_{s→1}[4πE_N(w_N z, s) + κ_N/(s−1)] = κ_N log y + λ_N + O(e^{−y}) (y = Im z → ∞), with λ_N = lim_{s→1}[4πN^{−s}φ(s) ∏_{p|N} (1 − p^{−2s+1})/(1 − p^{−2s}) + κ_N/(s−1)] = κ_N[log N + 2 log 2 − 2γ + 2(ζ′/ζ)(2) − 2Σ_{p|N} p log p/(p² − 1)], γ Euler's constant; also lim_{s→1}[4πE_N(z′, s)(1 − y^{1−s}/(2s−1))] = −κ_N(log y + 2).
items.note: A computation of this paper; no stage names it (GZ.7's 'matching normalization' is generic). Its inputs are in Mathlib (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/75). Checked numerically (SCR/t_lam.py, N = 2, 6, 11, 12): the limit and the closed form agree to 8 digits. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Classical constants used for λ_N
items.statement: Γ′/Γ(1) = −γ, Γ′/Γ(½) = −2 log 2 − γ, and ζ(2s − 1) = 1/(2s − 2) + γ + O(s − 1) as s → 1 (γ = Euler's constant).
items.note: Mathlib .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Digamma.lean:56 `Complex.digamma_one : digamma 1 = - Real.eulerMascheroniConstant` and :59 `Complex.digamma_one_half : digamma (1 / 2) = - 2 * log 2 - Real.eulerMascheroniConstant` (digamma = logDeriv Gamma, :48) — same statements. .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Harmonic/ZetaAsymp.lean:344 `tendsto_riemannZeta_sub_one_div : Tendsto (fun s ↦ riemannZeta s - 1 / (s - 1)) (𝓝[≠] 1) (𝓝 γ)`; :547 `riemannZeta_eq_inv_sub_add (hs : s ≠ 1) : riemannZeta s = (s - 1)⁻¹ + riemannZeta₀ s`, :542 `riemannZeta₀_one : riemannZeta₀ 1 = γ`, :554 `differentiable_riemannZeta₀` — together the O(s − 1) statement (after s ↦ 2s − 1).

items.name: Proposition (2.22): archimedean height pairing on X₀(N)
items.statement: Let N > 1 and x, x′ distinct non-cuspidal points of X₀(N)(ℂ), represented by z, z′ ∈ 𝔥. Then ⟨(x) − (∞), (x′) − (0)⟩_ℂ = lim_{s→1}[G_{N,s}(z, z′) + 4πE_N(w_N z, s) + 4πE_N(z′, s) + κ_N/(s − 1)] − λ_N + 2κ_N, with G_{N,s}, E_N, κ_N, λ_N as in (2.10), (2.14), (2.13), (2.21).
items.note: Planned: GZ.2 plans: "For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a number field, construct the arithmetic intersection pairing from finite-place intersection lengths and archimedean Green functions ... At infinite places prove existence and normalization of the Green kernel and the required analytic estimates ... Export local height decomposition". (existence/normalisation of the archimedean Green kernel and local height decomposition) and GZ.7 plans: "Prove the archimedean Green-function identity with convergent spectral expansion and matching normalization. ... prove the noncompact modular-curve boundary/cusp corrections rather than applying a compact formula unchanged." The stage is written in YZZ's quaternionic/adelic setting (X_U, which includes the split = modular-curve case); it does not name Γ₀(N), the Legendre-function kernel, κ_N or λ_N, and no stage plans specialising the LOCAL archimedean identity to X₀(N) (GZ.8's "Specialize to X₀(N)" concerns the global pairing).

items.name: Hecke operators on constants, on E_N and on G_{N,s}
items.statement: For m ≥ 1, (m, N) = 1: T_m acts on constants by σ₁(m) = #{γ ∈ Γ\R_N : det γ = m}, on E_N(z′, s) by m^s σ_{1−2s}(m) = m^s Σ_{d|m} d^{1−2s}, and G_{N,s}(z, z′)|_{z′} T_m = Σ_{γ ∈ R_N/{±1}, det γ = m} g_s(z, γz′). Since T_m((0)) = σ₁(m)(0), T_m((x′) − (0)) = Σ_{γ ∈ Γ\R_N, det γ = m} ((γx′) − (0)), hence ⟨(x) − (∞), T_m((x′) − (0))⟩_ℂ = Σ_{γ ∈ Γ\R_N, det γ = m} G(z, γz′). [Corrected: the paper justifies this by 'T_m maps each cusp to itself' (p. 241), which is false for general N; only T_m((0)) = σ₁(m)(0) and T_m((∞)) = σ₁(m)(∞) are needed and true.]
items.note: Library partial: Tau Ceti NumberTheory/HeckeRing/GL2/Degree.lean:146 `deg_heckeT (m : ℕ+) : deg (posDetInt 2) (SLnZ 2) ℤ (heckeT m) = (σ 1) (m : ℕ)` (the σ₁(m) count at level 1 only). No Eisenstein-series Hecke eigenvalue or kernel identity in any library or stage. Checked: T_p constant term (py)^s + p(y/p)^s = p^s σ_{1−2s}(p) y^s. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7. Reviewer R2 also checked the eigenvalue on the y^{1−s} term: Σ_{aδ=m} δ (a/δ)^{1−s} = m^s σ_{1−2s}(m), so E_N is an eigenfunction, not only its constant term.

items.name: Hecke-translated kernel G^m_{N,s} (2.24)
items.statement: For m ≥ 1, (m, N) = 1: G^m_{N,s}(z, z′) = ½ Σ_{a,b,c,d ∈ ℤ, N | c, ad − bc = m} g_s(z, (az′ + b)/(cz′ + d)) (= G_{N,s}(z, z′)|_{z′}T_m); G¹_{N,s} = G_{N,s}.
items.note: Planned only generically: GZ.6 "Prove pullback/push-forward, Hecke and diagonal identities needed by the generating series" and GZ.7 plans: "Prove the archimedean Green-function identity with convergent spectral expansion and matching normalization. ... prove the noncompact modular-curve boundary/cusp corrections rather than applying a compact formula unchanged." The stage is written in YZZ's quaternionic/adelic setting (X_U, which includes the split = modular-curve case); it does not name Γ₀(N), the Legendre-function kernel, κ_N or λ_N, and no stage plans specialising the LOCAL archimedean identity to X₀(N) (GZ.8's "Specialize to X₀(N)" concerns the global pairing). No library.

items.name: Proposition (2.23): Hecke-translated archimedean pairing
items.statement: Let N > 1, m ≥ 1, (m, N) = 1, x, x′ ∈ X₀(N)(ℂ) non-cuspidal with x ∉ T_m x′, represented by z, z′. Then ⟨(x) − (∞), T_m((x′) − (0))⟩_ℂ = lim_{s→1}[G^m_{N,s}(z, z′) + 4πσ₁(m)E_N(w_N z, s) + 4πm^s σ_{1−2s}(m)E_N(z′, s) + σ₁(m)κ_N/(s − 1)] − σ₁(m)λ_N + 2σ₁(m)κ_N, σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν.
items.note: Planned as for PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/76 (GZ.7 archimedean Green identity with modular-curve cusp corrections; GZ.6 Hecke identities). The stage is written in YZZ's quaternionic/adelic setting (X_U, which includes the split = modular-curve case); it does not name Γ₀(N), the Legendre-function kernel, κ_N or λ_N, and no stage plans specialising the LOCAL archimedean identity to X₀(N) (GZ.8's "Specialize to X₀(N)" concerns the global pairing). Checked: poles cancel (σ₁κ − σ₁κ − σ₁κ + σ₁κ, using mσ_{−1}(m) = σ₁(m)).

items.name: Atkin–Lehner invariance of G_{N,s}, G^m_{N,s} (2.25)
items.statement: For every d ‖ N: G^m_{N,s}(w_d z, w_d z′) = G^m_{N,s}(z, z′) (in particular for m = 1), because g_s(γz, γz′) = g_s(z, z′) for γ ∈ SL₂(ℝ) and w_d normalises {γ ∈ R_N : det γ = m}; compatible with the invariance of the height pairing under automorphisms.
items.note: Library partial: Tau Ceti AtkinLehner/Matrix.lean:279 (W γ = δ W, δ ∈ Γ₀(N): W normalises Γ₀(N); the det-m set is not treated). No stage. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Heegner-point invariants (3.1)–(3.3)
items.statement: Standing notation (Chap. I §3, restated p. 233): K imaginary quadratic, discriminant D, 𝒪 = 𝒪_K, (D, N) = 1, D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), D ≡ square (mod 4N) (all p | N split in K); H = Hilbert class field, Cl_K ≅ Gal(H/K); u = #𝒪^×/2; t = number of prime factors of D; s = number of prime factors of N; Γ = Γ₀(N) ⊂ PSL₂(ℤ); 𝔥 = upper half-plane; R_N = (ℤ ℤ; Nℤ ℤ); m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; √D = i√|D|. For m ≥ 1, (m, N) = 1, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K with r_𝒜(m) = 0 (r_𝒜(k) = number of integral ideals of norm k in 𝒜), and τ_{𝒜ᵢ,𝔫} as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/61: the values G^m_{N,s}(τ_{𝒜₁,𝔫}, τ_{𝒜₂,𝔫}) with 𝒜₁𝒜₂⁻¹ = 𝒜 (3.1); γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜; 𝔅) = Σ_{𝒜₁,𝒜₂ ∈ Cl_K, 𝒜₁𝒜₂⁻¹ = 𝒜, 𝒜₁𝒜₂[𝔫]⁻¹ = 𝔅} G^m_{N,s}(τ_{𝒜₁,𝔫}, τ_{𝒜₂,𝔫}) (3.2); γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜) = Σ_{𝒜₁𝒜₂⁻¹ = 𝒜} G^m_{N,s}(τ_{𝒜₁,𝔫}, τ_{𝒜₂,𝔫}) = Σ_{𝔅 ∈ Cl_K} γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜; 𝔅) (3.3). Because σ_𝒜 maps τ_{𝒜₁,𝔫} to τ_{𝒜₁𝒜⁻¹,𝔫} and Gal(H/K) permutes the archimedean places of H simply transitively, (3.3) with Proposition (2.23) computes Σ_{v|∞} ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v (c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0)); r_𝒜(m) = 0 is needed for (3.1) to be defined (x ∉ T_m x^σ).
items.note: Paper-specific invariants; no stage defines them (nearest GZ.7's archimedean Green-function identity for CM points in YZZ's setting). See PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E3 for the labelling τ_{𝒜,𝔫} (harmless) and PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E7 for the missing T_m in 'Σ_{v|∞}⟨c, d^σ⟩_v'. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜; 𝔅) is independent of 𝔫; number of terms
items.statement: (3.1) depends on 𝔫, but γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜; 𝔅) does not: w_d (d ‖ N) replaces (𝒜₁, 𝒜₂, 𝔫) by (𝒜₁[𝔡]⁻¹, 𝒜₂[𝔡]⁻¹, 𝔫𝔡⁻¹𝔡̄) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/60), leaving 𝒜₁𝒜₂⁻¹ and 𝒜₁𝒜₂[𝔫]⁻¹ unchanged, and G^m_{N,s} is w_d-invariant (2.25). The sum (3.2) has 2^{t−1} terms if {𝒜} = {𝔅𝔫} and is empty otherwise ({𝒜} = genus = class of 𝒜 in Cl_K/Cl_K² ≅ (ℤ/2ℤ)^{t−1}); all 𝔫 of norm N lie in one genus; if D is prime (|Cl_K| odd) the sum has one term.
items.note: Paper-specific; genus inputs are library (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/83). Checked numerically in the course of the (3.14) test (SCR/t_314.py). The invariance needs the corrected w_d rule [𝔡]⁻¹ (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E2). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Genus theory inputs (quoted, classical)
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic with t ramified primes: Cl_K/Cl_K² ≅ (ℤ/2ℤ)^{t−1} and #Cl_K[2] = 2^{t−1}; a class is a square iff every genus character is trivial on it (principal genus theorem); genus characters are functions of the norm, so a positive integer cannot be the norm of ideals in two different genera and all ideals of norm N (primitive or not) lie in one genus.
items.note: Tau Ceti NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Quadratic/TwoRank.lean:155 `twoRank_eq_ncard_ramifiedPrimes_sub_one (hmin : minpoly ℤ θ = X ^ 2 - C d) (hgen : Algebra.adjoin ℚ {(θ : K)} = ⊤) (hsf : Squarefree d) (hd : d < 0) : TauCeti.ClassGroup.twoRank (𝓞 K) = (ramifiedPrimes K).ncard - 1`; ClassGroup/ElementaryTwoQuotient.lean:188 `card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_two_pow_twoRank : Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient R) = 2 ^ twoRank R` and :240 `card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_card_twoTorsion : Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient R) = Nat.card {C : ClassGroup R // C ^ 2 = 1}`; Quadratic/GenusCharacter/PrincipalGenus.lean:150 `isSquare_iff_forall_genusCharFunNarrowClassGroupHom_eq_one ... (A : NarrowClassGroup K) : IsSquare A ↔ ∀ P ∈ s, genusCharFunNarrowClassGroupHom ... A = 1` (narrow class group), transported by NumberField/NarrowClassGroup/TotallyComplex.lean:47 `toClassGroupEquiv [IsTotallyComplex K] : NarrowClassGroup K ≃* ClassGroup (𝓞 K)`. The genus characters are built from norms (GenusCharacter/Basic.lean:212 `genusCharFun (s : Finset ℤ) (n : ℤ)`). Same statements up to packaging. Reviewer R2: the genus character of an ideal prime to D is genusCharFun of its norm by definition, TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Quadratic/GenusCharacter/CoprimeIdeal.lean:79 `genusCharFunCoprimeIdealHom` ('Its value on an ideal is genusCharFun t (N I)'), which gives 'all ideals of norm N lie in one genus' for N prime to D. The same statement for an arbitrary norm n (used on p. 247, 'a number cannot be the norm of an ideal in more than one genus', including (n, D) > 1) is not stated in the library; it follows because two integral ideals of the same norm differ by replacing split primes by their conjugates, and [𝔩̄] = [𝔩]⁻¹ has the same image in Cl_K/Cl_K².

items.name: G^m at Heegner points as a series over n (3.4), (3.5)
items.statement: Let τ₁, τ₂ be Heegner points with the same 𝔫, roots of A_iτ_i² + B_iτ_i + C_i = 0 as in (1.4) with the same β. For γ = (a b; c d) ∈ R_N with det γ = m > 0: g_s(γτ₁, τ₂) = −2Q_{s−1}(1 + |γτ₁ − τ₂|²/(2 Im(γτ₁) Im τ₂)) = −2Q_{s−1}(1 + 2nN/(|D| det γ)) with n = (A₁A₂/N)|cτ₁τ₂ + dτ₂ − aτ₁ − b|² (3.4), and n = (1/N)[c²C₁C₂ + ad(D − B₁B₂)/2 − bc(D + B₁B₂)/2 + a²C₁A₂ + d²A₁C₂ − cdB₁C₂ + acC₁B₂ + b²A₁A₂ + bdA₁B₂ − abB₁A₂] ∈ ℤ (3.5, corrected; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E4). Hence G^m_{N,s}(τ₁, τ₂) = −2 Σ_{n≥1} ρ^m(n) Q_{s−1}(1 + 2nN/(m|D|)), ρ^m(n) = #{γ ∈ R_N/{±1} : det γ = m, n(γ) = n} (n ≥ 1 when r_{𝒜₁𝒜₂⁻¹}(m) = 0). Example N = 1, D = −4, τ₁ = τ₂ = i: n = a² + b² + c² + d² − 2(ad − bc), (a − d)² + (b + c)² = n, (a + d)² + (b − c)² = n + 4m.
items.note: No library/stage (nearest: GZ.7, general). Checked numerically (SCR/t_35.py, t_35c.py): (3.4) and the corrected (3.5) agree in 3000/3000 random cases; the printed (3.5) fails in 2694. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Proposition (3.11): ρ^m as a count of pairs (α, β)
items.statement: Let 𝒜₁, 𝒜₂ ∈ Cl_K, 𝔫 primitive of norm N, 𝔞ᵢ ∈ 𝒜ᵢ integral with 𝔫 | 𝔞ᵢ, N(𝔞ᵢ) = Aᵢ, and — corrected hypothesis, see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E5 — 𝔞₁, 𝔞₂ prime to D; τ_{𝒜ᵢ,𝔫} the roots attached to 𝔞ᵢ by (1.4)–(1.5). Then for m ∈ ℕ (with (m, N) = 1) and r_{𝒜₁𝒜₂⁻¹}(m) = 0: G^m_{N,s}(τ_{𝒜₁,𝔫}, τ_{𝒜₂,𝔫}) = −2 Σ_{n≥1} ρ^m(n) Q_{s−1}(1 + 2nN/(m|D|)), ρ^m(n) = ρ^m_{𝒜₁,𝒜₂,𝔫}(n) = #{(α, β) ∈ (𝔞₁⁻¹𝔞̄₂⁻¹ × 𝔞₁⁻¹𝔞₂⁻¹𝔫)/{±1} : N(α) = (Nn + m|D|)/(A₁A₂), N(β) = Nn/(A₁A₂), A₁A₂α ≡ A₁A₂β (mod 𝔡)}, 𝔡 = (√D) the different. The bijection is γ ↦ (α, β), α = cτ₁τ̄₂ + dτ̄₂ − aτ₁ − b, β = cτ₁τ₂ + dτ₂ − aτ₁ − b (3.6), with α ∈ 𝔞₁⁻¹𝔞̄₂⁻¹, β ∈ 𝔞₁⁻¹𝔞₂⁻¹𝔫 (3.7), l = A₁A₂N(α), n = N⁻¹A₁A₂N(β) ∈ ℤ (3.8), l − Nn = |D| det γ (3.9), A₁A₂α ≡ A₁A₂β (mod 𝔡) (3.10); the inverse is cτ₁ + d = (A₂/√D)(β − α), aτ₁ + b = (A₂/√D)(τ̄₂β − τ₂α). (r_{𝒜₁𝒜₂⁻¹}(m) = 0 ensures n > 0.)
items.note: No library/stage (the YZZ analogue — decomposing γ ∈ B = K ⊕ Kj — is inside GZ.7's general archimedean identity, not planned for X₀(N)). Checked numerically (SCR/t_rho.py): with 𝔞₁ prime to D the (α, β) count equals the γ count for all n ≤ 29 (D = −7, N = 2, m = 3); with 𝔞₁ ⊂ (√−7) it doubles for 7 ∤ n (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E5). (3.9) verified in 3000 random cases. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (3.12): ρ^m when n ≡ 0 (mod D)
items.statement: If n ≡ 0 (mod D) (hypotheses of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/85): ρ^m_{𝒜₁,𝒜₂,𝔫}(n) = ½ #{α ∈ 𝔞₁⁻¹𝔞̄₂⁻¹ : N(α) = l/(A₁A₂)} · #{β ∈ 𝔞₁⁻¹𝔞₂⁻¹𝔫 : N(β) = Nn/(A₁A₂)} = 2u² r_{𝒜₁𝒜₂⁻¹}(l) r_{𝒜₁𝒜₂[𝔫]⁻¹}(n), l = Nn + m|D|, u = ½#𝒪^×.
items.note: No library/stage. Checked per pair of classes (SCR/t_312.py, D = −7 and −23, n = 7, 14, 21, 23). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (3.13): ρ^m for prime discriminant
items.statement: If |D| is prime (hypotheses of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/85): ρ^m_{𝒜₁,𝒜₂,𝔫}(n) = u² r_{𝒜₁𝒜₂⁻¹}(nN + m|D|) r_{𝒜₁𝒜₂[𝔫]⁻¹}(n) × (1 if D ∤ n, 2 if D | n); for D ∤ n exactly one of (α, β), (α, −β) satisfies the congruence (a quadratic residue mod D has exactly two square roots).
items.note: No library/stage. Checked per pair (SCR/t_312.py, D = −23, N = 2, m = 5, all 9 class pairs, n ∈ {1,2,3,4,6,8,23}; D = −7). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (3.14), (3.15): summed ρ^m over a genus coset
items.statement: D arbitrary (standing hypotheses), 𝒜, 𝔅 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(m) = 0: Σ_{𝒜₁,𝒜₂ ∈ Cl_K, 𝒜₁𝒜₂⁻¹ = 𝒜, 𝒜₁𝒜₂[𝔫]⁻¹ = 𝔅} ρ^m_{𝒜₁,𝒜₂,𝔫}(n) = u² δ(n) r_𝒜(nN + m|D|) r_𝔅(n) if {𝒜} = {𝔅𝔫}, and 0 otherwise, where δ(n) = ∏_{p|(n,D)} 2 (3.15) and {𝒜}, {𝔅𝔫} are the genera of 𝒜 and 𝔅[𝔫]. Proof: the other terms come from 𝔞ᵢ ↦ 𝔞ᵢ𝔠 with 𝔠² = (γ₀), (α, β) ↦ (α/N(𝔠), β/γ₀); the 2^{t−1} classes [𝔠] ∈ Cl_K[2] correspond to ±r (mod D) with r² ≡ 1 (mod D).
items.note: No library/stage. Checked numerically against direct γ counts (SCR/t_314.py): D = −15, −23, −35, −39, −55 and (D, N) = (−23, 6), all (𝒜, 𝔅) and n ≤ 8–12: 0 mismatches. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Proposition (3.16): γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜; 𝔅)
items.statement: Standing notation (Chap. I §3, restated p. 233): K imaginary quadratic, discriminant D, 𝒪 = 𝒪_K, (D, N) = 1, D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), D ≡ square (mod 4N) (all p | N split in K); H = Hilbert class field, Cl_K ≅ Gal(H/K); u = #𝒪^×/2; t = number of prime factors of D; s = number of prime factors of N; Γ = Γ₀(N) ⊂ PSL₂(ℤ); 𝔥 = upper half-plane; R_N = (ℤ ℤ; Nℤ ℤ); m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; √D = i√|D|. For m ≥ 1, (m, N) = 1, r_𝒜(m) = 0, s > 1: γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜; 𝔅) = −2u² Σ_{n≥1} δ(n) r_𝒜(nN + m|D|) r_𝔅(n) Q_{s−1}(1 + 2nN/(m|D|)) if {𝒜} = {𝔅𝔫}, and γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜; 𝔅) = 0 otherwise (δ(n) as in (3.15)).
items.note: No library. Nearest plan: GZ.7 plans: "Prove the archimedean Green-function identity with convergent spectral expansion and matching normalization. ... prove the noncompact modular-curve boundary/cusp corrections rather than applying a compact formula unchanged." — the YZZ archimedean identity is the general analogue, but no stage plans this X₀(N) local formula (GZ.8's specialisation is of the global pairing). Follows from PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/85 + PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/89; numerically confirmed through PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/89's test. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Corollary (3.17): γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜)
items.statement: Standing notation (Chap. I §3, restated p. 233): K imaginary quadratic, discriminant D, 𝒪 = 𝒪_K, (D, N) = 1, D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), D ≡ square (mod 4N) (all p | N split in K); H = Hilbert class field, Cl_K ≅ Gal(H/K); u = #𝒪^×/2; t = number of prime factors of D; s = number of prime factors of N; Γ = Γ₀(N) ⊂ PSL₂(ℤ); 𝔥 = upper half-plane; R_N = (ℤ ℤ; Nℤ ℤ); m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; √D = i√|D|. For m ≥ 1, (m, N) = 1, r_𝒜(m) = 0, s > 1: γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜) = −2u² Σ_{n≥1} δ(n) R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n) r_𝒜(nN + m|D|) Q_{s−1}(1 + 2nN/(m|D|)), where R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n) is the number of integral ideals of norm n in the genus {𝒜𝔫}.
items.note: No library; not planned for X₀(N) (nearest GZ.7, general; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/90). Consumed in §4 (Proposition (4.2)). Coefficients checked numerically (SCR/t_314.py, '(3.17) coefficient mismatches: 0'). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n) versus R(n); genus-character form
items.statement: R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n) is either R(n) or 0, where R(n) = Σ_{𝒜 ∈ Cl_K} r_𝒜(n) = Σ_{d|n} (D/d) is the number of integral ideals of norm n. If (n, D) = 1 then R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n) may be replaced by R(n) in (3.17) (r_𝒜(nN + m|D|) ≠ 0 ⇒ (A(nN + m|D|)/p) = 1 ∀p | D ⇒ (AN·n/p) = 1 ∀p | D ⇒ R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n) = R(n), A any integer prime to D that is a norm from the genus {𝒜}); in general δ(n)R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n)r_𝒜(nN + m|D|) may be replaced by ∏_{p|(n,D)} (1 + ε̂_p((nN + m|D|)/(nN))) · R(n) r_𝒜(nN + m|D|), where ε̂_p is the character of the group of norms of fractional ideals with ε̂_p(N𝔞) = 1 for 𝔞 principal and ε̂_p(n) = (n/p) for n ∈ ℤ, p ∤ n.
items.note: Nearest: Mathlib .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/DedekindZeta.lean:49 `NumberField.dedekindZeta (s : ℂ) := LSeries (fun n ↦ Nat.card {I : Ideal (𝓞 K) // absNorm I = n}) s` (R(n) as its coefficient, but no factorisation ζ_K = ζ·L(χ_D), i.e. no R(n) = Σ_{d|n}(D/d)); Tau Ceti GenusCharacter/Basic.lean:212 `genusCharFun (s : Finset ℤ) (n : ℤ) : ℤ` (genus characters on integers/norms). No stage plans R(n) = Σ(D/d) (ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layer 1 plans only norm-fibre coefficients). The replacement argument was checked by hand. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Hyperbolic distance on 𝔥 (quoted)
items.statement: The quantity 1 + |z − z′|²/(2yy′) is the hyperbolic cosine of the hyperbolic distance d(z, z′); |z − z′|/|z̄ − z′| = tanh(d/2); PSL₂(ℝ) acts by isometries, so a function of z, z′ satisfies a′) iff it is a function of d(z, z′).
items.note: Mathlib .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/UpperHalfPlane/Metric.lean:67 `UpperHalfPlane.cosh_dist (z w : ℍ) : cosh (dist z w) = 1 + dist (z : ℂ) w ^ 2 / (2 * z.im * w.im)` and :58 `UpperHalfPlane.tanh_half_dist (z w : ℍ) : tanh (dist z w / 2) = dist (z : ℂ) w / dist (z : ℂ) (conj ↑w)`; the instance `IsIsometricSMul SL(2, ℝ) ℍ` at :328 (unnamed instance). Same statements; the 'iff' (point-pair invariants are functions of d) is the standard transitivity of SL₂(ℝ) on pairs at fixed distance, not stated in Mathlib.

items.name: Archimedean part ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_∞ of the height pairing
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Assume r_A(m) = 0, so that c and T_m d^σ have disjoint support. Define ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_∞ := Σ_{v|∞} ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v, the sum over the h complex places of H of Néron's archimedean local symbols. Since Gal(H/K) ≅ Cl_K permutes these places simply transitively, ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_∞ = Σ_{A₁, A₂ ∈ Cl_K, A₁A₂⁻¹ = A} ⟨(τ_{A₁,𝔫}) − (∞), T_m((τ_{A₂,𝔫}) − (0))⟩_ℂ, where τ_{A,𝔫} ∈ 𝔥 are the points of Chap. II §1 (roots of aτ² + bτ + c = 0 of discriminant D with N | a) attached to the class A and the ideal 𝔫.
items.locator: Chapter II, §4, first two displays, p. 248
items.note: Planned: GZ.2 'For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a number field, construct the arithmetic intersection pairing from finite-place intersection lengths and archimedean Green functions … Prove the Faltings–Hriljac comparison for degree-zero divisors with the canonical Jacobian pairing … Export local height decomposition'. That plans the decomposition into local symbols in general; the rewriting over the h conjugate Heegner points is GZ-specific. Library: no local heights in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep localHeight/LocalHeight: none; 'Néron' in Tau Ceti occurs only in the elliptic-curve canonical-height files AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/CanonicalHeight.lean and MordellWeil/*); library-coverage audit of GZ.2 (AUDIT-25): arithmetic intersection pairing 'absent'.

items.name: (4.1) Eisenstein series of Γ₀(N) summed over Heegner points
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Let E(z, s) = Σ_{γ ∈ Γ_∞\SL₂(ℤ)} Im(γz)^s be the weight-0 Eisenstein series of SL₂(ℤ) (Γ_∞ = ±(1 *; 0 1); this normalization is the one forced by κ_N in (2.13) and by the identity 2^s ζ(2s) E(τ_A, s) = u|D|^{s/2} ζ_K(A, s) used on pp. 248, 252), E_N(z, s) the Eisenstein series (2.14) of Γ₀(N) at ∞, w_N z = −1/(Nz), Re s > 1. Then Σ_{A∈Cl_K} E_N(w_N τ_{A,𝔫}, s) = Σ_{A∈Cl_K} E_N(τ_{A,𝔫}, s) = N^{−s} Π_{p|N}(1 − p^{−2s})^{−1} Σ_{d|N} (μ(d)/d^s) Σ_{A∈Cl_K} E((N/d) τ_{A,𝔫}, s). For each d | N the points (N/d)τ_{A,𝔫} again satisfy quadratic equations over ℤ of discriminant D, and the inner sum is independent of d and equals Σ_{A} E(τ_A, s), where τ_A ∈ 𝔥 is any root of a primitive form of discriminant D in the class A. Hence Σ_A E_N(τ_{A,𝔫}, s) = N^{−s} Π_{p|N}(1 + p^{−s})^{−1} Σ_A E(τ_A, s) (the combination used in the display at the top of p. 249).
items.locator: Chapter II, §4, (4.1) and the paragraph after it, p. 248
items.note: Checked: if aτ² + bτ + c = 0 with a = Na₁ and τ′ = (N/d)τ, then a₁dτ′² + bτ′ + (cN/d) = 0, of discriminant b² − 4ac = D; the first equality is (2.16) applied termwise; Σ_{d|N} μ(d)d^{−s} = Π_{p|N}(1 − p^{−s}) gives the last form. Searched: Mathlib/Tau Ceti have only holomorphic Eisenstein series (Mathlib `eisensteinSeries`, NumberTheory/ModularForms/EisensteinSeries/Defs.lean:205, weight k level N); no non-holomorphic E(z, s). Atlas: AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.1 plans general Eisenstein-series convergence on reductive groups ('Prove absolute convergence of the Eisenstein sum over P(F)\G(F) …'), not this CM-point identity; no stage mentions E(z, s) at Heegner points. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Partial zeta function ζ_K(A, s) of an ideal class
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic, A ∈ Cl_K and Re s > 1: ζ_K(A, s) = Σ_{𝔞 ⊆ O integral, [𝔞] = A} N(𝔞)^{−s}. One has Σ_{A∈Cl_K} ζ_K(A, s) = ζ_K(s), the Dedekind zeta function of K.
items.note: Library: Mathlib has only the full Dedekind zeta `NumberField.dedekindZeta` (NumberTheory/NumberField/DedekindZeta.lean:49: `LSeries (fun n ↦ Nat.card {I : Ideal (𝓞 K) // absNorm I = n}) s`), not the class-restricted series; grep partialZeta/classZeta in both libraries: none. Atlas: no stage plans ideal-class partial zeta functions (AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4 plans Hecke/Dedekind interfaces generically; Tau Ceti GlobalNumberFields Layer 3 plans ray-class ideal counting with error term, not the zeta function). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 4: AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4.

items.name: Eisenstein series at a CM point equals a partial zeta function
items.statement: Let τ_A ∈ 𝔥 be a root of a primitive positive-definite binary quadratic form of discriminant D (K = ℚ(√D), u = #O_K^×/2) in the class A, and E(z, s) as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/94. For Re s > 1: E(τ_A, s) = 2^{−s} |D|^{s/2} u ζ(2s)^{−1} ζ_K(A, s); equivalently 2^s ζ(2s) E(τ_A, s) = u |D|^{s/2} ζ_K(A, s).
items.locator: Chapter II, §4, p. 248 ('As is well-known (and elementary)'); restated p. 252
items.note: Quoted as classical. Checked: ζ(2s)E(τ, s) = ½ Σ′_{(m,n)} y^s |mτ + n|^{−2s}; with a|mτ + n|² = Q(m, n) of discriminant D and y = √|D|/(2a) this is ½ (√|D|/2)^s Σ′ Q(m,n)^{−s}, and Σ′ Q(m,n)^{−s} = w ζ_K(A^{±1}, s) = 2u ζ_K(A, s) (ζ_K(A) = ζ_K(A⁻¹) by conjugation). Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (no non-holomorphic Eisenstein series, no partial zeta); no atlas stage plans it. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 4: AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4.

items.name: Factorization ζ_K(s) = ζ(s) L(s, ε)
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D and ε(n) = (D/n) (an odd primitive character of conductor |D|): ζ_K(s) = ζ(s) L(s, ε); near s = 1, ζ_K(s) = (1/(s − 1) + γ + O(s − 1))(L(1, ε) + L′(1, ε)(s − 1) + O((s − 1)²)), γ Euler's constant.
items.note: Planned only generically: AN.4 'Connect number-field ideal counting, Hecke characters and completed L-functions to the analytic class-number formula and Chebotarev'. No stage states the quadratic factorization explicitly. Library: absent — grep for products of riemannZeta with an L-function equal to dedekindZeta found nothing (the only hit, Mathlib NumberTheory/LSeries/Nonvanishing.lean:144, is an auxiliary function for Dirichlet characters); Tau Ceti has `dedekindZeta_eq_LSeries_normCoeff_one` (ArithmeticDirichletSeries/Trivial.lean:100), an L-series rewriting only.

items.name: Class number formula L(1, ε) = πh/(u√|D|)
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D, class number h and u = #O_K^×/2: L(1, ε) = π h / (u √|D|) (= 2πh/(w√|D|)).
items.locator: Chapter II, §4, p. 249 ('and the formula L(1, ε) = πh_K/u√|D|')
items.note: Planned: AN.4 '… to the analytic class-number formula'. Library (partial, not the statement): Mathlib `NumberField.tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT` (NumberTheory/NumberField/DedekindZeta.lean:77) proves (s − 1)ζ_K(s) → dedekindZeta_residue K = 2^{r₁}(2π)^{r₂} R h/(w√|disc K|) (definition at line 56), which for imaginary quadratic K is 2πh/(w√|D|) = πh/(u√|D|); with the (absent) factorization PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/97 this gives the stated L(1, ε).

items.name: Proposition (4.2): archimedean contribution when r_A(m) = 0
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Let x ∈ X₀(N) be a Heegner point for the full ring of integers of K, c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0), σ ∈ Gal(H/K), m ∈ ℕ prime to N, and A ∈ Cl_K the ideal class corresponding to σ under the Artin isomorphism. Suppose m is not the norm of an integral ideal in A. Then ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_∞ = lim_{s→1} [γ^m_{N,s}(A) − h σ₁(m) κ_N/(s − 1)] + h κ_N [σ₁(m)(log(N/|D|) + 2 Σ_{p|N} log p/(p² − 1) + 2 + 2(ζ′/ζ)(2) − 2(L′/L)(1, ε)) + Σ_{d|m} d log(m/d²)], where γ^m_{N,s}(A) is the invariant (3.3) (evaluated in Corollary (3.17)), κ_N = −12/[SL₂(ℤ) : Γ₀(N)] = −12 N^{−1} Π_{p|N}(1 + 1/p)^{−1} (2.13), and L(s, ε) is the L-function of K.
items.note: Checked the derivation from Prop. (2.23), (4.1), PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/96–PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/98: the Eisenstein terms equal F(s) = 2^{2−s}|D|^{s/2}πu (σ₁(m) + m^s σ_{1−2s}(m)) ζ_K(s) / (N^s Π_{p|N}(1 + p^{−s}) ζ(2s)), whose polar part is −2hσ₁(m)κ_N/(s − 1) (residue 24hσ₁(m)/(NΠ(1+1/p))); its constant term together with −hσ₁(m)λ_N + 2hσ₁(m)κ_N and (2.21) gives exactly the printed bracket, the Σ_{d|m} d log(m/d²) coming from (d/ds) log(σ₁(m) + m^s σ_{1−2s}(m)) at s = 1. Planned only as a method: GZ.7 'Prove the archimedean Green-function identity with convergent spectral expansion and matching normalization'; GZ.8 'Specialize to X₀(N)' (of YZZ's formula). GZ's explicit evaluation through Kronecker/partial zeta functions (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/94–PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/98) is not itself planned. Library: none.

items.name: (5.1) Local symbol for divisors with a common point (tangent-vector symbol)
items.statement: Let X be a curve over the number field H, v a place of H, and a, b divisors of degree 0 on X whose supports meet exactly in the point x. Let g be a uniformizing parameter at x (a function on X with ord_x(g) = 1). Define ⟨a, b⟩_v := lim_{y→x} {⟨a_y, b⟩_v − ord_x(a) ord_x(b) log|g(y)|_v}, where a_y is the divisor obtained from a by replacing every occurrence of x by a nearby point y not in the support of b, and ⟨·,·⟩_v on the right is Néron's local symbol of relatively prime divisors. The limit exists by the standard properties of local heights ([14] = Gross, 'Local heights on curves').
items.note: Quoted from Gross [14]. Planned only in a different form: GZ.2 'Handle rational degree-one Hodge classes and self-intersections by a genuine regularization/intersection construction'; GZ.7 'Handle self-intersection terms and the normalized Hodge divisor'. YZZ regularise via the Hodge class, not via a tangent vector; Conrad (in the roadmap's source contract, Conrad §§2–10) re-derives (5.1) as Theorem 8.3 (conrad.txt p. 31). Library: none.

items.name: (5.2) Change of uniformizer; the sum of local symbols is the global pairing
items.statement: In the setting of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/100: if g′ is another uniformizing parameter at x and g/g′ has the value α at x, then ⟨a, b⟩′_v = ⟨a, b⟩_v + ord_x(a) ord_x(b) log|α|_v. Consequently ⟨a, b⟩_v depends only on the non-zero tangent vector ∂/∂t at x determined by ∂g/∂t = 1, is unchanged if ∂/∂t is multiplied by a root of unity (|α|_v = 1 for all v), and — g being a single global function — Σ_v ⟨a, b⟩_v is independent of g and (product formula) equals the global height pairing of the classes of a and b [14].
items.locator: Chapter II, §5, (5.2) and the following paragraph, p. 250
items.note: Sign checked: with g′ = g/α + …, log|g′(y)|_v = log|g(y)|_v − log|α|_v. Agrees with Conrad (8.2) (conrad.txt p. 31), 'since our α is the reciprocal of that in [GZ]'. Planned as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/100 (GZ.2 local height decomposition and regularized self-intersections). Library: none.

items.name: Dedekind eta function
items.note: Mathlib NumberTheory/ModularForms/DedekindEta.lean:60 `noncomputable def eta (z : ℂ) := 𝕢 24 z * ∏' n, (1 - eta_q n z)` with 𝕢 = Periodic.qParam (𝕢 24 z = e^{2πiz/24}) and `eta_q n z = (𝕢 1 z) ^ (n + 1)` (line 44): the same function.

items.name: (5.4) The differential ω = η⁴ dq/q and the normalized tangent vector at x
items.statement: ω := η⁴(z) dq/q = 2πi η⁴(z) dz (5.4). It is well defined on X₀(N) only up to a 6th root of unity (η⁴ has a multiplier of order 6), which by PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/101 does not affect the local symbols. If x is not an elliptic point of X₀(N) (u = 1), ω is non-zero at x, the tangent vector ∂/∂t is taken dual to ω, and the uniformizing parameter g satisfies ω = (g + a₂g² + a₃g³ + …) dg/g near x. In general ω has order 1/u − 1 at x and g is normalized so that ω = (1/u)(g^{1/u} + higher degree terms) dg/g near x, i.e. ω = d(g^{1/u})·(1 + …) [corrected; the printed display omits the factor 1/u — see issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E12].
items.locator: Chapter II, §5, (5.4) and the two paragraphs after it, p. 250
items.note: Corrected per PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E12 (the corrected form is the one used in (5.5) and in Ch. III (8.3)). No atlas stage plans a tangent-vector normalization at Heegner points; Conrad §9 (conrad.txt pp. 34–35) replaces η⁴ dq/q, which lives only on a degree-6 cover, by the ℚ-rational 6-tensor Δ(q)(dq/q)^{⊗6} = ((2πi)η⁴(z) dz)^{⊗6}; this is in the GZ roadmap's source contract but not in any stage description. Library: only η (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/102). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (5.3) The local symbol ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v when r_A(m) ≠ 0
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. When r_A(m) ≠ 0 the point x occurs with multiplicity r_A(m) in T_m(x^σ) (Ch. III (4.3)), so c and T_m d^σ are not relatively prime; ord_x(c) = 1 and ord_x(T_m d^σ) = r_A(m). For every place v of H set ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v := lim_{y→x} {⟨c_y, T_m d^σ⟩_v − r_A(m) log|g(y)|_v}, c_y = (y) − (∞), with g the normalized uniformizing parameter at x of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/103. By PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/101, Σ_v ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v = ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩.
items.note: Special case of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/100 with the global g of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/103. Planned only in YZZ's Hodge-class form, as for PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/100. Library: none.

items.name: (5.5) The normalized uniformizer at a complex place
items.statement: Let v be a complex place of H (|·|_v = |·|² on ℂ), g as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/103 (corrected normalization). Then log|g(y)|_v − u log|2πi η⁴(z)(w − z)|_v → 0 as y → x, where z, w ∈ 𝔥 map to x, y on X₀(N)(ℂ).
items.note: Checked: the local parameter of X₀(N) at x is (w − z)^u·(unit); with ω = 2πiη⁴(w)dw and ω = (1/u)(g^{1/u} + …)dg/g one gets g = (2πiη⁴(z)(w − z))^u (1 + o(1)), which is (5.5); with the printed normalization one would get g = (2πiη⁴(z)(w − z)/u)^u and a spurious −u log|u|_v (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E12). Conrad Theorem 9.6 (conrad.txt p. 42) takes g_{z_v}(z′) = 2πiη⁴(z_v)(z′ − z_v) and says this is 'exactly the archimedean height contribution which is computed in [GZ, Ch II, (5.3), (5.5)]'. Not planned; no library. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (5.6) Archimedean local symbol when r_A(m) ≠ 0
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Let v be a complex place of H and z, z′ ∈ 𝔥 points mapping to x, x^σ. With R_N = {(a b; c d) ∈ M₂(ℤ) : N | c}, g_s(z, z′) = −2Q_{s−1}(1 + |z − z′|²/(2 Im z Im z′)) (2.9), κ_N, λ_N as in (2.13), (2.21): ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v = lim_{s→1} [Σ_{γ ∈ R_N/±1, det γ = m, γz′ ≠ z} g_s(z, γz′) + 4πσ₁(m) E_N(w_N z, s) + u r_A(m) lim_{w→z} {g_s(z, w) − log|2πi η⁴(z)(w − z)|_v} + 4π m^s σ_{1−2s}(m) E_N(z′, s) + σ₁(m)κ_N/(s − 1)] − σ₁(m)(λ_N − 2κ_N) [printed '−σ₁(m)(λ_N + 2κ_N)'; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E10]. The number of γ ∈ R_N/±1 of determinant m with γz′ = z is u r_A(m).
items.note: Obtained from Prop. (2.23), (5.3) and (5.5); the terms with γz′ ≠ z and E_N(w_N w, s) are continuous at w = z. Checked a = u r_A(m): each coset Γ₀(N)γ with γz′ ∈ Γ₀(N)z contains exactly u elements (mod ±1) with γz′ = z, and there are r_A(m) such cosets (Ch. III (4.3)). Planned as a method only (GZ.7 archimedean Green-function identity; GZ.7 'Handle self-intersection terms'). No library.

items.name: (5.7) Extension of G^m_{N,s}(z, z′) to all z, z′
items.statement: For all z, z′ ∈ 𝔥 (previously defined only for z ∉ T_m z′): G^m_{N,s}(z, z′) := Σ_{γ ∈ R_N/±1, det γ = m, γz′ ≠ z} g_s(z, γz′) + Σ_{γ ∈ R_N/±1, det γ = m, γz′ = z} lim_{w→z} (g_s(z, w) − log|2πi η(z)⁴ (z − w)|²). With this definition (5.6) is literally the formula of Proposition (2.23); the second sum equals a·g_s(z), a = #{γ ∈ R_N/±1 : det γ = m, γz′ = z} (= u r_A(m) for z, z′ over x, x^σ), g_s(z) the renormalized value PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/109.
items.locator: Chapter II, §5, (5.7) and the paragraph after it, p. 251
items.note: GZ-specific renormalization; the terms with γz′ ≠ z reproduce §3 and give the n > 0 part of the sum in Prop. (3.11). Not planned; no library. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Asymptotics of the Legendre function Q_{s−1}(t) as t ↘ 1
items.statement: For the Legendre function of the second kind Q_{s−1} (s > 1, s near 1) as t ↘ 1: Q_{s−1}(t) = ½ log((t + 1)/(t − 1)) − (Γ′/Γ(s) − Γ′/Γ(1)) + o(1) [printed '+ O(1)'; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E11].
items.note: Classical: Q_ν(t) = ½ log((t+1)/(t−1)) − γ − ψ(ν + 1) + O((t − 1) log(t − 1)), and −γ − ψ(s) = ψ(1) − ψ(s). Library: Mathlib has the digamma function `Complex.digamma` = logDeriv Gamma (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Digamma.lean:48) with `Complex.digamma_one` = −γ (line 56), but no Legendre functions (grep legendreQ/LegendreQ in both libraries: none); atlas: no stage mentions Legendre functions of the second kind. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6, the single owner of the Legendre function of the second kind Q_{s−1} (for complex s with Re s > 0), shared with PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/258 (Q_{k−1} of Chapter IV (5.7)) and /273, which the extraction already routes to GZ.6; GZ.7, which depends on GZ.6, imports it for the Green function. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Renormalized self-value g_s(z)
items.statement: g_s(z) := lim_{w→z} (g_s(z, w) − log|2πi η(z)⁴ (z − w)|²) = −log|2π (z − z̄) η(z)⁴|² + 2 Γ′/Γ(s) − 2 Γ′/Γ(1).
items.note: Checked from PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/108 with t = 1 + |z − w|²/(2y²): ½ log((t+1)/(t−1)) = log(2y/|z − w|) + o(1) and |z − z̄| = 2y. Not planned; no library. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: Kronecker's first limit formula (as used for g_s(z))
items.statement: For z ∈ 𝔥 and E(z, σ) the weight-0 Eisenstein series of SL₂(ℤ) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/94): g_s(z) = −2 log 2π + 2 Γ′/Γ(s) + 2 Γ′/Γ(1) + (2/π) lim_{σ→1} [2^σ ζ(2σ) E(z, σ) − π/(σ − 1)]; equivalently (Kronecker's first limit formula) lim_{σ→1} [2^σ ζ(2σ) E(z, σ) − π/(σ − 1)] = 2πγ − π log(2 Im z · |η(z)|⁴).
items.locator: Chapter II, §5, p. 251 (last display; 'By Kronecker's first limit formula')
items.note: Quoted classical result. Planned: node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/kronecker-limit-formulas of the accepted EllipticRegulators packet (REV-EllipticRegulators): 'For z ∈ H: ζ*_{0,0}(z) = 2π(γ − log 2 − log √y − 2 log|η(z)|)', where ζ_{0,0}(z, s) = Σ′_{(m,n)} y^s/|mz + n|^{2s} and ζ*_{0,0} is its value regularised by subtracting π/(s − 1) (node ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series, proof steps 1–2). Since ζ_{0,0}(z, σ) = 2ζ(2σ)E(z, σ), the limit here is lim_{σ→1}[2^{σ−1}ζ_{0,0}(z, σ) − π/(σ − 1)] = ζ*_{0,0}(z) + π log 2 = 2πγ − π log(2y|η(z)|⁴). The atlas description of ER.7 does not name the formula; the packet node does. Checked the printed consequence against PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/109 (with Γ′/Γ(1) = −γ both sides equal 2Γ′/Γ(s) − 2Γ′/Γ(1) − log|2π(z − z̄)η(z)⁴|²). Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (Mathlib has only ModularForm.eta, NumberTheory/ModularForms/DedekindEta.lean:60). GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7 imports it; it needs no route.
