items.name: Proposition (5.8): Proposition (4.2) when r_A(m) ≠ 0
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Proposition (4.2) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/99) remains true when m is the norm of an ideal in A, provided that the local symbols ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v (v | ∞) in the definition of ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_∞ are defined by (5.3) with the normalized uniformizer g of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/103, and γ^m_{N,s}(A) is defined by (3.3) with G^m_{N,s} as in (5.7). This invariant is then γ^m_{N,s}(A) = (expression in Corollary (3.17)) + 2h u r_A(m) (Γ′/Γ(s) − log 2π + (L′/L)(1, ε) + ½ log|D|).
items.note: Checked: total contribution of the γz′ = z terms is a·Σ_A g_s(τ_A) with a = u r_A(m) (g_s(z) is SL₂(ℤ)-invariant since Im z·|η(z)|⁴ is). As for PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/99, planned only as a method (GZ.7 archimedean Green-function identity and self-intersection terms; GZ.8 specialization to X₀(N)); Conrad Theorem 9.6 (conrad.txt p. 42) confirms that this archimedean term, paired with his non-archimedean terms, recovers the global height. Validity at elliptic points (D = −3) depends on the corrected normalization of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/103 (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E12).

items.name: (0.1) Néron's local symbol as an arithmetic intersection number
items.statement: Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Let 𝒳 be a regular model of the curve X over A_v, a, b relatively prime divisors of degree 0 on X over H_v, and A, B divisors on 𝒳 restricting to a, b on the general fibre. If A has zero intersection with every fibre component of 𝒳, then ⟨a, b⟩_v = −(A · B) log q.
items.note: Quoted from Gross [14]. Planned: GZ.2 'construct the arithmetic intersection pairing from finite-place intersection lengths and archimedean Green functions. Include regular models, vertical correction divisors, intersection matrices and their kernel … Prove the Faltings–Hriljac comparison for degree-zero divisors with the canonical Jacobian pairing … Export local height decomposition'. Library: none (coverage audit AUDIT-25 for GZ.2: intersection pairing 'absent', regular models 'partial' — Tau Ceti has flat finitely presented models over a DVR but no regularity predicate).

items.name: Announced p-inert formula for Σ_{v|p}⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v (case r_A(m) = 0)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Let p be a prime inert in K and assume r_A(m) = 0. Then Σ_{v|p} ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v = −u² log p Σ_{0 < n < m|D|/N, n ≡ 0 (mod p)} ord_p(pn) r_A(m|D| − nN) δ(n) R_{{A𝔮𝔫}}(n/p), where 𝔮 is an ideal of O with (N𝔮/l) = (−p/l) for all primes l | D, δ(n) = 2^{#{primes l | (n, D)}} (3.15), and R_{{B}}(k) is the number of integral ideals of norm k in the genus of B.
items.locator: Chapter III, introduction, p. 253 (proved as the r_A(m) = 0 case of Proposition (9.7), p. 266)
items.note: Announcement; agrees with the second term of Prop. (9.7) (the first term −r_A(m) h u ord_p(m) log p vanishes when r_A(m) = 0). Planned only as YZZ's analogue: GZ.7 'Prove the finite-place identities between CM intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local representation densities/Whittaker functions. Separate split, inert and ramified extensions, ordinary, supersingular and superspecial reduction'; GZ.8 'Specialize to X₀(N)'. The explicit quaternionic evaluation (GZ III §9, Conrad §10 and Mann's appendix, in the source contract) is not named in any stage. Library: none.

items.name: (0.4) The case m = 1 at a prime p ∤ ND
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Let m = 1, v | p with p ∤ ND, and r_A(1) = 0 (σ ≠ 1, so x ≠ x^σ over H). Then ⟨(x) − (∞), (x^σ) − (0)⟩_v = ⟨c, d^σ⟩_v = −½ Σ_{n≥1} Card(Isom_{W/π^n}(x^σ, x)) log q_v. The sum is zero unless x and x^σ meet mod π; by Deuring's theory it is zero if p splits in K; otherwise p is inert (as p ∤ D) and log q_v = 2 log p.
items.locator: Chapter III, introduction, (0.4) and following paragraph, p. 253
items.note: Special case m = 1 of Prop. (3.3) + Prop. (4.4) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/132, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/135); degree-1 homomorphisms are isomorphisms. q_v = p² because p inert in K splits completely in H/K ((p) is principal). Planned as for PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/137 (GZ.7 deformation-length calculations). Library: none.

items.name: Supersingular reduction of a Heegner diagram: Eichler order and Hom ≅ R𝔞
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Let p be inert in K and p ∤ N (in the paper's illustration p ∤ ND, m = 1). The endomorphism ring R = End_{W/π}(x mod π) of the (supersingular) reduction of the Heegner diagram is an Eichler order of index (level) N in the definite quaternion algebra B over ℚ of discriminant p (ramified exactly at p and ∞), and Hom_{W/π}(x^σ, x) is isomorphic to the left R-module R𝔞 (𝔞 an ideal in the class A). The points x and x^σ meet mod π if and only if R𝔞 is principal; then Card(Isom_{W/π}(x^σ, x)) is the number of generators of R𝔞.
items.note: Stated without proof in the illustration (made precise in §§7, 9). Searched: 'Eichler' in Mathlib and Tau Ceti: none; atlas 'Eichler order': no stage. Nearest plans: GZ.7 ('supersingular and superspecial reduction'), HE.1 ('For quaternionic curves construct optimal embeddings of the specified orders'), HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.3 (definite quaternionic forms on finite double cosets); none states the Eichler-order description of End of a supersingular Γ₀(N)-diagram. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 1 plans only that End of an ordinary curve over 𝔽_q is an order in ℚ(π_q). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (0.5) Explicit model of B and of the order R, and R𝔞
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Let p be inert in K (p ∤ ND) and q a prime with pq ≡ −1 (mod D), i.e. −pq ≡ 1 (mod D) (printed: 'q ≡ −p (mod D)', which makes the lattice below an order only when p² ≡ 1 modulo every prime l | D; see the new issue on (0.5) reported with this review; either condition gives (q/l) = (−p/l) for all l | D); then (q) = 𝔮𝔮̄ splits in K and B = K + Kj with jα = ᾱj (α ∈ K) and j² = −pq is the definite quaternion algebra of discriminant p. For some place v | p the order R = End_{W/π}(x mod π) is R = {α + βj ∈ B : α ∈ 𝔡⁻¹, β ∈ 𝔡⁻¹𝔮⁻¹𝔫, α − β integral at all primes dividing 𝔡}, 𝔡 = (√D) the different of K and 𝔫 the primitive ideal of norm N attached to x. For 𝔞 an ideal in the class A: Hom_{W/π}(x^σ, x) ≅ R𝔞 = {α + βj : α ∈ 𝔡⁻¹𝔞, β ∈ 𝔡⁻¹𝔮⁻¹𝔫𝔞̄, α − β integral at 𝔡}. (With the printed q ≡ −p (mod D) the same statements hold after replacing the congruence 'α − β integral at 𝔡' by 'α − pβ integral at 𝔡'.)
items.locator: Chapter III, introduction, (0.5), p. 253 (general version (9.2)–(9.3), p. 265)
items.note: Corrected choice of q: with the printed q ≡ −p (mod D) one has −pq ≡ p² (mod l) for l | D, and for α = β ∈ 𝔡⁻¹ with a simple pole at the prime 𝔣 | l (allowed by 'α − β integral') the reduced norm is (1 + pq)N(β) with ord_l N(β) = −1, integral only if l | 1 − p². Checked in exact arithmetic for D = −7, p = 3, N = 2, 𝔫 = ((1+√−7)/2): with q = 11 ≡ −3 (mod 7) the lattice contains elements of reduced norm 10/7 and 13/7 and is not closed under multiplication; with q = 23 (−69 ≡ 1 mod 7) it is closed, has integral norms and Gram determinant 36 = (pN)², i.e. it is an Eichler order of level N in B_{p,∞} (checked by computer in review). Otherwise as before: ε(q) = 1, so q splits; the Hilbert symbol (D, −pq) is −1 exactly at p and ∞; N(α + βj) = Nα + pqNβ; (α + βj)𝔞 = α𝔞 + β𝔞̄ j gives the form of R𝔞. The same defect in §9's model S is PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E19 (Mann's Remark A.7). Library: Mathlib has the carrier `QuaternionAlgebra` (Mathlib/Algebra/Quaternion.lean:65) and Tau Ceti has splitting criteria (TauCeti/Algebra/Quaternion/Split.lean), but no orders; no atlas stage plans this model (Tau Ceti QuadraticFormInvariants Layer 2 plans quaternion algebras over fields only). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (0.6)–(0.7) Generators of R𝔞 and solutions of l + nN = |D|
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. In the setting of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/117, R𝔞 is principal iff it contains b = α + βj with reduced norm Nb = Nα + pqNβ = N𝔞. If b is a generator, the ideals 𝔠 = (α)𝔡𝔞⁻¹ and 𝔠′ = (β)𝔡𝔮𝔫⁻¹𝔞̄⁻¹ are integral (0.6) and satisfy N𝔠 + pN·N𝔠′ = |D| (0.7). Putting n = pN𝔠′ and l = N𝔠 gives a solution of l + nN = |D| with n ≡ 0 (mod p) and r_A(l) ≠ 0; conversely such solutions yield generators of R𝔞 and contribute to the height in (0.4).
items.note: Checked: N𝔠 = Nα·|D|/N𝔞 and N𝔠′ = Nβ·|D|q/(N·N𝔞), so N𝔠 + pN·N𝔠′ = |D|(Nα + pqNβ)/N𝔞 = |D|; 𝔠 lies in A⁻¹ and r_{A⁻¹} = r_A. The 'conversely' is asserted without proof here (proved in §9). Not planned (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/117); no library. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (1.1)–(1.2) The moduli stack 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} of cyclic N-isogenies of generalized elliptic curves
items.statement: For a base scheme S, 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)}(S) is the groupoid of cyclic isogenies φ: E → E′ of degree N between generalized elliptic curves over S (1.1) such that the group scheme A = ker φ meets every irreducible component of each geometric fibre. 'Cyclic of degree N' means that locally on S there is a point P with A = Σ_{a=1}^{N} [aP] as Cartier divisors on E (1.2). When N is invertible on S this is equivalent to A being locally isomorphic to ℤ/Nℤ; when N is squarefree it is equivalent to A being locally free of rank N.
items.note: Planned: R13.2 'Construct compactified full and Γ₁ level problems, and the correct Γ₀(n) problem at general n. Follow Česnavičius' refined description when the naive cyclic-subgroup formulation fails; include the extra boundary data'; Tau Ceti ModularCurves 8D (KM 6.6.1, [Γ₀(N)] over Ell, elliptic curves only, 'Identify this locus with [Γ₀(N)]'); 3B 'Define a cyclic subgroup of order N …' (Drinfeld/KM cyclicity). Note: for N not squarefree this naive stack differs from the Deligne–Rapoport stack 𝒳₀(N) at the cusps (it is not Deligne–Mumford there), although it is algebraic, agrees with 𝒳₀(N) on the elliptic-curve locus and still has X₀(N) as its coarse moduli space (Česnavičius, A modular description of X₀(n), Algebra & Number Theory 11 (2017), §§1.1–1.2); the paper's description of the kernel at Cusp(d) fails there (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E13). R13.2 plans the refined (Česnavičius) stack instead. Library: none (grep generalizedElliptic/cyclicIsogen/coarseModuli in both libraries: none).

items.name: The model X of X₀(N) over ℤ (coarse moduli scheme)
items.statement: X := the coarse moduli scheme of 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} ([7] Deligne–Rapoport pp. 234–243; [21] Katz–Mazur pp. 407 ff.), a model of X₀(N) over ℤ. X ⊗ ℤ[1/N] is smooth and proper over ℤ[1/N]; for a prime p | N, X ⊗ ℤ/pℤ is singular and reducible over ℤ/pℤ.
items.note: Planned: R13.4a 'Construct coarse compactified curves from R13.2's actual stack presentations, with the necessary finite-inertia quotient, normalization and existence arguments. Treat full, fixed-pairing, Γ₁ and refined Γ₀ level separately … Prove properness, normality and the allowed base-change statements'; Tau Ceti ModularCurves 9D (coarse moduli M(𝒫) of affine KM problems) and Layer 10 (compactified curves over ℤ[1/N], prime N ≥ 5 only). Coverage audit (AUDIT-10): R13.4a 'not built'. For every N the coarse moduli space of the naive stack PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/119 is the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur model X₀(N) (Česnavičius, A modular description of X₀(n), Algebra & Number Theory 11 (2017), §1.1: the naive stack 'is algebraic, has X₀(n) as its coarse moduli space, and agrees with X₀(n) on the elliptic curve locus'), so the model X is the right one; for N not squarefree only the stack at the cusps, and the paper's description of the kernel at Cusp(d), are off (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E13).

items.name: Structure of the fibre X ⊗ 𝔽_p for p | N
items.statement: Let p | N, N = pⁿM with (p, M) = 1. Then X ⊗ ℤ/pℤ has n + 1 irreducible components 𝓕_{a,b}, indexed by pairs of non-negative integers with a + b = n; 𝓕_{a,b} is isomorphic to X₀(M) ⊗ ℤ/pℤ and occurs with multiplicity φ(p^c), c = min(a, b). All the 𝓕_{a,b} meet at each supersingular point of X (the points x = (φ: E → E′) with E, E′ supersingular). The non-supersingular points of 𝓕_{a,b} correspond to diagrams whose kernel A = ker φ is locally isomorphic to μ_{p^a} × ℤ/p^bℤ × ℤ/Mℤ.
items.note: Katz–Mazur ch. 13 ('crossings', KM 13.4.7). Not planned in this generality: ModularCurvesPartII:R13.5 plans 'the local models and supersingular intersections required by the proof … Begin with the prime-to-p level and one p-factor cases used by level lowering, then treat every higher p-power/composite-level case actually invoked by the Serre weight-and-level argument' — its scope is tied to level lowering, so Γ₀(pⁿM) with n ≥ 2 is not planned; Tau Ceti ModularCurves 8A plans only the pointwise fact that, for an ordinary p-power fibre, the rank-pⁿ subgroups of E[pⁿ] ≅ μ_{pⁿ} × ℤ/pⁿℤ are μ_{p^a} × p^{n−b}(ℤ/pⁿℤ), a + b = n; and the Tau Ceti ModularCurves README (§Scope and §The Mazur interface) excludes the characteristic-N compactified geometry and sends it to 'a future Deligne–Rapoport/semistable-reduction roadmap'. Coverage audit (AUDIT-10): R13.5 'not built'. Library: none. Checked the component count against Kronecker's congruence PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/122 (degrees p² + p for n = 2, M = 1; the congruence itself verified for N = 4 mod 2 and N = 9 mod 3). Routed (source) to ModularCurvesPartII:R13.5 together with PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/125: R13.5 must state the component structure of X₀(pⁿM) ⊗ 𝔽_p for all n (KM 13.4.7), which GZ use in §§1 and 3.

items.name: Kronecker's congruence for the modular polynomial
items.statement: For N = pⁿM with (p, M) = 1 and Φ_N(j, j′) the classical modular polynomial of level N: Φ_N(j, j′) ≡ Π_{a+b=n, c=min(a,b)} Φ_M(j^{p^{a−c}}, j′^{p^{b−c}})^{φ(p^c)} (mod p).
items.note: Quoted classical result illustrating PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/121. Checked n = 1, M = 1: Φ_p(j, j′) ≡ (j^p − j′)(j − j′^p) (mod p), the classical Kronecker congruence; for n = 2, M = 1 the j-degrees p² + (p − 1) + 1 = p² + p = ψ(p²) agree. Searched: modularPolynomial/ModularPolynomial in Mathlib and Tau Ceti: none; atlas: no stage mentions modular polynomials or Kronecker's congruence. Routed (source) to ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.3. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 5: ModularCurvesPartII R12.5, R12.6, R13.5, R14.1, R14.2.

items.name: (1.3) Aut_k(x) for a geometric point of X
items.statement: For a geometric point x = (φ: E → E′) of X over an algebraically closed field k, Aut_k(x) is the group of pairs of isomorphisms (f: E → E, f′: E′ → E′) with f′ ∘ φ = φ ∘ f (diagram (1.3)). It is finite, contains ⟨±1⟩, and equals the automorphism group of the pair (E, A), A = ker φ.
items.note: Planned implicitly with the stack: R13.4a 'Treat full, fixed-pairing, Γ₁ and refined Γ₀ level separately, with their bases and stabilizers'. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 1 plans Aut(E, O) (units of the geometric endomorphism ring) but not automorphisms of level structures. Library: none.

items.name: Strict henselization of X at x ([7, p. 172])
items.statement: The strict henselization of X at a geometric point x is isomorphic to the quotient of the strict henselization of 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} at the corresponding point by the group Aut_k(x)/⟨±1⟩.
items.note: Quoted from Deligne–Rapoport. Conrad Lemma 4.2 (conrad.txt p. 11) proves the complete-local version: the complete local ring of X at y₀ is the ring of Aut(y₀)-invariants in the universal deformation ring, on which −1 acts trivially. Planned: Tau Ceti ModularCurves 9D (M(𝒫) = 𝕄(𝒫, δ)/G, invariant quotients) and 9C ('at a supersingular point the completed local ring of the quotient is A^H', for the listed quotient problems); R13.4a (finite-inertia quotients). Library: none.

items.name: Proposition (1.4): regularity of X over ℤ
items.statement: X is regular at every point except the points x of characteristic p | N with Aut_k(x) ≠ ⟨±1⟩ that are supersingular or lie on a component 𝓕_{a,b} with a ≥ 1 and b ≥ 1; those exceptional points are singular. (Printed: 'X is regular over ℤ, except at the supersingular points x in characteristics p|N where Aut_k(x) ≠ ⟨±1⟩'.) The ordinary exceptions occur only when p² | N, at points with j = 1728 (p ≡ 1 mod 4) or j = 0 (p ≡ 1 mod 3) whose level structure is preserved by the extra automorphism (for N = p² every such point of 𝓕_{1,1}); they lie on components of multiplicity φ(p^{min(a,b)}) > 1, away from the Heegner sections (which reduce to 𝓕_{n,0}, 𝓕_{0,n} by (3.1)) and from the cusps.
items.note: Quoted by GZ as a consequence of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/124, Drinfeld [9] and Katz–Mazur [21, p. 166]; the printed exception set is too small (new issue reported with this review). Check for N = p², p ≡ 1 (mod 4), x = (E, A) with E ordinary, j(E) = 1728, A = μ_p × ℤ/p on 𝓕_{1,1}: [i] preserves A, so Aut_k(x) = μ₄. The complete local ring of the stack at x is W[ζ_p][[T]] (T the Serre–Tate coordinate, the p − 1 cyclic subgroups of type (1,1) over the generic fibre being indexed by a primitive p-th root of unity ζ), and [i] acts by T ↦ −T + O(T²) and ζ ↦ ζ^{−1}, i.e. by −1 on the cotangent space; this is not a pseudo-reflection, so the invariant ring W⁺[[X, Y]]/(Y² − ϖ₊X) (W⁺ = W[ζ + ζ^{−1}]) is not regular (Serre's criterion). Edixhoven, 'Minimal resolution and stable reduction of X₀(N)', Ann. Inst. Fourier 40 (1990) 31–67, §1.1.3 (p. 35), states the correct singular locus ('points … which have extra automorphisms, and are supersingular or have a ≠ 0 ≠ b … must be singular in the surface X₀(pⁿN)') and resolves them in §§1.3.3, 1.3.6 and 1.4.4–1.4.5; the Tau Ceti ModularCurves README (§The Mazur interface) records the prime-level case, 'regularity of M₀(N)/ℤ away from j ∈ {0, 1728}'. Nothing in GZ is affected: the resolution X^reg in the proof of (3.3) must also treat these points, but they meet neither the Heegner sections nor the cusps, so (3.2) and (3.3) stand. Nearest plans: Tau Ceti ModularCurves 8D ('prove the Notes Added in Proof descent theorem which passes regularity to [Γ₀(N)]' — the stack over Ell, not the compactified coarse space) and 9C ('No assertion is made that an arbitrary finite quotient of a regular moduli problem is regular'); R13.5 (regular models only at the levels used by level lowering). Conrad avoids the statement (Remark 2.3: X_v 'is usually not regular'; only the relative smooth locus is used). Library: none. Routed (source) to ModularCurvesPartII:R13.5, with Edixhoven 1990 as the source for the corrected statement and the minimal resolution.

items.name: Cusps of X and their reductions
items.statement: The subscheme Cusps of X is finite over ℤ, with one irreducible component Cusp(d) for each positive divisor d of N; Cusp(d) has φ(f) geometric points, f = gcd(d, N/d), and Cusp(d) ≅ Spec ℤ[μ_f]. [Printed: 'Cusp(d) corresponds to diagrams of Néron polygons where A = ker φ is isomorphic to μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ' — correct only when gcd(d, N/d) = 1; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E13.] The section ∞ of X is Cusp(N) (A ≅ μ_N) and the section 0 is Cusp(1) (A ≅ ℤ/Nℤ); in characteristic p | N they reduce to the components 𝓕_{n,0} and 𝓕_{0,n} respectively, and in general Cusp(d) (mod p) lies on 𝓕_{a,b} with a = ord_p(d) [21, Chap. 10].
items.note: Planned: R12.3 'Construct the local parameter at each cusp, compare its width with the Tate parameter … identify the scheme-theoretic cusp locus. … do not … assert that the coarse cusp fibre is always reduced'; R13.3 'classify boundary level data and compute completed local rings, cusp widths … The finite-flat cusp fibre, its reduced locus, and its Cartier structure are distinct assertions'; Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 10 treats only prime N ≥ 5 over ℤ[1/N]. The count φ(gcd(d, N/d)) and field ℚ(μ_f) are the classical cusp data of X₀(N). Only Cusp(N) and Cusp(1) (gcd = 1) are used later. Library: none (Tau Ceti has analytic cusps of congruence subgroups in NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps, not the integral cusp scheme).

items.name: (2.1) Hom_S(y, x) between Γ₀(N)-diagrams, its degree
items.statement: Let S be a complete local ring with algebraically closed residue field k, and x = (φ: E → E′), y = (ψ: F → F′) two S-valued points of X with non-cuspidal reduction, represented by diagrams of cyclic N-isogenies over S. Hom_S(y, x) is the set of pairs of homomorphisms (f: F → E, f′: F′ → E′) over S with f′ ∘ ψ = φ ∘ f (diagram (2.1)); addition uses the group laws of E and E′. It is a left module over End_S(x) = Hom_S(x, x) and a right module over End_S(y) (multiplication = composition). The degree of a non-zero (f, f′) is the positive integer deg f = deg f′; for each m ≥ 1 the set Hom_S(y, x)_{deg m} is finite and carries a faithful action of the finite group Aut_S(x). [GZ add: 'one can check that the definition of Hom_S(y, x) is independent of the diagrams chosen to represent the points x and y' — false in general for artinian S at points with extra automorphisms; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E14.]
items.note: deg f = deg f′ because deg φ = deg ψ = N. Planned as the object of the deformation-length method: GZ.7 'Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models'; A6 'Extend the field Hom/End API … with finite generation and torsion freeness … degree formulas for polarized isogenies' (abelian schemes, not diagrams). Library: none for diagrams (Tau Ceti has field-level isogenies of Weierstrass curves, AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/*).

items.name: Deuring: End_S(x) is ℤ, an imaginary quadratic order, or a quaternion order
items.statement: In the setting of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/127, the ring End_S(x) is either ℤ, an order in an imaginary quadratic field, or an order in a definite quaternion algebra of prime discriminant over ℚ [8].
items.note: Quoted from Deuring (1941). Searched: no endomorphism-ring classification in Mathlib or Tau Ceti ('supersingular' occurs once in Tau Ceti, in a comment of AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/QuadraticTwist.lean). Nearest plan: Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 1 ('The assertion that the endomorphism ring of an ordinary curve over 𝔽_q is an order in ℚ(π_q) is a substantial theorem … a named milestone'; also `GeometricEnd`, `HasGeometricCM`); the quaternion (supersingular) case and the characteristic-0 classification are not planned. Routed (source) to ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.5.

items.name: Reduction of Heegner sections (Deuring; potentially good reduction)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Since N is prime to D^h = disc(H/ℚ), X ⊗ A_v has the shape of §1. CM elliptic curves have potentially good reduction, so the sections x and x^σ do not meet the divisor Cusps in the special fibre. They reduce to supersingular points if and only if p is not split in K [29]. If p | N then p splits in K and x, x^σ have ordinary reduction.
items.note: Deuring's reduction criterion, quoted from Serre [29]. Nearest plans: GZ.7 'Separate split, inert and ramified extensions, ordinary, supersingular and superspecial reduction' (names the case division, not the criterion); ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.5 'Instantiate the Shimura–Taniyama formula for reductions … Supersingular reduction cannot be treated as ordinary'. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layers 3–4 plan the ordinary/supersingular dichotomy and HasGoodSupersingularReduction as definitions only. Library: none. Conrad Lemma 2.4 / Theorem 2.5 (conrad.txt pp. 4–6) supply the good models over W. Routed (source) to ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.5.

items.name: Proposition (3.1): component of the reduction when p | N
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Suppose p | N (so p = 𝔭𝔭̄ splits and v divides exactly one of 𝔫, 𝔫̄, where O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/Nℤ is the annihilator of ker φ). Then the sections x and x^σ reduce to ordinary points in the component 𝓕_{0,n} if v | 𝔫̄, and 𝓕_{n,0} if v | 𝔫 (n = ord_p N).
items.note: Proof: if v | 𝔫̄, ker φ is étale over A_v, ≅ ℤ/Nℤ over 𝔽, so the reduction lies on 𝓕_{0,n} ∋ Cusp(1) = 0; if v | 𝔫, ker φ ≅ μ_{pⁿ} × ℤ/Mℤ over 𝔽, so it lies on 𝓕_{n,0} ∋ Cusp(N) = ∞; x^σ has kernel also annihilated by 𝔫 (σ fixes K). Checked against PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/121, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/126. Used by Conrad Lemma 2.2 and Corollary 2.7. Planned only via GZ.7 'horizontal intersections and vertical corrections' (the vertical correction at p | N vanishes by PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/131). Library: none.

items.name: Corollary (3.2): one of c, d is orthogonal to all fibre components
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. One of the divisors c = (x) − (∞) and d^σ = (x^σ) − (0) (printed 'd = (x^σ) − (0)') has zero intersection with every fibral component 𝓕_{a,b} of X ⊗ A_v: when p | N (so v divides exactly one of 𝔫, 𝔫̄), c does if v | 𝔫 and d^σ does if v | 𝔫̄; when p ∤ N the special fibre is irreducible and both do.
items.locator: Chapter III, (3.2) Corollary and proof, pp. 256–257
items.note: For p ∤ N the fibre is irreducible and the statement is trivial. Planned as PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/130. Library: none.

items.name: Proposition (3.3) = (0.2): local symbol as intersection number
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Assume m ≥ 1 is prime to N and r_A(m) = 0. Then ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v = −(x · T_m x^σ) log q.
items.locator: Chapter III, (3.3) Proposition, p. 257 (announced as (0.2), p. 252)
items.note: Proof checked: resolve the quotient singularities of X to get X^reg — GZ say 'at the supersingular points', but the singular locus also contains the ordinary points with extra automorphisms on the components 𝓕_{a,b}, a, b ≥ 1 (Edixhoven 1990, §1.1.3; see /125) — the Heegner sections and cusps are unaffected either way; by PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/131 and Hecke-invariance of fibral components (m prime to N), PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/113 applies to c and T_m d; expand (c·T_m d^σ) = (x·T_m x^σ) − (x·T_m 0) − (∞·T_m x^σ) + (∞·T_m 0), where the middle terms vanish (potentially good reduction) and (∞·T_m 0) = σ₁(m)(∞·0) = 0 since N > 1. Regularity after base change to A_v holds: if p | D then p ∤ N and X is smooth over ℤ_p; if p | N then H_v/ℚ_p is unramified (cf. Conrad Remark 2.3, conrad.txt p. 4, which cites this proposition). Planned: GZ.2 (local height decomposition via regular models) and GZ.7 ('Assemble local formulas … including local terms supported at conductor and discriminant primes'). Library: none.

items.name: (4.1)–(4.2) Endomorphisms and homomorphisms of Heegner diagrams over W
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. End_W(x) = End_W(x^σ) = O (4.1), and Hom_W(x^σ, x) ≅ 𝔞 as a left O-module (4.2), where 𝔞 is an ideal in the class A corresponding to σ under the Artin isomorphism. If g_α ∈ Hom_W(x^σ, x) corresponds to α ∈ 𝔞, then deg g_α = Nα/N𝔞.
items.locator: Chapter III, §4, (4.1)–(4.2) and following paragraph, p. 257
items.note: Quoted: proved analytically via lattices [23] (Lang), algebraically by Serre [29] (x^σ = (Hom(𝔞, E) → Hom(𝔞, E′))). Checked analytically: E = ℂ/L, E^σ = ℂ/𝔞⁻¹L, Hom(ℂ/𝔞⁻¹L, ℂ/L) = 𝔞, deg = [L : α𝔞⁻¹L] = N(α)/N(𝔞). Planned: CM.1 'Construct the elliptic curve associated to a complex ideal lattice and its order action … Compute the action of an invertible prime ideal and its isogeny degree; compare analytic and algebraic endomorphisms'; HE.1 'prove descent to ring class fields by the main theorem of complex multiplication'. The passage to W (good models; Conrad Theorems 2.5–2.6) is not named in these stages. Library: none.

items.name: Proposition (4.3): multiplicity of x in T_m x^σ
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Assume m is prime to N. The multiplicity of the point x in the divisor T_m x^σ is r_A(m).
items.note: Proof: by (2.3) of Ch. I the multiplicity is the number of degree-m isogenies g_α ∈ 𝔞 ≅ Hom_W(x^σ, x) = Hom_{H̄}(x^σ, x) modulo O^× ≅ Aut_W(x), i.e. the number of integral ideals 𝔟 = (α)/𝔞 of norm m in A⁻¹, equivalently r_A(m) (conjugation). Refines Prop. (9.1) of Ch. I. Used by Conrad §4 (conrad.txt p. 10). Planned: HE.2 'Compute Hecke correspondences on CM points by classifying the local cyclic subgroups/optimal embeddings'. Library: none.

items.name: Proposition (4.4) = (0.3): intersection number as a sum of Hom counts
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. I §3, Ch. II): N > 1; K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D with D odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4), (D, N) = 1 and D ≡ □ (mod 4N) (so every p | N splits in K); O = O_K, h = h_K, u = #O^×/2 (u = 1 unless D = −3, then u = 3), w = 2u; H the Hilbert class field; ε(n) = (D/n); x = (φ: E → E′) ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ ≅ O/𝔫 for the primitive ideal 𝔫 of norm N); c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0); σ ∈ Gal(H/K) ↔ A ∈ Cl_K under the Artin isomorphism; m ≥ 1 with (m, N) = 1; T_m the m-th Hecke correspondence; r_A(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in A; σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν. Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. Assume m is prime to N and r_A(m) = 0. Then (x · T_m x^σ) = ½ Σ_{n≥1} Card(Hom_{W/πⁿ}(x^σ, x)_{deg m}).
items.locator: Chapter III, (4.4) Proposition, p. 258 (announced as (0.3), p. 252; proved in §§5–6)
items.note: (0.3) is printed with Hom_{W/πⁿ}(x, x^σ); duality f ↦ f̂ (compatible with the diagrams, Hom groups being torsion-free) gives a degree-preserving bijection, so the two counts agree — not a mistake. Same statement as Conrad Theorem 5.1 (conrad.txt p. 13, with W_n = W/π^{n+1}, n ≥ 0). Planned: GZ.7 'Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models'; A4 'Prove the Serre–Tate equivalence for deformations of abelian schemes'; Tau Ceti ModularCurves 7F (ST-1: the Serre–Tate equivalence). items.name: (4.5) Reduction of homomorphisms is injective; Hom_W = ∩ Hom_{W/πⁿ}
items.statement: Local notation (Ch. III): v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the ring of integers of H_v, π a uniformizer, q = q_v = p^f = #A_v/π; W the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (π is prime in W), 𝔽 = W/π an algebraic closure of A_v/π; X the model of X₀(N) over ℤ of §1; x, x^σ the sections of X ⊗ A_v (or X ⊗ W) extending x, x^σ. For S-valued diagrams y, x as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/127 over W: Hom_{W/π^{n+1}}(x^σ, x) ↪ Hom_{W/πⁿ}(x^σ, x) for n ≥ 1, and Hom_W(x^σ, x) = ∩_{n≥1} Hom_{W/πⁿ}(x^σ, x) [15, 30]. Hence, when r_A(m) = 0, the terms of the sum in (4.4) vanish for n sufficiently large.
items.note: Injectivity is rigidity (Conrad Theorem 2.1(2), Lemma 3.1); the intersection is Grothendieck's existence theorem (Conrad Theorem 3.4 and the display after it, conrad.txt p. 9); vanishing for large n follows since Hom_W(x^σ, x)_{deg m} = ∅ when r_A(m) = 0 (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/133–PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/134) and the finite sets decrease. Planned: A1 'Prove rigidity for pointed maps … Include the nonreduced-base argument'; SF.4 'formal schemes, algebraization'. Library: none.

items.name: The integer h_n(y, x)_{deg m}
items.statement: For sections y, x over W as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/127: h_n(y, x)_{deg m} := ½ Card Hom_{W/πⁿ}(y, x)_{deg m}.
items.locator: Chapter III, §4, last sentence before §5, p. 258
items.note: Notation used in §§5–9; h_n is an integer because −1 acts freely on Hom_{W/πⁿ}(y, x)_{deg m}. Planned at method level only, like PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/135 and /138: GZ.7 'Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models'; no stage names this X₀(N)-specific count. No library (rg for Hom groups of Γ₀(N)-diagrams over W/πⁿ in Mathlib and Tau Ceti: none). The same definition was also the first half of /138, which this review narrows to the 'new' homomorphisms.

items.name: 'New' homomorphisms and automorphisms Hom^{new}_{W/πⁿ}(y,x), Aut^{new}_{W/πⁿ}(x)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). For non-cuspidal W-sections y, x of X and n ≥ 1, reduction Hom_W(y, x) → Hom_{W/πⁿ}(y, x) is injective (4.5); set Hom^{new}_{W/πⁿ}(y, x) := Hom_{W/πⁿ}(y, x) ∖ (image of Hom_W(y, x)) and Aut^{new}_{W/πⁿ}(x) := Aut_{W/πⁿ}(x) ∖ Aut_W(x). For the Heegner points x, x^σ and p non-split in K, under the identification Hom_{W/πⁿ}(x^σ, x) ≅ End_{W/πⁿ}(x)·𝔞 ⊂ B of (7.3)(2), whose image of Hom_W(x^σ, x) ≅ 𝔞 lies in K, an element b is new exactly when b ∉ K, i.e. b₋ ≠ 0.
items.locator: Chapter III, §8, Lemma (8.2), p. 263 (Aut^{new}) and (8.4) with the following paragraph, p. 264 (Hom^{new}, and the reading b₋ ≠ 0); uses (4.5), p. 258
items.note: The superscript 'new' is used without a formal definition in (8.2) and (8.4); the meaning fixed here is the one required by (8.2)'s two lines (½Σ(Card Aut_{W/πⁿ} − Card Aut_W) = ½Σ Card Aut^{new}) and by the remark after (8.4). The definition of h_n itself is PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/137. Conrad (10.2)–(10.3) uses the same notion ('those not lifting to W'). Plan: method-level, GZ.7 ('Handle self-intersection terms … Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models'); the stage text is written for YZZ's Shimura-curve setting and names no X₀(N)-specific statement. No Mathlib/Tau Ceti object for Γ₀(N)-diagram Hom groups over W/πⁿ.

items.name: (5.1) Hom counts over T_m x^σ for m prime to p
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Assume p ∤ m. Every point y of the divisor T_m x^σ is a Heegner point over H̄ in the sense of Gross [13] (defined over the ring class field of its conductor, not in general over H), with End_{H̄}(y) = O_y an order in K of conductor dividing m. Each y is rational over W ⊗ ℚ_p and is the canonical lifting of its reduction. For every n ≥ 1, h_n(x^σ,x)_{deg m} = Σ_{y ∈ T_m x^σ} h_n(y,x)_{deg 1}. Reason: a degree-m isogeny f: x^σ → x over W/π^n is determined by its kernel, which lifts uniquely to an étale subgroup C of order m of x^σ over W, and f induces an isomorphism x^σ_C ≅ x over W/π^n.
items.note: GZ.7 plans the deformation-length calculations: GZ.7 (Local arithmetic identities and boundary contributions): 'Prove the finite-place identities between CM intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local representation densities/Whittaker functions. Separate split, inert and ramified extensions, ordinary, supersingular and superspecial reduction, horizontal intersections and vertical corrections. Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models. ... Handle self-intersection terms ... Assemble local formulas into the global kernel comparison of GZ.6, including local terms supported at conductor and discriminant primes.' The roadmap's primary source contracts include 'Gross–Zagier, Chapters II–IV' and 'Conrad, Gross–Zagier revisited, §§2–10' (README l.127), and Conrad §§4–10 re-prove exactly this chapter. The stage text is written in YZZ's generality (Shimura curves). No stage names the X₀(N)-specific statement, and GZ.8's 'Specialize to X₀(N)' specialises the global formula, not these local identities. This is a method-level plan. HE.2 'Compute Hecke correspondences on CM points by classifying the local cyclic subgroups/optimal embeddings' plans the identification of the points of T_m x^σ as CM points of conductor dividing m (global statement). Neither names the étale-lifting Hom count. Conrad re-proves it in §5 (Theorem 5.1 with p ∤ m).

items.name: Canonical and quasi-canonical liftings (Gross [15])
items.statement: Let v | p, W as in the standing notation, O_p = O ⊗ ℤ_p and, for s ≥ 0, O_s = ℤ_p + p^s·O_p. For a Heegner point z whose reduction z̄ is supersingular (p non-split), a canonical lifting of z̄ is a lifting over W whose formal group has endomorphism ring O_p (it is unique; z itself is one); for s ≥ 1 a quasi-canonical lifting of level s (level p^s) is a lifting whose formal group has endomorphism ring exactly O_s; it is defined over the ring of integers W_s of the totally ramified abelian extension of W ⊗ ℚ_p of degree [O_p^× : O_s^×] (= p^{s−1}(p + 1) if p is inert, p^s if p is ramified), and the level-s liftings form one Galois orbit. When p splits (ordinary reduction), the canonical lifting is the Serre–Tate canonical lift and the quasi-canonical liftings of level s are the deformations whose Serre–Tate parameter is a primitive p^s-th root of unity, over W[ζ_{p^s}] (degree p^{s−1}(p − 1)). The Heegner points in T_m x^σ with p ∤ m are canonical liftings, and the points of T_{p^t}z are quasi-canonical liftings of levels 0 ≤ s ≤ t (see /139, /140).
items.locator: Chapter III, §5, pp. 258–259 ('the theory of canonical and quasi-canonical liftings, as developed in [15]'; 'quasi-canonical liftings (of level p^s, with 0 ≤ s ≤ t) … ([15], Prop. (5.3))')
items.note: GZ use these objects in (5.1)–(5.4), in the proof of (4.4) (§6) and in (8.5), but only name them. Definition taken from Gross, 'On canonical and quasi-canonical liftings', Invent. Math. 84 (1986) 321–326, §§3–5, and for the ordinary case from Conrad, gzfinal.pdf p. 48 ('y(s) is a quasi-canonical lifting in the Serre–Tate sense'). Status mirrors the extraction's treatment of the theorems about these objects (/140, /142, /149: planned at method level by GZ.7, 'Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models'); no atlas stage, packet or decomposition names canonical or quasi-canonical liftings (searched atlas.json descriptions, research/blueprint/packets, data/decompositions: the only hits are an example in the FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory packet mentioning that the connected–étale sequence splits exactly for the canonical lift, and an unrelated 'canonical lift' in HeegnerPointEulerSystems). If the lead downgrades /140, /142, /149 to missing, this item goes with them into route 1. Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (declarations.tsv: no canonicalLift, quasiCanonical, supersingular). Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: (5.2) Decomposition of T_{p^t}z into quasi-canonical liftings (Gross [15], Prop. 5.3)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Let m = p^t·r with t ≥ 1 and (r,p) = 1, and let z ∈ T_r x^σ (rational over W ⊗ ℚ_p). The points y of T_{p^t}z are rational over ramified extensions of W ⊗ ℚ_p. The corresponding sections over the ring-class extensions W_y are quasi-canonical liftings of level p^s (0 ≤ s ≤ t) of their reductions ([15], Prop. 5.3). Let y(s) denote the W-divisor formed by a point of level s together with all its W-conjugates. Then: p split in K: T_{p^t}z = Σ_{0≤s≤t} Σ_{j=1}^{t−s+1} y(s)_j with deg y(s)_j = p^s − p^{s−1} (s ≥ 1); p inert in K: T_{p^t}z = Σ_{0≤s≤t, s≡t (mod 2)} y(s) with deg y(s) = p^s + p^{s−1} (s ≥ 1); p ramified in K: T_{p^t}z = Σ_{0≤s≤t} y(s) with deg y(s) = p^s (s ≥ 0). Level-0 components have degree 1.
items.note: Checked: the degrees add up to σ₁(p^t) = 1+p+…+p^t in each case (split: Σ_s (t−s+1)(p^s−p^{s−1}) + (t+1) telescopes; inert and ramified directly). The degrees equal [O_p^× : O_{s,p}^×] for O_s = ℤ + p^sO. Partial plan: HE.0 'Compute the kernels of Pic(O_cℓ)→Pic(O_c) and extension degrees with the exceptional unit indices retained; ℓ+1 is only the inert, prime-to-conductor, ordinary-unit case' (the global orbit sizes). HE.2 'Compute Hecke correspondences on CM points by classifying the local cyclic subgroups/optimal embeddings ... for split or ramified primes and repeated conductor primes prove the full recurrence' (the conductor decomposition). GZ.7 plans deformation-length calculations in general. No stage names Gross's quasi-canonical liftings: 'quasi-canonical' and 'canonical lift' do not occur in any atlas stage description (the only hit is BelyiMaps layer 12, unrelated). Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti either.

items.name: (5.3) Eichler's congruence T_{p^t} ≡ Σ F^{t−i}F′^i (mod p) (quoted, Eichler [11])
items.statement: For a prime p ∤ N and t ≥ 1, on the special fibre X ⊗ F_p: T_{p^t} ≡ F^t + F^{t−1}F′ + F^{t−2}F′² + … + F′^t (mod p). Here F is the Frobenius correspondence and F′ its transpose. Consequence used (with (5.2)): every point y of y(s) is congruent mod π_y to a canonical lifting y₀ of level zero over W.
items.note: Checked for t = 2 from T_p ≡ F + F′, FF′ = F′F = p·Δ and T_p² = T_{p²} + pΔ. R14.6: 'Supply the special-fibre Eichler–Shimura relation'. HE.2: 'Establish the Eichler–Shimura relation used in the proof in the appropriate geometric category'. The p^t form also needs the Hecke recursion as correspondences, planned by R14.1 ('Prove composition, double-coset and adjoint formulas'). Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti: rg for 'Eichler' finds nothing, and Tau Ceti's Frobenius isogenies are for a single curve over a field.

items.name: (5.4) Fundamental negative congruence (Gross [15])
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). In the setting of (5.2): if y is a point of y(s) with s ≥ 1 and y₀ is the level-0 canonical lifting with y ≡ y₀ (mod π_y) (π_y a uniformiser of W_y), then y ≢ y₀ (mod π_y²). When p is split or ramified in K, y₀ occurs in T_{p^t}z. For p inert: y₀ = z if t is even and y₀ = z^{(p)} if t is odd. For p ramified with prime 𝔭: y₀ = z if t is even and z^{σ𝔭} if t is odd.
items.locator: Chapter III, §5, (5.4), p. 259; identification of y₀ on pp. 260–261

items.name: (6.1) Intersection number as a sum of isomorphism counts
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Let x and y be W-sections of X which intersect properly (no common component) and reduce to regular, non-cuspidal points of the special fibre. Then (y·x) = Σ_{n≥1} h_n(y,x)_{deg 1} = Σ_{n≥1} ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg 1}. This is a general fact, independent of y and x being Heegner points.
items.locator: Chapter III, §6, (6.1) Proposition, p. 259 (proof pp. 259–260, including (6.2))
items.note: Proof: if Aut_{W/π}(x) = ⟨±1⟩, the completed local ring of X at x is the universal deformation space of (φ: E → E′). Otherwise pass to a rigid cover Y → X (full level M ≥ 3, M prime to Np), use (6.2) (ỹ·x̃) = Σ_n #Isom_{W/π^n}(ỹ, x̃) and the projection formula (y·x) = (ỹ·f*x). items.name: Local ring of X at a non-cuspidal point is the universal deformation space (quoted)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). If x̄ is a non-cuspidal point of the special fibre with Aut_{W/π}(x) = ⟨±1⟩ (and p ∤ N, or x̄ regular), the completion of the local ring of X ⊗ W at x̄ pro-represents deformations of the diagram (φ: E → E′). Hence (y·x) = k exactly when y ≅ x over W/π^k but not over W/π^{k+1}. In general the strict henselisation of X at x̄ is the quotient of that of the stack 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} by Aut(x̄)/⟨±1⟩ (§1, [7]). One may instead pull back to a modular cover Y (full level M ≥ 3, (M,Np) = 1), where the objects are rigid.
items.note: 7D (quoted in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/143) plans the universal deformation and its 'comparison with the completed local ring of a representing moduli scheme'. 9D plans coarse moduli M(𝒫) = 𝕄(𝒫,δ)/G via a finite étale rigidifier, as used for Y → X. 7F ST-4 plans pro-representability with level structure for [Γ(p^n)], [Γ₁(p^n)] only. For p ∤ N the Γ₀(N)-structure deforms uniquely, so 7D suffices there. The p | N case (Katz–Mazur [Γ₀(p^n)]) is not planned at the deformation-ring level. Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Deuring lifting for ordinary CM reduction (quoted, Deuring [8])
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). If p splits in K, then x and x^σ have ordinary reduction and reduction induces isomorphisms Hom_W(x^σ,x) ≅ Hom_{W/π^n}(x^σ,x) for all n ≥ 1. In particular Aut_{W/π^n}(x) = Aut_W(x). Two canonical liftings with the same reduction mod π coincide.
items.locator: Chapter III, §6, split case of the proof of (4.4), p. 260; also (7.1) proof, p. 261
items.note: GZ.7 plans the ordinary-reduction deformation-length calculations 'using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory' (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/138). ModularCurves 7F plans ST-1 (Serre–Tate equivalence) and 'the compatibility of ST-1 with connected–étale sequences and with the ordinary/supersingular dichotomy'. A4 plans 'the Serre–Tate equivalence for deformations of abelian schemes with endomorphism and polarization structures'. No stage names Serre–Tate canonical lifts or Deuring's lifting theorem, so the plan is for the inputs only. Tau Ceti/Mathlib have no ordinary/supersingular predicate (rg IsSupersingular|IsOrdinary: 0 hits). EllipticCurves layer 3 plans IsSupersingular/IsOrdinary over fields.

items.name: Proof of (4.4) at ramified p | m: intersection of x with T_{p^t}z
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III) as in /139. Assume r_𝒜(m) = 0, p ramified in K with prime 𝔭, m = p^t·r with t ≥ 1 and (r, p) = 1, and z ∈ T_r x^σ. Each component y(s) (0 ≤ s ≤ t) of T_{p^t}z is congruent mod π_y to z if t is even and to z^{σ_𝔭} if t is odd, and (T_{p^t}z · x) = Σ_{n≥1} h_n(z, x)_{deg 1} + t·h_1(z, x)_{deg 1} (t even), Σ_{n≥1} h_n(z^{σ_𝔭}, x)_{deg 1} + t·h_1(z^{σ_𝔭}, x)_{deg 1} (t odd; printed 't h(z^{σ𝔭}, x)_{deg 1}', PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E15). Summing over z ∈ T_r x^σ with (5.1): (x · T_m x^σ) = Σ_n h_n(x^σ, x)_{deg r} + t·h_1(x^σ, x)_{deg r} (t even), Σ_n h_n(x^{σσ_𝔭}, x)_{deg r} + t·h_1(x^{σσ_𝔭}, x)_{deg r} (t odd); and f ↦ 𝔭^t f (degree-r isogenies over W/πⁿ to degree-m isogenies x^σ → x over W/π^{n+t}) identifies this with Σ_{n≥1} h_n(x^σ, x)_{deg m}, which is (4.4) at ramified p.
items.locator: Chapter III, §6, proof of Proposition (4.4), ramified case, p. 261
items.note: Here the uniformiser ϖ of O_𝔭 is a uniformiser of B_p, and Gross's End_{W/πⁿ} = O_𝔭 + ϖ^{n−1}R_p gives the level shift by t. Conrad §6 re-proves it. Planned at method level only (GZ.7). Library: none. Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: Proof of (4.4) at inert p | m: intersection of x with T_{p^t}z
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III) as in /139. Assume r_𝒜(m) = 0, p inert in K, m = p^t·r with t ≥ 1 and (r, p) = 1, and let z ∈ T_r x^σ. The components y(s) of T_{p^t}z (s ≡ t mod 2, (5.2)) are all congruent to one level-zero point y₀, with y₀ = z if t is even and y₀ = z^{(p)} if t is odd, and by (5.4): (T_{p^t}z · x) = Σ_{n≥1} h_n(z, x)_{deg 1} + (t/2)·h_1(z, x)_{deg 1} if t is even, and ((t+1)/2)·h_1(z, x)_{deg p} if t is odd. Summing over z ∈ T_r x^σ (printed 'z ∈ T_r x', PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E26) and using (5.1): (x · T_m x^σ) = Σ_{n≥1} h_n(x^σ, x)_{deg r} + (t/2)·h_1(x^σ, x)_{deg r} (t even), ((t+1)/2)·h_1(x^σ, x)_{deg pr} (t odd). Since f ↦ p^{t/2}f takes degree-r isogenies over W/πⁿ to degree-m isogenies over W/π^{n+t/2} (and f ↦ p^{(t−1)/2}f takes degree-pr isogenies over W/π to degree-m ones over W/π^{(t+1)/2}), this equals Σ_{n≥1} h_n(x^σ, x)_{deg m}, which is (4.4) at inert p.
items.locator: Chapter III, §6, proof of Proposition (4.4), inert case, pp. 260–261
items.note: Checked the bijections behind the last step with Gross's End_{W/πⁿ} = O_p + p^{n−1}R_p (π = p here): an element of R_p whose reduced norm has even valuation t is p^{t/2} times a unit, and one with odd valuation t is p^{(t−1)/2}·Π·(unit), Π a uniformiser of B_p; an element of norm valuation 1 never lies in O_p + pR_p = End_{W/π²}, so the counts match level by level. Conrad re-proves this in §6 ((6.5)–(6.6), Theorems 6.1–6.2). Planned at method level only, like /139 (GZ.7 deformation-length calculations); no stage names the X₀(N) statement. Library: none. Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: (7.1) Vanishing at split primes when r_𝒜(m) = 0
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). If p splits in K and r_𝒜(m) = 0, then (x·T_m x^σ) = 0 at every place v | p (v ∤ N or v | N alike). Proof: Hom_{W/π^n}(x^σ,x) = Hom_W(x^σ,x) for all n ≥ 1, and this group has no element of degree m since r_𝒜(m) = 0.
items.note: GZ.7: 'Separate split, inert and ramified extensions, ordinary, supersingular ...' (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/138 for the full quote and caveat). Conrad Lemma 10.3 generalises it (p ∤ mN, no condition on r_𝒜(m)).

items.name: Deuring: structure of R = End_{W/π}(x) at a non-split prime (quoted)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Assume p has a unique prime factor 𝔭 in K (p inert or ramified; then p ∤ N). Then x and x^σ have supersingular reduction mod π. R = End_{W/π}(x) is an order in the definite quaternion algebra B over ℚ ramified exactly at ∞ and p. The reduced discriminant of R is Np. R ⊗ ℤ_p is the maximal order of B ⊗ ℚ_p. For every l ≠ p, R ⊗ ℤ_l is conjugate to the Eichler order {(a b; c d) ∈ M₂(ℤ_l): c ≡ 0 (mod N)} in B ⊗ ℚ_l ≅ M₂(ℚ_l).
items.note: Searched the atlas (regex over all stage descriptions) for 'Deuring', 'Eichler order', 'maximal order' near 'quaternion', 'endomorphism ring ... quaternion', 'B_{p,∞}': no stage plans the quaternionic structure of supersingular endomorphism rings. 'Deuring' occurs only in EllipticRegulators ER.5 (Deuring's L-function comparison) and AlgebraicCurves layer 8. Nearest: EllipticCurves layer 3 (IsSupersingular/IsOrdinary over fields; ordinary End is an order in ℚ(π)), GZ.7 ('supersingular and superspecial reduction'), HE.1 ('construct optimal embeddings of the specified orders' for quaternionic curves). Libraries: Mathlib has QuaternionAlgebra; Tau Ceti has Algebra/Quaternion/* and CentralSimple/* (norm forms, splitting, Skolem–Noether for central subalgebras) but no orders, Eichler orders or elliptic-curve endomorphism rings (rg 'Eichler|maximalOrder|QuaternionOrder' in both trees: 0 hits). Routed (source) to ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.5.

items.name: (7.2) Decomposition B = K + Kj and additivity of the reduced norm
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). With p non-split and R, B as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/147: the reduction map O = End_W(x) → R = End_{W/π}(x) extends to a ℚ-linear embedding K → B. This gives B = B₊ ⊕ B₋ = K ⊕ Kj, where j lies in the non-trivial coset of N_{B^×}(K^×)/K^× (so jα = ᾱj for α ∈ K). Writing b = b₊ + b₋, the reduced norm satisfies N(b) = N(b₊) + N(b₋).
items.note: Partial library coverage, for the explicit symbol algebra only: Tau Ceti QuaternionAlgebra.normForm_apply_coordinates (TauCeti/Algebra/Quaternion/NormForm.lean:82) states normForm c₁ c₂ c₃ x = x.re² + c₂·x.re·x.imI − c₁·x.imI² − c₃·x.imJ² − c₂c₃·x.imJ·x.imK + c₁c₃·x.imK². With c₂ = 0 this is N(α+βj) = N_K(α) − c₃N_K(β) for α = re + imI·i, β = imJ + imK·i. So it covers the norm identity once B is presented as ℍ[ℚ, D, 0, c₃] (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/165), not the abstract decomposition for an arbitrary embedding K ↪ B. Tau Ceti's TauCeti.skolemNoether (CentralSimple/SkolemNoether.lean:107) needs the source algebra central simple, so it does not give j for a quadratic subfield K. QuadraticFormInvariants layer 2 plans the norm form of ℍ[K,a,b] ('prove Nrd ≅ ⟨1, −a, −b, ab⟩'), not the decomposition relative to a given subfield. No stage plans the decomposition. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7. Also: Tau Ceti proves the real analogue only — TauCeti.Quaternion.ofComplex_conjAe (TauCeti/Algebra/Quaternion/ComplexSubfield.lean:202: complex conjugation on ℂ ⊆ ℍ[ℝ] is conjugation by j, a hand-proved instance of noncentral Skolem–Noether) — not the statement for a quadratic field K ⊂ B over ℚ.

items.name: Endomorphisms of the canonical formal group mod π^n (quoted, Gross [15])
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). p non-split with prime 𝔭 | p in K. Let x̂ = (φ̂: Ê → Ê′) be the diagram of p-divisible groups of x over W. Ê and Ê′ are formal groups of dimension 1 and height 2, φ̂ is an isomorphism (p ∤ N), and End_{W/π^n}(x̂) = End_{W/π^n}(Ê). End_{W/π}(x̂) = R_p = R ⊗ ℤ_p is the maximal order of B_p = B ⊗ ℚ_p, and for n ≥ 1: End_{W/π^n}(x̂) = {b ∈ R_p : D·N(b₋) ≡ 0 mod p·(N𝔭)^{n−1}}.
items.note: Checked against Gross's End_{W/π^n}(F) = O_p + π^{n−1}·End(F₀). Inert: R_p = O_p ⊕ O_pΠ, and βΠ ∈ p^{n−1}R_p ⟺ ord_p N(b₋) ≥ 2n−1 = ord_p(p·(p²)^{n−1}). Ramified: β ∈ 𝔭^{n−1} ⟺ ord_p(D·N b₋) ≥ n. GZ.7 (Local arithmetic identities and boundary contributions): 'Prove the finite-place identities between CM intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local representation densities/Whittaker functions. Separate split, inert and ramified extensions, ordinary, supersingular and superspecial reduction, horizontal intersections and vertical corrections. Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models. ... Handle self-intersection terms ... Assemble local formulas into the global kernel comparison of GZ.6, including local terms supported at conductor and discriminant primes.' The roadmap's primary source contracts include 'Gross–Zagier, Chapters II–IV' and 'Conrad, Gross–Zagier revisited, §§2–10' (README l.127), and Conrad §§4–10 re-prove exactly this chapter. The stage text is written in YZZ's generality (Shimura curves). No stage names the X₀(N)-specific statement, and GZ.8's 'Specialize to X₀(N)' specialises the global formula, not these local identities. This is a method-level plan. GZ.7 plans supersingular deformation-length calculations; Gross's theorem is not named in any stage. Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Serre–Tate: End_{W/π^n}(x) = End_{W/π}(x) ∩ End_{W/π^n}(x̂) (quoted [31, 40])
items.statement: For a Γ₀(N)-diagram x over W with p ∤ N and n ≥ 1, an endomorphism of x mod π lifts to W/π^n exactly when its action on the p-divisible group diagram x̂ lifts: End_{W/π^n}(x) = End_{W/π}(x) ∩ End_{W/π^n}(x̂) inside End_{W/π}(x̂).
items.note: A4: 'Prove the Serre–Tate equivalence for deformations of abelian schemes with endomorphism and polarization structures; identify its tangent map with the Hodge filtration.' ModularCurves 7F ST-1: 'For R artinian local ... the functor E/R ↦ E[p^∞] is an equivalence from the groupoid of deformations of E₀ over R to the groupoid of deformations of E₀[p^∞] over R'. 7F is stated for groupoids (isomorphisms). The Hom/End-lifting form needed here is the full Serre–Tate theorem of A4. rg 'serre.?tate' in Mathlib and Tau Ceti: 0 hits.

items.name: (7.3)(1) End_{W/π^n}(x) as a quaternionic congruence order
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Assume p has a unique prime factor 𝔭 in K, and let R = End_{W/π}(x) ⊂ B = K + Kj as in (7.2). Then for all n ≥ 1: End_{W/π^n}(x) = {b ∈ R : D·N(b₋) ≡ 0 mod p·(N𝔭)^{n−1}}.

items.name: (7.3)(2) Hom_{W/π^n}(x^σ,x) ≅ End_{W/π^n}(x)·𝔞 and the degree formula
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Assume p non-split. For any ideal 𝔞 in the class 𝒜 there is an isomorphism Hom_{W/π^n}(x^σ,x) ≅ End_{W/π^n}(x)·𝔞 ⊂ B, compatible in n. items.name: (7.4)(1) Inert primes: (x·T_m x^σ) as a sum over R𝔞
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). items.note: Printed '(x, T_m x^σ)' with a comma instead of the usual '·'. Harmless, and not recorded as an issue. Proof: (4.4) plus (7.3) give ½Σ_n #{b ∈ R𝔞 : Nb = mN𝔞, D·Nb₋ ≡ 0 mod p(N𝔭)^{n−1}}. Separate split, inert and ramified extensions, ordinary, supersingular and superspecial reduction, horizontal intersections and vertical corrections. Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models. ... Handle self-intersection terms ... Assemble local formulas into the global kernel comparison of GZ.6, including local terms supported at conductor and discriminant primes.'
