items.name: (8.1) Self-intersection via the tangent vector ∂/∂t
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Suppose r_𝒜(m) ≠ 0, so c and T_m d^σ share the point x and ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v is defined by Ch. II (5.1)/(5.3) using the tangent vector ∂/∂t at x. Here ∂/∂t is dual to ω = η⁴(q)dq/q when u = 1, is defined in general through the normalisation of the uniformiser g in Ch. II §5, read as ω = (1/u)(g^{1/u} + …)dg/g (printed without the factor 1/u; PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E12), and is defined up to a 6th root of unity. Define (x·x) := ord_v(α), where α ∈ H_v^× is given (corrected reading) by ∂/∂t = α·(a basis of the free W-module T_x X). Printed: 'where α∂/∂t is a basis'; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E16. With this convention the intersection formula (0.2), ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_v = −(x·T_m x^σ) log q_v, continues to hold.

items.name: (8.2) Lemma: ord_v(α) counts new automorphisms
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Let x be any W-section of X reducing to a non-cuspidal point of the special fibre (not necessarily a Heegner point), and let v ∤ N. With α as in (8.1): ord_v(α) = ½ Σ_{n≥1} (#Aut_{W/π^n}(x) − #Aut_W(x)) = ½ Σ_{n≥1} #Aut^{new}_{W/π^n}(x). In particular ∂/∂t generates T_x X if and only if Aut_{W/π^n}(x) = Aut_W(x).
items.note: Proof sketch: ω = η⁴dq/q is a Néron differential on the degree-6 cyclic cover Y′ of Y = X₀(1) (the commutator subgroup of PSL₂(ℤ)). X′ = X ×_Y Y′ → X is analysed by ramification over the section, exactly as in (6.1). The sketch is valid for v ∤ 6N; the case v | 6 is omitted (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E25). Correct only with the corrected (8.1) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E16). Conrad Theorem 9.2 with (9.9) and Definition 9.5 proves ord = ½Σ(#Aut_{W_n} − #Aut_W) at non-elliptic points for v ∤ N, all residue characteristics. Plans as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/155.

items.name: (8.3) Explicit α on X₀(1)
items.statement: Let N = 1, so X = Y = X₀(1) and X′ = Y′. For a point x as in (8.2), modulo μ₆ (printed 'mod μ₀', PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E17): α ≡ j(x)^{2/3}(j(x) − 1728)^{1/2} if j(x) ≠ 0, 1728; α ≡ 2⁶·3⁴ if j(x) = 1728; α ≡ 2⁹·3^{3/2} if j(x) = 0.
items.note: Exponents read on the 600-dpi scan (gz-wstein.pdf) and re-read by the review on an enlarged crop of the GDZ 1400 px page image of p. 263: j(x)^{2/3}(j(x) − 1728)^{1/2}, 2⁶·3⁴, 2⁹·3^{3/2}, 'mod μ₀'. Verified: from j = E₄³/Δ and q dj/dq = −E₆E₄²/Δ, ω = η⁴dq/q = −j^{−2/3}(j−1728)^{−1/2} dj. So ∂/∂t = −j^{2/3}(j−1728)^{1/2}∂/∂j, i.e. α = j^{2/3}(j−1728)^{1/2} under the corrected (8.1). At j = 1728 (u = 2) and j = 0 (u = 3) the corrected normalisation ω = (1/u)(g^{1/u}+…)dg/g of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E12 gives α = 72² = (2³·3²)² and (2³·3^{1/2})³ = 1536√3 up to roots of unity, matching the printed 2⁶·3⁴ and 2⁹·3^{3/2}; the normalisation as printed in Ch. II would give 144² = 2⁸·3⁴ and 2⁹·3^{9/2}. Consistency with (8.2) checked at elliptic points in residue characteristics 2 and 3 (N = 1): for j = 1728, D = −4, v | 2 (e = 2), ord_v(2⁶·3⁴) = 12 = ½[(24 − 4) + (8 − 4)] from Aut_{W/π} of order 24, Aut_{W/π²} = Q₈, Aut_{W/πⁿ} = μ₄ (n ≥ 3) by Gross's End_{W/πⁿ} = O + ϖ^{n−1}R; for j = 0, D = −3, v | 3, ord_v(2⁹·3^{3/2}) = 3 = ½(12 − 6). Libraries: Mathlib has WeierstrassCurve.j and the Dedekind eta function but no modular j-function relation of this kind. ModularCurves 9E plans the coarse j-line M([Γ(1)]) = Spec R[j], but no stage plans this differential computation. It is used by the paper only as a check, for v | 6. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Assume v ∤ N, p = 𝔭𝔭̄ split in K, v | 𝔭. Then (x·T_m x^σ) = u·r_𝒜(m)·k_𝔭, where k_𝔭 ≥ 0 and k_𝔭 + k_𝔭̄ = ord_𝔭(m) (printed with subscript 𝔭; equal to ord_p(m) since p splits). The k_𝔭 need not be integers: by Conrad (10.8), p. 49, u·r_𝒜(m)·k_𝔭 = u·κ_𝔭 with κ_𝔭 = Σ_𝔟 ord_𝔭(𝔟) over the integral ideals 𝔟 of norm m in 𝒜^{−1}, which 'in general is not divisible by r_𝒜(m)'. Conrad's form: (x·T_m x^σ)_v = u·κ_𝔭 with κ_𝔭, κ_𝔭̄ ∈ ℤ≥0 intrinsic to 𝔭, 𝔭̄ and κ_𝔭 + κ_𝔭̄ = r_𝒜(m)·ord_p(m).
items.note: GZ give no proof beyond 'a count of these liftings, together with their levels, as in §5'. Conrad Theorem 10.5(3) proves it (pp. 47–49). GZ.7 (Local arithmetic identities and boundary contributions): 'Prove the finite-place identities between CM intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local representation densities/Whittaker functions. Separate split, inert and ramified extensions, ordinary, supersingular and superspecial reduction, horizontal intersections and vertical corrections. Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models. ... Handle self-intersection terms ... Assemble local formulas into the global kernel comparison of GZ.6, including local terms supported at conductor and discriminant primes.' The roadmap's primary source contracts include 'Gross–Zagier, Chapters II–IV' and 'Conrad, Gross–Zagier revisited, §§2–10' (README l.127), and Conrad §§4–10 re-prove exactly this chapter. The stage text is written in YZZ's generality (Shimura curves). No stage names the X₀(N)-specific statement, and GZ.8's 'Specialize to X₀(N)' specialises the global formula, not these local identities. This is a method-level plan.

items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. When v | 𝔫̄ (x on the component of 0), ∂/∂t spans N^{−u}·T_x X (printed '(N)^u T_x X'; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E18).

items.name: Auxiliary prime q and the model B = (D, −pq) = K + Kj (inert case)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). Let p be inert in K and v | p. Fix a prime q with (q/l) = (−p/l) for every prime l | D. Such q exist by Dirichlet's theorem. For §9's order S one must in fact also impose −pq ≡ 1 (mod D) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E19). Then q splits in K, (q) = 𝔮𝔮̄. The quaternion algebra B with Hilbert symbol (D, −pq) is ramified only at ∞ and p, and B = K + Kj with j² = −pq and jα = ᾱj. For b = α + βj: N(b) = N(α) + pq·N(β) and N(b₋) = pq·N(β).
items.locator: Chapter III, §9, p. 265 (paragraph after (9.2); the norm identity is the first line of (9.4))
items.note: Status 'planned' because the ramification computation is not in any library; two ingredients are. (1) Mathlib Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_zmodEq (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean, namespace Nat): '(n : ℕ) {q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hq : q ≠ 0) (h : IsCoprime a q) : ∃ p > n, p.Prime ∧ p ≡ a [ZMOD q]'. By CRT this gives the congruence conditions on q modulo the primes l | D. (2) Tau Ceti QuaternionAlgebra.normForm_apply_coordinates (TauCeti/Algebra/Quaternion/NormForm.lean:82) on ℍ[ℚ, D, 0, −pq] gives normForm = re² − D·imI² + pq·imJ² − Dpq·imK² = N_K(α) + pq·N_K(β). The Hilbert-symbol ramification computation ((D,−pq)_l = 1 at l | D, at 2 since D ≡ 1 mod 4, and at q; = −1 at p and ∞) is planned in QuadraticFormInvariants 6C ('hilbertSymbol a b : ℤˣ ... Bimultiplicativity ... the frozen hilbertSymbol_productFormula'). No Hilbert symbol exists in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (rg 'hilbert ?symbol': 0 hits). Layer 2 plans the norm form and splitting criterion. Checked: ε(q) = Π_{l|D}(q/l) = ε(−p) = ε(−1)ε(p) = (−1)(−1) = 1, so q splits.

items.name: Eichler-order model S and Eichler's connecting-ideal theorem (quoted, Eichler [10, p. 118])
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). In the setting of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/165 (with −pq ≡ 1 mod D), let S = {α + βj : α ∈ 𝔡^{−1}, β ∈ 𝔡^{−1}𝔮^{−1}𝔫, α ≡ β mod O_𝔣 for every prime 𝔣 of O dividing 𝔡}. S is an order of B with reduced discriminant Np that is locally an Eichler order at every finite l ≠ p, like R = End_{W/π}(x). Eichler: there is an ideal 𝔟 of O with R𝔟 = 𝔟S inside B. The class 𝔅 of 𝔟 depends on v: if v′ = v^{σ_𝔠} then 𝔟′ = 𝔟𝔠, so 𝔅′ = 𝔅𝒞, and Gal(H/K) permutes the classes that arise simply transitively.
items.note: Two defects: S is an order only if −pq ≡ 1 (mod D) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E19, lead Mann); and the relation R𝔟 = 𝔟S versus (9.3) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E20). Mann's appendix proves the connecting-ideal statement as Theorem A.15 / Corollary A.16 (Eichler orders with the same reduced discriminant and S ∩ E = S′ ∩ E = O_E are conjugate by an O_E-ideal). Searched the atlas for 'Eichler order', 'optimal embed', 'quaternion order', 'maximal order': no stage plans Eichler orders or this theorem. Nearest: HE.1 ('For quaternionic curves construct optimal embeddings of the specified orders'). Libraries: nothing (rg 'Eichler|QuaternionOrder|maximalOrder': 0 hits in Mathlib and Tau Ceti). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (9.4)–(9.6) Ideals 𝔠, 𝔠′ attached to b = α + βj ∈ R𝔞 (inert case)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). p inert. For b = α + βj ∈ R𝔞 with (9.4) N(b) = N(α) + pq·N(β) = m·N(𝔞) and N(b₋) = pq·N(β) ≠ 0, define, with 𝔟 normalised as in the printed (9.3), i.e. 𝔟R = S𝔟 (with R𝔟 = 𝔟S replace 𝔟 by 𝔟̄ throughout, see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E20), the integral ideals (9.5) 𝔠 = (α)𝔡𝔞^{−1} and 𝔠′ = (β)𝔡𝔮𝔫^{−1}𝔟̄^{−1}𝔟𝔞̄^{−1}. Then 𝔠 ∈ 𝒜^{−1} and 𝔠′ ∈ 𝒜𝔅²[𝔮𝔫^{−1}], and (9.6) N𝔠 + N·p·N𝔠′ = m|D|. The integer n = p·N𝔠′ is non-zero and ord_p(n) = ord_p(N b₋) (using p ∤ N𝔞). δ(n) = Π_{l | (n,D)} 2 as in Ch. II (3.15).

items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N > 1 (GZ's standing assumption; for N = 1 the cusps ∞ and 0 coincide and c, T_m d^σ always share them); K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). If p is inert in K (r_𝒜(m) arbitrary), then ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_p = −r_𝒜(m)·h·u·ord_p(m)·log p − u²·log p·Σ_{0 < n < m|D|/N, n ≡ 0 (mod p)} ord_p(pn)·r_𝒜(m|D| − nN)·δ(n)·R_{{𝒜𝔮𝔫}}(n/p). Here δ(n) = 2^{#{primes l | (n,D)}}, R_{{𝒞}}(k) is the number of integral ideals of norm k in the genus of 𝒞 (Ch. II (3.17)), and 𝔮 | q is the auxiliary prime of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/165. The value does not depend on the choice of q, of 𝔮 | q, or of 𝔫 versus 𝔫̄.
items.note: The stated formula is correct: Mann, Theorem A.17, re-proves it, also for even D. The proof has three defects: the count '2·u²·δ(n)' should be u²·δ(n) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E22); the order S needs −pq ≡ 1 mod D (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E19); and 𝔞 must be prime to pD (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E21). Plan, method-level: GZ.7 plans the finite-place intersection side of the kernel identity at inert primes. It does so by YZZ's method, not through Eichler-order ideal counts; the X₀(N)-specific explicit formula is named in no stage. GZ.7 (Local arithmetic identities and boundary contributions): 'Prove the finite-place identities between CM intersection multiplicities and derivatives of local representation densities/Whittaker functions. Separate split, inert and ramified extensions, ordinary, supersingular and superspecial reduction, horizontal intersections and vertical corrections. Build the deformation-length calculations using the existing finite-flat/Serre–Tate theory and the actual local models. ... Handle self-intersection terms ... Assemble local formulas into the global kernel comparison of GZ.6, including local terms supported at conductor and discriminant primes.' The roadmap's primary source contracts include 'Gross–Zagier, Chapters II–IV' and 'Conrad, Gross–Zagier revisited, §§2–10' (README l.127), and Conrad §§4–10 re-prove exactly this chapter. The stage text is written in YZZ's generality (Shimura curves). No stage names the X₀(N)-specific statement, and GZ.8's 'Specialize to X₀(N)' specialises the global formula, not these local identities. This is a method-level plan.

items.name: Counting lemma in the proof of (9.7): elements of ⊔_v R_v𝔞 attached to a pair (𝔠, 𝔠′)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III) with N > 1, p inert in K, the auxiliary prime q chosen with −pq ≡ 1 (mod D) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E19) and 𝔞 ∈ 𝒜 prime to pD (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E21). Let 𝔠 ∈ 𝒜^{−1} and 𝔠′ be integral ideals with 𝔠′ in the class 𝒜[𝔮𝔫^{−1}]𝔅² for some 𝔅 ∈ Cl_K, with N𝔠 + N·p·N𝔠′ = m|D| and n = p·N𝔠′ > 0. Reversing (9.5) determines α, β up to units of O; integrality of N(α) + pqN(β) = m·N𝔞 forces α ≡ ±β mod O_𝔣 for every prime 𝔣 | 𝔡, and the resulting b = α + βj lie in R_{v′}𝔞 for places v′ | p in one Gal(H/K)-orbit. Each such pair contributes exactly u²·δ(n) elements b ∈ ⊔_{v|p} R_v𝔞/±1 (printed '2·u²·δ(n)', PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E22), each of weight ½(1 + ord_p N(b₋)) = ½·ord_p(pn) in Σ_{v|p}(x·T_m x^σ)_v; summing over pairs and over 𝔅 gives the second term of (9.7).
items.locator: Chapter III, §9, proof of Proposition (9.7), p. 266
items.note: This is the step that turns the quaternionic sums of (7.4)/(8.5) into the ideal-counting formula (9.7); it carries three of the recorded defects (E19, E21, E22). Mann's appendix to Conrad proves the corrected count (proof of Theorem A.17, and Remark A.19). Not planned: no stage plans GZ's explicit Eichler-order method (see /166–/168). Library: none. Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: (9.8)–(9.10) Ramified-case model: q, B = (D, −q), R𝔞 and the ideals 𝔠, 𝔠′
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. III): N ≥ 1; K = ℚ(√D) with D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant, D ≡ □ (mod 4N), so (D,N) = 1 and every prime dividing N splits in K; O = O_K, 𝔡 = (√D) its different, h = #Cl_K, u = #O^×/2; 𝔫 ⊂ O with O/𝔫 ≅ ℤ/N; x = (φ: E → E′) a Heegner point of discriminant D on X₀(N) (E, E′ with CM by O, ker φ killed by 𝔫), defined over the Hilbert class field H; σ ∈ Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K under the Artin map; r_𝒜(m) = number of integral ideals of norm m in 𝒜; m ≥ 1 with (m,N) = 1; v a finite place of H over the prime p; A_v the integers of H_v, π a uniformiser, q_v = #A_v/π; W = completion of the maximal unramified extension of A_v (residue field F̄_p); X = the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur coarse model of X₀(N) over ℤ; x, x^σ the W-sections of X ⊗ W; T_m the Hecke correspondence; Hom_S(y,x) = homomorphisms of Γ₀(N)-diagrams (§2), with degree deg(f,f′) = deg f; h_n(y,x)_{deg m} = ½·#Hom_{W/π^n}(y,x)_{deg m}; (·) = intersection pairing on X ⊗ W; c = (x) − (∞), d = (x) − (0). p ramified in K with prime 𝔭; f = order of [𝔭] in Cl_K. There are h/f places v | 𝔭 in H, each with q_v = p^f (printed 'residual degree p^f', PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E23). Choose a prime q with (q/p′) = (−1/p′) for all primes p′ ≠ p dividing D and (−q/p) = −1; for the order model one must also impose −q ≡ 1 (mod D/p) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E19). Then q = 𝔮𝔮̄ splits in K, B has Hilbert symbol (D, −q), and B = K + Kj with j² = −q. With 𝔟 normalised by 𝔟R = S𝔟 as in the printed (9.3) (with R𝔟 = 𝔟S replace 𝔟 by 𝔟̄ throughout; PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E20): (9.8) R𝔞 = {α + βj : α ∈ 𝔭𝔡^{−1}𝔞, β ∈ 𝔭𝔡^{−1}𝔮^{−1}𝔫𝔟̄𝔟^{−1}𝔞̄, α ≡ (−1)^{ord_𝔣(𝔟)}β mod O_𝔣 for 𝔣 | 𝔡} (β missing in print, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E24). The class of 𝔟 is well defined in Cl_K/[𝔭] by v. For b = α + βj ∈ R𝔞 with N(b) = m·N(𝔞) and N(b₋) ≠ 0, (9.9) 𝔠 = (α)𝔡𝔞^{−1} ∈ 𝒜^{−1} and 𝔠′ = (β)𝔡𝔮𝔫^{−1}𝔟̄^{−1}𝔟𝔞̄^{−1} ∈ 𝒜[𝔮𝔫^{−1}]𝔅² are integral and both divisible by 𝔭, and (9.10) N𝔠 + N·N𝔠′ = m|D|. The integer n = N𝔠′ is non-zero, with ord_p(n) = ord_p(D·N(b₋)).
items.note: Status 'missing' because the explicit order and ideal construction (the substance of the item) is planned nowhere; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/166 and PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/167. Partial support: Dirichlet (Mathlib) for q; the norm identity N(α+βj) = Nα + qNβ in ℍ[ℚ, D, 0, −q] (Tau Ceti normForm_apply_coordinates); the Hilbert-symbol checks (planned, QuadraticFormInvariants 6C). Checked the Hilbert symbols: (D,−q)_{p′} = (−q/p′) = 1 for p′ ≠ p; (D,−q)_p = (−q/p) = −1; trivial at 2 since D ≡ 1 mod 4. Checked (9.10): N𝔠 + N·N𝔠′ = |D|(Nα + qNβ)/N𝔞. Mann (A.6). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7.

items.name: (9.11) Ramified primes: explicit ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_p
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. If p is ramified in K with prime 𝔭 (r_𝒜(m) arbitrary), then ⟨c, T_m d^σ⟩_p = −r_𝒜(m)·h·u·ord_p(m)·log p − u²·log p·Σ_{0 < n < m|D|/N, n ≡ 0 (mod p)} ord_p(n)·r_𝒜(m|D| − nN)·δ(n)·R_{{𝒜𝔮𝔭𝔫}}(n/p), with δ and R as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/169 and 𝔮 the auxiliary prime of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/170.
items.note: Proof 'arguing as in (9.7)'. Mann, Theorem A.20, re-proves the same formula for all D. He explains that the factor 2 which p contributes to δ(n) is compensated by the missing order-2 action at p and by the h/f versus h counting of places. Plan: method-level GZ.7, as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/169.

items.name: Genus characters of Cl_K and the factorization of their L-series
items.statement: Standing data of Chap. IV (p. 267): K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D, ε = ε_D = (D/·), Cl_K its class group. A genus character is a character χ: Cl_K → {±1}. Such characters correspond bijectively to the unordered decompositions {D₁, D₂} of D as a product D = D₁·D₂ of two fundamental discriminants, one positive and one negative (D₁ = 1 is allowed and gives the trivial character). The character χ_{D₁·D₂} is characterized by χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞) for integral ideals 𝔞 prime to D, where ε_{D_i} is the Dirichlet character of ℚ(√D_i) (ε_1 = 1). Its L-series factors: L_K(s, χ_{D₁·D₂}) = Σ_𝔞 χ(𝔞)N𝔞^{−s} = L(s, ε_{D₁})·L(s, ε_{D₂}) (for D₁ = 1 this is ζ_K(s) = ζ(s)L(s, ε)).
items.locator: Chapter IV, introduction, p. 268 (after (0.3); quoted as known)
items.note: Quoted classical fact, used to explain (0.1)–(0.2) and to specialise the main formula. Library, for the character itself: Tau Ceti defines the genus characters on the narrow class group, tauceti:TauCeti.Multiquadratic.genusCharFunNarrowClassGroupHom (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Quadratic/GenusCharacter/NarrowClassGroup.lean:134), indexed by a subset t of a prime-discriminant factorization s of D (so D₁ = ∏_{P∈t} P), with value genusCharFun t (N𝔞) = ∏_{P∈t} primeDiscriminantCharFun P (N𝔞) on integral ideals whose norm is coprime to ∏_{P∈t} P (genusCharFunNarrowClassGroupHom_mk0, same file :157; singleton form :192). For K imaginary quadratic, tauceti:NumberField.NarrowClassGroup.toClassGroupEquiv (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/NarrowClassGroup/TotallyComplex.lean:47) identifies Cl⁺(K) with Cl_K. So χ_{D₁·D₂} is in the library. (The earlier statement that it is 'deliberately not yet packaged' quotes the docstring of the preparatory file GenusCharacter/Narrow.lean; the construction is completed in GenusCharacter/NarrowClassGroup.lean.) Missing: the L-series of a class-group character and the factorization L_K(s, χ) = L(s, ε_{D₁})L(s, ε_{D₂}) (Kronecker; equivalently Ind_K^ℚ χ_{D₁·D₂} = ε_{D₁} ⊕ ε_{D₂}). No atlas stage names it. Nearest plan: AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4 ('Connect number-field ideal counting, Hecke characters and completed L-functions to the analytic class-number formula and Chebotarev. Meromorphic continuation via induction ...'), which owns L-functions of Hecke characters and induction but does not name this factorization. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6; the review recommends AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4 as the owner, beside the class number formula (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/229), which the extraction already routes there. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 4: AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4.

items.name: (0.4) Factorization of L_K(f, χ_{D₁·D₂}, s) into twisted Hecke L-series
items.statement: Standing data of Chap. IV (p. 267): K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D, ε = ε_D = (D/·), Cl_K its class group; N ≥ 1 prime to D; f ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) with Fourier coefficients a(n); L_𝒜(f,s) as in (0.1). For χ: Cl_K → ℂ^× put L_K(f,χ,s) = Σ_{𝒜∈Cl_K} χ(𝒜)L_𝒜(f,s) (0.3). If f is a Hecke eigenform, L(f,s) = ∏_p (1−α_p p^{−s})^{−1}(1−β_p p^{−s})^{−1} with α_p+β_p = a(p), α_pβ_p = p^{2k−1} (p∤N), 0 (p|N), and χ = χ_{D₁·D₂} is a genus character, then the convolution of L(f,s) with L_K(s,χ) equals L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε)^{−1}·L(f,ε_{D₁},s)·L(f,ε_{D₂},s), where L(f,ε_{D_i},s) = Σ ε_{D_i}(n)a(n)n^{−s}; hence (0.4) L_K(f, χ_{D₁·D₂}, s) = L(f,ε_{D₁},s)·L(f,ε_{D₂},s). (The printed text writes L^{(N)}(2s+2k−1, ε) here; see the source issue.)
items.note: The weight-2 definition (0.3)/(5.4) is item 'The L-function L(f, χ, s)' of Chapter I. The factorization is planned only in the special case χ = 1, weight 2, rational coefficients: RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0 ('construct the existing quadratic twist ... then the factorization L(E/K,s)=L(E,s)L(E^K,s)'). No stage plans the genus-character case or weight 2k; the Euler-factor computation behind it is the 'simple calculation' the paper leaves to the reader. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Functional equation of the twisted Hecke L-series L(f, ε_{D_i}, s)
items.statement: Standing data of Chap. IV (p. 267): K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D, ε = ε_D = (D/·), Cl_K its class group; N ≥ 1 prime to D; f ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) with Fourier coefficients a(n); L_𝒜(f,s) as in (0.1). Let f ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) be a newform with Atkin–Lehner eigenvalue w = ±1 under W_N: f(z) ↦ N^{−k}z^{−2k}f(−1/(Nz)), and let D_i be a fundamental discriminant prime to N. Then L(f, ε_{D_i}, s) = Σ ε_{D_i}(n)a(n)n^{−s} has analytic continuation and a functional equation with gamma factor (2π)^{−s}N^{s/2}|D_i|^s Γ(s) and sign (−1)^k ε_{D_i}(−N) w. Consequently, multiplying the two, L_K(f, χ_{D₁·D₂}, s) satisfies a functional equation with the gamma factor and sign of (0.2), independent of w and of the genus character; if ε(N) = 1 exactly one of the two twisted L-series has sign −1, and the main result specialises to a formula for L′(f,ε_{D₁},k)·L(f,ε_{D₂},k) (p. 269).
items.note: Tau Ceti's ModularForms roadmap plans Hecke's functional equation for the completed L-function of a newform (Layer 7: 'The completed L-function and Hecke's functional equation — in AINTLIB's proved form (Modularforms/LFunctionFEqN.lean)') and the twist f ⊗ ψ by a Dirichlet character with its modularity (Layer 9: 'the twist f ⊗ ψ of a q-expansion by a Dirichlet character ψ'), and Layer 6 pins the sign convention i^k·ε_N. The explicit root number (−1)^k ε_{D}(−N) w of a quadratic twist of conductor prime to N is not named in either layer, so the plan covers the functional equation but not the stated sign; the elliptic-curve case of the parity is RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0 ('Prove the root-number parity relation').

items.name: Moderate-growth spaces M̃_k(Γ₀(N), χ) and the weight-k slash operator
items.statement: For f: ℌ → ℂ, k ∈ ℤ and γ = (a b; c d) with ad−bc > 0, (f|_kγ)(z) = (ad−bc)^{k/2}(cz+d)^{−k} f((az+b)/(cz+d)). For N ∈ ℕ and a Dirichlet character χ mod N, M̃_k(Γ₀(N), χ) is the space of functions f: ℌ → ℂ, not necessarily holomorphic, such that f|_kγ = χ(d)f for all γ = (a b; c d) ∈ Γ₀(N), and which have at most polynomial growth at the cusps: for every γ ∈ SL₂(ℤ) there is C > 0 with (f|_kγ)(z) = O(y^C) as y → ∞. The character is omitted when it is trivial.
items.note: Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti for a space of non-holomorphic functions with a Nebentypus transformation law and moderate growth, and found none. Nearest in the libraries: mathlib:SlashInvariantForm (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/SlashInvariantForms.lean:34) has invariance under a subgroup of GL(2,ℝ) but no character and no growth condition. Mathlib's slash (SlashActions.lean:92) is σ(γ)(f(γz))·|det γ|^{k−1}·(cz+d)^{−k}; it agrees with GZ's (ad−bc)^{k/2} normalisation on SL₂ only. tauceti:modFormCharSpace is holomorphic only (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/176). Nearest plans, neither of which is this classical space: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.0 ('Define height functions … and independence of the moderate-growth condition', adelic) and QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3 (harmonic Maass forms with 'growth conditions, holomorphic/nonholomorphic Fourier parts'). The slash formula and the space are stated on p. 270, the page where this chunk starts; the chunk that covers §0 may list them too. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Holomorphic spaces M_k(Γ₀(N), χ) and S_k(Γ₀(N), χ)
items.statement: M_k(Γ₀(N), χ) and S_k(Γ₀(N), χ) are the subspaces of M̃_k(Γ₀(N), χ) consisting of holomorphic modular forms and holomorphic cusp forms. Used here with (k, N, χ) = (1, |D|, ε) for θ_𝒜, and (2k, N, trivial) for f.
items.note: TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/DiamondOperators.lean:315 defines `modFormCharSpace (k : ℤ) (χ : (ZMod N)ˣ →* ℂˣ) : Submodule ℂ (ModularForm ((Gamma1 N).map (mapGL ℝ)) k)` as the joint χ-eigenspace of the diamond operators. :279 defines `cuspFormCharSpace` in the same way. :344 `mem_modFormCharSpace_iff_nebentypus` proves that membership is equivalent to `∀ g : Γ₀(N), f ∣[k] g = χ((Gamma0Map N).toHomUnits g) • f`, the classical Nebentypus law. Mathlib's `ModularForm`/`CuspForm` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Basic.lean:74, 82) with `CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0` (CongruenceSubgroups.lean:79) cover the trivial-character case. This is the same notion; Tau Ceti puts the character on Γ₁(N)-forms rather than defining a separate type.

items.name: Theta series θ_𝒜 of an ideal class (1.1)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. θ_𝒜(z) = Σ_{n≥0} r_𝒜(n) qⁿ = (1/w) Σ_{λ∈𝔞} q^{N(λ)/A}, where 𝔞 is any ideal in the class 𝒜 and A = N(𝔞).
items.note: Same object as PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/19 (the construction θ_𝒜 of Chapter I (5.2), whose locator already includes Chapter IV (1.1)), which the extraction records as missing; the two must have the same status and the same route. The second expression uses r_{𝒜^{−1}} = r_𝒜: λ ↦ (λ)𝔞^{−1} maps 𝔞 ∖ {0} w-to-1 onto the integral ideals of the class 𝒜^{−1} with norm N(λ)/A, and complex conjugation matches these with the ideals of 𝒜 (new missing item after PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/194). No theta series of a lattice or quadratic form in Mathlib or Tau Ceti; searched 'theta series', 'thetaSeries' and `def .*[tT]heta`. Mathlib has only the one-variable Jacobi theta functions (JacobiTheta/OneVariable.lean, TwoVariable.lean). GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.3's stage text mentions 'theta-series interfaces', but the GN packet (research/blueprint/packets/GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic.json, coverage and gaps for GN.3) and the GN README (readmes/GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic.md:2100) record 'MetaplecticAutomorphicForms owns theta', so GN.3 does not plan it. The general (adelic) setting is MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.5 ('For a rational quadratic/symplectic datum define the theta series by summing the transformed Schwartz function over rational vectors'); the classical binary theta series of an ideal class is not named there, and MP.0's README leaves classical rank-one theta to QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.1, which does not cover rank two.

items.name: θ_𝒜 is a weight-one modular form of level |D| with character ε (quoted)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. θ_𝒜 ∈ M₁(Γ₀(|D|), ε), i.e. θ_𝒜 is holomorphic on ℌ and at the cusps, and θ_𝒜((az+b)/(cz+d)) = ε(d)(cz+d)θ_𝒜(z) for all (a b; c d) ∈ Γ₀(|D|). The paper cites this as known ('It is known that θ_𝒜 belongs to M₁(Γ₀(D), ε)'); Lemma (2.3) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/194) re-proves the transformation under all of SL₂(ℤ) when D is odd.
items.note: Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti for modularity of theta series of binary quadratic forms or ideal classes, and for weight-one forms with quadratic character, and found none. The nearest library results are mathlib:jacobiTheta_S_smul (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/JacobiTheta/OneVariable.lean:43) and jacobiTheta₂_functional_equation (TwoVariable.lean:465), which cover one-variable theta only. Nearest plan: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.5 ('Prove … transformation under rational points, moderate growth and the specified central character using Poisson summation'). That is the adelic theta kernel; the comparison with the classical level-|D| weight-1 form with Nebentypus ε is not planned (MP.7 compares with classical forms only for half-integral weight). Classical source: Hecke; Schoeneberg, Elliptic modular functions, Ch. IX. Routed (source) to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.3. Review: GN.3 is not the owner recorded in the atlas. The GN packet and README (readmes/GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic.md:2100) state 'MetaplecticAutomorphicForms owns theta', so route 3 into GN.3 conflicts with GN's own ownership record. The better owner is MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.5, the general theta layer (transformation under rational points, moderate growth and central character via Poisson summation); the classical comparison for this weight-one, level-|D| case is what the source route would add. Checked numerically together with Lemma (2.3) (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/194).

items.name: Non-holomorphic Eisenstein series E_s = E_{M,ε,2k−1,s} of level M = N|D|
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. With M = N|D|: E_s(z) = E_{M,ε,2k−1,s}(z) = L^{(N)}(2s+2k−1, ε) Σ_{±(∗ ∗; c d) ∈ Γ_∞\Γ₀(M)} ε(d)(cz+d)^{−(2k−1)} y^s |cz+d|^{−2s} = ½ Σ_{c,d∈ℤ, c≡0 (mod M), (d,M)=1} ε(d)(cz+d)^{−(2k−1)} y^s |cz+d|^{−2s}, for Re(s) large. Here L^{(N)}(s, ε) = Σ_{(n,N)=1} ε(n)n^{−s} and Γ_∞ = {±(1 n; 0 1)}. E_s ∈ M̃_{2k−1}(Γ₀(M), ε). (The two expressions agree: pull out g = gcd(c,d), which is prime to M, and pair ±(c,d) using ε(−1)(−1)^{2k−1} = 1.)
items.note: Mathlib's `eisensteinSeries` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/EisensteinSeries/Defs.lean:205) is holomorphic, of level Γ(N), indexed by a congruence class a, with no y^s factor and no Dirichlet character, so it is not this series. Nothing in Tau Ceti: searched 'Eisenstein', 'eisensteinSeries', 'nonHolomorphic', 'realAnalytic'. The nearest plan is the packet node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series (stage EllipticRegulators:ER.7): 'E_x(z, s) = Σ′ y^s / |mz + n|^{2s} … (m, n) ≡ (u, v) mod N'. That is weight 0 with no odd character, a different series. AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.1–AS.2 plan adelic Eisenstein series and their continuation, not this classical one. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Review: the atlas now has an accepted owner for classical non-holomorphic Eisenstein series. PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16/57 (the weight-0, level-one series E(z,s) = Σ_{Γ∞\PSL₂(ℤ)} Im(γz)^s, with convergence and ΔE = s(1−s)E) is routed as a source of AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0/AS.1/AS.2/AS.4, and that route is accepted in PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16.review.json. AS.1 ('Prove absolute convergence of the Eisenstein sum ... automorphy') and AS.2 ('Prove meromorphic continuation of operators and Eisenstein series, the functional equations') are the general setting of this series (GL₂, Borel, character datum ε, archimedean weight 2k−1). The review recommends routing the definition, convergence, automorphy and continuation of this series to AS.1–AS.2 beside the DIT series, so that the atlas has one owner for classical non-holomorphic Eisenstein series; GZ.6 keeps the GZ-specific uses. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Petersson scalar product on Γ₀(M)
items.statement: For f ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(M)) and g ∈ M̃_{2k}(Γ₀(M)): (f, g)_{Γ₀(M)} = ∬_𝓕 f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dxdy/y², where 𝓕 is a fundamental domain for Γ₀(M). The integral is unnormalised: no division by the volume.
items.note: TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Petersson/Basic.lean:107: `def peterssonInner (k : ℤ) (D : Set ℍ) (f g : ℍ → ℂ) : ℂ := ∫ τ in D, petersson k f g τ`. Its integrand is Mathlib's `UpperHalfPlane.petersson k f f' τ = conj (f τ) * f' τ * τ.im ^ k` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Petersson.lean:31). Convention: Tau Ceti is conjugate-linear in the first argument, so GZ's (f, g)_{Γ₀(M)} = peterssonInner (2k) 𝓕 g f with 𝓕 a Γ₀(M)-fundamental domain. :163 `peterssonInner_eq_of_isFundamentalDomain` proves independence of the domain for any slash-invariant F, F′, so holomorphy is not required. That covers the (cusp form, non-holomorphic form) pairing used here, but integrability of such a pairing is not proved in the library. The bundled `CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets` (Petersson/FiniteIndex.lean:94) is for two cusp forms only. ModularForms Layer 3 (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-3-the-petersson-inner-product-adjoints-oldforms-and-newforms) is the owner.

items.name: Rankin unfolding: L_𝒜(f, s+2k−1) as a Petersson product with θ_𝒜 E_s̄ on Γ₀(M)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. Let f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) (any cusp form) and M = N|D|. For Re(s) large, Γ(s+2k−1)(4π)^{−s−2k+1} L_𝒜(f, s+2k−1) = ∬_𝓕 f(z) \overline{θ_𝒜(z) E_s̄(z)} y^{2k} dxdy/y² = (f, θ_𝒜 E_s̄)_{Γ₀(M)}, with E_s as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/179 and 𝓕 a fundamental domain for Γ₀(M). Proof as printed: Γ(s+2k−1)(4π)^{−s−2k+1} Σ a(n)r_𝒜(n)n^{−s−2k+1} = ∬_{Γ_∞\ℌ} f \overline{θ_𝒜} y^{s+2k} dxdy/y². Then write Γ_∞\ℌ = ∪_{γ ∈ Γ_∞\Γ₀(M)} γ𝓕, use the transformation laws of f and θ_𝒜 under Γ₀(M), and interchange sum and integral.
items.note: No Rankin–Selberg unfolding for classical modular forms in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. Searched 'Rankin'; the only Tau Ceti hit is an unrelated ideal count in EffectiveBounds/IdealCount. Nearest plans: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.3 ('Prove unramified calculations and the global unfolding for cuspidal data') is adelic GL_n×GL_m with cuspidal data, whereas θ_𝒜 is not cuspidal and the Eisenstein kernel is not planned. The packet node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/rankin-selberg-integral unfolds a weight-2 form against a weight-0 real-analytic Eisenstein series: 'Unfold to ∫_{Γ∞\H} and use the constant term'. GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 plans the adelic YZZ analytic kernel ('Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels'), not this classical identity. The paper writes E_s̄ (the conjugate parameter), so the identity is holomorphic in s on both sides. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Trace map Tr^M_N
items.statement: For N | M: Tr^M_N: M̃_{2k}(Γ₀(M)) → M̃_{2k}(Γ₀(N)), g ↦ Σ_{γ ∈ Γ₀(M)\Γ₀(N)} g|_{2k}γ.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/NormTrace.lean:55: `protected def SlashInvariantForm.trace [𝒢.IsFiniteRelIndex ℋ] : SlashInvariantForm ℋ k`. It is `∑ q : ℋ ⧸ 𝒢.subgroupOf ℋ, quotientFunc f q`, with `quotientFunc f ⟦h⟧ = f ∣[k] h⁻¹` (:43), i.e. the sum over the right cosets (𝒢 ⊓ ℋ)\ℋ of f|γ. It is defined for any 𝒢-slash-invariant function, holomorphic or not, which is what GZ need here with 𝒢 = Γ₀(M), ℋ = Γ₀(N). `ModularForm.trace` (:82) is the holomorphic version. Same construction. The library does not prove that the trace preserves the moderate-growth condition of M̃, because M̃ itself is missing (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/175).

items.name: Trace adjointness for the Petersson product
items.statement: For N | M, f ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) and g ∈ M̃_{2k}(Γ₀(M)): (f, g)_{Γ₀(M)} = (f, Tr^M_N g)_{Γ₀(N)}. Consequently (4π)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)L_𝒜(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Tr^M_N(θ_𝒜 E_s̄))_{Γ₀(N)} for Re(s) large, with M = N|D|.
items.note: The Petersson integral exists (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/180) and so does the trace (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/182), but no lemma relates them: searched 'trace' in TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Petersson/*.lean and Norm/Trace.lean, with no hit. The proof is the fundamental-domain decomposition 𝓕_M = ∪_{γ ∈ Γ₀(M)\Γ₀(N)} γ𝓕_N together with the invariance of the integrand, which is TauCeti `UpperHalfPlane.petersson_smul_of_mem` (Petersson/Basic.lean). tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-3-the-petersson-inner-product-adjoints-oldforms-and-newforms plans the Petersson product and Hecke adjoints, not trace adjointness. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Möbius decomposition of E_s and discarding the lower-level terms
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. With M = N|D| and E^{(1)}_s as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/185: E_s(z) = ½ Σ_{e|N} μ(e) Σ_{c,d∈ℤ, M|c, e|d} ε(d)(cz+d)^{−(2k−1)} y^s|cz+d|^{−2s} = Σ_{e|N} μ(e)ε(e) e^{−(2s+2k−1)} (N/e)^{−s} E^{(1)}_s(Nz/e). Only e squarefree and prime to D contribute. For e > 1 the term Tr^M_N(θ_𝒜(z)E^{(1)}_s(Nz/e)) has level N/e < N: any system of representatives of Γ₀(M)\Γ₀(N) is one of Γ₀(M/e)\Γ₀(N/e), because (e, D) = 1. Hence, for f ∈ S^new_{2k}(Γ₀(N)), those terms are orthogonal to f. For non-holomorphic terms this uses §5: the product of f with a non-holomorphic form equals its product with a holomorphic form of the same level.
items.note: Checked the substitution c = N c″, d = e d″ (the paper's 'replacing c, d by c/N, d/e'). The coset claim follows because Γ₀(N) ∩ Γ₀(M/e) = Γ₀(lcm(N, N|D|/e)) = Γ₀(M) and both indices equal ψ(|D|). The coset claim has no library support; the index is known in Tau Ceti only for prime powers (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0_prime_index, Gamma0_prime_power_index in TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups/Basic.lean). Orthogonality of S^new to level-raised forms is the definition tauceti:TauCeti.cuspFormsNew (Newforms/Basic.lean:200, the Petersson-orthogonal complement of cuspFormsOld), but only for holomorphic cusp forms. The non-holomorphic case needs holomorphic projection (§5, not in this chunk; GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 plans 'holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection' adelically). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: The Rankin kernel Φ̃_s = Φ̃_{s,𝒜}
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. items.name: Proposition (1.2): L_𝒜(f, s) as the Petersson product of f with the Rankin kernel
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}.
