items.name: Remark after (1.2): only the Fourier coefficients of Φ̃_s with index prime to N matter
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. Write Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{m∈ℤ} A_m(s, y)e(mx) (1.3). The proof of (1.2) used only the orthogonality of f with forms of level strictly dividing N. f ∈ S^new_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) is also orthogonal to g(dz) for d > 1 and g of level dividing N/d, so in (1.2) only the A_m(s, y) with (m, N) = 1 are relevant. If Φ̃, Φ̃′ ∈ M̃_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) (with the growth of §5) have A_m = A′_m for all m prime to N, then (f, Φ̃) = (f, Φ̃′). In particular, the functional equation (0.2) and the formulas for L_𝒜(f, k) and L′_𝒜(f, k) reduce to identities for A_m(s, y), (m, N) = 1.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §1, Remark after (1.2) and (1.3), p. 272
items.note: The holomorphic core is in the library (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/189): a holomorphic form whose coefficients vanish at all indices prime to N is old. Applying it to Φ̃ − Φ̃′ needs holomorphic projection (§5), which is missing: no Sturm holomorphic projection in the libraries, while GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 plans it adelically. The paper asserts the remark without proof; it follows from Atkin–Lehner theory plus §5, so it is not recorded as a gap. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Atkin–Lehner Main Lemma (used implicitly in the Remark after (1.2))
items.statement: Let N ≥ 1, k ∈ ℤ, χ a character of (ℤ/N)ˣ. If g ∈ S_k(Γ₁(N), χ) has Fourier coefficients a_n(g) = 0 for every n prime to N, then g lies in the old subspace; hence g is Petersson-orthogonal to S_k^new(Γ₁(N)). GZ use it with χ trivial: S^new_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) is orthogonal to the forms g(dz), d > 1, with g of level dividing N/d.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §1, Remark after (1.2), p. 272 (not stated explicitly; Atkin–Lehner, Math. Ann. 185 (1970), Lemma 6)
items.note: TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/MainLemma.lean:178: `theorem mem_cuspFormsOld_of_forall_coprime_qExpansion_coeff_eq_zero {χ : (ZMod N)ˣ →* ℂˣ} {f : CuspForm ((Gamma1 N).map (mapGL ℝ)) k} (hf : f ∈ cuspFormCharSpace k χ) (hvan : ∀ n, Nat.Coprime n N → (qExpansion 1 f).coeff n = 0) : f ∈ cuspFormsOld N k` (Miyake Lemma 4.6.8). `cuspFormsNew N k` (Newforms/Basic.lean:200) is the Petersson-orthogonal complement of `cuspFormsOld N k` (:103, spanned by the level raises V_d from proper divisor levels). Same statement for holomorphic cusp forms. The GZ remark applies it to the holomorphic projection of a non-holomorphic form, which is not covered (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/188).

items.name: Cusps of Γ₀(D) correspond to the positive divisors of D
items.statement: In general a cusp of Γ₀(n) is specified by a divisor n′ of n and an element of (ℤ/(n′, n/n′)ℤ)ˣ. If 16 ∤ n and p² ∤ n for every odd prime p (e.g. n = |D|, D a fundamental discriminant), the cusps of Γ₀(n) are in bijection with the positive divisors of n. In §2 a cusp is labelled by δ₁ | δ, with δ₂ = δ/δ₁ = (c, D) for a matrix (a b; c d) sending ∞ to it.
items.note: Planned in the general setting by tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#10a--the-analytic-modular-curve: 'For congruence subgroups, prove cofiniteness, identify its cusp-orbit subtype with Γ\ℙ¹(ℚ), and compute the cusp count ε∞'. For Γ₀(n) that computation is exactly this parametrization (ε∞(Γ₀(n)) = Σ_{n′|n} φ((n′, n/n′))), and the extraction already records the Γ₀(N) cusp count as planned there (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/55, /261). Partial: the explicit labelling by (n′, unit mod (n′, n/n′)) and the corollary for n = |D| are not named. Libraries: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps.lean defines cusps of a subgroup of GL(2,ℝ) but does not classify those of Γ₀(n); TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps/Basic.lean has cusp widths only (TauCeti.Subgroup.integerCuspWidth). Checked: φ((d, n/d)) = 1 for every d | n exactly when (d, n/d) ∈ {1, 2} for all d, i.e. 16 ∤ n and p² ∤ n for odd p. Only the |D| squarefree odd case is used after the restriction to odd D.

items.name: Decomposition data D = D₁·D₂ (δ_i, ε_i, 𝔡_i, 𝒟₁, κ, c*) and the restriction to odd D
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. Write δ = |D|, δ₁ | δ a positive divisor, δ₂ = δ/δ₁. δ_i = N(𝔡_i) for unique integral ideals 𝔡_i of K that are products of ramified primes. If (δ₁, δ₂) = 1 there are unique fundamental discriminants D₁, D₂ (1 allowed) with δ_i = |D_i| and D₁D₂ = D; then ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character of §0, 𝒟₁ is the class of 𝔡₁ (𝔡₁² = (D₁)), and κ(D₁) = 1 if D₁ > 0, i if D₁ < 0. For odd D, (δ₁, δ₂) = 1 always; for even D, (δ₁, δ₂) = 2 can occur. The paper assumes from here on that D is odd (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4). For c prime to D₁, c* denotes an inverse of c modulo D₁; in (2.2) it is also chosen ≡ 0 (mod D₂).
items.note: The integer-level genus characters are in Tau Ceti: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.genusCharFun (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Quadratic/GenusCharacter/Basic.lean:212, a product of prime-discriminant characters), with the factorisation of a fundamental discriminant into prime discriminants (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsFundamentalDiscriminant.exists_finset_primeDiscriminant, FundamentalDiscriminant/Factorization.lean:131). The ideal-class character χ_{D₁·D₂}: Cl_K → {±1} is in Tau Ceti too: tauceti:TauCeti.Multiquadratic.genusCharFunNarrowClassGroupHom (GenusCharacter/NarrowClassGroup.lean:134) on Cl⁺(K), with tauceti:NumberField.NarrowClassGroup.toClassGroupEquiv (NarrowClassGroup/TotallyComplex.lean:47) for Cl⁺(K) ≃ Cl_K; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/172. The class 𝒟₁ of 𝔡₁ and a representative of a class prime to a given modulus (tauceti:NumberField.NarrowClassGroup.exists_mk0_eq_and_isCoprime_absNorm, NarrowClassGroup/CoprimeRepresentative.lean:162) are available. The package (𝔡_i, 𝒟₁, κ, c*) is bookkeeping with no library counterpart. Conrad (2004, §1) notes that GZ's analytic results are proved only for odd D, and that the main results would extend to even D 'provided the analytic results in [GZ] are proven for even discriminants'. This is the restriction made here. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Eisenstein series E^{(D₁)}_s attached to a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ (2.1)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. E^{(D₁)}_s(z) = ½ Σ_{m,n∈ℤ, D₂|m} ε₁(m)ε₂(n) (mz+n)^{−(2k−1)} y^s |mz+n|^{−2s} (Re(s) large). For D₁ = 1 this is E^{(1)}_s, and E^{(D₁)}_s ∈ M̃_{2k−1}(Γ₀(D), ε) ('as is easily checked': under (a b; c d) ∈ Γ₀(D), ε₁(ma+nc)ε₂(mb+nd) = ε₁(a)ε₂(d)ε₁(m)ε₂(n) = ε(d)ε₁(m)ε₂(n)).
items.note: Same search as PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/179: no non-holomorphic Eisenstein series with a pair of characters in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. The nearest plan, EllipticRegulators:ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series, is weight 0 with congruence classes and no character. The Γ₀(D)-invariance claim was checked here by the substitution (m, n) ↦ (m, n)γ. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Review: the atlas now has an accepted owner for classical non-holomorphic Eisenstein series. PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16/57 (the weight-0, level-one series E(z,s) = Σ_{Γ∞\PSL₂(ℤ)} Im(γz)^s, with convergence and ΔE = s(1−s)E) is routed as a source of AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0/AS.1/AS.2/AS.4, and that route is accepted in PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16.review.json. AS.1 ('Prove absolute convergence of the Eisenstein sum ... automorphy') and AS.2 ('Prove meromorphic continuation of operators and Eisenstein series, the functional equations') are the general setting of this series (GL₂, Borel, character datum ε, archimedean weight 2k−1). The review recommends routing the definition, convergence, automorphy and continuation of this series to AS.1–AS.2 beside the DIT series, so that the atlas has one owner for classical non-holomorphic Eisenstein series; GZ.6 keeps the GZ-specific uses. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Transformation of E^{(1)}_s under SL₂(ℤ) (2.2)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. For γ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL₂(ℤ) with (c, D) = |D₂|, D₁D₂ = D, and c* an inverse of c (mod D₁) with c* ≡ 0 (mod D₂): (E^{(1)}_s|_{2k−1}γ)(z) = ε_{D₁}(c) ε_{D₂}(dδ₁) δ₁^{−s−2k+1} E^{(D₁)}_s((z + c*d)/δ₁), where (F|_{2k−1}γ)(z) = (cz+d)^{−(2k−1)}F(γz).
items.note: Verified: replace (m, n) by γ^{−1}(m, n), and use md ≡ nc (mod D) ⇒ ε(an−bm) = ε₁(c)ε₁(m)ε₂(d)ε₂(n). Then md ≡ nc (mod D) ⇔ D₂ | m and n ≡ c*md (mod D₁); set n = c*md + δ₁n′. No library counterpart, since E^{(D₁)}_s is missing (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/192). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Checked numerically (review): for D = −15, k = 2, s = 1.6 + 0.3i and nine matrices γ covering all four decompositions, both sides agree to relative error ≤ 3·10⁻⁸ (lattice truncation).

items.name: Lemma (2.3): transformation of θ_𝒜 under SL₂(ℤ)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. For γ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL₂(ℤ) (printed 'PSL₂(ℤ)', see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E30) with (c, D) = |D₂|, D₁·D₂ = D, and c* an inverse of c (mod D₁): (θ_𝒜|₁γ)(z) = ε_{D₁}(c/δ₂) ε_{D₂}(d) κ(D₁)^{−1} δ₁^{−1/2} χ_{D₁·D₂}(𝒜) θ_{𝒜𝒟₁}((z + c*d)/δ₁), where κ(D₁) = 1 or i according as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0, and 𝒟₁ is the class of 𝔡₁ with 𝔡₁² = (D₁).
items.note: Proof checked line by line. The reduction to c = δ₂ goes via γ₁ = (∗ ∗; δ₂ x), γ₀ = γγ₁^{−1} ∈ Γ₀(D). Then: split λ modulo 𝔞𝔡₂; 2-dimensional Poisson summation (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/195); substitute ν ↦ ν/δ₂; take the representatives λ₀μ; complete the square with R*; evaluate the quadratic Gauss sum (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/196); and identify ε_{D₂}(R) = ε_{D₂}(d)χ(𝒜). Sanity check: γ = S = (0 −1; 1 0) gives θ_𝒜(−1/z)/z = −iδ^{−1/2}θ_𝒜(z/δ), which also follows from lattice Poisson summation (dual lattice 𝔞𝔡^{−1}). No library support: θ_𝒜 is missing (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/177, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/178). Nearest plan: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.5 (adelic theta transformation), with no classical specialisation planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Checked numerically (review): for D = −15 (h = 2), both classes, all four decompositions and 72 matrices γ ∈ SL₂(ℤ), both sides agree to relative error 4·10⁻¹³; replacing γ by −γ changes the sign of both sides, confirming PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E30. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 3: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.5, MP.6.

items.name: Every ideal class contains an integral ideal prime to a given modulus (used to choose λ₀ in the proof of (2.3))
items.statement: For every ideal class 𝒞 of K and every nonzero integer m there is an integral ideal 𝔟 ∈ 𝒞 with N𝔟 prime to m. In the proof of (2.3): choose 𝔟 ∈ 𝒜^{−1} with N𝔟 prime to δ₂; then 𝔟𝔞 = (λ₀) with λ₀ ∈ 𝔞 and (λ₀)𝔞^{−1} = 𝔟 prime to 𝔡₂, and the products λ₀μ (μ ∈ O/𝔡₂) represent 𝔞/𝔞𝔡₂.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §2, proof of (2.3), p. 275 ('Choose λ₀ ∈ 𝔞 so that the ideal (λ₀)𝔞^{−1} is prime to 𝔡₂')
items.note: TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/NarrowClassGroup/CoprimeRepresentative.lean:162: `theorem exists_mk0_eq_and_isCoprime_absNorm (C : NarrowClassGroup K) {m : ℤ} (hm : m ≠ 0) : ∃ J : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰, mk0 J = C ∧ IsCoprime (Ideal.absNorm (J : Ideal (𝓞 K)) : ℤ) m`; for K imaginary quadratic, NarrowClassGroup/TotallyComplex.lean:47 identifies Cl⁺(K) with Cl(K). The step 'λ₀μ represent 𝔞/𝔞𝔡₂' is the Chinese remainder theorem for the coprime ideals 𝔟 and 𝔡₂ and is not stated separately. Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: Conjugation symmetry of r_𝒜 and θ_𝒜: r_{𝒞^{−1}} = r_𝒞, and 𝒟₁² = 1
items.statement: For every ideal class 𝒞 of the imaginary quadratic field K and every n ≥ 0, r_{𝒞^{−1}}(n) = r_𝒞(n): complex conjugation 𝔞 ↦ 𝔞̄ maps the integral ideals of norm n in 𝒞 bijectively onto those in 𝒞^{−1}, because 𝔞𝔞̄ = (N𝔞). Hence θ_{𝒞^{−1}} = θ_𝒞. Also 𝒟₁² = 1, since 𝔡₁² = (D₁). Consequences used in the paper: the second expression (1/w)Σ_{λ∈𝔞} q^{N(λ)/A} in (1.1), which counts ideals of the class 𝒜^{−1}, equals θ_𝒜; and θ_{𝒜^{−1}𝒟₁^{−1}} = θ_{𝒜𝒟₁} at the end of the proof of (2.3).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §1, (1.1), p. 270 (implicit) and §2, last line of the proof of (2.3), p. 275 ('θ_{𝒜^{−1}𝒟₁^{−1}} = θ_{𝒜𝒟₁}')
items.note: Not in the libraries: r_𝒜 and θ_𝒜 are undefined (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/19, /177). Ingredients available: Mathlib's absolute ideal norm and the Galois action on ideals; ClassGroup inverse. Needed twice in the range, so it is recorded separately rather than left inside a proof. Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: Poisson summation over an ideal lattice of K
items.statement: For any z ∈ ℌ, any fractional ideal 𝔟 of K and any λ ∈ ℂ = K⊗ℝ: Σ_{μ∈𝔟} e(N(λ+μ)z) = (iδ^{−1/2}/(N(𝔟)z)) Σ_{ν ∈ 𝔟^{−1}𝔡^{−1}} e(−N(ν)/z) e(Tr λν), where 𝔡 is the different of K (N(𝔡) = δ), N(x) = |x|² and Tr(x) = x + x̄. (Consider the left side as a periodic function of λ ∈ ℂ/𝔟 and compute its Fourier development.)
items.note: Checked: covol(𝔟) = N(𝔟)√δ/2; the dual of 𝔟 for x·ξ = Re(x ξ̄) is 2𝔟̄^{−1}𝔡^{−1}; the Fourier transform of e(z|x|²) on ℝ² is (i/(2z))e(−|ξ|²/(4z)). Mathlib has only one-dimensional Poisson summation: `Real.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier_of_rpow_decay` (Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/PoissonSummation.lean:205), `SchwartzMap.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier` (:219) and `Complex.tsum_exp_neg_quadratic` (Gaussian/PoissonSummation.lean:86). Nothing for lattices in ℝ² or for ideal lattices in Tau Ceti. Nearest plans: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.0 ('Prove Fourier inversion … and adelic Poisson summation, with the diagonal lattice and volume from GlobalNumberFields') and MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.5. Specialising adelic Poisson summation to this classical identity is not planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Review: the general lattice form of Poisson summation on ℝ^r is already requested from AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.0 by the QSeries packet (research/blueprint/packets/QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms.json, request to AL.0: 'Poisson summation on ℝ^r for the lattice ℤ^r ... Mathlib 082e2d3 has only the case r = 1'). This item is its r = 2 instance for an ideal lattice with a Gaussian test function; GZ.6 should import the general statement from AL.0 rather than plan it. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 3: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.5, MP.6.

items.name: Evaluation of the quadratic Gauss sum Σ_{n mod δ₂} e_{δ₂}(Rn²)
items.statement: Let D₂ be an odd fundamental discriminant, δ₂ = |D₂| (squarefree), and R an integer prime to δ₂. Then Σ_{μ ∈ O/𝔡₂} e_{δ₂}(R N(μ)) = Σ_{n ∈ ℤ/δ₂ℤ} e_{δ₂}(Rn²) = κ(D₂) δ₂^{1/2} ε_{D₂}(R), with κ(D₂) = 1 if D₂ > 0 and i if D₂ < 0. The first equality holds because δ₂ is squarefree and totally ramified, so ℤ/δ₂ represents O/𝔡₂. The second is 'the usual evaluation of Gauss sums', Gauss's sign determination included.
items.note: Mathlib has the square but not the sign, and the square only for prime moduli: `gaussSum_sq` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/GaussSum.lean:222) gives τ(χ)² = χ(−1)·#R for a nontrivial quadratic χ and a primitive ψ on a finite field R (section variable `[Field R] [Fintype R]`), so τ = ±√D₂ when δ₂ is prime; for composite squarefree δ₂ Mathlib's DirichletCharacter/GaussSum.lean has only the shift identity, and `DirichletCharacter.rootNumber` (LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:272) is not evaluated for real characters. The sign (τ = +√D₂, i.e. +i√δ₂ when D₂ < 0) is Gauss's theorem and is not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. Tau Ceti's TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Cyclotomic/GaussSum.lean only extracts a square root of p* in a cyclotomic field. The reduction Σ_n e(Rn²/δ₂) = (R/δ₂)·Σ_n e(n²/δ₂) is also absent for composite squarefree δ₂. Nearest plans: FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.1 ('Construct … Gauss and Jacobi sums and their norm/product identities') and AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.1 ('functional equations include conductor, Gauss sum and parity'); neither states the sign determination. Routed (source) to AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.1. The QSeries packet records the same need as a gap ('the general quadratic Gauss evaluations ... positive-phase evaluation of composite-modulus quadratic exponential sums', gap 'Selberg–Whiteman bridge'), so the owner chosen here should serve both. Checked numerically for D₂ ∈ {5, −3, −7, 13, −15, 21, −35, 65, −231} and several R.

items.name: Gauss sum of the primitive character ε_{D₂}: Σ_{n mod δ₂} ε₂(n)e(rn/δ₂) = ε₂(r)κ(D₂)δ₂^{1/2}
items.statement: For D₂ a fundamental discriminant (odd here), δ₂ = |D₂| and every r ∈ ℤ: Σ_{n mod δ₂} ε_{D₂}(n) e(rn/δ₂) = ε_{D₂}(r) κ(D₂) δ₂^{1/2}. The right side is 0 when (r, δ₂) > 1.
items.note: Partly in the library. `gaussSum_mulShift_of_isPrimitive` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/GaussSum.lean:57): for primitive χ, `gaussSum χ (e.mulShift a) = χ⁻¹ a * gaussSum χ e`. That gives Σ ε₂(n)e(rn/δ₂) = ε₂(r)τ(ε₂) for all r, zero included. The value τ(ε_{D₂}) = √D₂ = κ(D₂)√δ₂ is the missing sign determination of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/196. Routed (source) to AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.1.

items.name: Reciprocity ε_{D₁}(δ₂) ε_{D₂}(δ₁) = 1
items.statement: Let D = D₁D₂ < 0 with D₁, D₂ coprime odd fundamental discriminants (one of them may be 1), δ_i = |D_i|. Then ε_{D₁}(δ₂) ε_{D₂}(δ₁) = 1.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §2, p. 276 ('where we have used ε_{D₁}(δ₂)ε_{D₂}(δ₁) = 1')
items.note: Proof: for D_i ≡ 1 (mod 4) and n > 0, ε_{D_i}(n) = (n/δ_i) (Jacobi symbol). Since D < 0, exactly one of D₁, D₂ is negative, so one δ_i is ≡ 1 (mod 4). Then Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/JacobiSymbol.lean:431 `jacobiSym.quadratic_reciprocity_one_mod_four {a b : ℕ} (ha : a % 4 = 1) (hb : Odd b) : J(a | b) = J(b | a)` gives (δ₂/δ₁) = (δ₁/δ₂), and the product is (δ₁/δ₂)² = 1. The library has the general law. The identification ε_D(n) = J(n | |D|) for a fundamental discriminant D is not stated in Mathlib. Tau Ceti identifies the genus character of the full prime-discriminant factorisation with the splitting symbol (d/q) at odd primes q (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.genusCharFun_natCast_eq_legendreSym, GenusCharacter/Basic.lean:308); passing from (D/q) to (q/|D|) is Jacobi reciprocity again. The bridge is in Tau Ceti: for an odd prime discriminant P, tauceti:TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantCharFun P n = jacobiSym n |P| (primeDiscriminantCharFun_eq_jacobiSym_of_not_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant, Legendre/PrimeDiscriminant/Character.lean:102), and ε_{D₁} = genusCharFun t (the product over the prime discriminants dividing D₁; GenusCharacter/Basic.lean:212), so ε_{D₁}(n) = J(n | δ₁) by multiplicativity of the Jacobi symbol in the modulus.

items.name: Coset representatives of Γ₀(ND)\Γ₀(N)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. [Γ₀(N) : Γ₀(N|D|)] = Σ_{δ₁|δ} δ₁. The cosets Γ₀(N|D|)γ, γ = (a b; c d) ∈ Γ₀(N), are classified by δ₂ = (c, D) together with the residue class of c*d modulo δ₁ = δ/δ₂. So Tr^{ND}_N F = Σ_{D=D₁D₂} Σ_{j mod δ₁} F|_{2k}γ_{D₁,j}, where γ_{D₁,j} is any representative with (c, D) = δ₂ and c*d ≡ j (mod δ₁).
items.note: It is the P¹(ℤ/δ)-parametrisation of Γ₀(δ)\SL₂(ℤ) transported to level N, using (N, D) = 1. Tau Ceti has only prime-level indices: `CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0_prime_index : (Gamma0 p).index = p + 1` and `Gamma0_prime_power_index` (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups/Basic.lean:489, 574). No general coset classification and no multiplicativity in coprime levels. No atlas stage plans it. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: The operator U_n on 1-periodic functions
items.statement: For n ∈ ℕ and a function f on ℌ of period 1: (f|U_n)(z) = (1/n) Σ_{j mod n} f((z+j)/n). On Fourier expansions, Σ_{m∈ℤ} A_m(y)e(mx) ↦ Σ_{m∈ℤ} A_{mn}(y/n)e(mx).
items.note: TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/HeckeSlash/UpperTri/Sum.lean:70: `noncomputable def heckeSlashUpperTri (f : ℍ → ℂ) : ℍ → ℂ := ∑ b : Fin p, f ∣[k] upperTriRep p b` with upperTriRep p b = !![1, b; 0, p] (HeckeRing/GL2/CosetDecomposition.lean:141, 145). Mathlib's slash gives f∣[k](1 b; 0 p) (τ) = p^{k−1}·p^{−k}·f((τ+b)/p). So heckeSlashUpperTri k p f = (1/p)Σ_b f((τ+b)/p) = f|U_p for every weight k and every function f, holomorphic or not; p is any natural number, not only a prime. This is the same operator. The coefficient rule is in the library only for holomorphic forms: `qExpansion_coeff_heckeSlashUpperTri'` (UpperTri/QExpansion.lean:233) gives a_m(U_p f) = a_{pm}(f). The rule A_m(y) ↦ A_{mn}(y/n) for non-holomorphic 1-periodic functions is not stated (it is immediate from the definition).

items.name: Passing from U_{δ₁} to U_δ via θ_𝒜𝒟₁(δ₂z) and θ_𝒜(z)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. For every 1-periodic function f on ℌ: (f(z)θ_{𝒜𝒟₁}(z))|U_{δ₁} = (f(δ₂z)θ_{𝒜𝒟₁}(δ₂z))|U_δ = (f(δ₂z)θ_𝒜(z))|U_δ. The reason is that θ_{𝒜𝒟₁}(δ₂z) and θ_𝒜(z) have the same n-th Fourier coefficient for every n divisible by δ₂: r_{𝒜𝒟₁}(n/δ₂) = r_𝒜(n). This holds because 𝒜𝒟₁ = 𝒜𝒟₂ and every integral ideal of norm n (δ₂ | n) is 𝔡₂ times an integral ideal of norm n/δ₂.
items.note: Checked: (g(δ₂z))|U_δ = g|U_{δ₁} for 1-periodic g. In the Fourier coefficient of index m ≡ 0 (mod δ) of f(δ₂z)h(z), only the coefficients of h at multiples of δ₂ occur. The ideal-counting identity (𝔡₂ divides every ideal whose norm is divisible by δ₂, δ₂ squarefree and totally ramified) is not in the libraries. Its ingredients are: r_𝒜 (not in library), and the ramified prime above p | D being the unique prime above p, which is in Mathlib's Dedekind-domain API. No plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: The Eisenstein combination ℰ_s
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. ℰ_s(z) = Σ_{D=D₁·D₂} ε_{D₁}(N) χ_{D₁·D₂}(𝒜) / (κ(D₁)|D₁|^{s+2k−3/2}) · E^{(D₁)}_s(|D₂|z), the sum over all ordered decompositions (D₁, D₂) of D as a product of two fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed; (D₁, D₂) and (D₂, D₁) are different terms, so there are 2^t terms, t the number of prime factors of D). ℰ_s depends on N (in fact only on N mod D) and on 𝒜 (in fact only on the genus of 𝒜); the paper suppresses this in the notation.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §2, (2.4) Proposition and the note after it, pp. 276–277
items.note: Not in the libraries: E^{(D₁)}_s and the class-group genus character χ_{D₁·D₂}(𝒜) are missing (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/192, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/191). No stage plans this classical combination. GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 plans the adelic analytic kernel. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Proposition (2.4): the Rankin kernel as U_{|D|} of ℰ_s(Nz)θ_𝒜(z)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. Assume (D, 2N) = 1. Then Φ̃_s(z) = Tr^{ND}_N(E^{(1)}_s(Nz)θ_𝒜(z)) from Proposition (1.2) equals (ℰ_s(Nz)θ_𝒜(z))|U_{|D|}, where ℰ_s(z) = Σ_{D=D₁·D₂} ε_{D₁}(N)χ_{D₁·D₂}(𝒜)/(κ(D₁)|D₁|^{s+2k−3/2}) E^{(D₁)}_s(|D₂|z), summed over all ordered decompositions (D₁, D₂) of D as a product of two fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed). χ_{D₁·D₂} is the corresponding genus character, κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0, and E^{(D₁)}_s is the Eisenstein series (2.1).
items.note: Checked. For γ ∈ Γ₀(N) with (c, D) = δ₂, (2.2) and (2.3) give E^{(1)}_s(Nz)θ_𝒜(z)|_{2k}γ = ε₁(N)κ(D₁)^{−1}δ₁^{−s−2k+1/2}χ(𝒜)E^{(D₁)}_s(N(z+c*d)/δ₁)θ_{𝒜𝒟₁}((z+c*d)/δ₁), using ε_{D₁}(δ₂)ε_{D₂}(δ₁) = 1 (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/198). Then sum over the coset representatives (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/199), convert Σ_j to δ₁·U_{δ₁} (factor δ₁^{−s−2k+3/2}), and apply PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/201. (The page's 'From (2.3) and (2.4)' should read '(2.2) and (2.3)'; see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E32.) No library or plan (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/186, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/202). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Checked numerically (review): for D = −15, k = 2, s = 1.6 + 0.3i, N ∈ {1, 2} and both ideal classes, the trace over 24 coset representatives of Γ₀(15N)\Γ₀(N), with E^{(1)}_s|γ computed as a re-indexed lattice sum and θ_𝒜 as a lattice sum, agrees with (ℰ_s(Nz)θ_𝒜(z))|U_15 to relative error ≤ 5·10⁻¹².

items.name: Special case of ℰ_s: k = 1, |D| = p prime, ε(N) = 1
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. If k = 1, |D| = p is prime (so D = −p, p ≡ 3 mod 4) and ε(N) = 1, then ℰ_s(z) = E^{(1)}_s(pz) − i p^{−s−1/2} E^{(D)}_s(z) (printed with superscript (p); see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E33).
items.note: Direct from PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/202: the decompositions are (1, D) and (D, 1), with κ(D) = i and χ_{D·1} trivial. It is the simplest instance of the weight-2 (k = 1), ε(N) = 1 setting of the main theorem. No library or plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Fourier expansion (3.1) of the Rankin kernel
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. Write ℰ_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ} e_s(n, y) e(nx) (z = x+iy ∈ ℌ). Then Φ̃_{s,𝒜}(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_𝒜(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ), with δ = |D|.
items.note: Immediate from (2.4) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/203). Multiply ℰ_s(Nz) = Σ e_s(n, Ny)e(nNx) by θ_𝒜(z) = Σ_{l≥0} r_𝒜(l)e^{−2πly}e(lx), then apply U_δ, which keeps the indices Nn+l ≡ 0 (mod δ) and replaces y by y/δ (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/200). No library or plan, since the kernel is missing (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/186). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: The sign function ε_𝒜(n, d)
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. For n ∈ ℤ ∖ {0} and d a positive divisor of n: ε(n, d) = ε_𝒜(n, d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1, and ε(n, d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−N n/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(𝒜) if (d, n/d, D) = 1, where D = D₁D₂ is the decomposition with (d, D) = |D₂|.
items.note: When (d, n/d, D) = 1 the decomposition is determined by d, and the value is in {±1}. It depends on the class-group genus character χ_{D₁·D₂}, which is not packaged in Tau Ceti (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/191). No plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: The archimedean integral V_s(t)
items.statement: Fix k ≥ 1. For s ∈ ℂ with Re(s) > 1−k and t ∈ ℝ: V_s(t) = ∫_{−∞}^{∞} e^{−2πixt} dx / ((x+i)^{2k−1}(x²+1)^s). This is the Fourier transform of x ↦ (x+i)^{−(2k−1)}(x²+1)^{−s}, which is absolutely integrable exactly when Re(s) > 1−k.
items.note: The paper notes that tables express V_s(t) through Whittaker functions but 'the results found in various tables do not agree', so it proves every property directly (p. 279). Mathlib and Tau Ceti have no Whittaker or K-Bessel functions; searched 'whittaker', 'bessel', 'confluent', and found only Mathlib's OrdinaryHypergeometric/RegularizedHypergeometric (₂F₁). Nearest plan: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 ('normalized local Whittaker terms' of the incoherent Eisenstein kernel). That is the adelic analogue: V_s is the archimedean Whittaker function of the weight-(2k−1) Eisenstein series, but GZ.6 plans neither this classical normalisation nor its properties. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Poisson (Lipschitz-type) identity for Σ_l (z+l)^{−(2k−1)}|z+l|^{−2s}
items.statement: For k ≥ 1, z = x+iy ∈ ℌ and Re(s) > 1−k: Σ_{l∈ℤ} 1/((z+l)^{2k−1}|z+l|^{2s}) = y^{−2s−2k+2} Σ_{r∈ℤ} V_s(ry) e^{2πirx}.
items.note: The general theorem is in Mathlib; the instance is not, because its hypotheses need missing input. `Real.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier_of_rpow_decay` (Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/PoissonSummation.lean:205): `{f : ℝ → ℂ} (hc : Continuous f) {b : ℝ} (hb : 1 < b) (hf : f =O[cocompact ℝ] (|·| ^ (-b))) (hFf : (𝓕 f) =O[cocompact ℝ] (|·| ^ (-b))) (x : ℝ) : ∑' n : ℤ, f (x + n) = ∑' n : ℤ, 𝓕 f n * fourier n (x : UnitAddCircle)`. Apply it to f(u) = (u+iy)^{−(2k−1)}|u+iy|^{−2s}, whose Fourier transform is y^{−2s−2k+2}V_s(ry) (substitute u = yv). The hypothesis on 𝓕f is the decay of V_s(ry) in r, i.e. (3.3b) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/213), which is missing; so the identity is not available as it stands. The holomorphic case s = 0, 2k−1 ≥ 2 is Mathlib's Lipschitz formula `EisensteinSeries.qExpansion_identity` (EisensteinSeries/QExpansion.lean:174): `∑' n : ℤ, 1 / ((z : ℂ) + n) ^ (k + 1) = ((-2 * π * I) ^ (k + 1) / k !) * ∑' n : ℕ, n ^ k * cexp (2 * π * I * z) ^ n` for 1 ≤ k. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Fourier expansion of E^{(D₁)}_s
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. Write E^{(D₁)}_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ} e^{(D₁)}_s(n, y) e(nx). Then e^{(D₁)}_s(0, y) = L(2s+2k−1, ε) y^s if D₁ = 1, D₂ = D; = V_s(0) L(2s+2k−2, ε) y^{−s−2k+2} if D₁ = D, D₂ = 1; = 0 otherwise. For n ≠ 0, e^{(D₁)}_s(n, y) = ε₁(δ₂)κ(D₂)/δ₂^{2s+2k−3/2} · (Σ_{m|n, m>0} ε₁(m)ε₂(n/m) m^{−(2s+2k−2)}) · y^{−s−2k+2} V_s(ny). Here L(s, ε) = Σ_{n≥1} ε(n)n^{−s}. Valid for Re(s) large, and it gives the meromorphic continuation in s.
items.note: Checked. The m = 0 terms of (2.1) give L(2s+2k−1, ε)y^s only when D₁ = 1 (ε₁(0) = 0 otherwise). Pair ±m, write m ↦ mδ₂ and n = n₀ + δ₂l, apply PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/208 with z replaced by mz + n₀/δ₂, and evaluate Σ_{n₀ mod δ₂} ε₂(n₀)e(rn₀/δ₂) = ε₂(r)κ(D₂)δ₂^{1/2} (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/197). No library counterpart. Mathlib's q-expansions of Eisenstein series (EisensteinSeries/QExpansion.lean) are level one, even weight and holomorphic. Nearest plan: the node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series (weight-0 Fourier expansion), a different series. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Nearest plan at s = 0 (k ≥ 2): E^{(D₁)}_0 is the holomorphic weight-(2k−1) Eisenstein series with the character pair (ε₁, ε₂); by (3.3d) its coefficients are the twisted divisor sums Σ_{m|n} ε₁(m)ε₂(n/m)(n/m)^{2k−2}, i.e. the series E_{2k−1}^{ψ,φ} that tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-0-diamond-operators-and-modular-forms-with-character-nebentypus plans ('Eisenstein series with character ... with q-expansions via generalized Bernoulli numbers and twisted divisor sums'). That fixes a consistency test for this item. Checked numerically (review) through Proposition (3.2) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/210, /211). Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Proposition (3.2), n = 0: constant term of ℰ_s
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. The 0-th Fourier coefficient of ℰ_s(z) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/202) is e_s(0, y) = L(2s+2k−1, ε)(δy)^s + (ε(N)/(i√δ)) V_s(0) L(2s+2k−2, ε) (δy)^{−s−2k+2}.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.2) Proposition (first formula), p. 277; proof pp. 278–279
items.note: Checked from PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/209. The D₁ = 1 term gives L(2s+2k−1, ε)(δy)^s. The D₁ = D term gives ε(N)/(κ(D)δ^{s+2k−3/2}) · V_s(0)L(2s+2k−2, ε)y^{−s−2k+2}, with κ(D) = i, which equals (ε(N)/(i√δ))V_s(0)L(2s+2k−2, ε)(δy)^{−s−2k+2}. Dirichlet L-functions are in Mathlib (DirichletCharacter.LFunction), but the Eisenstein coefficients are not. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Checked numerically (review): D = −15, N = 2, 𝒜 non-principal, k = 2, s = 1.6 + 0.3i, y = 1; the constant term of ℰ_s computed by FFT from lattice sums agrees with the formula to relative error 2·10⁻¹².

items.name: Proposition (3.2), n ≠ 0: non-constant coefficients of ℰ_s
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. For n ≠ 0, the n-th Fourier coefficient of ℰ_s(z) is e_s(n, y) = (ε(N)/(i√δ)) (δy)^{−s−2k+2} V_s(ny) Σ_{d|n, d>0} ε_𝒜(n, d) d^{−(2s+2k−2)}, with ε_𝒜(n, d) as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/206.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.2) Proposition (second formula), p. 277; proof p. 279
items.note: Checked. The proof gives e_s(n, y) = iδ^{−s−2k+3/2}(Σ_{D₂|n} ε_{D₁}(−N)χ(𝒜) Σ_{m|n/δ₂} ε_{D₁}(mδ₂)ε_{D₂}(n/mδ₂)(mδ₂)^{−(2s+2k−2)}) y^{−s−2k+2}V_s(ny), using κ(D₂)/κ(D₁) = iε_{D₁}(−1). Put d = mδ₂: the nonzero terms are exactly those with (d, D) = δ₂ and (n/d, δ₂) = 1, i.e. (d, n/d, D) = 1. Matching prefactors needs iε_{D₁}(−N) = (ε(N)/i)ε_{D₂}(−N), which is ε_{D₁}(−1)ε_{D₂}(−1) = ε(−1) = −1. That holds because D < 0. No library or plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Checked numerically (review), same data as PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/210: the coefficients for n = 1, −1, 2, −2, 3 agree to relative error ≤ 10⁻⁴ (the absolute agreement is at the 10⁻¹⁴ level of the lattice sums); this also tests ε_𝒜(n, d) and the factor ε(N)/(i√δ).

items.name: Meromorphic continuation in s of E^{(D₁)}_s, ℰ_s and the Rankin kernel Φ̃_s (implicit)
items.statement: For each decomposition D = D₁·D₂ and each z ∈ ℌ, s ↦ E^{(D₁)}_s(z), defined by (2.1) for Re(s) > 3/2 − k, extends to a meromorphic function of s ∈ ℂ, given by the Fourier expansion of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/209: the terms n ≠ 0 are entire in s (V_s(t) is entire for t ≠ 0, (3.3b)) and the series converges locally uniformly in (s, z) by the estimate V_s(t) = |t|^{O(1)}e^{−2π|t|}; the only possible poles come from the constant term V_s(0)L(2s+2k−2, ε)y^{−s−2k+2}. The continued function keeps the transformation law of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/192. Consequently ℰ_s and Φ̃_s = (ℰ_s(Nz)θ_𝒜(z))|U_{|D|} continue meromorphically, Φ̃_s keeps its Γ₀(N) transformation law, and the expansions (3.1) and (3.2) hold for all s. This is what gives meaning to Φ̃_{−r} in Corollary (3.4) and to the values and derivatives at s = 0 and s = 1 − k used in §4.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, implicit in Corollary (3.4) ('Φ̃_{−r}(z)', p. 281) and in §4 (p. 282); the paper states continuation only for V_s(t) (pp. 280–281)
items.note: The paper proves continuation of V_s(t) (3.3a–c) and of each Fourier coefficient, and then evaluates Φ̃_s at s = −r without stating that the function continues; the step is standard (locally uniform convergence of the Fourier series) and is not recorded as a gap. Nearest plan: AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.2 ('Prove meromorphic continuation of operators and Eisenstein series'), adelic; no stage plans this classical kernel. Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: Proposition (3.3a): the value V_s(0)
items.statement: For k ≥ 1: V_s(0) = (−1)^k π i 2^{−2s−2k+3} Γ(2s+2k−2)/(Γ(s)Γ(s+2k−1)). This holds for Re(s) > 1−k and gives the meromorphic continuation of V_s(0) in s.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.3) Proposition a), p. 277; proofs pp. 279–280
items.note: Two proofs, both checked. (i) Expand (x−i)^{2k−1}, use the Beta integral and the duplication formula, and reduce to the identity Σ_{j=0}^{k−1}(−1/4)^{k−1−j}(2k−1)!/((2j+1)!(k−1−j)!)(s+k−½)…(s+k+j−3/2) = s(s+1)…(s+k−2). The paper leaves that identity to 'a tedious induction'; it was checked here for k = 1, 2, 3. (ii) The Hankel integral for 1/Γ(s) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/218), complete; it contains the misprint PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E35. Numerical spot checks: k = 1, s = 1 gives V_1(0) = −iπ/2; k = 2, s = 1 gives iπ/8; the formula agrees in both. Tools in Mathlib: Complex.Gamma_mul_Gamma_add_half, Complex.Gamma_mul_Gamma_eq_betaIntegral (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/220). The formula itself is not in the libraries, since V_s is missing (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/207). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Review: the finite identity was also checked symbolically for k = 1, …, 9, the intermediate display on p. 279 numerically for k = 1, …, 4, and the final formula against direct numerical integration for (k, s) = (1, 0.7), (2, 0.3+0.5i), (3, −0.5+0.2i), (4, −1.2). Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Proposition (3.3b): holomorphy of V_s(t) in s and exponential decay in t
items.statement: For t ≠ 0 the function s ↦ V_s(t) continues holomorphically to all s ∈ ℂ and satisfies, locally uniformly in s, V_s(t) = |t|^{O(1)} e^{−2π|t|} as |t| → ∞.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.3) Proposition b), p. 277; proof pp. 280–281
items.note: Proof as printed: first meromorphic continuation, from the u-integral representation of V*_s(t) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/214), which converges for all s. Then holomorphy for t < 0 by deforming the x-path to a contour C around [i, i∞), and similarly for t > 0 around (−i∞, −i]. The estimate comes from the integral representations or the K-Bessel formula (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/217). No library or plan (V_s missing). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Proposition (3.3c): V*_s(t) is entire and satisfies V*_s(t) = sign(t) V*_{2−2k−s}(t)
items.statement: For t ≠ 0 set V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1} Γ(s+2k−1) V_s(t). Then V*_s(t) is entire in s and V*_s(t) = sign(t) V*_{2−2k−s}(t). For t > 0 this comes from V*_s(t) = ∫_0^∞ u^{s+k−1} e^{−πt(u+1/u)} ∫_{−∞}^{∞} e^{−πtv²} (v + (u^{1/2}+u^{−1/2})/i)^{2k−1} dv du/u.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.3) Proposition c), p. 278; proof p. 280
items.note: Checked. The integral form comes from Γ(s+2k−1)(πt(x²+1))^{−(s+2k−1)} = ∫_0^∞ u^{s+2k−2}e^{−πt(x²+1)u}du, completing the square, shifting to Im x = −1/u and substituting x = −i/u + v/√u; u ↦ 1/u exchanges s+k−1 ↔ −(s+k−1). For t < 0 the paper says only 'the proof for t < 0 is exactly similar'. Checked here: after shifting to Im x = +1/u the inner factor is (v + i(u^{−1/2} − u^{1/2}))^{2k−1}, which is odd under u ↦ 1/u (with v ↦ −v). This produces the sign −1 = sign(t), consistent with V_{1−k}(t) = 0 for t < 0 (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/215). Mathlib has the real-scale Gamma integral `Complex.integral_cpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_Ioi` (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Basic.lean:372). No library or plan for V*. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Checked numerically (review): the u-integral forms for t > 0 and t < 0 agree with the defining integral, and V*_s(t) = sign(t)V*_{2−2k−s}(t) holds, for (k, s, t) = (1, 0.4+0.3i, ±0.7), (2, 0.2−0.4i, ±0.5), (3, −1.3, ±0.4). Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Proposition (3.3d): V_{−r}(t) for integers 0 ≤ r ≤ k−1
items.statement: Let r ∈ ℤ with 0 ≤ r ≤ k−1. Then V_{−r}(t) = 0 for t < 0 and V_{−r}(t) = 2πi(−1)^{k−r} p_{k,r}(4πt) e^{−2πt} for t > 0, where p_{k,r}(t) = (t/2)^{2k−2−2r} Σ_{j=0}^{r} C(r, j) (−t)^j/(2k−2r−2+j)! (a polynomial). Here V_{−r}(t) = ∫ (x−i)^r (x+i)^{−(2k−1−r)} e^{−2πixt} dx, conditionally convergent for r = k−1.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.3) Proposition d), p. 278; proof p. 281
items.note: Checked by the residue at x = −i: for t < 0 close upward (no pole); for t > 0 close downward. Then V_{−r}(t) = −2πi Res and the binomial expansion of (x−i)^r = ((x+i)−2i)^r gives the printed polynomial. Special case r = 0: V_0(t) = 2πi(−1)^k(2πt)^{2k−2}e^{−2πt}/(2k−2)!. For 2k−1 ≥ 2 this is equivalent to Mathlib's Lipschitz formula `EisensteinSeries.qExpansion_identity` (EisensteinSeries/QExpansion.lean:174), via PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/208 at s = 0. The general r is not in the libraries. No plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Checked numerically (review) against the defining integral for (k, r) = (2, 0), (3, 0), (3, 1), (4, 1), (4, 2) with t > 0, and the vanishing for t < 0 for (k, r) = (2, 0), (3, 1). Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Proposition (3.3e): ∂_s V_s(t) at the centre s = 1−k for t < 0
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, (3.3) Proposition e), p. 278; proof p. 281
items.note: Checked. Deform the x-path to the contour C circling [i, i∞) counterclockwise and differentiate under the integral sign: ∂_s(x²+1)^{−s} = −log(x²+1)(x²+1)^{−s}, and at s = 1−k the kernel is (x−i)^{k−1}/(x+i)^k (misprinted 's = i−k', PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E36). log(x²+1) jumps by 2πi across the cut (right side minus left side), which gives −2πi∫_i^{i∞}. Substituting x = 2ix′ − i gives q_{k−1}(4π|t|)e^{−2πt}. This is the input for the derivative L′_𝒜(f, k) in §4. q_{k−1} is a finite combination of upper incomplete gamma values: q_{k−1}(t) = Σ_{j=0}^{k−1} C(k−1, j)(−1)^{k−1−j} t^{k−1−j} Γ(j+1−k, t) (checked numerically for k = 1, 2, 3, 5); for k = 1 it is E₁(t) = Γ(0, t). Libraries: Tau Ceti has only the lower incomplete gamma for positive parameter (TauCeti.lowerIncompleteGamma, TauCeti/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/IncompleteGamma.lean:110), no upper one and no exponential integral. Planned carriers: the upper incomplete gamma Γ(s, x) for every real s and x > 0 is the packet node QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3/upper-incomplete-gamma, and the exponential integral Ei with the s-derivative of K_s at s = 1/2 is PAPER-ZHANG-21/98, whose accepted route is AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StandardDistributions#layer-2-incomplete-special-functions-and-closed-form-cdfs plans incomplete special functions for distributions; it does not plan these. No plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Checked numerically (review): the formula agrees with a numerical derivative of V_s(t), computed from the u-integral representation, for (k, t) = (1, −0.3), (2, −0.4), (3, −0.25). Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: K-Bessel expression for V*_s(t), t > 0
items.statement: For t > 0: V*_s(t) = i Σ_{a,b,c≥0, 2a+b+c=2k−1} (−1)^{k−a}(2k−1)!/((2a)! b! c!) · Γ(a+½)/(πt)^{a+½} · ∫_0^∞ u^{s+k+(b−c)/2−2} e^{−πt(u+1/u)} du = (2(−1)^k i/t^{1/2}) Σ_{a,b,c≥0, 2a+b+c=2k−1} (2k−1)!/(a! b! c!) · (−1/(4πt))^a · K_{s+k−1+(b−c)/2}(2πt). For k = 1: V*_s(t) = (−2i/√t)(K_{1/2+s}(2πt) + K_{1/2−s}(2πt)). The functional equation (3.3c) for t > 0 follows from K_ν = K_{−ν} by interchanging b and c.
items.note: Checked: trinomial expansion; ∫v^{2a}e^{−πtv²}dv = Γ(a+½)(πt)^{−a−½}; (−i)^{2k−1−2a} = i(−1)^{k−a}; Γ(a+½)/(2a)! = √π/(4^a a!); and ∫_0^∞ u^{ν−1}e^{−πt(u+1/u)}du = 2K_ν(2πt). Not used later in this chunk beyond the estimate (3.3b). No K-Bessel functions in Mathlib or Tau Ceti; the atlas plans only other Bessel functions (QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.2 for Rademacher's I-Bessel series). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Checked numerically (review) against the defining integral for (k, s, t) = (1, 0.4+0.3i, 0.7), (2, 0.2−0.4i, 0.5), (3, −1.3, 0.4). Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Hankel's integral formula for 1/Γ(s) (quoted)
items.statement: For Re(s) > 1 (the formula extends to Re(s) > 0 with a conditionally convergent integral) and c > 0: 1/Γ(s) = (1/2πi) ∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞} e^{w} w^{−s} dw (principal branch of w^{−s}). Equivalently, for u > 0: ∫_{1−i∞}^{1+i∞} z^{−s} e^{uz} dz = 2πi u^{s−1}/Γ(s).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §3, proof of (3.3a), pp. 279–280 ('uses the Hankel integral formula for 1/Γ(s)')
items.note: Planned: the packet node QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.2/bromwich-integral-reciprocal-gamma ('Laplace's integral for the reciprocal of the Gamma function': for every real c > 0 and Re s > 1, 1/Γ(s) = (1/(2πi))∫_{c−i∞}^{c+i∞} t^{−s}e^{t}dt, absolutely convergent), planned for the module TauCeti/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Bessel. Re s > 1 suffices for GZ: the interchange of the u- and x-integrals in the proof of (3.3a) needs absolute convergence, i.e. Re s large, and V_s(0) is then continued analytically. The substitution w = uz gives the second form. Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti for 'Hankel': only Hankel matrices; Mathlib has Γ as an integral, reflection and duplication, and 1/Γ entire (Gamma/Beta.lean), but no contour formula. (The paper's use contains the misprint e^{−uz} for e^{uz}, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E35.)

items.name: Integral representation of K_ν and K_ν = K_{−ν} (quoted)
items.statement: For t > 0 and ν ∈ ℂ: ∫_0^∞ u^{ν−1} e^{−πt(u+1/u)} du = 2K_ν(2πt), where K_ν is the modified Bessel function of the second kind; K_ν = K_{−ν}.
items.note: No K-Bessel function in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched 'bessel' and 'besselK'). The paper needs K_ν only to rewrite V*_s (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/217) and for the estimate in (3.3b), which also follows from the u-integral directly (as the paper says). No atlas stage plans K_ν: 'K-Bessel' has 0 hits, and the Bessel mentions are Rademacher I-Bessel (QM.2) and Bessel-potential spaces (PDE). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Review: the same statement is PAPER-ZHANG-21/98 ('K_s(c) = ½∫_0^∞ e^{−c(u+u^{−1})/2}u^s du/u. Then K_s(c) is entire in s, K_{−s} = K_s ...'), routed as a source of AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0 ('owns ... parameter-integration tools, including the Bessel/Mellin calculation'), and that route is accepted in PAPER-ZHANG-21.review.json. With c = 2πt this is 2K_ν(2πt) = ∫_0^∞ u^{ν−1}e^{−πt(u+1/u)}du. Route this item to AL.0 as well, so that K_ν has one owner; PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/217 stays with GZ.6 and imports K_ν. (PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16/113 also routes a Whittaker–Bessel comparison mentioning K_ν to AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0; the lead may want to reconcile the two accepted routes.) Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 10: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0.

items.name: Legendre duplication formula and the Euler Beta integral (tools for (3.3a))
items.statement: Γ(s)Γ(s+½) = 2^{1−2s}√π Γ(2s); and for Re a, Re b > 0: ∫_0^∞ x^{2a−1}(x²+1)^{−(a+b)} dx = ½ Γ(a)Γ(b)/Γ(a+b), used in the form ∫_0^∞ x^{2k−2j−2}(x²+1)^{−(s+2k−1)} dx = ½ Γ(k−j−½)Γ(s+k+j−½)/Γ(s+2k−1).
items.note: Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Beta.lean:559: `theorem Gamma_mul_Gamma_add_half (s : ℂ) : Gamma s * Gamma (s + 1 / 2) = Gamma (2 * s) * (2 : ℂ) ^ (1 - 2 * s) * ↑(√π)` (namespace Complex); this is the same statement. :124 `Gamma_mul_Gamma_eq_betaIntegral {s t : ℂ} (hs : 0 < re s) (ht : 0 < re t) : Gamma s * Gamma t = Gamma (s + t) * betaIntegral s t`, with `betaIntegral u v = ∫ x in 0..1, x^(u-1)(1-x)^(v-1)` (:60). The (0, ∞) form used by GZ is the substitution x² = y/(1−y), which is not stated separately in Mathlib.

items.name: Corollary (3.4): the Fourier expansion of Φ̃_{−r} for 0 ≤ r ≤ k−1
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. For r ∈ ℤ, 0 ≤ r ≤ k−1 (Φ̃ continued in s through its Fourier coefficients): Φ̃_{−r}(z) = Σ_{m=0}^{∞} ( Σ_{0≤n≤mδ/N} e_{n,r}(y) r_𝒜(mδ − nN) ) e^{2πimz}, where e_{n,r}(y) := e_{−r}(n, Ny/δ) e^{2πNny/δ} is given by e_{0,r}(y) = L(2k−2r−1, ε)(Ny)^{−r} if r < k−1, and e_{0,k−1}(y) = [L(1, ε) − ε(N)(π/√δ) L(0, ε)] (Ny)^{1−k}; e_{n,r}(y) = (−1)^{k−r} ε(N) (2π/√δ) (Ny)^{r−2k+2} p_{k,r}(4πNny/δ) Σ_{d|n, d>0} ε_𝒜(n, d) d^{2r−2k+2} for n > 0, with p_{k,r} as in (3.3d) and ε_𝒜(n, d) as in (3.2). The coefficients are polynomials in 1/y of degree r.
items.note: Checked from (3.1), (3.2) and (3.3d). The terms with n < 0 vanish because V_{−r}(t) = 0 for t < 0. V_{−r}(0) = 0 for r < k−1 since 1/Γ(−r) = 0 while Γ(2k−2−2r) is finite; V_{1−k}(0) = −πi from the limit Γ(2h)/Γ(1−k+h) → (−1)^{k−1}(k−1)!/2. The factor e^{−2πNny/δ} of V_{−r} cancels against e^{2πNny/δ}. For r = k−1 the bracket equals (1 − ε(N))L(1, ε), by L(1, ε) = πL(0, ε)/√δ; §4 uses this, but it is not stated here. This finite formula at s = 0 (r = 0) and s = 1−k (r = k−1) feeds Propositions (4.4) ff. No library or plan (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/186). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Φ̃_{0,𝒜} is a holomorphic modular form
items.statement: Standing notation (Ch. IV §0, p. 267): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, δ = |D|, ε(n) = (D/n) the odd primitive quadratic character of conductor δ, w = #O_K^×, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K an ideal class, r_𝒜(n) = #{integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜} (n ≥ 1), r_𝒜(0) = 1/w; k ≥ 1 an integer; N ≥ 1 with (N, D) = 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_{2k}^new(Γ₀(N)); L_𝒜(f,s) = L^{(N)}(2s−2k+1, ε) Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_𝒜(n) n^{−s} (0.1); z = x+iy ∈ ℌ, q = e^{2πiz}, e(x) = e^{2πix}, e_n(a) = e^{2πia/n}. From §2 on: D odd, so (D, 2N) = 1, D squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; for a decomposition D = D₁·D₂ into fundamental discriminants (D_i = 1 allowed), δ_i = |D_i|, ε_i = ε_{D_i} (mod δ_i), 𝔡_i the integral ideal of norm δ_i (product of ramified primes, 𝔡_i² = (D_i)), 𝒟₁ the class of 𝔡₁, χ_{D₁·D₂} the genus character of §0 (χ(𝔞) = ε_{D₁}(N𝔞) = ε_{D₂}(N𝔞)), κ(D₁) = 1 or i as D₁ > 0 or D₁ < 0. At s = 0, Φ̃_{0,𝒜} ∈ M_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) (holomorphic, not in general cuspidal). This is the case r = 0 of (3.4); a priori it holds because ℰ_s(z) is holomorphic in z at s = 0.
items.note: With r = 0, p_{k,0}(T) = (T/2)^{2k−2}/(2k−2)!, so every e_{n,0} is constant in y. The a-priori argument is literal only for k ≥ 2, where the weight-(2k−1) series converges absolutely at s = 0. For k = 1 holomorphy at s = 0 follows from the Fourier expansion: V_0(0) = −πi and the exponent of y is 0. The paper postpones the k = 1 modifications to §6, so this is not recorded as a gap. No library or plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Nearest plan: for k ≥ 2, E^{(1)}_0 is a holomorphic Eisenstein series of weight 2k−1 and character ε on Γ₀(|D|), of the kind planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-0-diamond-operators-and-modular-forms-with-character-nebentypus, so Φ̃_0 = Tr^{ND}_N(θ_𝒜E^{(1)}_0(Nz)) is holomorphic a priori; the layer does not plan the trace or the product with θ_𝒜.

items.name: (4.1) Functional equation of the kernel coefficients e*_s(n, y)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Let n ∈ ℤ satisfy (4.2): Nn + l ≡ 0 (mod D) for some l = N(𝔞), 𝔞 an integral ideal in A, and y > 0. Put e*_s(n,y) := π^{−s} δ^s Γ(s+2k−1) e_s(n,y). Then e*_s(n,y) = −ε(N) e*_{2−2k−s}(n,y) for all s. Explicitly: e*_s(0,y) = (s+k)(s+k+1)⋯(s+2k−2)[π^{−s}δ^sΓ(s+k)L(2s+2k−1,ε)](δy)^s − ε(N)(2−k−s)(3−k−s)⋯(−s)[π^{1/2−s}δ^{s−1/2}Γ(s+k−1/2)L(2s+2k−2,ε)](δy)^{2−2k−s}, the two brackets being interchanged by s ↦ 2−2k−s by the functional equation of L(s,ε); and for n ≠ 0, e*_s(n,y) = −iε(N)|n|^k π^{2k−1} δ^{−2k+3/2} y V*_s(ny) Σ_{d|n, d>0} ε_A(n,d)(|n|/d²)^{s+k−1}, so that (4.1) for n ≠ 0 follows from V*_s(t) = sgn(t)V*_{2−2k−s}(t) (Prop. 3.3c) and (4.3).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §4, (4.1)–(4.2) and the two displays after (4.2), p. 282
items.note: Checked by hand on the page image: the n = 0 formula follows from Prop. (3.2) and (3.3a) with the duplication formula (2^{−2s−2k+3}Γ(2s+2k−2) = π^{−1/2}Γ(s+k−1)Γ(s+k−1/2)); writing both brackets as (δ/π)^{1/2−k}Λ(σ) with Λ(σ) = (δ/π)^{(σ+1)/2}Γ((σ+1)/2)L(σ,ε), σ = 2s+2k−1 resp. 2s+2k−2, they are swapped by s ↦ 2−2k−s exactly when Λ(σ) = Λ(1−σ) (root number +1, item PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/226). The n ≠ 0 display follows from (3.2) and the definition of V*_s. No library statement: neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has the Rankin kernel Φ̃_s, the Eisenstein combination 𝓔_s, its coefficients e_s(n,y) or V_s(t) (searched: Rankin, Poincaré, nonholomorphic/real-analytic Eisenstein; the only real-analytic Eisenstein series in the atlas is the packet node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series, a different series). Nearest plan: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 ‘Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels and their central derivatives … Prove the functional-equation vanishing that permits differentiation’ — the same method for YZZ's adelic weight-2 kernel, not this classical weight-2k coefficient identity, whose specialisation is not planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (4.3) Symmetry of the genus signs: ε_A(n, |n|/d) = −ε(N) sgn(n) ε_A(n, d)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Let n ≠ 0 satisfy (4.2): Nn + l ≡ 0 (mod D) for some l = N(𝔞), 𝔞 an integral ideal in A and let d be a positive divisor of n. Then ε_A(n, |n|/d) = −ε(N)·sgn(n)·ε_A(n, d). (Both sides vanish unless (d, n/d, D) = 1. If (d, n/d, D) = 1 write D = D₀D′D″ with D₀, D′, D″ discriminants, |D′| = (d, D), |D″| = (n/d, D), D₀ prime to n; then the product ε_A(n,d)ε_A(n,|n|/d) equals ε_{D₀}(|n|) ε_{D′D″}(−N sgn n) χ_{D₀·D′D″}(A), and (4.2) gives χ_{D₀·D′D″}(A) = ε_{D₀}(l) = ε_{D₀}(−Nn), whence the product is ε_D(−N sgn n) = −ε(N)sgn(n).) In particular, if ε(N) = +1 and n > 0 satisfies (4.2), then Σ_{d|n, d>0} ε_A(n,d) = 0.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §4, (4.3) and its proof, pp. 282–283
items.note: Checked on the page images (p. 283): the three-way splitting and the product formula are correct; ε_D(−N sgn n) = ε(−1)ε(N)ε(sgn n) = −ε(N)sgn(n) since ε is odd. Hypothesis (4.2) is essential (it is what makes χ_{D₀·D′D″}(A) = ε_{D₀}(−Nn)); see issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E37. Library: Tau Ceti has genus characters of a fundamental discriminant (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Quadratic/GenusCharacter/Basic.lean, genusCharFun, and CoprimeIdeal.lean, genusCharFunCoprimeIdealHom) but no ε_A(n,d) and no statement of this symmetry. No stage plans this computation (searched atlas stage descriptions and packets for ‘genus character’, ‘Rankin’, ‘Gross–Zagier’). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Functional equation of L(s, ε) with root number +1 (quoted input)
items.statement: Let ε = (D/·) with D < 0 a fundamental discriminant, δ = |D|. Then Λ(s, ε) := (δ/π)^{(s+1)/2} Γ((s+1)/2) L(s, ε) extends to an entire function and Λ(1−s, ε) = Λ(s, ε). (Used in §4 to swap the two brackets of e*_s(0,y) under s ↦ 2−2k−s, and in §5 to rewrite the n = 0 term of b_{m,r}: ‘We have used the functional equation of L(s, ε)’, p. 290.)
items.locator: Chapter IV, §4, p. 282 (‘by the functional equation of L(s, ε)’) and §5, p. 290 (after (5.4))
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:284: theorem DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N} (hχ : IsPrimitive χ) (s : ℂ) : completedLFunction χ (1 − s) = N ^ (s − 1/2) * rootNumber χ * completedLFunction χ⁻¹ s, with rootNumber χ = gaussSum χ stdAddChar / I^(0 or 1) / N^(1/2) (line 272). For ε real, χ⁻¹ = χ, so this is the needed equation up to the root number; the evaluation rootNumber ε = 1 (Gauss's sign τ(ε) = i√δ) is in neither library (Mathlib only has rootNumber_modOne; Tau Ceti's Multiquadratic/Cyclotomic/GaussSum.lean only proves τ² = p*) and no stage or packet plans it (searched ‘Gauss sum sign’, ‘quadratic Gauss sum’, ‘rootNumber’). Hence status missing although the general functional equation is in Mathlib. GZ's use needs the sign exactly: with root number −1 the two brackets in e*_s(0,y) would not be interchanged. Routed (source) to AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.1.

items.name: Analytic class number formula for K: L(1, ε) = πh/(u√δ), L(0, ε) = h/u (implicit input)
items.statement: For K imaginary quadratic of discriminant D < 0 (δ = |D|, h = h_K, w = 2u = #O_K^×) and ε = (D/·): L(1, ε) = 2πh/(w√δ) = πh/(u√δ), and (by the functional equation PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/226) L(0, ε) = 2h/w = h/u. Used implicitly: the n = 0 coefficient L(1,ε) − ε(N)(π/√δ)L(0,ε) of e_{0,k−1} becomes (2πh/(u√δ)) when ε(N) = −1, giving the term (h/u)r_A(m) of Prop. (4.4); and in Prop. (4.5) the m-th coefficient of the n = 0 term, (N^{k−1}√δ/2π)·2L(1,ε)(Ny)^{1−k}[…]·r_A(mδ), becomes (h/u)r_A(m)y^{1−k}[…]; the same factor h/u then appears in Theorems (5.6) and (5.8).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §4, Propositions (4.4) and (4.5), pp. 283–284 (used without comment)
items.note: Status made consistent with PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/98, which records the same formula L(1, ε) = πh/(u√|D|) (Chapter II §4, p. 249) as planned by AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4 ('Connect number-field ideal counting, Hecke characters and completed L-functions to the analytic class-number formula and Chebotarev'), through the factorisation ζ_K(s) = ζ(s)L(s, ε) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/97, also recorded as planned generically by AN.4). This is planning of the general setting: the AN.4 nodes in research/blueprint/packets/AnalyticNumberTheory--AN.0.json (dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue, artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy, hecke-primitive-functional-equation) state the residue of ζ_K and Artin induction, not the imaginary quadratic formula itself. Library (partial, not the statement): Mathlib NumberTheory/NumberField/DedekindZeta.lean:77, NumberField.tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT, gives the residue 2^{r₁}(2π)^{r₂}Rh/(w√|d_K|) = 2πh/(w√|D|) of ζ_K at s = 1; the factorisation is in neither library. The second formula L(0, ε) = h/u follows from the first by the functional equation with root number +1, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/226, which is missing (the sign of the quadratic Gauss sum is neither in the libraries nor planned). Used without comment in (4.4), (4.5), (5.6), (5.8) and §6; checked numerically: L(1, χ₋₇) = 1.1874104117… = π/√7, L(1, χ₋₁₁) = 0.9472258250… = π/√11, and the constants of (4.4), (4.5), (5.6), (5.8) that depend on it were confirmed numerically (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/246, /251, /259). Named in the source route to AnalyticNumberTheory (AN.1, AN.4) as a planned item for which the paper is a source.

items.name: r_A(mδ) = r_A(m) (implicit step)
items.statement: With the standing notation (D odd, so D squarefree), for every m ≥ 0 and every class A: r_A(m|D|) = r_A(m). (The different 𝔡 = (√D) is principal and every integral ideal of norm m|D| is divisible by every ramified prime, hence equals 𝔡·𝔟 with N(𝔟) = m; for m = 0 both sides are 1/w.)
items.locator: Chapter IV, §4, used in (4.4) and (4.5) (the n = 0 term of Cor. (3.4), r_A(mδ − 0·N), is printed as r_A(m)), pp. 283–284; Theorems (5.6), (5.8) use both forms
items.note: Implicit identification, needed to match Cor. (3.4) (whose n = 0 term has r_A(mδ)) with the (h/u)r_A(m) of Props. (4.4)/(4.5). Checked: for squarefree odd D every ideal of norm divisible by p | D is divisible by the unique prime above p, and 𝔡 = (√D). Theorem (5.6) keeps r_A(m|D|) while (5.8) uses r_A(m); consistent by this identity. No library statement (Tau Ceti has ideal-count bounds in NumberTheory/EffectiveBounds/IdealCount but no class-restricted ideal counts r_A); not planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

Genus notation (p. 284–285): {𝔫} is the genus of any integral ideal 𝔫 of K with N(𝔫) ≡ ε(N)N (mod D) (independent of the choice); {A𝔫} its product with the genus of A; R_{A𝔫}(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in the genus {A𝔫} (for n = 0 the sum of r_B(0) over the classes B of that genus); δ(n) = 2^s, s = number of prime factors of (n, D) (δ(0) = 2^t, t = number of prime factors of D). For a prime p with ε(p) ≠ 1, {𝔠} denotes the genus of any integral ideal 𝔠 with N(𝔠) ≡ −p (mod D): for ε(p) = −1 this is the genus attached to −p ∈ {x ∈ (ℤ/Dℤ)^× : ε(x) = 1}; for ε(p) = 0 it is the genus whose genus characters at the primes p′ | D, p′ ≠ p, are (−p/p′) (the character at p being fixed by the product formula); explicitly 𝔠 = 𝔮 with N(𝔮) ≡ −p (mod D) if ε(p) = −1, and 𝔠 = 𝔮𝔭 with 𝔭² = (p) and N(𝔮) ≡ −1 (mod D/p) if ε(p) = 0.

items.name: Genus theory: {genera of K} ↔ {x ∈ (ℤ/Dℤ)^× : ε(x) = 1}/(ℤ/Dℤ)^{×2}; each genus has h/2^{t−1} classes (quoted input)
items.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic with odd fundamental discriminant D having t prime factors. The map sending an ideal class to the residue mod D of the norm of any integral ideal in it prime to D (modulo squares) induces a bijection {genera of K} = Cl_K/Cl_K² ≅ {x ∈ (ℤ/Dℤ)^× : ε(x) = 1}/(ℤ/Dℤ)^{×2}; equivalently the t genus characters χ_p (p | D) separate genera and take exactly the sign vectors of product 1. Hence there are 2^{t−1} genera, each containing h/2^{t−1} ideal classes.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §4, Remark 1 after (4.6), p. 285 (‘the usual correspondence’); §5, p. 291 (‘each genus contains h/2^{t−1} ideal classes’)
items.note: TauCeti/NumberTheory/Multiquadratic/Quadratic/GenusCharacter/PrincipalGenus.lean:79 (a sign vector v indexed by the prime discriminants s of D is in the range of the genus-character family on Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)² iff Σ v = 0, i.e. product of signs 1), :112 (the family is injective on Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)²), :150 (principal genus theorem: a narrow class is a square iff all genus characters are 1); hypotheses: K = ℚ(θ), minpoly θ = X² − d, d squarefree, ∏_{P∈s} P = fundamentalDiscriminant d. This is the same statement in sign-vector form (via CRT, (ℤ/Dℤ)^×/squares ≅ {±1}^t by Legendre symbols, ε(x) = 1 being the product-one condition) and for Cl⁺(K), which equals Cl_K for imaginary K; the (ℤ/Dℤ)^× phrasing and the count h/2^{t−1} are immediate corollaries not stated as such.
