items.name: Proposition (5.1): holomorphic projection lemma (Sturm, GZ's version)
items.statement: Let k ≥ 2 (weight 2k > 2) and N ≥ 1. Let Φ̃ ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) (p. 270: a function Φ̃ : 𝔥 → ℂ, not necessarily holomorphic, with Φ̃|_{2k}γ = Φ̃ for all γ ∈ Γ₀(N) and (Φ̃|_{2k}γ)(z) = O(y^C) as y → ∞ for all γ ∈ SL₂(ℤ) and some C > 0) with Fourier expansion Φ̃(z) = Σ_{m∈ℤ} a_m(y) e^{2πimz}, and suppose (Φ̃|_{2k}α)(z) = O(y^{−ε}) as y = Im z → ∞, for some ε > 0 and every α ∈ SL₂(ℤ). For m > 0 put a_m := (4πm)^{2k−1}/(2k−2)! · ∫_0^∞ a_m(y) e^{−4πmy} y^{2k−2} dy. Then Φ(z) := Σ_{m≥1} a_m e^{2πimz} is a holomorphic cusp form of weight 2k and level N, and (f, Φ) = (f, Φ̃) for all f ∈ S_2k(Γ₀(N)). (Proof: unfold (Φ̃, P_m) against the Poincaré series P_m (item on P_m), using P*_m(z) = O(y^{1−2k}) uniformly under SL₂(ℤ); represent f ↦ (Φ̃, f) by some Φ ∈ S_2k (Riesz) and compare (Φ, P_m) = (2k−2)!(4πm)^{1−2k}b_m.)
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, (5.1) Proposition and proof, pp. 288–289; source: Sturm [33] (‘since our hypotheses are slightly different from Sturm's, prove’)
items.note: Proof checked (one misprint in the unfolding display, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E41; the first estimate uses |e^{2πiz}| where the c = 0 term is |e^{2πimz}| ≤ |e^{2πiz}|, which is correct as an inequality; the Γ₀(N)-invariant function P*_m|Φ̃|y^{2k} is O(y^{1−ε}), which justifies the unfolding). Library: no holomorphic projection and no Poincaré series in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched ‘holomorphic proj’, ‘Poincaré series’, ‘Sturm’ — the Sturm hits are the Sturm bound, TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/SturmBound.lean, a different theorem). The Petersson product of cusp forms exists (tauceti:CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosets, Petersson/FiniteIndex.lean:94; the pairing of a cusp form with an arbitrary function over a set D is tauceti:UpperHalfPlane.peterssonInner, Petersson/Basic.lean:107; both conjugate-linear in the FIRST argument, opposite to GZ). Planned only as a method: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 ‘Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels and their central derivatives, normalized local Whittaker terms, holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection’ plans holomorphic projection for Yuan–Zhang–Zhang's weight-2 kernels on quaternionic Shimura curves, and the roadmap's scope is weight 2 (its README: 'curves and abelian varieties parametrized by them'). The lemma here, for weight 2k > 2 (Sturm's lemma in GZ's hypotheses), is not a special case of that plan but the same method in higher weight; no stage, packet node or decomposition node states it (searched atlas stages, packets and decompositions for 'holomorphic projection', 'Sturm', 'Poincaré'). It is used only for k > 1 (Theorems (5.5), (5.6) for k > 1, (5.8)), so the higher-weight Part II must state it, importing the method from GZ.6. The Poincaré-series input is planned separately (QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3, node QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series: even weight ≥ 4, level N, the same series). Review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86): changed to missing. The statement is for weight 2k > 2, and GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights is weight two throughout (GZ.6 plans holomorphic projection only in weight two), so GZ.6 plans at most the method. It goes to the higher-weight Part II (route 8), which states and proves Sturm's lemma in weight 2k. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 8: HigherGreenFunctionCMValues (Part II).

items.name: Holomorphic Poincaré series P_m and the unfolding identity
items.statement: For k ≥ 2, N ≥ 1, m ≥ 1: P_m(z) := Σ_{γ∈Γ_∞\Γ₀(N)} (e^{2πimz})|_{2k}γ = Σ_{(a b; c d)∈Γ_∞\Γ₀(N)} (cz+d)^{−2k} e^{2πim(az+b)/(cz+d)}, Γ_∞ = {±(1 n; 0 1)}. The series converges absolutely (k > 1) and P_m ∈ S_2k(Γ₀(N)). Its majorant P*_m (absolute values of the terms) satisfies P*_m(z) ≤ e^{−2πy} + y^{−k}(E(z,k) − y^k) = O(y^{1−2k}) as y → ∞, and the same bound holds for P*_m|_{2k}α, α ∈ SL₂(ℤ). Unfolding: for Φ̃ as in (5.1), (Φ̃, P_m) = ∫_0^∞ e^{−4πmy} a_m(y) y^{2k−2} dy; in particular for Φ = Σ b_n q^n ∈ S_2k(Γ₀(N)), (Φ, P_m) = (2k−2)!/(4πm)^{2k−1} · b_m.
items.note: Checked (the Γ₀(N)-invariance of P*_m(z)|Φ̃(z)|y^{2k} and its O(y^{1−ε}) bound justify the interchange). Packet node QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series: ‘For N ≥ 1, an even integer k ≥ 4 and m ∈ ℤ: P(m, k, N; τ) := Σ_{A ∈ Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} (e(mτ)|_kA)(τ) … The series converges absolutely and locally uniformly for k ≥ 3 when m ≥ 0’ — the same series with their k = GZ's 2k ≥ 4; stage QM.3 ‘construct Poincare series and pairing/exact-sequence interfaces’. The unfolding identity (Petersson coefficient formula) is covered only by that stage sentence, not by a node, and the majorant estimate is not planned explicitly. No library object (no Poincaré series in Mathlib or Tau Ceti).

items.name: Growth of the SL₂(ℤ) Eisenstein series: E(z,s) = y^s + O(y^{1−s}) (quoted input)
items.statement: For real s > 1 let E(z,s) = Σ_{γ∈Γ_∞\SL₂(ℤ)} Im(γz)^s = Σ_{(c,d)=1, mod ±} y^s/|cz+d|^{2s}. Then E(z,s) = y^s + O(y^{1−s}) as y → ∞ (uniformly in x).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, proof of (5.1), p. 289 (‘since for any s > 1 the Eisenstein series E(z,s) for SL₂(ℤ) satisfies E(z,s) = y^s + O(y^{1−s})’)
items.note: Used with s = k to bound the Poincaré majorant. No non-holomorphic Eisenstein series in Mathlib (NumberTheory/ModularForms/EisensteinSeries/* are the holomorphic ones; Summable.lean gives summability of Σ|cz+d|^{−k}, not the asymptotic) or Tau Ceti (grep ‘nonholomorphic’, ‘real-analytic Eisenstein’: none). Planned in general form by AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.1 ‘Prove absolute convergence of the Eisenstein sum over P(F)\G(F) in a specified positive chamber, locally uniform convergence with differentiated growth estimates and automorphy. Derive its constant term’ (for GL₂/ℚ the constant term y^s + φ(s)y^{1−s} plus exponential decay of the rest gives the estimate); the classical level-one specialisation is not a separate node. A different real-analytic Eisenstein series (level N, congruence classes) is the packet node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/real-analytic-eisenstein-series.

items.name: Riesz representation on S_2k(Γ₀(N)) (quoted input)
items.statement: S_2k(Γ₀(N)) with the Petersson product is a finite-dimensional Hilbert space; hence every antilinear functional f ↦ (Φ̃, f) on it is of the form f ↦ (Φ, f) for a unique Φ ∈ S_2k(Γ₀(N)).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, proof of (5.1), p. 289 (‘the map f ↦ (Φ̃, f) is an antilinear map … so is represented by (Φ, ·) for some holomorphic cusp form Φ’)
items.note: Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Dual.lean:137: InnerProductSpace.toDual : E ≃ₗᵢ⋆[𝕜] StrongDual 𝕜 E for a complete inner product space (Fréchet–Riesz). Tau Ceti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Petersson/FiniteIndex.lean:296: CuspForm.peterssonInnerCosetsCore : InnerProductSpace.Core ℂ (CuspForm (Γ.map (mapGL ℝ)) k) for finite-index Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) (positive definite, Hermitian). Caveat: Tau Ceti deliberately does not derive the InnerProductSpace instance from the core (docstring at :285–296), so the composite statement for cusp forms is one instance-construction away; completeness follows from finite-dimensionality (used in Petersson/Orthogonal.lean, isCompl_peterssonOrthogonal :201). Tau Ceti's pairing is conjugate-linear in the first argument, GZ's in the second.

items.name: Holomorphic projection of forms with polynomial-in-1/y coefficients (special case of (5.1))
items.statement: Let k ≥ 2 and Φ̃ ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) be small at the cusps ((Φ̃|α)(x+iy) = O(y^{−ε}) for all α ∈ SL₂(ℤ)), with Fourier coefficients that are polynomials of degree ≤ 2k−2 in 1/y. Then the holomorphic form obtained from Φ̃ by dropping the terms y^{−j} (the constant term) and replacing each term y^{−j}e^{2πimz} (m > 0, 0 ≤ j ≤ 2k−2) by ((2k−2−j)!/(2k−2)!)(4πm)^j e^{2πimz} has the same Petersson product as Φ̃ with every f ∈ S_2k(Γ₀(N)).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, paragraph after the proof of (5.1), p. 289
items.note: Checked: (4πm)^{2k−1}/(2k−2)!·∫_0^∞ y^{−j}e^{−4πmy}y^{2k−2}dy = (2k−2−j)!(4πm)^j/(2k−2)!. Gamma integral in Mathlib: Real.integral_rpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_Ioi (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Basic.lean:465). Planned only as a method, as for (5.1) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/239): GZ.6 plans holomorphic projection for weight-2 kernels; this weight-2k > 2 rule is stated in no stage or node and belongs with (5.1) in the higher-weight Part II. Review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86): changed to missing. The statement is for weight 2k > 2, and GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights is weight two throughout (GZ.6 plans holomorphic projection only in weight two), so GZ.6 plans at most the method. It goes to the higher-weight Part II (route 8), which states and proves Sturm's lemma in weight 2k. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 8: HigherGreenFunctionCMValues (Part II).

items.name: Holomorphic projection of Φ̃_{−r} (0 ≤ r ≤ k−1) and the relation a_{m,r} = C_r b_{m,r}
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Let 0 ≤ r ≤ k−1. Φ̃_{−r} (Cor. (3.4)) is holomorphic for r = 0; for r ≥ 1 (so k > 1) it is small at all cusps (at ∞ its constant term is a multiple of y^{−r} and the other terms are O(e^{−2πy}); at the other cusps by the trace-of-theta-times-Eisenstein description), so its holomorphic projection is Φ_{−r} = Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,r}q^m with a_{m,r} = (4πm)^{2k−1}/(2k−2)! · Σ_{n=0}^{[mδ/N]} r_A(mδ − nN) ∫_0^∞ e_{n,r}(y)e^{−4πmy}y^{2k−2}dy = (−1)^{k−r} 2^{2k−1} ε(N) r! π^{2k−1−r} / ((2k−2)! N^r |D|^{2k−r−3/2}) · b_{m,r}, with b_{m,r} as in (5.2)–(5.4) (for r ≤ k−2; for r = k−1 the n = 0 term of b_{m,r} is doubled).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, pp. 289–290 (paragraph before (5.2) and the display defining a_{m,r})
items.note: The a_{m,r} ↔ b_{m,r} constant re-derived: for n > 0 the integral gives r!·(4π/δ)^r·P_{k,r}(Nn, mδ)·(2π/δ)^{2k−2−2r}(2π/√δ)N^{−r}σ_{2k−2r−2,A}(n)/(2k−2)!; for n = 0 the functional equation of L(s,ε) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/226) turns (4πm)^r(2k−2−r)!N^{−r}L(2k−2r−1,ε)/(2k−2)! into the same constant times P_{k,r}(0,mδ)σ_{2k−2r−2,A}(0). Numerically: for N = 1, k = 6, D = −7 and r = 1,…,4, Σ_m b_{m,r}q^m is exactly b_{1,r}·Δ (ratios −24, 252, −1472), and for r = 0 it is a modular form with the expected Eisenstein part. Nothing planned for this classical computation. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 8: HigherGreenFunctionCMValues (Part II).

items.name: (5.2)–(5.4): b_{m,r}, P_{k,r}(x,y) and σ_{2l,A}(n)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). For 0 ≤ r ≤ k−1, m ≥ 0: b_{m,r} := Σ_{0≤n≤m|D|/N} r_A(m|D| − nN)·P_{k,r}(Nn, m|D|)·σ_{2k−2r−2,A}(n) (5.2), where P_{k,r}(x, y) := Σ_{j=0}^{r} C(r, j)·C(2k−2+j−r, r)·(−x)^j y^{r−j} (5.3) and, for l ≥ 0, σ_{2l,A}(0) := −½ ε(N) L(−2l, ε), σ_{2l,A}(n) := Σ_{d|n} ε_A(n,d)(n/d)^{2l} for n > 0 (5.4).
items.note: Checked on the zoomed page image. Printed misprint: the sum in the second line of (5.4) is printed over 'n | d'; it must be over the positive divisors d | n (new issue recorded in this review). With d | n, and σ_{2l,A}(0) = −½ε(N)L(−2l, ε), the b_{m,r} were recomputed independently for N = 1, k = 6, D = −7 (Σ_m b_{m,r}q^m = b_{1,r}Δ for r = 1,…,4 and E₁₂-part plus multiple of Δ for r = 0) and for N = 3, k = 3, D = −7 (Σ_m b_{m,1}q^m = −12(η(z)η(3z))⁶), and they reproduce Theorem (5.5) with the corrected factorial. Note σ_{0,A}(n) = σ_A(n) for n > 0. P_{k,r} is a homogenised Jacobi polynomial (item PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/248). L(−2l, ε) = −B_{2l+1,ε}/(2l+1) is planned by DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0 (‘Construct generalized Bernoulli numbers … Compare the algebraic values with the complex analytic L-functions’), but b_{m,r} itself is not defined or planned anywhere. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 8: HigherGreenFunctionCMValues (Part II).

items.name: Theorem (5.5): L_A(f, 2k−1−r) for 0 ≤ r < k−1
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Let 0 ≤ r < k−1 and define b_{m,r} (m ≥ 0) by (5.2)–(5.4). Then Σ_{m≥0} b_{m,r}q^m is a modular form of weight 2k and level N (a cusp form if r ≠ 0), and L_A(f, 2k−1−r) = (−1)^{k−r}(2π)^{2(2k−1−r)}/(2k−2−r)! · 2^{2k−1}/(2k−2)! · ε(N) r!/|D|^{2k−r−3/2} · (f, Σ_m b_{m,r}q^m) for every f in the space spanned by newforms of weight 2k and level N. CORRECTED: the paper prints (2k−2−2r)! in the first denominator; the correct factor is (2k−2−r)! = Γ(2k−1−r) (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E42). The two agree only for r = 0.
items.note: Derivation: Prop. (1.2) at s = −r gives (4π)^{r−2k+1}N^{−r}Γ(2k−1−r)L_A(f,2k−1−r) = (f, Φ_{−r}), and a_{m,r} = C_r b_{m,r} with C_r as in the preceding item; hence the stated constant with Γ(2k−1−r) = (2k−2−r)!. Numerical confirmation (N = 1, f = Δ, k = 6, D = −7, h = 1, so L_A(Δ,s) = L(Δ,s)L(Δ⊗χ₋₇,s), computed by the approximate functional equation and cross-checked against the Dirichlet series at s = 11): with (2k−2−r)! the implied Petersson norm (Δ,Δ) is 1.03536205680432·10⁻⁶ for r = 0,1,2,3,4 (the known value), while the printed (2k−2−2r)! gives 1.15·10⁻⁷, 1.85·10⁻⁸, 4.93·10⁻⁹, 2.88·10⁻⁹ for r = 1,…,4. Also checked at N = 3, k = 3, D = −7, f = (η(z)η(3z))⁶, r = 1: consistent with Theorem (5.6) (corrected) at the same f. No library object; not planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 8: HigherGreenFunctionCMValues (Part II).

(3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). items.note: Checked the integrality claim σ_{2l,A}(0) ∈ ℤ, i.e. ½L(−2l,ε) = −B_{2l+1,ε}/(2(2l+1)) ∈ ℤ, for all odd fundamental D with −399 ≤ D ≤ −3 and l = 1,…,5: the only failures are at D ≥ −4l−3 (l = 1: D = −3, −7; l = 2: −3, −11; l = 3: −3; l = 4: −3, −7, −19; l = 5: −3, −23), so the bound is correct and sharp in this range (for l = 0, i.e. r = k−1, it fails, but that case is excluded from (5.5)). items.name: P_{k,k−1} is a Legendre polynomial and P_{k,r} a Jacobi polynomial
items.statement: For the polynomials of (5.3): P_{k,k−1}(x, y) = y^{k−1} P_{k−1}(1 − 2x/y), with P_{k−1} the (k−1)st Legendre polynomial; and in general P_{k,r}(x, y) = y^r P_r^{(2k−2−2r, 0)}(1 − 2x/y), with P_n^{(α,β)} the Jacobi polynomials.
items.note: Checked: P_{k,k−1}(x,y) = Σ_j C(k−1,j)C(k−1+j,j)(−x)^j y^{k−1−j}, and P_n(z) = Σ_j C(n,j)C(n+j,j)((z−1)/2)^j; the Jacobi case from P_n^{(α,0)}(z) = Σ_m C(n,m)C(n+α+m, n)((z−1)/2)^m with α = 2k−2−2r. Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/ShiftedLegendre.lean:37: Polynomial.shiftedLegendre n = Σ_{k≤n} (−1)^k C(n,k)C(n+k,n) X^k ∈ ℤ[X], which is exactly x ↦ P_n(1 − 2x); so the Legendre half is the homogenisation of a library polynomial (y^{k−1}·shiftedLegendre(k−1)(x/y)), but the identity itself is not stated. Jacobi polynomials are in neither library (grep ‘Jacobi polynomial’, ‘gegenbauer’: none) and not planned; status missing for the item as a whole. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 8: HigherGreenFunctionCMValues (Part II).

items.name: Legendre polynomials P_n (quoted standard object)
items.statement: P_n(z) = 2^{−n} Σ_{0≤j≤n/2} (−1)^j C(n, j) C(2n−2j, n) z^{n−2j}; equivalently P_n(z) = Σ_{j=0}^{n} C(n,j)C(n+j,j)((z−1)/2)^j, so that P_n(1 − 2x) = Σ_j (−1)^j C(n,j)C(n+j,j) x^j.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, p. 291 and Theorem (5.8), p. 294 (explicit formula for P_{k−1})
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/ShiftedLegendre.lean:37: noncomputable def Polynomial.shiftedLegendre (n : ℕ) : ℤ[X] := Σ_{k∈range(n+1)} C((−1)^k·n.choose k·(n+k).choose n)·X^k, with Rodrigues' formula factorial_mul_shiftedLegendre_eq (:43). This is the same polynomial after the affine change z = 1 − 2x (the only form in which GZ evaluate it: P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(m|D|))); the z-variable expansion printed in (5.8) is not in Mathlib. Checked that the (5.8) formula is the standard one.

items.name: Jacobi polynomials P_n^{(α,β)} (quoted standard object)
items.statement: P_n^{(α,β)}(z) = Γ(α+n+1)/(n!Γ(α+β+n+1)) Σ_{m=0}^{n} C(n,m) Γ(α+β+n+m+1)/Γ(α+m+1) ((z−1)/2)^m; used only for the remark P_{k,r}(x,y) = y^r P_r^{(2k−2−2r,0)}(1−2x/y).
items.note: Only a remark (‘these are much less familiar functions’); nothing depends on it. Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti; not planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 8: HigherGreenFunctionCMValues (Part II).

items.name: Theorem (5.6) for k = 1: the central value L_A(f,1) when ε(N) = −1
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Suppose ε(N) = −1 and k = 1. For m ≥ 0 define b_{m,A} = r_A(m|D|)·h/u + Σ_{0<n≤m|D|/N} δ(n) R_{A𝔫}(n) r_A(m|D| − nN), with δ(n), R_{A𝔫}(n) as in (4.6). Then Σ_{m≥0} b_{m,A}q^m is a modular form of weight 2 and level N, and L_A(f,1) = (8π²/√|D|)·(f, Σ_m b_{m,A}q^m) for every f in the space spanned by newforms of weight 2 and level N. (At k = 1 the printed constant (2π)^{2k}2^{2k−1}(k−1)!/((2k−2)!|D|^{k−1/2}) equals 8π²/√|D|, so E43 does not affect this case, and no holomorphic projection is needed because Φ̃ of (4.4) is holomorphic.) The case k ≥ 2 is PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/335.
items.note: Derivation from Prop. (4.4): holomorphic projection of y^{1−k}·p_{k−1}(4πNny/δ) gives (4πm)^{k−1}(k−1)!/(2k−2)!·P_{k−1}(1−2nN/(mδ)) (and (h/u)r_A(m) gives (4πm)^{k−1}(k−1)!/(2k−2)!·(h/u)r_A(m)), so a_m = (4π)^{k−1}(k−1)!/((2k−2)!δ^{k−1})·b_{m,A} (using σ_A(n) = δ(n)R_{A𝔫}(n) from (4.6a) and r_A(mδ) = r_A(m)); multiplying by the constant 2^{2k+1}π^{k+1}/((k−1)!√δ) of (4.4), the (k−1)! cancels: L_A(f,k) = 2^{4k−1}π^{2k}/((2k−2)!δ^{k−1/2})·(f, Σ b_{m,A}q^m). This is exactly parallel to the printed constant of Theorem (5.8), which does not carry (k−1)!. Numerically: N = 3, k = 3, D = −7, f = (η(z)η(3z))⁶: Σ b_{m,A}q^m = 6·f (checked to q⁵), and L_A(f,3) = L(f,3)L(f⊗χ₋₇,3) = 0.2183120582… gives (f,f) = 5.74981176452619·10⁻⁵ with the corrected constant — the same value as from Theorem (5.5) at r = 1 (corrected) — and half of it with the printed one. For k = 1 the formula is the analytic side of Gross's definite-quaternion formula (Ch. V §3); GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.5 plans the Waldspurger formula with ‘definite-quaternionic specializations’, but not this Fourier-coefficient statement, so status missing. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86): split. This item keeps the case k = 1, which Chapter V §3 uses; the case k ≥ 2 is PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/335, in the higher-weight Part II.

items.name: Theorem (5.6) for k ≥ 2: the central value L_A(f,k) when ε(N) = −1, in weight 2k > 2
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Suppose ε(N) = −1 and k ≥ 2. For m ≥ 0 define b_{m,A} = (m|D|)^{k−1}[ r_A(m|D|)·h/u + Σ_{0<n≤m|D|/N} δ(n) R_{A𝔫}(n) r_A(m|D| − nN) P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(m|D|)) ], with δ(n), R_{A𝔫}(n) as in (4.6) and P_{k−1} the Legendre polynomial. Then Σ_{m≥0} b_{m,A}q^m is a modular form of weight 2k and level N (a cusp form), and L_A(f,k) = (2π)^{2k} 2^{2k−1}/((2k−2)! |D|^{k−1/2}) · (f, Σ_m b_{m,A}q^m) for every f in the space spanned by newforms of weight 2k and level N. CORRECTED: the paper prints the constant (2π)^{2k}2^{2k−1}(k−1)!/((2k−2)!|D|^{k−1/2}); the factor (k−1)! must be deleted (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E43). The two agree for k = 1, 2.
items.note: Split off from PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/251 in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86): the case k ≥ 2 is a weight-2k > 2 statement, outside the weight-two GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights layers, and goes to the higher-weight Part II (route 8). The corrected constant (E43) was checked numerically in review against known Petersson norms (Δ at level 1, and (η(z)η(3z))⁶ at level 3, where the printed constant gives exactly half).

items.name: Example: N = 5, k = 2, D = −p (sum over classes) and the table of b₁
items.statement: Let p ≡ 3 (mod 4) be prime with (5/p) = −1, D = −p, N = 5, k = 2, ε = (·/p), and f = q − 4q² + 2q³ + 8q⁴ − ⋯ the unique normalised newform spanning S₄(Γ₀(5)). Summing Theorem (5.6) over all classes A (Σ_A L_A(f,s) = L(f,s)L_ε(f,s), P₁(x) = x): p^{3/2}/(64π⁴) · L(f,2)L_ε(f,2)/(f,f) = Σ_A b_{1,A} = p·h(−p) + Σ_{1≤n<p/5} (p − 10n) R(n) R(p − 5n), with R(n) = Σ_{d|n}(d/p) and h(−p) replaced by 1/3 for p = 3. The values for p = 3, 7, 23, 43, 47, 67, 83, 103, 107, 127, 163, 167, 223, 227, 263, 283 are 1, 1, 1, 49, 25, 121, 361, 25, 289, 25, 169, 81, 121, 2025, 1, 121 — all squares, in accordance with Waldspurger's theorem.
items.note: Recomputed the right-hand side exactly (class numbers from reduced forms): all 16 printed values are correct and the printed list of p is complete up to 283; the next values are 4489 (p = 307), 225 (347), 1 (367), 441 (383), all squares. Checked the eigenform (η(z)η(5z))⁴ = q − 4q² + 2q³ + 8q⁴ − 5q⁵ − ⋯. The constant 64π⁴/p^{3/2} agrees with both the printed and the corrected constant of (5.6) because (k−1)! = 1 for k = 2. The step Σ_A L_A = L(f,s)L_ε(f,s) is (0.3)/(0.4) (chunk covering pp. 267–269). Not planned. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 8: HigherGreenFunctionCMValues (Part II).

items.name: Waldspurger's theorem (quoted, for the squareness of the example values)
items.statement: (As invoked:) the central values L(f,k)L(f⊗ε,k), suitably normalised, are squares — more precisely, Waldspurger's theorem expresses L(f,k)L(f⊗ε_D,k) (or the product of the central values of a form and its twist) as the square of a toric period / Fourier coefficient of a half-integral-weight form, times explicit factors, so the rational numbers Σ_A b_{1,A} of the example are squares.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, p. 292 (‘in accordance with Waldspurger's theorem, they are all squares’)
items.note: Quoted without statement or reference number on this page; nothing in the proof depends on it. Planned: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.5 ‘Establish the Waldspurger period formula for the stated GL₂/quaternionic toric data. Give the actual pairing identity including adjoint L-value, zeta/eta factors and normalized local toric forms … Export the explicit split, ramified and definite-quaternionic specializations’. The squareness of the specific example (definite quaternion algebra ramified at 5 and ∞, weight 4) is a specialisation that GZ.5 exports only in general terms. No library statement.

items.name: Growth of Φ̃ of Prop. (4.5) at the cusps (k > 1)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chapter IV (pp. 267–282): K = ℚ(√D) imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant D < 0, assumed odd from §2 on (so D ≡ 1 mod 4, squarefree); δ = |D|; ε(n) = (D/n), the odd primitive quadratic character mod δ; h = #Cl_K; w = 2u = #O_K^×; A ∈ Cl_K a fixed ideal class; r_A(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in A (n ≥ 1), r_A(0) = 1/w; N ≥ 1 an integer prime to D; k ≥ 1; f = Σ a(n)qⁿ ∈ S_2k^new(Γ₀(N)); L_A(f,s) = L^(N)(2s−2k+1, ε)·Σ_{n≥1} a(n) r_A(n) n^{−s} (0.1); Petersson product (f,g) = ∫_{Γ₀(N)\𝔥} f(z) \overline{g(z)} y^{2k} dx dy/y² (linear in f, antilinear in g); Φ̃_s ∈ M̃_2k(Γ₀(N)) the Rankin kernel of Prop. (1.2), (4π)^{−s−2k+1} N^s Γ(s+2k−1) L_A(f, s+2k−1) = (f, Φ̃_s); e_s(n,y) the n-th Fourier coefficient of 𝓔_s (§3), so that Φ̃_s(z) = Σ_{n∈ℤ, l≥0, Nn+l≡0 (mod D)} e_s(n, Ny/δ) r_A(l) e^{−2πly/δ} e((Nn+l)x/δ) (3.1); for n ≠ 0 and 0 < d | n, ε_A(n,d) = 0 if (d, n/d, D) ≠ 1 and ε_A(n,d) = ε_{D₁}(d) ε_{D₂}(−Nn/d) χ_{D₁·D₂}(A) otherwise, where D = D₁D₂ with |D₂| = (d, D) and χ_{D₁·D₂} is the genus character (Prop. (3.2)); V_s(t), V*_s(t) = (π|t|)^{−s−2k+1}Γ(s+2k−1)V_s(t), p_{k,r}(t) and q_{k−1}(t) = ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}x^{−k}e^{−xt}dx as in Prop. (3.3). Suppose ε(N) = +1 and k > 1, and let Φ̃ be as in Prop. (4.5) with coefficients a_m(y) (of e^{2πimz}). Using p_{k−1}(t) = O(t^{k−1}), q_{k−1}(t) = O(t^{k−1}e^{−t}) (t → ∞), σ′_A(n), r_A(n) = O(n^ε): a_m(y) = O(m^{k+ε}) (m > 0), O(y^{1−k} log y) (m = 0), O(|m|^{k+ε}e^{−4π|m|y}) (m < 0), uniformly for y ≥ 1; hence Φ̃(z) = O(y^{1−k} log y), and the same holds at every cusp (by the theta × Eisenstein description). So Φ̃ satisfies the hypotheses of Prop. (5.1).

items.note: Checked at ∞ (for m < 0 only n ≥ |m|δ/N contribute and q_{k−1}(4πnNy/δ) ≤ e^{−4π|m|y}·(…)); the estimate q_{k−1}(t) = O(t^{k−1}e^{−t}) is meant for t → ∞ (as t → 0, q_{k−1}(t) grows like log(1/t)), which is the regime used since n ≥ 1 and y → ∞. The other cusps are asserted, not computed (‘as we can see by going back to the definition’). No library/plan. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. items.name: The four integrals in the holomorphic projection of Prop. (4.5)
items.statement: For k ≥ 1, m, n, N, δ > 0 and z = 1 + 2nN/(mδ): (i) ∫_0^∞ p_{k−1}(4πnNy/δ) y^{k−1}e^{−4πmy} dy = (k−1)!/(4πm)^k · P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(mδ)); (ii) ∫_0^∞ y^{k−1} log y · e^{−4πmy} dy = ∂/∂s(Γ(s)/(4πm)^s)|_{s=k} = (k−1)!/(4πm)^k (Γ′/Γ(k) − log 4πm); (iii) ∫_0^∞ y^{k−1}e^{−4πmy}dy = (k−1)!/(4πm)^k; (iv) ∫_0^∞ q_{k−1}(4πnNy/δ) y^{k−1}e^{−4πmy} dy = (k−1)!/(4πm)^k ∫_1^∞ (x−1)^{k−1}dx/(x^k(1 + nNx/(mδ))^k) = (k−1)!/(4πm)^k · 2Q_{k−1}(z), the last step by the substitution x = 1 + √((z+1)/(z−1))·e^t, which gives ∫_{−∞}^{∞} dt/(z + √(z²−1) cosh t)^k [printed substitution x = 1 + √((z−1)/(z+1))e^t; issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E45].
items.note: All four checked by hand; (i) is the same computation as in (5.6). Library: only (iii) is in Mathlib (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Basic.lean:465, Real.integral_rpow_mul_exp_neg_mul_Ioi {a r : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hr : 0 < r) : ∫ t in Ioi 0, t^(a−1)·exp(−(r·t)) = (1/r)^a·Gamma a); (ii) needs differentiation under the integral; (i), (iv) and Legendre functions of the second kind are absent. Not planned. Status missing for the item as a whole. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 8: HigherGreenFunctionCMValues (Part II).

items.name: (5.7) Legendre function of the second kind Q_{k−1} and its integral representation (quoted)
items.statement: For k ≥ 1, Q_{k−1} is the function on z > 1 characterised by Q_{k−1}(z) = ½P_{k−1}(z) log((z+1)/(z−1)) + (polynomial in z) and Q_{k−1}(z) = O(z^{−k}) as z → ∞ (5.7); Q₀(z) = ½log((z+1)/(z−1)), Q₁(z) = ½z log((z+1)/(z−1)) − 1. It has the integral representation 2Q_{k−1}(z) = ∫_{−∞}^{∞} dt/(z + √(z²−1) cosh t)^k (Heine).
items.locator: Chapter IV, §5, (5.7) and the preceding sentence, p. 294 (‘Legendre function of the second kind as in Chap. II’)
items.note: Checked the characterisation, the two first values and the integral representation (numerically as well, e.g. Q₀(3) = ½log 2 and Q₁(3) = (3/2)log 2 − 1 against the hypergeometric formula; in this review 2Q_{k−1}(3) = ∫_{−∞}^{∞}(3 + √8 cosh t)^{−k}dt was confirmed for k = 1, 2, 3, 6). Q_{k−1} is the case s = k of the Legendre function Q_{s−1} of Chapter II (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/64, (2.5)–(2.6)); the integral representation is (2.5) with s = k, since the integrand is even in t. Both items must have the same owner layer: /64 is placed in GZ.7, this one in GZ.6; place both in the same layer. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has Legendre functions of the second kind (grep ‘second kind’, ‘legendreQ’: only Chebyshev/Stirling hits); no stage or packet plans them (the Legendre hits in packets are the Legendre elliptic curve and the Legendre symbol). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights (GZ.6 or GZ.7, together with /64). Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Theorem (5.8): the central derivative L′_A(f,k) for k > 1, ε(N) = +1
items.statement: Suppose k > 1, N ≥ 1, and A an ideal class of the imaginary quadratic field K of (odd) discriminant D with ε(N) = +1 (ε = (D/·)). For m > 0 put a_{m,A} = m^{k−1}[ −Σ_{0<n≤m|D|/N} σ′_A(n) r_A(m|D| − Nn) P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(m|D|)) + (h/u) r_A(m)(2Γ′/Γ(k) − 2 log 2π + log(N|D|/m) + 2L′/L(1, ε)) − 2 Σ_{n=1}^∞ σ_A(−n) r_A(m|D| + nN) Q_{k−1}(1 + 2nN/(m|D|)) ], with σ_A, σ′_A as in (4.4)–(4.6) (so σ_A(−n) = δ(n)R_{A𝔫}(n) by (4.6a)), P_{k−1} the Legendre polynomial and Q_{k−1} the Legendre function of the second kind (5.7). Then Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,A}q^m is a cusp form of weight 2k and level N, and L_A(f,k) = 0, L′_A(f,k) = 2^{4k−1}π^{2k}/((2k−2)!√|D|) · (f, Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,A}q^m) for all f in the space spanned by newforms of weight 2k and level N. CORRECTED: (a) the paper prints σ_A(n) in the last sum; it must be σ_A(−n) (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E38); (b) the paper writes Σ_{m≥0} in the final formula although a_{m,A} is defined only for m > 0 (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E46).
items.note: Derived from (4.5) + (5.1) + the four integrals: (2k−2)!/(4πm)^{2k−1}·a_m = (k−1)!/(4πm)^k·[…], and −log 4πm + log(Nδ/π) = −2log 2π + log(Nδ/m); renormalising a_m = (4π)^{k−1}(k−1)!/(2k−2)!·a_{m,A} gives the constant 2^{4k−1}π^{2k}/((2k−2)!√δ) (checked). Numerical confirmation (N = 1, f = Δ, k = 6, D = −7): with σ_A(−n), a_{2,A}/a_{1,A} = −24.0000000000 and a_{3,A}/a_{1,A} = 252.000000000, and L′_A(Δ,6) = L(Δ,6)·L′(Δ⊗χ₋₇,6) = 1.46317630872233 = 2^{23}π^{12}/(10!√7)·a_{1,A}·(Δ,Δ) with (Δ,Δ) = 1.03536205680432·10⁻⁶ (the known Petersson norm); with the printed σ_A(n) the coefficients are not proportional to Δ. Second check at level N = 3 (f = (η(z)η(3z))⁶, k = 3, D = −11, ε(3) = +1): a_{2,A}/a_{1,A} = −5.9999967, a_{4,A}/a_{1,A} = 4.00011 (tail truncated at n = 2000; exact values −6, 4 = a(2), a(4)), and L′_A(f,3) = L(f,3)L′(f⊗χ₋₁₁,3) = 3.92350251067 matches 2^{11}π⁶/(4!√11)·a_{1,A}·(f,f) to 6·10⁻⁸ with (f,f) = 5.74981176452619·10⁻⁵ obtained independently from the corrected (5.5)/(5.6) — which also confirms PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E43 against the paper's own (5.8) constant. Nearest plans: GZ.6/GZ.8 (YZZ's weight-2 analytic kernel and its specialisation to X₀(N)); nothing plans the weight-2k (k > 1) formula, whose arithmetic interpretation (Ch. V §4, heights of Heegner cycles) is also not planned (GeneralizedHeegnerCycles GH.0–GH.8 concern p-adic Abel–Jacobi images, not heights). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 8: HigherGreenFunctionCMValues (Part II).

items.name: Logarithmic growth condition (6.1) at the cusps
items.statement: Let Φ̃ ∈ M̃₂(Γ₀(N)), i.e. a smooth function on ℌ with Φ̃|₂γ = Φ̃ for all γ ∈ Γ₀(N) (Chap. IV §5). For a cusp ξ ∈ ℚ ∪ {∞} choose α ∈ SL₂(ℤ) with α(∞) = ξ. Φ̃ satisfies (6.1) at ξ if there are constants A_ξ, B_ξ and ε > 0 with (Φ̃|₂α)(z) = A_ξ log y + B_ξ + O(y^{−ε}) as y = Im z → ∞. Motivation stated on p. 295: for k = 1 the kernel Φ̃ of Prop. (4.5) has m = 0 Fourier term (A log y + B)y^{1−k} + O(e^{−cy}), all other terms exponentially small, so it grows like A log y + B instead of the decay O(y^{−ε}) required by Prop. (5.1); a priori there are 2H constants A_ξ, B_ξ (H = number of cusps).
items.note: No carrier for a non-holomorphic weight-2 Γ₀(N)-invariant function with prescribed log-growth at every cusp exists in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. Nearest: Tau Ceti cusp-vanishing/boundedness of slashed functions, tauceti:IsZeroAt/IsBoundedAt lemmas in TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps/Rat/Slash.lean:55-77 (isZeroAt_rat_slash, isBoundedAt_rat_slash: holomorphic-type conditions, not log growth). The growth-condition bookkeeping is part of holomorphic projection, whose adelic version GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 plans ("Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels ..., holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection"), but no stage names this classical condition. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Cusps of Γ₀(N): number and invariants (quoted standard fact)
items.statement: The number H of cusps of Γ₀(N) is Σ_{N₁ | N, N₁ > 0} φ(gcd(N₁, N/N₁)) (φ = Euler's function). A cusp ξ = a/c with (a, c) = 1 is determined by the pair of invariants N₁ = (c, N) and the class of (c/N₁)^{−1}·a modulo (N₁, N/N₁).
items.note: Planned by the Tau Ceti ModularForms roadmap, Layer 10A: "For congruence subgroups, prove cofiniteness, identify its cusp-orbit subtype with Γ\ℙ¹(ℚ), and compute the cusp count ε∞". The explicit Γ₀(N) formula and the (N₁, class) invariants are not named there (planning of the general setting, of which this is the Γ₀(N) case). Library: Mathlib has only the surjection from cosets to cusp orbits (mathlib:cosetToCuspOrbit, Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps.lean:174; surjective_cosetToCuspOrbit :195) and widths (CongruenceSubgroup.strictWidthInfty_Gamma0 :448); Tau Ceti has cusp widths (tauceti:TauCeti.Subgroup.integerCuspWidth, TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps/Basic.lean:143). No count formula found (grep for totient in both ModularForms trees: none).

items.name: Hecke's-trick Poincaré series P_{m,s} of weight 2 and the unfolding identity
items.statement: For N ≥ 1, m ≥ 1 and Re(s) > 0 put P_{m,s}(z) = Σ_{Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} y^s e^{2πimz}|₂γ = Σ_{(a b; c d) ∈ Γ∞\Γ₀(N)} (cz+d)^{−2}|cz+d|^{−2s} y^s e^{2πim(az+b)/(cz+d)} (absolutely convergent). The majorant P*_{m,σ} (σ = Re s, termwise absolute values) is O(y^{−1−σ}) at every cusp with O-constant O(σ^{−1}) as σ → 0. If Φ̃ = Σ a_m(y)e^{2πimx} ∈ M̃₂(Γ₀(N)) is O(y^{−ε}) at each cusp and 0 < σ < ε, then (Φ̃, P_{m,s̄}) = ∫₀^∞ e^{−4πmy} a_m(y) y^s dy, and for a holomorphic Φ = Σ a_m q^m, (Φ, P_{m,s̄}) = Γ(1+s)(4πm)^{−1−s} a_m. P_m = lim_{s→0} P_{m,s} is a holomorphic cusp form of weight 2 on Γ₀(N) ("known", proved by computing the Fourier coefficients of P_{m,s} as functions of s). Consequently the holomorphic projection Φ of Φ̃ has a_m = 4πm lim_{s→0, Re s>0} ∫₀^∞ e^{−4πmy} a_m(y) y^s dy (the case A = B = 0 of (6.2)).
items.note: No Poincaré series for Γ₀(N) in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep 'Poincare' in TauCeti/NumberTheory: no file). QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3 plans holomorphic Poincaré series only in even weight k ≥ 4 (node QM.3/holomorphic-poincare-series) and Maass–Poincaré series for harmonic Maass forms; GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6 plans adelic holomorphic projection. Neither plans the weight-2 Hecke-trick continuation to s = 0. The unfolding display on p. 296 omits dx, as on p. 289 (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E41; recorded as a new issue in this review). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 11: QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.3.

items.name: (6.2) Proposition: holomorphic projection of a weight-2 form with logarithmic growth at the cusps
items.statement: Let Φ̃(z) = Σ_{m∈ℤ} a_m(y)e^{2πimx} ∈ M̃₂(Γ₀(N)) satisfy the growth condition (6.1) at all cusps ξ, and suppose A_ξ = A(N₁), B_ξ = B(N₁) depend only on N₁ = gcd(N, denominator of ξ). Let {α(M), β(M) : M | N} be the solution of the non-singular linear system (6.3) Σ_{M|N} ((M,N₁)²/M²) α(M) = A(N₁) (N₁ | N), (6.4) Σ_{M|N} ((M,N₁)²/M²) {β(M) + α(M) log((M,N₁)²/M)} = B(N₁) (N₁ | N). Then there is a holomorphic cusp form Φ = Σ_{m≥1} a_m e^{2πimz} ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) with (Φ, f) = (Φ̃, f) for all f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) and, for (m, N) = 1, (6.5) a_m = lim_{s→0} [4πm ∫₀^∞ a_m(y) e^{−4πmy} y^s dy + 24α(1)σ₁(m)s^{−1}] + 24β(1)σ₁(m) + 48α(1)[σ′₁(m) − σ₁(m)(log 2m + 1/2 + ζ′/ζ(2))], where σ₁(m) = Σ_{d|m} d, σ′₁(m) = Σ_{d|m} d log d. (Proof: subtract Σ_{M|N}{α(M)F(Mz) + β(M)E(Mz)}, which is orthogonal to cusp forms and has expansion A(N₁) log y + B(N₁) + O(y^{−1} log y) at ξ, then apply the case A = B = 0.)
items.note: The method (holomorphic projection of a non-holomorphic kernel of moderate growth, with Eisenstein corrections) is planned in its adelic Yuan–Zhang–Zhang form by GZ.6: "Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels and their central derivatives, normalized local Whittaker terms, holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection ... Compare the arithmetic height kernel with the analytic derivative modulo the explicitly identified constant/Eisenstein/old components". This explicit classical form (log growth, the system (6.3)-(6.4), formula (6.5)) is not named in any stage; if the atlas wants this paper's route, it is a new target. I re-derived (6.5) from the p. 298 asymptotics (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/267); consistent.

items.name: Weight-2 non-holomorphic Eisenstein series E_{2,s} on SL₂(ℤ) and the functions E = E_{2,s}|_{s=0}, F = ∂_s E_{2,s}|_{s=0}
items.statement: E_{2,s}(z) = Σ_{γ∈Γ∞\SL₂(ℤ)} y^s|₂γ = ½ Σ_{(c,d)=1} (cz+d)^{−2}|cz+d|^{−2s} y^s, absolutely convergent for Re(s) > 0 (printed: Re(s) > 2, see issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E51), a non-holomorphic modular function of weight 2 on SL₂(ℤ), orthogonal to holomorphic cusp forms (it is P_{m,s} for N = 1, m = 0), of the form y^s + c(s)y^{−1−s} + O(e^{−y}) with c(s) and the O-coefficients holomorphic near s = 0. E(z) := E_{2,s}(z)|_{s=0}, F(z) := ∂/∂s E_{2,s}(z)|_{s=0} (holomorphic continuation, or limit s ↘ 0) lie in M̃₂(SL₂(ℤ)), are orthogonal to cusp forms, and E(z) = 1 + O(1/y), F(z) = log y + O(y^{−1} log y) as y → ∞. Consequently, if Φ̃ ∈ M̃₂(SL₂(ℤ)) has Φ̃ = A log y + B + O(y^{−ε}), then Φ̃ − AF − BE has the same scalar products with holomorphic forms and is O(y^{−ε}).
items.note: Mathlib has only the holomorphic quasimodular E₂: mathlib:EisensteinSeries.E2 (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/EisensteinSeries/E2/Defs.lean:60), its q-expansion mathlib:EisensteinSeries.E2_eq_tsum_cexp (E2/Summable.lean:102, E2 z = 1 − 24 Σ σ₁(n) qⁿ) and transformation law mathlib:EisensteinSeries.E2_slash_action (E2/Transform.lean:229, E2|γ = E2 − (1/(2ζ(2)))·D2 γ). GZ's E equals E₂ − 3/(πy) (c(0) = −3/π; checked: sζ(2s+1) → ½ gives c(0) = −√π·Γ(½)·½/ζ(2) = −3/π). This value E is planned: packet node QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3/nonholomorphic-eisenstein-series-e2-star ('E₂*(τ) := E₂(τ) − 3/(πv) … SL₂(ℤ)-invariant of weight 2'). The family E_{2,s}, its continuation to s = 0, the function F = ∂_sE_{2,s}|_{s=0} and the orthogonality to cusp forms are not planned, so the item as a whole is missing. AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.2 plans adelic Eisenstein series continuation ('Prove meromorphic continuation of operators and Eisenstein series'), not this classical weight-2 family. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 11: QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.3.

items.name: Fourier expansion of the weight-0 Eisenstein series and of E_{2,s} (quoted 'well-known')
items.statement: For E(z,s) = Σ_{Γ∞\SL₂(ℤ)} Im(γz)^s (weight 0): E(z,s) = y^s + π^{1/2}Γ(s−½)ζ(2s−1)/(Γ(s)ζ(2s)) · y^{1−s} + (2π^s y^{1/2}/(Γ(s)ζ(2s))) Σ_{m≠0} |m|^{1/2−s} σ_{2s−1}(m) K_{s−1/2}(2π|m|y) e^{2πimx}, σ_ν(m) = Σ_{d|m} d^ν, K_ν = K-Bessel function. The identity (cz+d)^{−2}|cz+d|^{−2s} y^s = (2i/(s+1)) ∂/∂z (y^{s+1}/|cz+d|^{2s+2}) (printed with (cz+d)^{−1}, see issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E47) gives E_{2,s}(z) = (2i/(s+1)) ∂/∂z E(z, s+1), hence E_{2,s}(z) = y^s − π^{1/2} s Γ(s+½)ζ(2s+1)/(Γ(s+2)ζ(2s+2)) · y^{−1−s} + Σ_{m≠0} e_{2,s}(m,y)e^{2πimz} with e_{2,s}(m,y) = (2π^{s+1}|m|^{−s−1/2}/(Γ(s+2)ζ(2s+2))) σ_{2s+1}(m) e^{2πmy} (∂/∂y − 2πm)(√y K_{s+1/2}(2π|m|y)).
items.note: Checked: the ∂_z identity (with the square), the constant term (−s/(s+1))·φ(s+1), and e_{2,s} by differentiating the m-th term of E(z,s+1). No real-analytic Eisenstein series or K-Bessel function in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep besselK/BesselK: only unrelated hits; grep nonholomorphic/realAnalytic: none). AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.2 plans adelic Eisenstein series and their continuation, not the explicit classical Fourier expansion. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 9: AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.0, AS.1, AS.2.

items.name: Tabulated K-Bessel integral
items.statement: For m ≥ 1 and 0 < t < Re(s): ∫₀^∞ y^{s−1/2} K_{t+1/2}(2πmy) e^{−2πmy} dy = Γ(s+t+1)Γ(s−t)π^{1/2} / (Γ(s+1)(4πm)^{s+1/2}). With the integration by parts ∫₀^∞ e_{2,t}(m,y) e^{−4πmy} y^s dy = −(2π^{1+t} m^{−1/2−t}/(Γ(2+t)ζ(2+2t))) σ_{1+2t}(m) · s · ∫₀^∞ y^{s−1/2} K_{1/2+t}(2πmy) e^{−2πmy} dy.
items.note: Checked against the standard formula ∫₀^∞ x^{μ−1}e^{−αx}K_ν(αx)dx = √π Γ(μ+ν)Γ(μ−ν)/((2α)^μ Γ(μ+½)) with μ = s+½, α = 2πm, ν = t+½: agrees. No K-Bessel function in either library; no stage plans it. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 10: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0.

items.name: Mellin asymptotics of the Fourier coefficients of E and F
items.statement: Write E(z) = Σ_m e(m,y)e^{2πimz}, F(z) = Σ_m f(m,y)e^{2πimz}. For m > 0: e(m,y) = −24σ₁(m), and as s → 0 (Re s > 0): ∫₀^∞ e(m,y)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy = −(6/(πm))σ₁(m) + o(1); ∫₀^∞ f(m,y)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy = ∂/∂t[−2π^{3/2+t}m^{−1/2−t}Γ(s+t+1)Γ(s−t)σ_{1+2t}(m)/((4πm)^{s+1/2}Γ(2+t)Γ(s)ζ(2+2t))]_{t=0} = −24 Γ(s+1)/(4πm)^{s+1} · [2σ′₁(m) + σ₁(m)(log(π/m) + γ − 1 − 2ζ′/ζ(2) + 1/s)] = −(6/(πm))σ₁(m)s^{−1} − (12/(πm))σ′₁(m) + (12/(πm))σ₁(m)(log 2m + ½ + ζ′/ζ(2)) + o(1), γ = Euler's constant. For (m, N) = 1 the m-th coefficient of Φ̃* = Φ̃ − Σ_{M|N}{α(M)F(Mz) + β(M)E(Mz)} is a*_m(y) = a_m(y) − α(1)f(m,y) − β(1)e(m,y); these give (6.5).
items.note: Verified the Laurent expansion by hand (ψ(s+1) − ψ(s) = 1/s, ψ(2) = 1 − γ, ζ(2) = π²/6) and that it yields (6.5); re-verified numerically in this review (for m = 1, 6 and s = 10⁻⁴, 10⁻⁶ the t-derivative of the bracket equals the closed form −24Γ(s+1)(4πm)^{−s−1}[2σ′₁(m) + σ₁(m)(log(π/m) + γ − 1 − 2ζ′/ζ(2) + 1/s)] and agrees with the three-term expansion up to O(s)). Library: the statement e(m,y) = −24σ₁(m) for m > 0 is the non-constant part of the q-expansion mathlib:EisensteinSeries.E2_eq_tsum_cexp (E2/Summable.lean:102) since E = E₂ − 3/(πy) (E is planned as QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3/nonholomorphic-eisenstein-series-e2-star); the Mellin statements have no library or stage counterpart. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Behaviour of E(Mz) and F(Mz) at the cusps of Γ₀(N)
items.statement: Let M | N and ξ = a/c with (a,c) = 1, (c, N) = N₁; α = (a b; c d) ∈ SL₂(ℤ). Put a′ = (M/(M,N₁))a, c′ = c/(M,N₁) ((a′,c′) = 1), complete to α′ = (a′ b′; c′ d′) ∈ SL₂(ℤ), and relate z, z′ by c′z′ + d′ = ((M,N₁)/M)(cz+d); then (a′z′+b′)/(c′z′+d′) = M(az+b)/(cz+d), y′ = ((M,N₁)²/M)y, and E_{2,s}(Mz)|₂α = ((M,N₁)^{2+2s}/M^{2+s}) y^s + O(y^{−1−s}); hence E(Mz)|₂α = (M,N₁)²/M² + O(1/y), F(Mz)|₂α = ((M,N₁)²/M²)(log y + log((M,N₁)²/M)) + O(y^{−1} log y). Therefore Σ_{M|N}{α(M)F(Mz) + β(M)E(Mz)} has expansion A(N₁) log y + B(N₁) + O(y^{−1} log y) at ξ iff (6.3), (6.4) hold.
items.note: Checked (M, c) = (M, N₁) since M | N, and the scaling of y′. No library or stage counterpart (depends on PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/264). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: E(Mz) and F(Mz) are orthogonal to S₂(Γ₀(N)) for M | N
items.statement: Let N ≥ 1 and M | N, and let E(z) = E_{2,s}(z)|_{s=0}, F(z) = ∂_sE_{2,s}(z)|_{s=0} as in the proof of (6.2) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/264). Then z ↦ E(Mz) and z ↦ F(Mz) lie in M̃₂(Γ₀(N)) and (f, E(M·)) = (f, F(M·)) = 0 for every f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)). Consequently Σ_{M|N}{α(M)F(Mz) + β(M)E(Mz)} has the same Petersson products with cusp forms as 0, and Φ̃ and Φ̃* = Φ̃ − Σ_{M|N}{α(M)F(Mz) + β(M)E(Mz)} have the same holomorphic projection.
items.locator: Chapter IV, §6, proof of (6.2), p. 298 ('the function Σ_{M|N}{α(M)F(Mz) + β(M)E(Mz)}, which is orthogonal to cusp forms')
items.note: Asserted without proof. Checked: for Re s > 0, substituting w = Mz turns (f, E_{2,s}(M·)) into a constant times the Petersson product over SL₂(ℤ)\𝔥 of E_{2,s} with the trace to level one of the weight-2 cusp form f(w/M), which is a weight-2 cusp form of level one and hence 0 (S₂(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0; equivalently, unfold E_{2,s}, the case m = 0 of the Hecke-trick Poincaré series); then continue to s = 0 and differentiate. Item /264 states the orthogonality only for N = 1 (E and F themselves) and /268 only the behaviour at the cusps. No library or stage counterpart (GZ.6 plans adelic holomorphic projection; nothing classical). Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: Invertibility of the matrix C_N and the tridiagonal inverse (6.6)
items.statement: Let C_N = (C_N(N₁, M))_{N₁, M | N}, C_N(N₁, M) = (M, N₁)²/M² (a σ₀(N) × σ₀(N) matrix). The entries are multiplicative, C_{∏p^{ν_p}}(∏p^{λ_p}, ∏p^{μ_p}) = ∏ C_{p^{ν_p}}(p^{λ_p}, p^{μ_p}), so C_N is the Kronecker product of the C_{p^ν} (N = ∏ p^ν). For N = p^ν, C_{p^ν}(p^λ, p^μ) = p^{2 min(λ,μ) − 2μ} (rows λ = 0..ν: (1, p^{−2}, …, p^{−2ν}), (1, 1, p^{−2}, …, p^{−2ν+2}), …, (1, …, 1)), and (6.6) C_{p^ν}^{−1} = (p² − 1)^{−1} × the tridiagonal matrix with diagonal (p², p²+1, …, p²+1, p²), superdiagonal −1, subdiagonal −p². In particular C_N is invertible and (6.3)-(6.4) have a unique solution.
items.note: Verified C·C^{−1} = I for ν = 1, 2 by hand. Generic Kronecker-product facts exist in Mathlib (Matrix.kroneckerMap), but not these matrices; no stage plans them. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (6.7) Proposition: explicit α(1), β(1)
items.statement: In the setting of (6.2): α(1) = ρ^{−1} Σ_{N₁|N} (μ(N₁)/N₁²) A(N₁), β(1) = ρ^{−1} Σ_{N₁|N} (μ(N₁)/N₁²)(B(N₁) − 2A(N₁) log N₁) − 2α(1) Σ_{p|N} log p/(p² − 1), where μ is the Möbius function and ρ = ∏_{p|N}(1 − p^{−2}) = Σ_{N₁|N} μ(N₁)/N₁². (Proof: C_N^{−1}(1, N₁) = ρ^{−1}μ(N₁)/N₁², and Σ_{N₁|N} (μ(N₁)/N₁²) s_p(N₁) = −2 Σ_{N₁|N} (μ(N₁)/N₁²) A(N₁)(v_p(N₁) + 1/(p²−1)) with s_p(N₁) = Σ_{M|N} C_N(N₁,M)α(M)(v_p(M) − 2 min{v_p(N₁), v_p(M)}).)
items.note: Proof re-checked (bracket μC(1,p^μ) − p^{−2}(μ−2)C(p,p^μ) = 2p^{−2μ}; Σ_{μ≥1} p^{−2μ}C^{−1}(p^μ,p^κ) = −μ(p^κ)p^{−2κ}(κ + 1/(p²−1))). One misprint in the proof (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E48). Mathlib has the Möbius function (ArithmeticFunction.moebius) but nothing specific; no stage. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (6.8) Proposition: the constants A(N₁), B(N₁) of the weight-2 kernel Φ̃
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. IV: N ≥ 1; D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; Chap. IV §2, p. 273), (D, N) = 1, δ := |D|, K = ℚ(√D), ε = ε_D = (D/·), h = h_K, u = #O_K^×/2, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜 (r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u)); weight 2k with k = 1; ε(N) = 1. Let Φ̃ be the function of Prop. (4.5) for k = 1, i.e. Φ̃ = (√δ/2π)·∂/∂s Φ̃_s|_{s=0} with Φ̃_s = Tr^{ND}_N(θ_𝒜(z)E_s^{(1)}(Nz)) (Prop. (1.2)). Then Φ̃ satisfies the hypotheses of (6.2) with A(N₁) = (h/(2u²)) ε(N₁)N₁/N, B(N₁) = A(N₁)(log(N₁²δ/(Nπ)) − γ + 2(L′/L)(1, ε)) (N₁ | N), γ = Euler's constant. (Proof: at a cusp with invariant N₁, (Φ̃_s|₂α)(z) = (1/(2u))(ε(N₁)/N₂)[L(2s+1,ε)(N₁y/N₂)^s − (iV_s(0)/|D|^{1/2}) L(2s,ε)(N₁y/N₂)^{−s}] + … with N₂ = N/N₁, V_s(0) = −π^{1/2}Γ(s+½)i/Γ(s+1), using Lemma (2.3) and (2.2) of Chap. IV and the count of cosets of Γ₀(ND)\Γ₀(N)α with D | c (one) and (c, D) = 1 (|D| of them).)
items.locator: Chapter IV, §6, (6.8) Proposition and proof, pp. 301-303
items.note: I re-derived A, B from the displayed cusp expansion using L(0,ε) = (√δ/π)L(1,ε) and the functional equation (log-derivative of L at 0), and checked the per-coset factor δ^{−3/2} (printed δ^{−3/2}, confirmed on the high-resolution page p. 303). The case N₁ = N reproduces the constant term of Prop. (4.5). No library or stage counterpart. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: α(1), β(1) for the kernel Φ̃ (Props. (6.7) + (6.8))
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. IV: N ≥ 1; D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; Chap. IV §2, p. 273), (D, N) = 1, δ := |D|, K = ℚ(√D), ε = ε_D = (D/·), h = h_K, u = #O_K^×/2, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜 (r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u)); weight 2k with k = 1; ε(N) = 1. For Φ̃ as in (6.8): α(1) = (h/(2u²)) N^{−1} ρ^{−1} Σ_{N₁|N} μ(N₁)ε(N₁)/N₁ = (h/(2u²)) N^{−1} ∏_{p|N}(1 + ε(p)/p)^{−1}, β(1) = α(1)(log(δ/(Nπ)) − γ + 2(L′/L)(1, ε) − 2 Σ_{p|N} log p/(p² − 1)).
items.note: Checked: ρ^{−1}∏(1 − ε(p)/p) = ∏(1 + ε(p)/p)^{−1} since ε(p)² = 1 for p | N. Note 24α(1) = −hκ/u² with κ of (6.9). No library/stage counterpart. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Mellin integral of the coefficients of Φ̃ (k = 1) and the Legendre-function asymptotics
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. IV: N ≥ 1; D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; Chap. IV §2, p. 273), (D, N) = 1, δ := |D|, K = ℚ(√D), ε = ε_D = (D/·), h = h_K, u = #O_K^×/2, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜 (r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u)); weight 2k with k = 1; ε(N) = 1. For m > 0, a_m(y) = A_m log y + B_m + Σ_{n≥1} C_{mn} q₀(4πnNy/δ) (from Prop. (4.5); q₀(t) = ∫₁^∞ e^{−tx}dx/x), with A_m = (h/u)r_𝒜(m), B_m = A_m(log(Nδ/π) − γ + 2(L′/L)(1,ε)) − Σ_{1≤n≤mδ/N} σ′_𝒜(n) r_𝒜(mδ − Nn), C_{mn} = −σ_𝒜(−n) r_𝒜(mδ + Nn) (σ_𝒜, σ′_𝒜 as in Prop. (4.6)). Then ∫₀^∞ a_m(y)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy = Γ(s+1)(4πm)^{−s−1}(A_m (Γ′/Γ)(s+1) − A_m log 4πm + B_m) + Σ_n C_{mn} ∫₀^∞ q₀(4πnNy/δ)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy, and ∫₀^∞ q₀(4πnNy/δ)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy = 2Γ(2s+2)/((4πm)^{s+1}Γ(s+2)) · Q_s(1 + 2nN/(mδ)) + ε_n(s), ε_n(s) = O(n^{−s−2}) (uniformly near s = 0), ε_n(0) = 0, using Q₀(1+2t) = ½ log(1 + 1/t) and Q_s(1+2t) = (Γ(s+1)²/(2Γ(2s+2)))[t^{−s−1} + O(t^{−s−2})] (t → ∞). Since C_{mn} = O(n^c) for all c > 0, 4πm ∫₀^∞ a_m(y)e^{−4πmy}y^s dy = B_m − A_m(γ + log 4πm) + (2Γ(2s+2)/((4πm)^sΓ(s+2))) Σ_n C_{mn} Q_s(1 + 2nN/(mδ)) + o(1) (s → 0).
items.note: Checked the s = 0 and n → ∞ matching and the Legendre asymptotic (from Q_ν(z) ~ √πΓ(ν+1)/(Γ(ν+3/2)(2z)^{ν+1}) and duplication). No Legendre function of the second kind in either library (Mathlib has only Polynomial.shiftedLegendre); no stage. Corrected at integration: the third (archimedean) term carries σ_𝒜(−n), not the printed σ_𝒜(n) (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E38, which covers this page too). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: (6.9) Theorem (i): the weight-2 cusp form Φ_𝒜 representing L′_𝒜(f,1)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. IV: N ≥ 1; D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; Chap. IV §2, p. 273), (D, N) = 1, δ := |D|, K = ℚ(√D), ε = ε_D = (D/·), h = h_K, u = #O_K^×/2, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜 (r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u)); weight 2k with k = 1; ε(N) = 1. There exists a holomorphic cusp form Φ_𝒜(z) = Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,𝒜} e^{2πimz} of weight 2 and level N such that L_𝒜(f, 1) = 0 and L′_𝒜(f, 1) = (8π²/√δ)(f, Φ_𝒜) for every cusp form f in the space spanned by newforms of weight 2 and level N. (δ = |D|; the constant equals 8π²/√|D|, consistent with Chap. I (6.2).)
items.note: The analytic half of Gross–Zagier (derivative of the Rankin kernel, holomorphic projection) is planned in adelic form by GZ.6 ("Construct incoherent Eisenstein/Weil kernels and their central derivatives, ... holomorphic projection and cuspidal projection. Prove the functional-equation vanishing that permits differentiation") and specialised by GZ.8 ("Specialize to X₀(N) ..."); L_𝒜(f,1) = 0 is the sign −1 statement (GZ.8: "For matching local signs deduce the global sign −1"). Existence of some Φ_𝒜 with this property is formal (Riesz representation on the newspace); the content is (ii). Printed issue on this line: duplicated word (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E49). Coordinator lead 'constant should be √|D|' checked: not a mistake, δ := |D| is Chap. IV notation (p. 273).

items.name: (6.9) Theorem (ii): the Fourier coefficients a_{m,𝒜} of Φ_𝒜 for (m, N) = 1
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. IV: N ≥ 1; D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; Chap. IV §2, p. 273), (D, N) = 1, δ := |D|, K = ℚ(√D), ε = ε_D = (D/·), h = h_K, u = #O_K^×/2, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜 (r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u)); weight 2k with k = 1; ε(N) = 1. For m prime to N, a_{m,𝒜} = − Σ_{1≤n≤m|D|/N} σ′_𝒜(n) r_𝒜(m|D| − nN) + (h/u) r_𝒜(m)[log(N|D|/(4π²m)) − 2γ + 2(L′/L)(1, ε)] + lim_{s→0}[−2 Σ_{n≥1} σ_𝒜(−n) r_𝒜(m|D| + nN) Q_s(1 + 2nN/(m|D|)) − (hκ/u²) σ₁(m) s^{−1}] + (hκ/u²)[σ₁(m)(log(N/|D|) + 2 Σ_{p|N} log p/(p² − 1) + 2 + 2(ζ′/ζ)(2) − 2(L′/L)(1, ε)) + Σ_{d|m} d log(m/d²)], where σ₁(m) = Σ_{d|m} d, κ = −12/(N ∏_{p|N}(1 + ε(p)/p)), σ_𝒜, σ′_𝒜 as in Prop. (4.6), Q_s = Legendre function of the second kind, γ = Euler's constant.
items.note: Re-derived from (6.5), (6.7), (6.8) and the Mellin integral (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/273): B_m − A_m(γ + log 4πm) gives the first two lines, 24α(1) = −hκ/u², and the remaining terms combine using σ₁(m) log m − 2σ′₁(m) = Σ_{d|m} d log(m/d²). Agrees with print. No stage plans the explicit Fourier coefficients of the holomorphic projection (GZ.6/GZ.8 plan YZZ's kernel, whose explicit X₀(N) coefficients are not a named target). Nearest: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8. Corrected at integration: the third (archimedean) term carries σ_𝒜(−n), not the printed σ_𝒜(n) (issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E38, which covers this page too). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.6.

items.name: Endomorphisms act faithfully on the cotangent space; the Hecke algebra embeds in End_ℚ(S) (quoted)
items.statement: If J is an abelian variety over ℚ and S its cotangent space at the origin, End_ℚ(J) acts faithfully on S. For J = J₀(N), S is identified with the space of cusp forms of weight 2 and level N with rational Fourier coefficients; hence 𝕋 → End_ℚ(S) is injective and dim_ℚ 𝕋 ≤ d², d = dim_ℚ S = dim_ℂ S₂(Γ₀(N)).
items.note: Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (no Jacobian of X₀(N) as an abelian variety). The Γ₁(N) analogues are planned in ModularCurvesPartII packet nodes: ModularCurvesPartII:R14.2/integral-hecke-algebra ('It acts faithfully on the finite free ℤ-module H¹(X₁(N)^an, ℤ) and on the finite free ℤ_ℓ-module T_ℓ(J₁(N))'), ModularCurvesPartII:R14.5/modular-quotient-differentials ('S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ) = Cot₀(J₁(N)_ℂ)', with Conrad's warning that the Picard action on Cot₀ is the Petersson adjoint of the classical action), and stage R12.5 ('Identify weight-two cusp forms with regular differentials on the compact curve ... Check the q-expansion of f(q)dq/q'). Not named anywhere: the J₀(N), ℚ-rational statement (cotangent space over ℚ = cusp forms with rational q-expansion, 𝕋 ↪ End_ℚ(S)), and the general faithfulness of End(J) on the cotangent space of an abelian variety in characteristic 0 (only dimension one, EllipticCurveModularity:R29.1). The owner is ModularCurvesPartII (R14.2 with R12.5), not GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.3, whose ξ-normalized maps X_U → A on quaternionic Shimura curves do not contain this. Routed (source) to ModularCurvesPartII:R14.2. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 5: ModularCurvesPartII R12.5, R12.6, R13.5, R14.1, R14.2.

items.name: Perfect pairing between the Hecke algebra and cusp forms; Hom(𝕋, ℂ) ↔ cusp forms
items.statement: With S = S₂(Γ₀(N)) ∩ ℚ[[q]] and a_m : S → ℚ the m-th Fourier coefficient, the pairing β : 𝕋 × S → ℚ, β(T, f) = a₁(Tf), is perfect (so dim_ℚ 𝕋 = d), using a₁(T_m f) = a_m(f). Consequently every ℚ-linear α : 𝕋 → ℂ is β(·, f) for a unique f ∈ S ⊗ ℂ, and Σ_{m≥1} α(T_m) q^m = f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)).
items.note: Ingredient in library: tauceti:HeckeRing.GL2.qExpansion_coeff_one_heckeRingHomCharSpace_heckeTCompositeGamma0 (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/HeckeSlash/Nebentypus/Composite.lean:123): for n ≠ 0 and F in the character space modFormCharSpace k χ of Γ₁(N), (qExpansion 1 (T_n F)).coeff 1 = (qExpansion 1 F).coeff n — the relation a₁(T_n f) = a_n(f), on the complex space. The perfect pairing over ℂ for Γ₁(N) is a proof step of packet node ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3/betti-free-rank-two ('The pairing S₂(Γ₁(N), ℂ) × (ℂ ⊗ T₁(N)) → ℂ, (f, T) ↦ a₁(Tf) is perfect (a₁(T_n f) = a_n(f) and T ↪ End S₂)'); the Γ₀(N) case follows by applying the idempotent that averages the diamond operators, but the ℚ-rational statement (𝕋 ⊂ End_ℚ(J₀(N)) ⊗ ℚ, dim_ℚ 𝕋 = d, every ℚ-linear α: 𝕋 → ℂ is β(·, f)) is not named. Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8G plans only the newspace version ('after ⊗ℂ its characters — equivalently its eigenlines — are exactly the normalized newforms'). Routed (source) to ModularCurvesPartII:R14.3. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 5: ModularCurvesPartII R12.5, R12.6, R13.5, R14.1, R14.2.

items.name: Generating series of Hecke-translated heights is a cusp form; g_𝒜 is a cusp form (first assertion of Chap. I, Theorem (6.1))
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. For any y, z ∈ J₀(N)(H), Σ_{m≥1} <y, T_m z> q^m is a cusp form of weight 2 and level N (with complex coefficients), since T ↦ <y, Tz> is ℚ-linear on 𝕋. In particular g_𝒜(z) = Σ_{m≥1} <c, T_m c^σ> e^{2πimz} ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) ⊗ ℂ. This has nothing to do with Heegner points.
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, p. 306 (proof of the first assertion of Theorem (6.1) of Chap. I)
items.note: The adelic analogue (modularity of the Hecke-correspondence generating series) is planned in GZ.6: "Establish modularity of the curve-level Chow-valued series through the relevant product formula and theta construction"; pairing with the height pairing gives this statement. The paper's elementary route (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/276, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/277: faithfulness + perfect pairing) is not planned. Partial coverage.

items.name: Manin–Drinfeld theorem (quoted): the cuspidal class (0) − (∞) is torsion
items.statement: The divisor class of (0) − (∞) on X₀(N) has finite order in J₀(N)(ℚ). Hence c = (x) − (∞) and d = (x) − (0) give the same class in J(H) ⊗ ℚ, and <c, T_m c^σ> = <c, T_m d^σ>.
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, p. 306 (cited as '[4], Cor. 3.6'; intended [41] = Manin, 'Parabolic points and zeta functions of modular curves', Cor. 3.6; issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E50); also Chapter I, §9, p. 232
items.note: ER.7: 'Construct modular units, their divisors at cusps, the relevant Manin–Drinfeld relation and the modular-curve K₂ classes'. Its packet node EllipticRegulators:ER.7/manin-drinfeld states the theorem for X₁(N) over ℂ ('every degree-zero divisor supported on the cusps has finite order in Pic⁰(X₁(N)(ℂ))'); (0) − (∞) on X₀(N) is the push-forward of a degree-zero cuspidal divisor of X₁(N), so the X₀(N) statement is an instance. Not in the libraries (no J₀(N)).

items.name: Local decomposition of <c, T_m d^σ> and the archimedean contribution
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. items.name: The coefficient identity <c, T_m c^σ> = u² a_{m,𝒜} for (m, N) = 1
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. For (m, N) = 1, <c, T_m c^σ> = u² a_{m,𝒜}, where a_{m,𝒜} is the m-th Fourier coefficient of the cusp form Φ_𝒜 of Theorem (6.9) of Chap. IV. Consequently g_𝒜 − u² Φ_𝒜 is an old form in S₂(Γ₀(N)).
items.note: Checked: the archimedean and finite sums (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/280, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/281) add up to u² times (6.9)(ii) (the hu r_𝒜(m) terms combine to hu r_𝒜(m)[log(N|D|/(4π²m)) − 2γ + 2L′/L(1,ε)], since −2 log 2π + log|D| + log(N/m) = log(N|D|/(4π²m))); both carry σ_𝒜(−n) after PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E38. Planned as the X₀(N) case of GZ.6: 'Compare the arithmetic height kernel with the analytic derivative modulo the explicitly identified constant/Eisenstein/old components; prove why those components disappear upon projection', with the local identities in GZ.7 and GZ.8's 'Specialize to X₀(N)'; the explicit coefficient formula is not named. The same identity from Chapter I, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/52, is recorded as planned in these three stages. The step 'the coefficients agree for (m, N) = 1, so the difference is old' is the Atkin–Lehner main lemma, in the library as tauceti:TauCeti.mem_cuspFormsOld_of_forall_coprime_qExpansion_coeff_eq_zero (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/MainLemma.lean:178: a cusp form in S_k(Γ₁(N), χ) whose q-expansion coefficients vanish at every index prime to N lies in the old subspace).

items.name: Dependence of g_𝒜 on the Heegner point x
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. g_𝒜 is not quite independent of the choice of the Heegner point x (as erroneously asserted in the announcement [17]), but it is independent up to the addition of an old form. For (m, N) = 1, <c, T_m c^σ> is independent of x, because any two choices of x are related by an element of G × W and this action commutes with T_m for (m, N) = 1.
items.note: HE.1: "Construct a compatible family of points P_c and show its dependence on choices is given by the specified Galois/Hecke actions and torsion translation." items.name: The χ-component c_χ, the f-isotypical component c_{χ,f}, and L(f, χ, s)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. For a character χ of G (≅ Cl_K): c_χ = Σ_{σ∈G} χ^{−1}(σ) c^σ ∈ J(H) ⊗ ℂ (h times the standard eigencomponent). By G-invariance of <,>, <c_χ, T_m c_χ> = h Σ_{σ∈G} χ(σ) <c, T_m c^σ>. For a normalized newform f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)), c_{χ,f} = projection of c_χ to the f-isotypical component of J(H) ⊗ ℂ under 𝕋. L(f, χ, s) = Σ_𝒜 χ(𝒜) L_𝒜(f, s) (Chap. I (5.4)), so L′(f, χ, 1) = Σ_𝒜 χ(𝒜) L′_𝒜(f, 1); and, by the identity for <c_χ, T_m c_χ> above (not by the definition of L(f, χ, s)), Σ_𝒜 χ(𝒜) g_𝒜 = h^{−1} Σ_{m≥1} <c_χ, T_m c_χ> q^m.

items.name: Hecke operators prime to N are self-adjoint for the height pairing; isotypic components are orthogonal
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1. For (m, N) = 1 and a, b ∈ J(H) ⊗ ℂ, <T_m a, b> = <a, T_m b> for the hermitian extension of the Néron–Tate pairing (T_m is its own transpose as a correspondence on X₀(N), Chap. I (2.3)). Hence the T_m with (m, N) = 1 act on the finite-dimensional space J(H) ⊗ ℂ as commuting self-adjoint operators for a positive-definite hermitian form, so simultaneously diagonalizably with real eigenvalues, and eigenspaces for distinct systems of eigenvalues are orthogonal. In particular, for a normalized newform f, the f-isotypical component c_{χ,f} of c_χ is orthogonal to c_χ − c_{χ,f} (by strong multiplicity one every other system of eigenvalues occurring differs from that of f at some T_m, (m, N) = 1).
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, p. 308 (used in the proof of Chap. I Theorem (6.3): '<c_χ^{(i)}, c_χ^{(1)}> = 0 for i ≠ 1 since c_χ^{(i)} and c_χ^{(1)} are eigenvectors with different eigenvalues of some T_m, (m, N) = 1')
items.note: GZ.1: 'Construct the bilinear height ... with adjunction under homomorphisms' and 'For strict GL₂-type A, construct the M-linear pairing ... and verify dual-endomorphism compatibility'; GZ.2: 'Export local height decomposition, base-change and correspondence-adjunction APIs'. Self-duality of T_m for (m, N) = 1 is in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/4 (planned R14.1/R14.2). The orthogonality is also what the corrected argument of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E59 uses. Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: (1.1) Corollary: non-negativity of L′(f, χ, 1)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. Let f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) be any (normalized) newform and χ any character of Gal(H/K). Then L′(f, χ, 1) ≥ 0. (Immediate from Theorem (6.3): the Petersson product and the global height pairing are positive definite.)
items.note: Not stated in any stage. Ingredients planned: GZ.8 (the formula) and GZ.1 ("Prove positivity for ample symmetric bundles and characterize the zero locus as torsion"); library ingredient for elliptic curves: tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.canonicalHeight_nonneg (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/CanonicalHeight.lean:266).
