items.name: (1.2) Corollary: Galois conjugates of L(f, χ, s) vanish to the same order ≤ 1 or all to order ≥ 3
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m. Let f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) be any newform and χ any character of Gal(H/K). Then either all conjugates L(f^α, χ^α, s) (α ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)) have a simple zero at s = 1 or else all have a zero of order ≥ 3. (Each has odd order by the functional equation; L′(f^α, χ^α, 1) = 0 iff c_{χ^α, f^α} = c^α_{χ,f} = 0 in J(H) ⊗ ℂ.)
items.note: No stage plans Galois-invariance of the order of vanishing. Nearest: Tau Ceti ModularForms Layer 8G (conjugate newforms f^σ, a_n(f^σ) = σ(a_n(f))) and GZ.8. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8.

items.name: (1.3) Corollary: Galois invariance of ord_{s=1} L(f, s) in low orders
items.statement: Let f be any newform of weight 2 (level N) and f^α (α ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)) any conjugate. Then ord_{s=1} L(f,s) = 0 ⇔ ord_{s=1} L(f^α,s) = 0; = 1 ⇔ = 1; ≥ 2 ⇔ ≥ 2; and, when the functional equation of L(f,s) has sign −1 (f|w_N = f), ≥ 3 ⇔ ≥ 3. (Corrected: the paper states the last equivalence for every newform; for sign +1 it says ord ≥ 4 ⇔ ord ≥ 4, which its argument does not prove.) (Proof: L(f,1) = (non-vanishing period)·(algebraic number conjugated by α); same parity by the functional equations (f and f^α have the same w_N-eigenvalue); if L(f,1) = 0 ≠ L′(f,1) the sign is −1, choose K as in the paper with L_ε(f,1) ≠ 0 by Waldspurger, then L′(f,1)L_ε(f,1) = L′(f,1_K,1) and Corollary (1.2).)
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, (1.3) Corollary and proof, p. 309
items.note: No stage plans it. Inputs planned elsewhere: twist nonvanishing (RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.2, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/288), period algebraicity (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/289), the GZ formula (GZ.8). The argument gives: order 0 is Galois-invariant (algebraicity), the parity is Galois-invariant, and order exactly 1 is Galois-invariant; for sign −1 this yields all four lines, for sign +1 (even orders) only the first and third, so the printed fourth line is unproved for sign +1 (new issue in this review). Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8.

items.name: Waldspurger's nonvanishing theorem, as used (quoted: [36] Th. 2.3, [37] Th. 4)
items.statement: If f is a weight-2 newform of level N whose L-function has sign −1 (f|w_N = f), there is an imaginary quadratic field K = ℚ(√D) as in this paper (D odd fundamental, (D, N) = 1, every p | N split in K) with L_ε(f, 1) ≠ 0, where L_ε(f, s) = Σ ε(n) a(n) n^{−s}, ε = (D/·).
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, proof of (1.3), p. 309; §2, p. 312
items.note: BSD.2: "Prove the quadratic-twist nonvanishing theorem needed to choose a Heegner field, including finitely many prescribed splitting/local character conditions compatible with the functional equation. For a weight-two newform, construct twists with nonzero central value in the sign + branch" (route via Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein, not Waldspurger; same statement). BSD.2 also asks D ≠ −3, −4 and infinitely many K.

items.name: Algebraicity of L(f, 1) up to a period, compatible with Galois conjugation (quoted 'known')
items.statement: For a weight-2 newform f, L(f, 1) = Ω·a with Ω a non-vanishing period and a an algebraic number such that the corresponding number for f^α is a^α; in particular L(f,1) = 0 ⇔ L(f^α,1) = 0, and similarly for L_ε(f,1).
items.note: L1: "For a fixed normalized newform construct its coefficient field and the plus/minus eigenspaces over that field. Define period lines first ... Prove algebraicity of the period-normalized values". Galois equivariance of the period-normalized value under conjugation of f is not stated explicitly; partial.

items.name: Factorization L(f, 1_K, s) = L(f, s)·L_ε(f, s); for f ↔ E, L(E/K, s) = L(E, s)·L(E′, s)
items.statement: Let f be a weight-2 newform of level N and K as above (ε(N) = 1 with all p | N split). For χ = 1 (trivial character), L(f, 1, s) = Σ_𝒜 L_𝒜(f, s) = L(f, s)·L_ε(f, s), with functional equation of sign −1; L_ε(f, s) has sign equal to −(sign of L(f,s)). If L(E, s) = L(f, s), then L(f, 1, s) = L(E/K, s) and L_ε(f, s) = L(E′, s), E′ the twist of E by K (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/300).
items.locator: Chapter V, §1, proof of (1.3), p. 309; §2, pp. 310, 312
items.note: BSD.0: "For a quadratic character construct the existing quadratic twist and prove every local Euler-factor comparison, including bad primes, then the factorization L(E/K,s)=L(E,s)L(E^K,s)". Only the elliptic-curve case is planned; the case of f with non-rational coefficients (used in (1.3)) is not. Checked the Euler factors at p | N (split): (1 − a_p p^{−s})^{−2} on both sides.

items.name: Strong Weil curve and modular parametrization (quoted: [25], Faltings)
items.statement: (a) If E/ℚ has L(E, s) = L(f, s) for a modular form f, then f is a Hecke eigenform of weight 2 with coefficients in ℤ (verifiable by a finite computation for given E). (b) Conversely, for such f the periods of ω_f = 2πif(z)dz = Σ_{n≥1} a_n q^n dq/q define an elliptic curve E₀/ℚ (the strong Weil curve) with L(E₀, s) = L(f, s) [25]. (c) By Faltings' isogeny theorem every E/ℚ with L(E, s) = L(f, s) is isogenous to E₀ and admits a covering π: X₀(N) → E over ℚ (N = level of f) with π(∞) = 0.
items.note: R29.5: "Apply the weight-two, trivial-nebentypus quotient theorem ModularCurvesPartII R14.5 to the primitive newform ..., obtaining A_f as a quotient of J₀(N_E) ... Use R19's Tate-module identification and R28's isogeny theorem to obtain an isogeny A_f→E over Q. Compose the rational-cusp-normalised Abel–Jacobi map, the quotient map and this isogeny"; R28.4: "Establish the isogeny criterion when the rational Tate modules are isomorphic". (c) is exactly this route.

items.name: Manin constant c of the parametrization π
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. Let ω be a Néron differential on E (unique up to sign). Then π*(ω) = c·ω_f for a non-zero integer c; the sign of ω is chosen so that c > 0. (Quoted conjecture, not assumed: c divides the index of π_*H₁(X₀(N), ℤ) in H₁(E, ℤ) [25]; for the strong Weil parametrization this is Manin's conjecture c₀ = 1.)
items.note: GZ.3: "Construct differential pullbacks and Manin constants as comparison quantities with exact isogeny functoriality; never assume the Manin constant is universally one"; GZ.8 keeps "Manin constants" in the explicit formulas. That c is an integer is itself a theorem (not proved in the paper); no stage names the integrality.

items.name: The Heegner point P_K ∈ E(K) and its height
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. For a Heegner point x of discriminant D on X₀(N): P_K = Σ_{σ∈Gal(H/K)} π(x^σ) = Σ_σ π(x)^σ ∈ E(K) (sum in E(H)). It is independent of the choice of x up to sign and addition of a rational torsion point (printed: 'up to sign'; issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E58), and ĥ(P_K) = ĥ(c_{1,f})·deg(π), canonical heights on E and J₀(N) over K.
items.note: HE.1: "Map CM points to degree-zero Jacobian classes using a cusp ..., then to A or E through the existing modular quotient. Track denominators of ξ and the degree of the parametrization integrally ... Preserve the distinction between a trace to K and a point over its ring class field"; GZ.1: "Construct the bilinear height ... with adjunction under homomorphisms" (gives ĥ(π_* c_f) = deg π·ĥ(c_f)); GZ.0 packet node GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.0/trace-versus-average.

items.name: Period comparison ‖ω‖² = c²‖ω_f‖²/deg(π)
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. With ‖ω‖² := ∬_{E(ℂ)} |ω ∧ ω̄| and ‖ω_f‖² = ∬_{X₀(N)(ℂ)} |ω_f ∧ ω̄_f| = 8π²(f, f): ‖ω‖² = c²‖ω_f‖²/deg(π).
items.note: GZ.3: "In dimension one identify the composition with the degree of the parametrization. Construct differential pullbacks and Manin constants"; GZ.0: "Construct explicit comparison maps for the choices of volume, differential ...". Checked: π*ω = cω_f and ∫_X |π*ω ∧ π*ω̄| = deg π ∫_E |ω ∧ ω̄|.

items.name: (2.1) Theorem: L′(E/K, 1) = ‖ω‖² ĥ(P_K)/(c² u_K² |D|^{1/2})
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. Then L′(E/K, 1) = ‖ω‖²·ĥ(P_K)/(c²·u_K²·|D|^{1/2}), ĥ the canonical height on E over K, c the Manin constant, ‖ω‖² = ∬_{E(ℂ)}|ω ∧ ω̄| for a Néron differential ω.
items.note: GZ.8: "Specialize to X₀(N), a rational elliptic modular quotient ... keeping unit-group factors, discriminants, degrees and Manin constants. Compare trace-normalized and averaged Heegner points and the existing elliptic height"; BSD.5: "use ... the Gross–Zagier/period/index comparison at rank one". Checked the constant: Chap. I (6.3) with χ = 1 has ĥ over H; ĥ_H = h·ĥ_K (Chap. I (6.4)) cancels the 1/h. Height normalisation hazards (Tau Ceti canonicalHeight = ½ x-height) are recorded in GZ.0 packet nodes GZ.0/x-height-canonical-height and GZ.0/bsd-height-pairing.

items.name: Consequences of Theorem (2.1) over K: rank at least one, and the BSD formula up to a rational square
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2. If ord_{s=1} L(E/K, s) = 1, then ĥ(P_K) ≠ 0 by (2.1), so P_K has infinite order and rank E(K) ≥ 1. If moreover rank E(K) = 1, then (2.1) can be written L′(E/K, 1) = [‖ω‖²·m²·ĥ(P_K)/(|D|^{1/2}·[E(K) : ℤP_K]²)]·([E(K) : ℤP_K]/(c·m·u_K))², where ĥ(P_K)/[E(K) : ℤP_K]² = Reg(E/K)/|E(K)_tors|²: the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula for L′(E/K, 1) holds with |Ш(E/K)| replaced by the square of the rational number [E(K) : ℤP_K]/(c·m·u_K). If Ш(E/K) is finite its order is a square (Cassels, [35]), so the BSD formula over K holds up to a non-zero rational square.
items.locator: Chapter V, §2, pp. 310–311 ('if ord_{s=1} L(E/K,s) = 1, then rk E(K) ≥ 1, and if ord_{s=1} L(E/K,s) = rk E(K) = 1 then the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjectural formula for L′(E/K,1) holds up to a non-zero rational square'; p. 311: 'Theorem (2.1) confirms this up to a rational square')
items.note: BSD.3: 'Prove that L(E/K,s) has a simple central zero. Apply GZ.8 with a suitable nonzero test vector and its explicit positive height comparison to obtain a non-torsion Heegner point in E(K)'; BSD.5: 'Relate the height of a non-torsion Heegner point to the squared index of its class in the rank-one lattice, with torsion and rational-versus-quadratic regulator factors'. m is the product of Tamagawa numbers as in PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/296. Checked the algebra against (2.1) and the prediction on p. 311. Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: BSD prediction for E over K (quoted conjecture, [35])
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. Assume P_K has infinite order (so L′(E/K,1) ≠ 0). BSD predicts rank E(K) = 1 and L′(E/K, 1) = ‖ω‖²·m²·ĥ(P_K)·|Ш_K| / (|D|^{1/2}·[E(K) : ℤP_K]²), where for a place 𝔭 | N of K, m_𝔭 = the Tamagawa number [E(K_𝔭) : E⁰(K_𝔭)] = #Φ_𝔭(k_𝔭), the number of k_𝔭-rational points of the group of connected components of the special fibre of the Néron model of E over O_𝔭 (the paper: 'the order of the finite group of connected components in the Néron model for E over O_𝔭'; the rational points are meant, as in Tate [35]); as p = 𝔭𝔭̄ is split, m_𝔭 = m_𝔭̄ =: m_p and m_𝔭m_𝔭̄ = m_p²; m = ∏_{p|N} m_p; Ш_K = Ш(E/K), conjecturally finite, and then of square order [35].
items.note: Arithmetic side planned in Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 7 (stretch): "assuming Ш(E/K) finite the arithmetic side of BSD is definable: the BSD quotient Ω(E)·Reg(E/K)·#Ш(E/K)·∏_p c_p/#E(K)_tors²"; BSD.5: "Define the rational BSD defect as the analytic leading term divided by the arithmetic expression" (over ℚ); BSD.1 relates invariants under quadratic base change. Note: m_p must be read as the Tamagawa number c_p = #Φ(𝔽_p) (for p split, E over K_𝔭 = ℚ_p); Reg/|tors|² = ĥ(P_K)/[E(K):ℤP_K]². 'Ш is a square' (Cassels) is not separately planned.

items.name: (2.2) Conjecture: the Heegner index formula
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. If P_K has infinite order in E(K), then it generates a subgroup of finite index and [E(K) : ℤP_K] = c·m·u_K·|Ш_K|^{1/2}. (Given Theorem (2.1) this is equivalent to the BSD formula over K in rank 1. It is independent of the parametrization: for another π′, n′_E∘π′ = n_E∘π with integers n, n′ ≥ 1, so n′c′ = nc and n′P′_K = nP_K; henceforth π is taken of minimal degree, which minimizes the index of ℤP_K.)
items.note: BSD.5 ("Rational leading-term quotient and Heegner index formula"): "Relate the height of a non-torsion Heegner point to the squared index of its class in the rank-one lattice, with torsion and rational-versus-quadratic regulator factors"; HE.6: "prove the length bound by the index of the bottom class". Planned is the equivalence with BSD and one-sided bounds; the conjecture itself is open in general (p-parts under hypotheses in RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.6).

items.name: (2.3) Conjecture and the divisibility of the index by t = |E(ℚ)_tors|
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. The index of ℤP_K in E(K) is divisible by t = |E(ℚ)_tors| (when P_K has infinite order), so (2.2) implies: (2.3) if E(K) has rank 1, then c·m·u_K·|Ш_K|^{1/2} is divisible by t. (Meaningful without finiteness of Ш_K: for divisibility by n one may replace Ш_K by its n-torsion, which is finite.)
items.note: No stage. (Implicitly (2.3) also needs P_K of infinite order, i.e. rank 1 together with L′(E/K,1) ≠ 0; the paper's phrasing relies on BSD for that step.) Routed (source) to RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.5.

items.name: Examples N = 11 and N = 65; Kramer's 2-Selmer bound (quoted [22])
items.statement: Values (E; c, m, t): N = 11: (E₀ = J₀(11); 1, 5, 5), (E₀/μ₅ = J₁(11); 5, 1, 5), (E₀/(ℤ/5ℤ); 1, 1, 1). N = 65 = 5·13: (E₀ = J₀(65)/<w₅, w₁₃>; 1, 1, 2), (E₀/(ℤ/2ℤ); 1, 4, 2). For E = E₀ of level 65, (2.3) predicts: if K is imaginary quadratic with 5 and 13 split then (a) K = ℚ(i) (u_K = 2), or (b) Ш(E/K)₂ ≠ 0, or (c) rank E(K) > 1. Using Kramer [22] one shows that for K ≠ ℚ(i) the 2-Selmer group of E over K has ℤ/2ℤ-rank ≥ 4, so (b) or (c) holds.
items.note: Checked against LMFDB: 65a1 (optimal, [1,0,0,−1,0]) has c₅ = c₁₃ = 1, torsion ℤ/2, Manin constant 1; 65a2 has Tamagawa product 4 = 2·2, torsion ℤ/2. N = 11 values agree with the known data (11a1: c₁₁ = 5, torsion 5; 11a3 = X₁(11): c₁₁ = 1, torsion 5; 11a2: trivial torsion). Re-checked independently: Δ(65a1) = 65 (type I₁ at 5 and 13, m = 1); a₅ = a₁₃ = −1 for 65a1, so w₅ = w₁₃ = +1 and E₀ is the quotient of J₀(65) on which both involutions are +1, as printed; Vélu's 2-isogenous curve y² + xy = x³ + 4x + 1 has Δ = −65² (type I₂ at 5 and 13, m = 4) and odd discriminant, so its Vélu differential is Néron at 2 and pulls back to ω₀, giving c = 1; point counts over 𝔽_p (p = 3, 7, 11, 17, 19, …) have gcd 2 for both curves, so t = 2. Note K = ℚ(i) (D = −4) is outside the paper's standing D odd, so (a) is only meaningful for the conjecture. The Kramer computation is not reproduced. No stage. Routed (source) to RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.5.

items.name: The quadratic twist E′ of E by K
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. E′ is the twist of E by K: if y² = x³ + ax + b is a Weierstrass equation for E, E′ is Dy² = x³ + ax + b.
items.note: tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwist (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/QuadraticTwist.lean:451): quadraticTwist (E : WeierstrassCurve K) (L) [Algebra.IsQuadraticExtension K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L] : WeierstrassCurve K, the twist by the trace and norm of a generator of L/K; different generators give isomorphic models (exists_smul_quadraticTwist_eq, :488), so for L = ℚ(√D) it is ℚ-isomorphic to Dy² = x³ + ax + b. Also tauceti:WeierstrassCurve.quadraticTwistPointEquiv (:809) identifies points of the twist with the (−1)-eigenspace. The L-function identity L_ε(f,s) = L(E′,s) is PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/290 (planned, BSD.0).

items.name: Rationality of L(E′, 1)/Ω′ by modular symbols (quoted [25])
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. L(E′, 1) = α′·Ω′, where Ω′ is the fundamental real period of the Néron differential ω′ = ω/√D on E′ (ω transported by the K-isomorphism E′ ≅ E, (x, y) ↦ (x, √D·y), √D = ±i√|D|; printed ω/√|D|, new issue in this review) and α′ ∈ ℚ (non-zero by the choice of K).
items.note: BSD.5: 'use modular-symbol rationality at rank zero'; L1: 'Prove algebraicity of the period-normalized values'. Checked: ω/√D is ℚ-rational on E′ (Galois moves both φ*ω and √D by −1) and is, up to sign, its Néron differential: at p ∤ 2D and at 2 (D ≡ 1 mod 4) the twist is unramified; at odd p | D, E has good reduction, E′ has type I₀* with v_p(Δ_min) = 6, and comparing minimal models over ℤ_p[√D] (where E′ ≅ E) gives ω′ = unit·ω/√D. The literal ω/√|D| = ±i·ω/√D is not ℚ-rational. Numerically, for E = 11a1 and D = −7, −19, −43 the identity of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/302 holds with Ω′ the least positive real period of ω/√D (D = −7: Ω′ = 0.183794, whereas the reading ω/√|D| would give Ω/√7 = 0.079953).

items.name: Period identity ‖ω‖²/|D|^{1/2} = [E(ℝ) : E(ℝ)⁰]·Ω·Ω′
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2: f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) a newform with rational integer coefficients, E/ℚ an elliptic curve with L(E, s) = L(f, s), π: X₀(N) → E a covering over ℚ with π(∞) = 0; K = ℚ(√D) as in §1 (D odd fundamental, every p | N split in K), u_K = #O_K^×/2. With Ω the fundamental real period of ω on E and Ω′ that of ω′ on E′: ‖ω‖²/|D|^{1/2} = [E(ℝ) : E(ℝ)⁰]·Ω·Ω′.
items.note: BSD.1: "Relate component groups, minimal differentials and periods under quadratic base change and twist"; GZ.0 packet node GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.0/real-period-components (Ω⁰ least positive real period, c∞ = #π₀(E(ℝ))). Checked for both lattice shapes (Δ > 0 rectangular: ‖ω‖² = 2ω₁|ω₂|, Ω′ = |ω₂|/√|D|, index 2; Δ < 0: ‖ω‖² = ω₁|ω₂|, index 1).

items.name: Complex conjugation on P_K when f|w_N = f, and the rational point P = P_K + P̄_K
items.statement: Setting of Chap. V §2 with f|w_N = f (sign −1). Complex conjugation maps x to w_N(x^τ) for some τ ∈ Gal(H/K) (Chap. II §1, p. 235: c(𝒜, 𝔫) = (𝒜⁻¹, 𝔫̄), and w_N changes 𝔫 to 𝔫̄ and multiplies 𝒜 by a fixed class), and w_N commutes with Gal(H/K); since w_N*ω_f = ω_f, the map π∘w_N − π is constant, equal to π(0), which is a rational torsion point (Manin–Drinfeld). Hence P̄_K = P_K + h·π(0), so P := P_K + P̄_K = 2P_K + h·π(0) ∈ E(ℚ) and, with the normalization <,>_K = 2<,>_ℚ of Chap. I (6.4), ĥ_K(P_K) = ĥ_ℚ(P)/2. Combining (2.1), L(E′, 1) = α′Ω′ and ‖ω‖²/|D|^{1/2} = [E(ℝ) : E(ℝ)⁰]·Ω·Ω′ with L′(E/K, 1) = L′(E, 1)·L(E′, 1) gives L′(E, 1) = α·Ω·ĥ_ℚ(P) with α = [E(ℝ) : E(ℝ)⁰]/(2α′c²u_K²) ∈ ℚ^× (Chap. I Theorem (7.3)).
items.locator: Chapter V, §2, p. 312 ('If we take P = P_K + P̄_K ∈ E(ℚ), and combine Theorem (2.1) and the last two formulas, we obtain the desired formula L′(E,1) = αΩĥ(P) with α ∈ ℚ^×'; the conjugation law is used implicitly); Chapter II, §1, p. 235
items.note: BSD.3: 'Show that the rational trace/eigenspace selected by the functional equation gives the rank-one part for E and not its twist, using the established conjugation law'; HE.1: 'show its dependence on choices is given by the specified Galois/Hecke actions and torsion translation'. The actions of c and w_N on Heegner points are PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/60 (with the correction PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E2); Theorem (7.3) itself is PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/35. Without the conjugation law the step on p. 312 does not go through (new issue in this review). Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86).

items.name: Modular abelian variety A_f and (2.4) L(A/ℚ, s) = ∏ L(f^α, s)
items.statement: Let f = Σ a_n q^n be a normalized newform of weight 2 and level N (the paper says 'Hecke eigenform'; §2's standing hypothesis, p. 310, is a newform, and (2.4) needs it) whose coefficients generate a totally real field M_f of degree m (f lies in an m-dimensional irreducible representation of the Hecke algebra over ℚ). One associates to f an m-dimensional abelian variety A₀/ℚ, a quotient of J₀(N); for A₀ or any A isogenous to A₀ over ℚ, (2.4) L(A/ℚ, s) = ∏_{α: M_f ↪ ℝ} L(f^α, s).
items.note: R14.5: 'For a normalised cuspidal newform f of weight exactly two ... construct its Hecke ideal and the quotient A_f of J₁(N), or J₀(N) for trivial character, as an abelian variety over Q. Prove its dimension equals the degree of the coefficient field'. R19.6: 'For weight-two f only, prove V_ℓ(A_f) ≅ ⨁_{λ|ℓ} ρ_{f,λ} as Q_ℓ-representations with K_f-action', which with R19.1's Eichler–Shimura relation gives the Euler factors of (2.4) at p ∤ Nℓ; the factors at p | N need local–global compatibility, which is not named, and the equality of L-functions itself is not named; partial. 'Newform' is needed: for N = Mp² and g a newform of level M, v = g − a_p(g)·g|V_p + p·g|V_{p²} is an eigenform of every T_m with U_p v = 0 and totally real coefficients, but L(v, s) lacks the Euler factor at p while the Hecke quotient of J₀(N) attached to v is isogenous to A_g, so (2.4) fails for v.

items.name: Consequences for A_f: order of vanishing m or ≥ 3m, rank ≥ m, BSD up to ℚ^×
items.statement: In the setting of (2.4) assume f|w_N = f (sign −1). Then ord_{s=1} L(A/ℚ, s) is m or ≥ 3m according as L′(f, 1) ≠ 0 or = 0 (Cor. (1.3)); if it is m, then L^{(m)}(A/ℚ, 1) = m!·∏_α L′(f^α, 1) (printed without m! and with s for 1; issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E52). Imitating m = 1: ord_{s=1} L(A/ℚ, s) = m implies rk A(ℚ) ≥ m (A(ℚ) ⊗ ℝ contains the m-dimensional span of the c_{1,f^α}), and if equality holds the BSD formula for L^{(m)}(A/ℚ, 1) is true up to a non-zero rational multiple.
items.note: Only sketched in the paper ("We now imitate the argument"). Not planned: GZ.8 plans heights for strict GL₂-type A ("A totally real extension concerns the precise parametrized strict-GL₂-type abelian variety and coefficient-character component") and HE.7 the Kolyvagin–Logachev RM extension, but no stage states the rank ≥ m / BSD-up-to-ℚ^× conclusion for A_f over ℚ. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.8.

items.name: Generalized setting: the set S, the quaternion algebra B, the order R and the embedding ι: K → B
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. IV: N ≥ 1; D < 0 an odd fundamental discriminant (hence squarefree, D ≡ 1 mod 4; Chap. IV §2, p. 273), (D, N) = 1, δ := |D|, K = ℚ(√D), ε = ε_D = (D/·), h = h_K, u = #O_K^×/2, 𝒜 ∈ Cl_K, r_𝒜(n) = number of integral ideals of norm n in 𝒜 (r_𝒜(0) = 1/(2u)); weight 2k with k = 1; k = 1. Let S = {p prime : ord_p(N) odd, ε(p) = −1}; then (−1)^{|S|} = ε(N). If |S| is even (L_𝒜(f,s) has an odd-order zero at s = 1), B is the indefinite quaternion algebra over ℚ ramified exactly at S; if |S| is odd, B is the definite quaternion algebra ramified at S ∪ {∞}. Every prime ramified in B is inert in K, so there is an embedding ι: K → B. R is an order of B containing ι(O_K) with reduced discriminant N; such orders exist [15]; they are unique up to conjugacy in the indefinite case and fall into finitely many conjugacy classes in the definite case. Γ = R^×/{±1} is a discrete subgroup of G = (B ⊗ ℝ)^×/ℝ^×.
items.note: HE.1: "For quaternionic curves construct optimal embeddings of the specified orders and their CM points in the same canonical tower. Prove the local embedding conditions"; R18.1 applies ShimuraData to a quaternion algebra. The non-Eichler orders of reduced discriminant N when ε(p) = −1 (and the existence reference [15]) are not specifically named.

items.name: Shimura curves: canonical model, Hecke correspondences and Heegner points (quoted: Shimura [32])
items.statement: Indefinite case: G ≅ PGL₂(ℝ), Γ⁺ = Γ ∩ PGL₂⁺(ℝ) is a Fuchsian group acting on ℌ; if (3.1) (ε(p) = 1 for all p | N) holds then Γ⁺ ≅ Γ₀(N); Γ⁺\ℌ is an algebraic curve over ℂ, complete iff S ≠ ∅. It has a canonical model X over ℚ, characterized by the fields of rationality of its special points, with a modular description as coarse moduli of polarized abelian surfaces with endomorphisms by R. The Hecke correspondences are rational over ℚ and determine the zeta function. ι|_O gives a Heegner point x of discriminant D on X rational over H; Pic(O) acts freely on the Heegner points of discriminant D, via Gal(H/K) by Shimura's reciprocity law.
items.note: R18.1: "Apply ShimuraData and ShimuraVarieties to a quaternion algebra over a totally real field split at one specified real place, constructing its canonical Shimura curve and complex uniformization"; HE.1: "prove descent to ring class fields by the main theorem of complex multiplication and the canonical-model reciprocity law".

items.name: Generalized main identity, indefinite case (announced; proof in a later paper)
items.statement: With B indefinite (|S| even, ε(N) = 1, k = 1) and X, x as above: the coefficients a_{m,𝒜} of Theorem (6.9) of Chap. IV are a fixed multiple of <x, T_m x^{σ_𝒜}>, <,> the Néron–Tate height pairing on Pic(X). The constant κ = −12 N^{−1} ∏_{p|N}(1 + ε(p)/p)^{−1} of (6.9) arises, as in Chap. II (2.13), as the residue at s = 1 of the resolvent kernel function G_s of X(ℂ).
items.note: GZ.8: "Specialize to X₀(N), a rational elliptic modular quotient, generalized-Heegner quaternionic curves and finite ring-class characters". The residue statement for κ is consistent with vol(Γ⁺\ℌ) (local unit indices N_p(1 + ε(p)/p)), my check; not separately planned.

items.name: Definite case: the curve X = ⊔ Γ_i\Y, Brandt matrices, Heegner points and the height pairing
items.statement: Definite case: G ≅ SO₃(ℝ) ⊂ PGL₂(ℂ) and Γ is finite, acting on ℙ¹(ℂ); Γ\ℙ¹(ℂ) has the canonical model Γ\Y over ℚ, Y the genus-0 curve over ℚ attached to B. For Hecke operators take X = ⊔_{i=1}^n Γ_i\Y, n = class number of R, Γ_i = projective unit group of the right order of the i-th left ideal class (an adelic double coset space). The Hecke algebra acts on Pic(X) ≅ ℤ^n by the Brandt matrices [16]. ι gives a Heegner point x of discriminant D on X, defined over K; Pic(O) acts freely on such points. Height pairing on Pic(X): <x, y> = 0 if x, y lie on different components, and <x, y> = |Γ_i| if both lie on Γ_i\Y.
items.note: R18.3: "Define algebraic automorphic forms on the finite double-coset set with their weight module and integral coefficients. Prove finiteness, the Hecke action, change of level". The Brandt-matrix identification and this particular pairing (Gross's) are not named; partial.

items.name: Definite main identity and the special-value formula for L(f, χ, 1) (announced; N prime, ε(N) = −1 in [16])
items.statement: In the definite case (|S| odd, ε(N) = −1, k = 1): the coefficients b_{m,𝒜} of Theorem (5.6) of Chap. IV are fixed multiples of Σ_{ℬ∈Pic(O)} <x_ℬ, T_m x_{ℬ𝒜}>. An argument as in §1 then relates L(f, χ, 1) and <x_{χ,f}, x_{χ,f}> for a newform f ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)) and χ: Cl_K → ℂ^×, x_{χ,f} the (χ, f)-eigencomponent.
items.note: GZ.5: "Establish the Waldspurger period formula for the stated GL₂/quaternionic toric data ... Export the explicit split, ramified and definite-quaternionic specializations needed by Euler-system and level-raising consumers". This is the classical form of that specialization (Gross's formula); the explicit Brandt-module form is not named.

items.name: Waldspurger–Vignéras: L(f, 1_K, 1) is proportional to a square in M_f
items.statement: In the definite setting, since x_{1,f} lies in a fixed one-dimensional space as K varies, the theorem of Waldspurger and Vignéras (cf. [36]) that L(f, 1_K, 1) is proportional to the square of an element of M_f (M_f = field of Fourier coefficients of f) follows immediately.
items.note: Not stated in any stage; nearest GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.5 (Waldspurger formula) and RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.2. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.5.

items.name: Closed formula for γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜) (Chap. II Prop. (5.8) rewritten with Chap. IV Prop. (4.6a))
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; hypothesis (3.1): ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; k > 1 an integer (weight 2k). For s ∈ ℂ and m ∈ ℕ prime to N, γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜) = Σ_{τ∈G} G^m_{N,s}(x^τ, x^{τσ}), where x is a Heegner point of discriminant D, σ ∈ G ↔ 𝒜, G^m_{N,s} = G_{N,s}|T_m and G_{N,s} is the resolvent kernel function for Γ₀(N) (when r_𝒜(m) ≠ 0 some terms are infinite and γ^m_{N,s} is modified as in Chap. II §5). Then γ^m_{N,s}(𝒜) = −2u² Σ_{n≥1} σ_𝒜(−n) r_𝒜(nN + m|D|) Q_{s−1}(1 + 2nN/(m|D|)) + 2hu r_𝒜(m)((Γ′/Γ)(s) − log 2π + ½ log|D| + (L′/L)(1, ε)). (Corrected: printed σ_𝒜(n); by Chap. IV Prop. (4.6a), σ_𝒜(−n) = δ(n)R_{{𝒜𝔫}}(n), which is the coefficient in Chap. II Cor. (3.17); new issue in this review, the p. 315 recurrence of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E38.)
items.note: No resolvent kernel G_{N,s} of Γ₀(N) and no Legendre function of the second kind in either library (Tau Ceti's resolvent API, TauCeti/Analysis/Normed/Operator/Resolvent, concerns unbounded operators). Numerical check of the corrected formula: N = 1, s = k = 2, D = −7, 𝒜 = [O], m = 1 (h = u = 1): the series with σ_𝒜(−n) = δ(n)R(n), R(n) = Σ_{d|n}(−7/d), summed to n ≤ 320000 and extrapolated in 1/n, gives γ = −6.9021711, equal to G((1+i√7)/2) = −log 7 − 2 log 3 − (12/7) log 5 = −6.9021711 of p. 318; with the printed σ_𝒜(n), computed from the definition of ε_𝒜(n, d) in Chap. IV Prop. (3.2), the same computation gives −6.52641. (σ_𝒜(n) and σ_𝒜(−n) agree when (n, D) = 1 and differ otherwise, e.g. σ_𝒜(7) = 0, σ_𝒜(−7) = 2.) For general s this is Chap. II Cor. (3.17) and Prop. (5.8) (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/90, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/112), routed to GZ.7; the use at s = k > 1 is consumed by the Part II of route 8. Routed (source) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.7. Rerouted in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) to route 8: HigherGreenFunctionCMValues (Part II).

items.name: (4.1) Theorem and (4.2): higher-weight analogue of the main identity
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; hypothesis (3.1): ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; k > 1 an integer (weight 2k). There is a holomorphic cusp form Φ = Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,𝒜} q^m ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) (printed 'm ≦ 1', issue PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E53) with L′_𝒜(f, k) = (2^{4k−1}π^{2k}/((2k−2)!·√|D|))·(f, Φ) for all f ∈ S^{new}_{2k}(Γ₀(N)), and for m prime to N: (4.2) a_{m,𝒜} = (m^{k−1}/u²) γ^m_{N,k}(𝒜) + (h/u) r_𝒜(m) m^{k−1} log(N/m) − m^{k−1} Σ_{0<n≤m|D|/N} σ′_𝒜(n) r_𝒜(m|D| − nN) P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(m|D|)), P_{k−1} the (k−1)-st Legendre polynomial. Since P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(m|D|)) r_𝒜(m|D| − nN) ∈ ℚ and σ′_𝒜(n) is a non-negative even integral multiple of the logarithm of a single prime (remark after Chap. IV Prop. (4.6)), (4.2) writes a_{m,𝒜} as a finite sum of values of G^m_{N,k} at Heegner points plus a rational combination of logarithms of primes.
items.note: Checked: substituting the γ^m_{N,k} formula (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/311) into (4.2) reproduces a_{m,𝒜} of Chap. IV Theorem (5.8). No stage plans the higher-weight Gross–Zagier formula (S.-W. Zhang's heights of Heegner cycles); GeneralizedHeegnerCycles:GH.0-GH.8 plan Kuga–Sato and generalized Heegner cycles with étale/p-adic Abel–Jacobi and BDP/Castella–Hsieh p-adic formulas, not complex heights or this identity. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: Deligne's Heegner vectors and height pairing (reported, unpublished)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; hypothesis (3.1): ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; k > 1 an integer (weight 2k). Deligne defined Heegner vectors s_x in the stalks above Heegner points x of the local coefficient system Sym^{2k−2}(H¹) (H¹ = first cohomology of the universal elliptic curve over X₀(N)) and a height pairing <,> with <s_x, T_m s_{x^σ}> = a_{m,𝒜}; the pairing is defined as a sum of local heights characterized by axioms similar to Chap. I §4, computed by intersection theory at finite places and by values of an eigenfunction of the Laplacian (namely G_{N,k}) at archimedean places. The definitions extend to the curves of §3 (Sym^{2k−2}(H¹) replaced by Γ⁺\ℌ × W or ⊔_i Γ_i\(ℙ¹(ℂ) × W), W the unique (2k−1)-dimensional irreducible representation of B^×/ℚ^×), giving formulas for heights of Heegner vectors in terms of L_𝒜(f, k) or L′_𝒜(f, k). The global meaning of the sum of local heights (e.g. when it vanishes) was not understood.
items.note: Nearest plans: GeneralizedHeegnerCycles:GH.0 ("Construct the relevant desingularized fiber powers of the universal elliptic curve") and GH.1 ("Form generalized Heegner cycles ... Construct the étale Abel–Jacobi map"); neither plans an archimedean/complex height pairing of Heegner cycles. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: Relations λ for S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)); G_{N,k,λ} and γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; hypothesis (3.1): ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; k > 1 an integer (weight 2k). A relation for S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) is a sequence λ = {λ_m}_{m≥1} with (i) λ_m ∈ ℤ, λ_m = 0 for all but finitely many m; (ii) Σ_{m≥1} λ_m a_m = 0 for every cusp form Σ a_m q^m ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)); (iii) λ_m = 0 for m not prime to N. Put G_{N,k,λ}(z₁, z₂) = Σ_{m≥1} λ_m m^{k−1} G^m_{N,k}(z₁, z₂) and γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜) = Σ_{m≥1} m^{k−1} λ_m γ^m_{N,k}(𝒜) = Σ_{τ∈G} G_{N,k,λ}(x^τ, x^{τσ}). (If S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) = 0 every a_{m,𝒜} vanishes and (4.2) gives γ^m_{N,k}(𝒜) directly.)
items.note: Depends on the resolvent kernel (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/311); no library or stage counterpart. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: (4.3) Corollary: γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜) is a rational combination of logarithms of primes
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; hypothesis (3.1): ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; k > 1 an integer (weight 2k). Let λ be a relation for S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) and 𝒜 an ideal class of K. Then γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜) = Σ_{m>0} λ_m m^{k−1} hu r_𝒜(m) log(m/N) + u² Σ_{m,n∈ℤ, m|D| ≥ nN > 0} λ_m m^{k−1} σ′_𝒜(n) r_𝒜(m|D| − nN) P_{k−1}(1 − 2nN/(m|D|)). In particular exp((D^{k−1}/u²)·γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜)) is a rational number, and in fact a rational square unless |D| is prime.
items.locator: Chapter V, §4, (4.3) Corollary and proof, pp. 316-317
items.note: Formula checked from (4.2) and Σλ_m a_{m,𝒜} = 0. Integrality step: (m|D|)^{k−1}P_{k−1}(1 − 2t·…) ∈ ℤ because P_n(1 − 2t) has integer coefficients; this polynomial is mathlib:Polynomial.shiftedLegendre n (Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/ShiftedLegendre.lean:40, coefficients (−1)^k C(n,k) C(n+k,n) by coeff_shiftedLegendre :84), but Mathlib has no identification with the classical Legendre polynomial. Two misprints in statement/proof: PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E54, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E55. No stage. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: Weight 2 (k = 1): G_{N,1,λ} at Heegner points are logarithms of absolute values of algebraic numbers in H
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; (3.1). For k = 1, a relation λ for S₂(Γ₀(N)) (λ_m ∈ ℤ, almost all zero, Σ λ_m a_m = 0 for every cusp form Σ a_m q^m ∈ S₂(Γ₀(N)), λ_m = 0 for (m, N) > 1) gives Σ_m λ_m T_m = 0 in End(J₀(N)), since the Hecke action on J₀(N) is the same as on S₂(Γ₀(N)); so Σ_m λ_m T_m((x) − (∞)) = (φ) for a rational function φ on X₀(N) over H, and the local height axioms give <Σ_{m≥1} λ_m T_m((x) − (∞)), (x^σ) − (0)>_v = log|φ(x^σ)/φ(0)|_v for every place v of H (with the modified symbols of Chap. II §5 when r_𝒜(m) ≠ 0 for some m with λ_m ≠ 0). At an archimedean place this local height is Σ_m λ_m G(z, z′)|_{z′}T_m, where G is the Green's function of X₀(N) of Chap. II (2.15), (2.22), normalized at the cusps ∞ and 0 (so that <(x) − (∞), T_m((x′) − (0))>_ℂ = G(z, z′)|_{z′}T_m, p. 241), and z, z′ represent x^τ, x^{στ}. Hence these numbers, which the paper writes G_{N,1,λ}(x^τ, x^{στ}), are logarithms of absolute values of the conjugates of an element of H. (If G_{N,1,λ} is read as lim_{s→1} Σ_m λ_m G^m_{N,s}, the k = 1 case of the definition on p. 316, it exists only when Σ_m λ_m σ₁(m) = 0, and then equals the local height minus κ_N Σ_m λ_m Σ_{d|m} d log(m/d²), by Chap. II Prop. (2.23); new issue in this review.)
items.note: The principal-divisor axiom of local heights is part of GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.2 ('Export local height decomposition, base-change and correspondence-adjunction APIs'); the Green's function G of Chap. II (2.15) is PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/73 and Prop. (2.23) is PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/79 (both planned in GZ.7); the conclusion is not named. Uses Σλ_m T_m = 0 in 𝕋 (perfect pairing, PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/277). Checked from (2.23): G^m_{N,s} has the pole σ₁(m)κ_N/(s − 1) at s = 1. For N = 11 (newform q − 2q² − q³ + …), λ = (2, 1, 0, …) is a relation with Σλ_mσ₁(m) = 5, so lim_{s→1}Σλ_mG^m_{11,s} diverges; λ = (1, 1, −1, 0, …) is a relation with Σλ_mσ₁(m) = 0, and there the limit differs from the local height by −κ₁₁ log(9/2) = log(9/2) (κ₁₁ = −1); for N = 37, κ₃₇ = −6/19 and the constant would need a 19th root. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: (4.4) Conjecture: algebraicity of higher Green's functions at Heegner points (and its refined form)
items.statement: Standing notation of Chap. V §1 (= Chaps. II–III): as in Chap. IV and moreover every prime p | N splits in K; H = Hilbert class field of K; x ∈ X₀(N)(H) a Heegner point of discriminant D (one of the 2^s·h such points, permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K), W = Atkin–Lehner group); J = J₀(N) = Jac X₀(N); c = class of (x) − (∞), d = class of (x) − (0) in J(H); σ ∈ G = Gal(H/K) corresponds to 𝒜 under the Artin map; <,> = global Néron–Tate height pairing on J(H) (heights over H), extended to J(H)⊗ℂ as a hermitian pairing; 𝕋 = ℚ-subalgebra of End_ℚ(J)⊗ℚ generated by the Hecke operators T_m; hypothesis (3.1): ε(p) = 1 for all p | N; k > 1 an integer (weight 2k). Let λ be a relation for S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)), fix a Heegner point x and an embedding H ↪ ℂ. Then there is α ∈ H^× with G_{N,k,λ}(x^τ, x^{στ}) = u² D^{1−k} log|α^τ| for all τ ∈ G = Gal(H/K). (When r_𝒜(m) ≠ 0 for some m with λ_m ≠ 0, the values at coincident points are the regularized values of Chap. II §5, as in the example G(z) = G_{1,2}(z, z) of (4.5).) Refined form (stated informally): the expression (4.3) for γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜) predicts the ideal generated by α, hence α up to a unit, and with (4.4) up to a root of unity.
items.note: Compatible with (4.3): summing over τ gives (u²D^{1−k}/2) log|N_{H/ℚ} α|. No stage plans it (searched atlas for Green function / algebraicity / CM value: only GZ.2/GZ.7 archimedean Green kernels for weight 2). Later literature treats this conjecture (e.g. Viazovska; Bruinier–Ehlen–Yang; Y. Li); not reviewed here. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: (4.5) Fourier expansion of G(z) = G_{1,2}(z, z) (stated; proof deferred)
items.statement: For N = 1, k = 2, with G(z) = G_{1,2}(z, z) defined by the limiting procedure of Chap. II §5: G(x + iy) = −(2π/3) y − (119 ζ(3)/(2π²)) y^{−2} + (8 − 480/(πy) − 240/(π²y²)) e^{−2πy} cos 2πx − (282876 + 283968/(πy) + 70992/(π²y²)) e^{−4πy} cos 4πx + O(e^{−6πy}), with an O-constant of about 10⁸.
items.note: Checked numerically for consistency with the stated values (PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/319): residuals 1.1e−3 (D = −7), 1.1e−19 (D = −43), 1.8e−40 (D = −163), each within the stated tail 10⁸·e^{−6πy}. No stage. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

items.name: Numerical examples of (4.3) and (4.4) (D = −p, N = 1, k = 2, λ = (1, 0, 0, …))
items.statement: D = −p with p > 3 prime, p ≡ 3 (mod 4), 𝒜 = [O], N = 1, k = 2, λ = (1, 0, 0, …) (a relation since S₄(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0): γ_{N,k,λ}(𝒜) = Σ_z G(z) over the h(−p) points z ∈ ℌ/SL₂(ℤ) satisfying a quadratic equation of discriminant −p. For h(−p) = 1: G((1+i√7)/2) = −log 7 − 2 log 3 − (12/7) log 5; G((1+i√43)/2) = −log 43 + (2/43) log(5⁶·7²⁹/(2¹²⁷·3⁵⁴)); G((1+i√163)/2) = −log 163 + (2/163) log(2²³³·5⁶·7³⁷·19¹²⁵/(3¹⁶³·11³⁵·23⁴²·29¹³⁸·127⁹¹)). For p = 31 (h = 3): G((1+i√31)/2) + G((1+i√31)/4) + G((−1+i√31)/4) = −log 31 − (2/31) log(3¹¹⁶·11⁸·23³⁰·17⁶), and the refined (4.4) predicts G((1+i√31)/2) = −log π₃₁ − (2/31) log(π₃⁵⁴π₉³¹π₁₂₁¹³π₁₇⁶π₂₃³⁰/(π₁₁¹⁸θⁿ)) for some n ∈ ℤ, θ ≈ 1.465571232 the real root of θ³ − θ² − 1 = 0, π₃ = θ + 1, π₉ = 3/π₃, π₁₁ = 3θ − 4, π₁₂₁ = 11/π₁₁, π₁₇ = −θ + 3, π₂₃ = −3θ + 5, π₃₁ = 3θ + 1 in ℚ(θ) = ℚ(j((1+√−31)/2)), the real subfield of the Hilbert class field of ℚ(√−31); this holds numerically to ≥ 15 decimal places with n = 61.
items.note: Verified with mpmath (40 digits) using (4.5): D = −43 agrees to 1.1e−19 and D = −163 to 1.8e−40; D = −7 to 1.1e−3 and the p = 31 sum to 5.3e−5, both within the tail bound for y = √7/2, √31/4. The refined p = 31 prediction holds to 1.2e−15 with n = 61, and the best real n is 60.99999999999995. Norms of the π_q were checked from θ³ − θ² − 1 (N(π_q) = q). Exponents read from 4x zooms of p. 318. No stage. Routed (part-ii) to GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeightsPartIIHigherWeight.

routes.reason: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights names 'Gross–Zagier, Chapters II–IV' among its primary source contracts, and its layers GZ.2 (admissible pairings), GZ.6 (arithmetic generating series and incoherent analytic kernels, with holomorphic projection), GZ.7 (local arithmetic identities and boundary contributions) and GZ.8 ('Specialize to X₀(N)') are written for Yuan–Zhang–Zhang's adelic proof, of which this paper's theorem is the classical case. The paper's own proof is therefore the blueprint source for the X₀(N) instances of those layers. Chapter II's archimedean heights (the Green's functions G_{N,s}, their values at Heegner points and the counts ρ^m) and Chapter III's finite heights (the Eichler-order models R𝔞, the intersection formula, the explicit quaternion algebras) belong to GZ.7. Chapter IV's Rankin kernel θ_𝒜E_s, its trace and Fourier coefficients, the functional equations, Propositions IV.(4.4)–(4.6), §6 and the weight-two coefficient formulas (Theorem IV.5.6 for k = 1, Theorem IV.6.9) belong to GZ.6; GZ.6 plans the classical Rankin kernel uniformly in k because the higher-weight Part II imports it. The coefficient identity ⟨c,T_mc^σ⟩ = u²a_{m,𝒜} and the corollaries on L-values (Chapter V §1) belong to GZ.8, and the Waldspurger–Vignéras square statement to GZ.5. Every planned item of the paper whose layer is in this roadmap is named too, since the paper supplies its classical statement. Review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86): the generic analytic inputs go to their existing owners rather than to GZ.6 or GZ.7. The Legendre functions, point-pair invariants and non-holomorphic Eisenstein series with their Fourier expansions go to AutomorphicSpectralTheory (route 9, following the accepted route 2 of PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16). The K-Bessel integrals go to AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0 (route 10, following PAPER-ZHANG-21). Hecke's-trick Poincaré series and E₂* go to QSeries QM.3 (route 11). Partial zeta functions and the genus factorization go to AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4 (route 4), and the theta transformation and Poisson summation go with the theta series (route 3). The weight-2k > 2 statements of Chapter IV §5 and V §4 go to the higher-weight Part II (route 8). The Hecke-algebra faithfulness and pairing of V §1 go to ModularCurvesPartII (route 5). This fixes one ordering error: the Legendre function Q_{s−1} was planned twice, in GZ.7 (items 64, 65, 108) and GZ.6 (item 258), although GZ.6 consumes it and sits upstream of GZ.7. The stage graph lacks edges from CM.5, HE.2, AN.4, MP.5, ER.7, QM.3 and AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.2 into GZ.6/GZ.7; the review checked by reachability that adding them creates no cycle. One ordering question remains for the design job: GZ.5's definite identity (items 309, 310) uses Theorem IV.5.6 and Proposition IV.4.4, planned here in GZ.6, which sits downstream of GZ.5. No new layer is needed: each item is a step of a theorem these layers already own, specialised to X₀(N).

Chapter III quotes Deuring's reduction theory: the endomorphism ring of an elliptic curve over a field is ℤ, an order in an imaginary quadratic field or a maximal order in the quaternion algebra ramified at p and ∞; the reduction of CM curves (good reduction potentially, supersingular exactly at non-split primes); and the structure of End at a non-split prime. CM.5 ('Reduction, isogenies and certified computation', with 'Supersingular reduction cannot be treated as ordinary') is the layer that owns reduction of CM elliptic curves; it must state Deuring's classification for all elliptic curves in characteristic p, not only for reductions of CM curves. Deuring 1941 is the primary reference (see prerequisites). Review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86): Kronecker's congruence for Φ_N describes the bad fibres of X₀(N) and moved to route 5; nothing in CM.3 covers modular polynomials. The classical dictionary between CM points of 𝔥, positive-definite forms of discriminant D and ideal classes (added in review) joins CM.1, which identifies isomorphism classes of CM curves with ideal classes. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6, whose packet uses 'End⁰ of a supersingular curve is the quaternion algebra ramified at p and ∞' as an acceptance test, is an alternative owner for Deuring's classification.

The theta series θ_𝒜(z) = 1/(2u) + Σ_{𝔞 ∈ 𝒜 integral} e^{2πiN(𝔞)z} of an ideal class is the theta series of the binary quadratic space (𝔞, N(·)/N(𝔞)). Its modularity, θ_𝒜 ∈ M₁(Γ₀(|D|), ε), with the SL₂(ℤ) transformation law of Lemma IV.(2.3) proved by Poisson summation over an ideal lattice, is the input of the Rankin kernel. Review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86): the route named GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.3, but the GN packet and README say 'MetaplecticAutomorphicForms owns theta', and the accepted route of PAPER-LI-23 follows that. MP.5 ('Theta kernels, convergence and automorphic spaces') owns theta series of rational quadratic data, and MP.6 exports the quadratic-character instance. This route adds the classical weight-one, level-|D|, character-ε form of the binary instance, with Hecke and Schoeneberg as classical sources. Poisson summation for lattices is imported from AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0 (packet node AL.0/adelic-poisson-summation). Items 19 and 177 are the same definition, from Chapters I and IV.

Chapter IV uses the functional equation of L(s,ε) for the odd quadratic character with root number +1, the evaluation of the quadratic Gauss sum with its sign (Σ ε₂(n)e(rn/δ₂) = ε₂(r)κ(D₂)δ₂^{1/2}) and the analytic class number formula L(1,ε) = πh/(u√|D|). Chapters II and IV use the partial zeta function ζ_K(𝒜,s) of an ideal class, its expression through the Eisenstein series at a CM point, and the genus-character factorization L_K(s,χ_{D₁·D₂}) = L(s,ε_{D₁})L(s,ε_{D₂}). Review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86): the route named AN.1, which the accepted restructuring RS-07 dropped (Mathlib supplies Dirichlet L-functions and their functional equation, with the root number unevaluated). AN.4 keeps the Dedekind/Hecke comparison. From ζ_K = ζ·L(s,ε) (item 97, planned in AN.4) and the functional equations of ζ_K (AN.4) and ζ (Mathlib) one gets root number +1 for ε_D, hence Gauss's sign; Mathlib's residue of ζ_K gives L(1,ε). The accepted route 6 of PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16 already puts the partial ideal zeta function, the CM partial-zeta identity and the genus factorization in AN.3–AN.4, so items 95, 96 and 172 join them here. The genus character itself is in Tau Ceti (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.genusCharFunNarrowClassGroupHom).

Proposition III.(1.4), the regularity of the model of X₀(N) over ℤ used for the intersection theory, and the structure of its fibres at p | N are the regular-model statements R13.5 ('Bad fibres and regular/semistable models') plans. R13.5's text limits it to the cases its proof needs, so it must add Gross–Zagier's case: the Deligne–Rapoport/Katz–Mazur model of X₀(N) for arbitrary N (Katz–Mazur 13.4.7 for Γ₀(pⁿM)), with the corrected singular locus of (1.4) (review finding; Edixhoven 1990 gives the locus and its resolution). Kronecker's congruence Φ_p(X,Y) ≡ (X^p − Y)(X − Y^p) mod p describes the same bad fibre. Review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86) added: the Atkin–Lehner involutions w_d and the group W on X₀(N) (items 3 and 57) at R14.1, which constructs the algebraic Hecke correspondences but not these involutions; the modular polynomial Φ_N and the function field ℚ(j, j′) of X₀(N) at R12.6; and Chapter V §1's faithfulness of the Hecke algebra on S₂(Γ₀(N),ℚ) and the perfect pairing (T,f) ↦ a₁(Tf) at R12.5 and R14.2, whose packet nodes state the Γ₁(N), complex versions.

Conjecture V.(2.3), that the index of the Heegner point is divisible by the order of the rational torsion, and the worked examples N = 11 and N = 65 (with Kramer's 2-Selmer bound) are statements about the Heegner index in BSD, which BSD.5 ('Rational leading-term quotient and Heegner index formula') owns; the paper is a source for its tests.

routes.title: Analytic number theory, zeta functions and prime distribution, Part II: the effective class number problem after Goldfeld, Gross and Zagier
routes.brief: First prerequisite: Analytic number theory, zeta functions and prime distribution (AnalyticNumberTheory); this Part II starts where AN.3–AN.4 stop, with Siegel's ineffective bounds, and adds the effective lower bound. Final theorems, as Gross–Zagier state them (Invent. Math. 84, I §§7–8, pp. 231–232): Proposition (7.4): the curve −139y² = x³ + 10x² − 20x + 8 (conductor 714877 = 37·139²) has ord_{s=1}L(E,s) = rank E(ℚ) = 3; the triviality of its Heegner point is proved in Gross–Zagier, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 297 (1983) [17] or Zagier, Notices AMS 31 (1984) [39], not in this paper. Theorem (8.1): for any ε > 0 there is an effectively computable κ(ε) > 0 with h(D) > κ(ε)(log|D|)^{1−ε}. (8.2): C(t)h(D) ≥ log|D|, with C(t) an explicit function of the number t of prime divisors of D and log C(t) ~ 4√(t/log t); (8.2) implies (8.1) because 2^{t−1} | h(D) by genus theory. With the curve y² − y = x³ − 7x + 6 of conductor 5077, (8.2) holds for D prime to 5077 with C(1) = 55, i.e. h(D) > (1/55) log|D| for |D| prime. The largest |D| with h(D) = 3 is 907. Cover the following. Goldfeld's theorem in Oesterlé's form (Bourbaki exp. 631, §3, conditions (C1)–(C4), and Théorème 1: h(−d) bounded below by (1/C) log d · ∏_{p | d, p ≠ max} (1 − ⌊2√p⌋/(p+1)); the displayed inequality is garbled in the Numdam text layer, so read it on the page). This includes the degree-four series L(f,s)L(f⊗χ_D,s), its expression through the reduced binary quadratic forms of discriminant D, the order ≥ 3 zero at s = 1, and the symmetric-square L-function of f. Cover C = 7000 from the curve of (7.4) (exp. 631, §4) and C = 55 from the 5077 curve (Oesterlé 1988). Cover the certification that both curves have analytic rank exactly 3: sign −1, L′(E,1) = 0 through the Gross–Zagier formula and the triviality of the Heegner point, a certified nonzero L‴(E,1) (Buhler–Gross–Zagier 1985 for 5077), and rank 3 from three independent points and a descent. Cover Montgomery–Weinberger's h(−d) ≠ 3 for 907 < d < 10^2500 and the final enumeration. Imports, by title and id: Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), GZ.8, for the Gross–Zagier formula over X₀(N); Rank-zero and rank-one Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer theory (RankZeroOneBSD), BSD.0 for L(E,s), twists and analytic rank, and BSD.9 for analytic certificates; Modularity and modular parametrisations of elliptic curves over Q (EllipticCurveModularity) for the modularity of the two curves; Analytic number theory, zeta functions and prime distribution (AnalyticNumberTheory), AN.3 and AN.4, for Siegel's theorem as the ineffective comparison, and the class number formula and partial zeta functions; Dirichlet L-functions and their functional equations from Mathlib (AnalyticNumberTheory AN.1 was retired by RS-07 in favour of Mathlib); Automorphic L-functions and local factors (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors), AL.3, for Rankin–Selberg and symmetric-square continuation; Geometry of numbers, quadratic forms and homogeneous arithmetic (GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic), GN.3, for reduced binary forms; Certified computational number theory and arithmetic data (ComputationalNumberTheory), CN.2–CN.4, for class groups, descents and validated L-values; Multiquadratic fields and genus theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Multiquadratic) for genus theory. Plan none of these again. Non-goal: the class-number-one theorem of Heegner, Stark and Baker, which this paper does not use.
routes.reason: Chapter I §8 derives the effective lower bound for class numbers of imaginary quadratic fields from Goldfeld's theorem and the analytic-rank-3 curve of Proposition (7.4), and quotes Oesterlé's explicit version and the class-number-3 consequence. No stage plans Goldfeld's effective bound. Review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86): the extraction proposed a new roadmap, claiming that nothing in the atlas plans class-number lower bounds. That is not so: accepted routes already put Siegel's (ineffective) lower bound in AnalyticNumberTheory AN.3/AN.4 (PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16 route 6, PAPER-BINYAMINI-22 route 5). The effective bound continues that direction, so it is a Part II of AnalyticNumberTheory. The brief is rewritten. Goldfeld's method uses L(f,s)L(f⊗χ_D,s) with a zero of order ≥ 3 and the symmetric-square L-function, not the twists by class-group characters. Oesterlé's Bourbaki exposé proves the constant C = 7000 with the curve of (7.4) and only announces C = 55, which is proved in Oesterlé 1988. The class-number-3 enumeration needs Montgomery–Weinberger. The certification of analytic rank 3 for the conductor-5077 curve is Buhler–Gross–Zagier 1985. The imports are named by title and id.

routes.title: Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights, Part II: CM values of higher Green functions on orthogonal Shimura varieties
routes.brief: First prerequisite: Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights). Final statements, as printed (Invent. Math. 84, V §4, pp. 315–318, and IV §5, pp. 290–294, with the corrections recorded in this extraction's sourceIssues (E38, E42, E43, E46, E53–E55) applied all confirmed in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86)): Sturm's holomorphic projection lemma in weight 2k > 2 (Proposition IV.(5.1) and its special case for coefficients polynomial in 1/y), which this Part II states and proves (method from GZ.6, Poincaré series from QSeries QM.3); the holomorphic projection of Φ̃_{−r}; Theorem IV.(5.5) (L_𝒜(f, 2k−1−r), 0 ≤ r < k−1) with the corrected factor (2k−2−r)! (E42); Theorem IV.(5.6) for k ≥ 2 with the corrected constant (2π)^{2k}2^{2k−1}/((2k−2)!|D|^{k−1/2}) (E43); Theorem IV.(5.8) = Theorem V.(4.1): for (3.1) and k > 1 there is Φ = Σ_{m≥1} a_{m,𝒜}q^m ∈ S_{2k}(Γ₀(N)) with L′_𝒜(f,k) = 2^{4k−1}π^{2k}/((2k−2)!√|D|)·(f,Φ) for all f ∈ S^new_{2k}(Γ₀(N)), and (4.2) for (m,N) = 1; Corollary (4.3) with its displayed formula (above) and the rationality/square statement; Conjecture (4.4), as printed (fix x and H ↪ ℂ; α ∈ H^× with G_{N,k,λ}(x^τ,x^{στ}) = u²D^{1−k}log|α^τ| for all τ ∈ Gal(H/K)), together with its known proofs: Li 2023 Theorem 1.1 at individual CM points on X₀(1)², with its hypotheses; Bruinier–Ehlen–Yang 2021 Theorem 6.1 for CM points in the same field; Viazovska; Mellit. The design job must state which level-N cases remain open; the Fourier expansion (4.5) and the numerical examples, the p = 31 refined prediction with n = 61 included, as tests. Heights: the higher-weight identity for heights of Heegner cycles on Kuga–Sato varieties (S.-W. Zhang 1997), which realises Deligne's Heegner vectors. Plan the arithmetic intersection pairing of homologically trivial cycles it needs, or name it explicitly as a gap. Imports, by title and id: Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights), GZ.2, GZ.6–GZ.8, including the uniform-in-k Rankin kernel of Chapter IV planned in GZ.6; Generalized Heegner cycles and their Iwasawa variation (GeneralizedHeegnerCycles), GH.0–GH.1, for Kuga–Sato varieties, projectors and Heegner cycles; Automorphic spectral theory and trace distributions (AutomorphicSpectralTheory), AS.0–AS.4, for the resolvent kernel G_{N,s} and the Legendre functions Q_ν; Q-series, partitions, Jacobi and mock modular forms (QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms), QM.3, for harmonic Maass forms, ξ and Poincaré series; Metaplectic groups, Weil representations and automorphic theta kernels (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms), MP.4–MP.6, as the BEY/Li routes require; Modular forms — Hecke theory, newforms, and L-functions (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms) for weight-2k forms and newforms. Plan none of these again.
routes.reason: Chapter V §4 gives a proved analytic identity in weight 2k > 2 (Theorem 4.1 with Corollary 4.3) and the algebraicity conjecture (4.4) for higher Green's functions at Heegner points; Chapter IV §5 proves the weight-2k coefficient formulas behind it. The parent roadmap is weight two throughout (GZ.0–GZ.9), and GeneralizedHeegnerCycles builds Heegner cycles for p-adic and Kolyvagin-system purposes but plans neither their complex heights nor higher Green's functions. So these are new layers in the parent's direction: a Part II. Review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86): coalesced with the Part II HigherGreenFunctionCMValues that PAPER-LI-23 and PAPER-BRUINIER-EHLEN-YANG-21 propose (same roadmap id, parent, title and area; those reviews rejected only details of the brief and agreed on the direction and on keeping exactly one such Part II). X₀(N)×X₀(N) is the signature-(2,2) case of their orthogonal Shimura varieties. The route now also carries the weight-2k > 2 items of Chapter IV §5 (Sturm's lemma in weight 2k, the holomorphic projection of Φ̃_{−r}, Theorems IV.5.5, IV.5.6 for k ≥ 2 and IV.5.8), item 50 (Chapter I (9.2) for k > 1) and the closed formula for γ^m_{N,s} (item 311), which were routed to the weight-two layers. The brief is rewritten: Conjecture (4.4) is now proved at individual CM points in level one (Li 2023), with earlier cases by Mellit and Viazovska and by Bruinier–Ehlen–Yang 2021; the height interpretation (Deligne's Heegner vectors) is proved by S.-W. Zhang 1997; Corollary (4.3) is stated as printed.

Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86). Chapters II and IV use the classical analytic objects on 𝔥: the Legendre function of the second kind Q_{s−1} and its asymptotics (the resolvent kernel of the Laplacian, through the point-pair invariants g_s), the level-N series E_N, and the non-holomorphic Eisenstein series E_{M,ε,κ,s} of level M with character, with their Fourier expansions through the archimedean integral V_s(t) and its properties (Propositions IV.(3.3a)–(3.3e)). The accepted route 2 of PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16 already puts the non-holomorphic Eisenstein series, their Fourier expansions and continuation, the weight-0 resolvent kernel and the Whittaker and Bessel functions in AS.0–AS.2 ('Induced families and Eisenstein convergence', 'Intertwiners and meromorphic continuation'). Planning them again in GZ.6 or GZ.7 would give them two owners. This route plans them once, in the generality the atlas uses (integer weight, level M, Dirichlet character), and GZ.6/GZ.7 import them. Q_ν is one carrier, with Q_{k−1} (item 258) its integer specialisation; items 64, 65, 108 and 258 describe it.

Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86). The integral representation of the K-Bessel function K_ν with K_{−ν} = K_ν, and the tabulated K-Bessel integral used for V*_s(t), are the statements of PAPER-ZHANG-21/98 ('Bessel and exponential-integral kernels'), whose accepted route 2 puts them in AL.0 ('Schwartz–Bruhat and Fourier theory'). They are planned once there.

Added in review (REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86). Chapter IV §6 uses Hecke's trick for the weight-2 Poincaré series P_{m,s} and its unfolding identity, and the weight-2 non-holomorphic Eisenstein series E_{2,s} with E = E₂*. QM.3 ('Harmonic Maass forms') constructs Poincaré series, and its packet already has nodes for the holomorphic Poincaré series and for E₂*; the weight-2 Hecke-trick versions extend those nodes.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter II, §1, p. 234 (cusps of X₀(N)), Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source gives m/n (m, n∈ℤ, (m, n)=1) ↦ (n/d)⁻¹ m(mod f_d), with d=(n, N). It claims coprimality of n/d with f_d and says the result is determined solely by the class of m/n modulo Γ.
sourceIssues.correction: m/n ↦ (n/d)·m (mod f_d) (equivalently m⁻¹(n/d)⁻¹); the printed map is Γ₀(N)-invariant only when (ℤ/f_dℤ)^× has exponent ≤ 2, i.e. f_d | 24.
sourceIssues.reason: For γ = (a b; c d′) ∈ Γ₀(N): m′ = am + bn, n′ = cm + d′n, (n′, N) = d, n′/d ≡ d′(n/d) and m′ ≡ am (mod f_d), ad′ ≡ 1 (mod N); hence m′(n′/d) ≡ m(n/d) but (n′/d)⁻¹m′ ≡ a²(n/d)⁻¹m (mod f_d). Example N = 25: γ = (−2 1; −25 12) ∈ Γ₀(25) sends 2/5 to 1/10; the printed invariant gives 2 and 2⁻¹ = 3 (mod 5), the corrected one 2 and 2. Brute force (SCR/t_cusp.py): violations of the printed invariant for N = 25, 49, 50, none of the corrected one for N ∈ {8, 9, 16, 25, 27, 32, 45, 49, 50, 72}. Checked on the page image (zoomed): the exponent −1 is printed. Reach: the bijection with ∐(ℤ/f_dℤ)^× and the cusp count Σφ(f_d) = ∏(p^{[ν/2]} + p^{[(ν−1)/2]}) are correct with the corrected map; the map is not used later.

sourceIssues.correction: 𝒜 is replaced by 𝒜[𝔡]⁻¹ (= 𝒜[𝔡̄]); (i) w_N : (𝒜, 𝔫) → (𝒜[𝔫]⁻¹, 𝔫̄) = (𝒜[𝔫̄], 𝔫̄). This is the rule the paper itself uses on p. 243: τ_{𝒜,𝔫} ↦ τ_{𝒜[𝔡]⁻¹, 𝔫𝔡⁻¹𝔡̄}.
sourceIssues.reason: Chap. I (2.2): w_d(x) = (E/D → E′/D′) with D ⊂ ker φ of order d. For x = (ℂ/𝔞 → ℂ/𝔞𝔫⁻¹): D = 𝔞𝔡⁻¹/𝔞, E/D = ℂ/𝔞𝔡⁻¹ of class 𝒜[𝔡]⁻¹, and the new kernel gives 𝔫𝔡⁻¹𝔡̄. For w_N (dual isogeny, Chap. I (2.1)): ℂ/𝔞𝔫⁻¹ → ℂ/𝔞N⁻¹ = ℂ/(𝔞𝔫⁻¹)𝔫̄⁻¹, i.e. ([𝔞𝔫⁻¹], 𝔫̄). In coordinates: −1/(Nτ) is the root of [CN, −B, A/N], whose (1.5)-ideal is 𝔫̄·(ℤC + ℤ(−B+√D)/2) ~ 𝔞𝔫̄; numerically class(𝔞′) = class(𝔞𝔫̄) ≠ class(𝔞𝔫) for (D, N) = (−23, 2), (−23, 3), (−47, 2), (−71, 2) (SCR/t_wN.py). Reach: p. 243 states and uses the correct rule; statement (ii) is true either way.

sourceIssues.printed: "(3.11) Proposition. Let 𝒜₁, 𝒜₂ be two ideal classes of K, 𝔫 a primitive ideal of norm N and 𝔞_i (i=1, 2) an integral ideal in 𝒜_i with 𝔫|𝔞_i, N(𝔞_i)=A_i. Then for m∈ℕ, r_{𝒜₁𝒜₂⁻¹}(m)=0 we have: ... ρ^m(n) = #{(α, β)∈(𝔞₁⁻¹𝔞̄₂⁻¹×𝔞₁⁻¹𝔞₂⁻¹𝔫)/{±1} | N(α)=(Nn+m|D|)/(A₁A₂), N(β)=Nn/(A₁A₂), A₁A₂α≡A₁A₂β(mod 𝔡)}"; p. 245: "If α and β satisfy (3.7) and (3.10) then the right-hand sides of these two equations are in 𝔫𝔞₁⁻¹=Nℤτ₁+ℤ and 𝔞₁⁻¹=ℤτ₁+ℤ, respectively"
sourceIssues.correction: Add the hypothesis that 𝔞₁, 𝔞₂ are prime to D (possible in every class, keeping 𝔫 | 𝔞_i), or replace (3.10) by the exact conditions (A₂/√D)(β − α) ∈ 𝔫𝔞₁⁻¹ and (A₂/√D)(τ̄₂β − τ₂α) ∈ 𝔞₁⁻¹.
sourceIssues.reason: The converse divides by √D; at a ramified 𝔭 | 𝔞₁ (or 𝔞₂) the numbers A₁A₂α, A₁A₂β lie in 𝔭 automatically, so (3.10) carries no information there. Counterexample (SCR/t_rho.py, t_rho2.py; recomputed independently by the reviewer): D = −7, N = 2, β = 1, m = 3 (3 inert, h = 1), τ₂ from [2, 1, 1], 𝔞₁ = ℤ14 + ℤ(21+√−7)/2 from [14, 21, 8] (N(𝔞₁) = 14, 𝔞₁ ⊂ (√−7)): the true γ-counts are ρ(1), ρ(2), ρ(4), ρ(8) = 2, 2, 6, 8 while the (α, β)-set of (3.11) has 4, 4, 12, 16 elements (every n with 7 ∤ n doubles; n = 14, 28 agree); with 𝔞₁ from [2, 1, 1] (prime to 7) the two counts agree for all n ≤ 29. The p. 246 argument for (3.13) ('exactly half of the pairs') also presupposes 𝔞ᵢ prime to D. Reach: Proposition (3.11) is false in its stated generality; nothing downstream is affected, because (3.12)–(3.17) are statements about classes and follow with representatives prime to D (verified numerically).

review.reason: Read (3.10), the converse paragraph and (3.11) on the p. 245 image; the quotes match. Recomputed the counterexample with my own exact-arithmetic script (lattices in ℚ(√−7), enumeration of all γ = (a b; c d) with N | c, det γ = m, and of all (α, β) in the sets of (3.11)): D = −7, N = 2, β = 1, m = 3, τ₂ from [2,1,1]. With 𝔞₁ from [14,21,8] (norm 14, divisible by (√−7)) the (3.11) set has 4, 4, 12, 16 elements for n = 1, 2, 4, 8 against true γ-counts 2, 2, 6, 8; every n ≤ 29 with 7 ∤ n doubles and n = 14, 28 agree. With 𝔞₁ from [2,1,1] the two counts agree for all n ≤ 29. The reason is as stated: if a ramified 𝔭 divides 𝔞₁ then A₁A₂α ∈ 𝔞̄₁𝔞₂ ⊂ 𝔭 automatically, so (3.10) is vacuous at 𝔭 and the division by √D in the converse loses integrality; the 'exactly half of the pairs' argument for (3.13) on p. 246 likewise needs both sides non-zero mod 𝔭. Kind: the Proposition as stated is false for admissible choices of 𝔞₁ (a counterexample exists), so by PROTOCOL §18 this is an error rather than a gap; affects a stated result is right. Item 85 adds the hypothesis.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter II, §5, normalization of the uniformizing parameter g at an elliptic point, p. 250 (display after 'In general, ω has order 1/u − 1 at x'), Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)

sourceIssues.correction: ω = (1/u)(g^{1/u} + higher degree terms) dg/g, i.e. ω = d(g^{1/u})·(1 + …); equivalently, keep the printed display with g replaced by u^u·g.
sourceIssues.reason: At a Heegner point x with u > 1 the local parameter of X₀(N) is (w − z)^u·(unit), and ω = 2πiη⁴(w) dw. With the printed normalization one gets g = (2πiη⁴(z)(w − z)/u)^u(1 + o(1)), so log|g(y)|_v − u log|2πiη⁴(z)(w − z)|_v → −u log|u|_v ≠ 0, contradicting (5.5) (p. 251), which is what (5.6)–(5.8) use. With the corrected normalization g = (2πiη⁴(z)(w − z))^u(1 + o(1)) and (5.5) holds. Independent check against the non-archimedean normalization Ch. III (8.3) (p. 263, N = 1): from ω^{⊗6} = Δ(dq/q)^{⊗6} and q dj/dq = −E₆j/E₄ one gets ω = dj/(j^{2/3}(j − 1728)^{1/2}) up to a root of unity; at j = 1728 (u = 2) the corrected normalization gives ∂/∂t = 2⁶·3⁴ ∂/∂j and the printed one 2⁸·3⁴ ∂/∂j, and at j = 0 (u = 3) the corrected one gives |2⁹·3^{3/2}| and the printed one |2⁹·3^{9/2}|; (8.3), read on a full-resolution IIIF crop of image 00000269, prints 'α ≡ j(x)^{2/3}(j(x) − 1728)^{1/2} (mod μ₀), j(x) ≠ 0, 1728; ≡ 2⁶ · 3⁴, j(x) = 1728; ≡ 2⁹ · 3^{3/2}, j(x) = 0' — exactly the three values computed with the corrected normalization (the generic value j^{2/3}(j − 1728)^{1/2} is the same for both, since u = 1 there). sourceIssues.locator: Chapter III, §1, definition of 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} (p. 254) and the description of the cusps (p. 255), Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source defines 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} as the algebraic stack of cyclic degree N isogenies (1.1) φ: E → E′ between generalized elliptic curves over S, requiring A = ker φ to meet all irreducible components in every geometric fibre. It takes X as the coarse moduli scheme of 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)}. It describes Cusp(d) using Néron polygon diagrams with A = ker φ isomorphic to μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ.
sourceIssues.correction: 'A = ker φ is isomorphic to μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ' holds only when gcd(d, N/d) = 1. In general, at the cuspidal points of Cusp(d) the kernel A is a cyclic group scheme of order N that is an extension of dℤ/Nℤ ≅ ℤ/(N/d)ℤ by μ_d, and it is non-split when f = gcd(d, N/d) > 1 (on a Néron polygon, e.g. ⟨(ζ_N, 1)⟩ ⊂ G_m × ℤ/(N/d)ℤ). The coarse moduli scheme X of (1.1)–(1.2) is still the Deligne–Rapoport and Katz–Mazur model of X₀(N) (Česnavičius 2017, §1.1), so the model itself needs no change; but for N not squarefree the stack 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)} of (1.1)–(1.2) differs from the Deligne–Rapoport stack at these cusps, and Česnavičius' refined Γ₀(N)-structures give the correct moduli description there.
sourceIssues.reason: (i) Check: Cusp(d) ≅ Spec ℤ[μ_f] is flat over ℤ, so its geometric points include characteristic-0 points; there μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ ≅ ℤ/d × ℤ/(N/d) is not cyclic when f = gcd(d, N/d) > 1, contradicting the cyclicity condition (1.2) that defines 𝓜_{Γ₀(N)}. On a Néron polygon a cyclic A of order N meeting every component is e.g. ⟨(ζ_N, 1)⟩ ⊂ G_m × ℤ/(N/d), a non-split extension. (ii) Česnavičius, 'A modular description of X₀(n)', Algebra & Number Theory 11 (2017) (arXiv:1511.07475), abstract: 'when a positive integer n is not squarefree, even over ℂ the moduli stack that parametrizes generalized elliptic curves equipped with an ample cyclic subgroup of order n does not agree at the cusps with the Γ₀(n)-level modular stack'. The stack of (1.1)–(1.2) is exactly that naive stack. Katz–Mazur [21] treat [Γ₀(N)] only for elliptic curves and compactify by normalization, so the generalized-elliptic-curve description is not in the cited sources for non-squarefree N. Wording re-checked on imgHR/p254.jpg and p255.jpg ('A = ker φ is isomorphic to μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ'). (Also recorded by an earlier worker: Česnavičius 2017 (for the moduli description at the cusps); the inconsistency with the stated group structure μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ is new. The atlas stage ModularCurvesPartII:R13.2 already routes around it ('Follow Česnavičius' refined description when the naive cyclic-subgroup formulation fails')..)

review.reason: Read on p. 255 (image): 'The component Cusp(d) corresponds to diagrams of Néron polygons where A = ker φ is isomorphic to μ_d × dℤ/Nℤ. One part of the correction needs changing: Česnavičius §1.1 says the naive stack 'is algebraic, has X₀(n) as its coarse moduli space, and agrees with X₀(n) on the elliptic curve locus'; what differs for non-squarefree N is the stack at the cusps (it is not Deligne–Mumford there, §1.2), not the coarse model. sourceIssues.locator: Chapter III, §2, paragraph after (2.1), p. 256, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source uses algebraic closedness of k to claim that Hom_S(y, x) does not depend on which diagrams represent x and y.
sourceIssues.correction: True for S = W (a complete DVR of characteristic 0 with algebraically closed residue field: two W-diagrams inducing the same W-point are isomorphic, Conrad Theorem 2.6) and hence for the reductions to W/πⁿ of fixed W-diagrams, which is the only way §§4–9 use it; false for general complete local S (e.g. artinian S) at points with Aut_k ≠ ⟨±1⟩, where Hom_S must be defined for chosen diagrams.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample: p ≥ 5, N = 2, E: y² = x³ − x over 𝔽̄_p with p ≡ 1 (mod 4) (ordinary, j = 1728), A = ⟨(0,0)⟩, which is stable under [i]: (x, y) ↦ (−x, iy); so Aut_k(x₀) = μ₄. The universal deformation ring is W[[T]] with Aut/±1 = ℤ/2 acting faithfully (Conrad p. 12), linearizably T ↦ −T, so the complete local ring of X is W[[T²]] (Conrad Lemma 4.2). Over S = k[ε]/(ε²) the deformations T ↦ 0 (constant) and T ↦ ε both give T² ↦ 0, i.e. the same S-point of X, but they are not isomorphic: the constant one has Aut_S = μ₄, while [i] carries T ↦ ε to T ↦ −ε ≠ ε, so the other has Aut_S = ±1. Hence Card Hom_S(y, y)_{deg 1} is 4 or 2 depending on the representing diagram. Wording re-checked on imgHR/p256.jpg. (Also recorded by an earlier worker: new (Conrad 2004 restricts to W-diagrams: Theorem 2.6 and Lemma 4.2, conrad.txt pp. 6 and 11).)

review.reason: Read on p. 256 (image): 'Using the fact that k is algebraically closed, one can check that the definition of Hom_S(y, x) is independent of the diagrams chosen to represent the points x and y.' The statement is for any complete local S with algebraically closed residue field (p. 255, §2). The counterexample works: for p ≡ 1 (mod 4), p ≥ 5, N = 2, E: y² = x³ − x, A = ⟨(0,0)⟩ is stable under [i], so Aut_k = μ₄; μ₄/±1 acts on the Serre–Tate parameter by q ↦ q⁻¹ (ι(i)² = −1 in ℤ_p), faithfully and linearizably T ↦ −T, and the complete local ring of X is the ring of invariants (Conrad, Lemma 4.2: 'the complete local ring of X at the closed point y₀ of y is the subring of Aut(y₀)-invariants in the universal deformation ring'). Over S = k[ε]/(ε²) the deformations T ↦ 0 and T ↦ ε define the same S-point of X but have automorphism groups μ₄ and ±1, so Hom_S(y, y)_{deg 1} has 4 or 2 elements depending on the diagram. Conrad works only with W-models and notes (text before Theorem 4.1) that 'such models over W are unique up to non-unique isomorphism' (by his Theorem 2.6), which is the case GZ use. Error, affects nothing: right.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter III, §8, convention (8.1), p. 263, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: Convention (8.1) sets (x · x) = ord_v(α), with α∂/∂t chosen as a basis of T_x X, a free W-module.
sourceIssues.correction: (x · x) = ord_v(α), where ∂/∂t = α·(a basis of T_x X); equivalently α^{-1}∂/∂t is a basis of T_x X, or αω_x is a basis of the cotangent line when ω_x is the covector dual to ∂/∂t. This is Conrad's α_x.
sourceIssues.reason: (i) Derivation. Take f with ord_x f = 1, write f = T·h with T the integral local parameter of the section x, and normalise g by dg(∂/∂t) = 1. The local symbol of Ch. II (5.1)/(5.3) gives ⟨x, div f⟩_v = log|(f/g)(x)|_v. If ∂/∂t = c·∂/∂T, then (T/g)(x) = c, so the self-intersection that makes (0.2) hold is ord_v(c), with c defined by ∂/∂t = c·basis. (ii) Consistency. With that reading, (8.2) (ord_v α = ½Σ(#Aut_{W/π^n} − #Aut_W) ≥ 0) and (8.3) (α ≡ j^{2/3}(j−1728)^{1/2}, read on the high-resolution scan) are correct. For N = 1 one computes ω = η⁴dq/q = −j^{−2/3}(j−1728)^{−1/2} dj, so ∂/∂t = −j^{2/3}(j−1728)^{1/2}∂/∂j. Under the printed wording, α would be the reciprocal j^{−2/3}(j−1728)^{−1/2}, with ord_v(α) ≤ 0, contradicting (8.2) and (8.3). Conrad's Theorem 8.4 defines (x.x) = ord_v(α_x) with α_xω_x a basis of Cot_x, and his (9.9) and Definition 9.5 show that this equals GZ's ½Σ(#Aut_{W/π^n} − #Aut_W) when v ∤ N. (Also recorded by an earlier worker: Conrad 2004, Remark 8.5 ('Our α_x is the reciprocal of the α in [GZ]').)

II (5.1)–(5.3) differs from the one with g = T (self-intersection 0) by log|c|_v = −ord_v(c) log q_v, and with ⟨ , ⟩_v = −( · ) log q_v (Prop. III.(3.3), p. 257) the self-intersection is ord_v(c). A toy check on ℙ¹ over ℤ_p with ω_x = p·dT gives (x·x) = −1 = ord_v(c) with c = p⁻¹.
