sourceIssues.locator: Chapter III, §8, sentence before Proposition (8.6), p. 264, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source invokes the action of w_N on ω to claim that, when v|n̄, the vector ∂/∂t generates the submodule (N)^u T_x X.
sourceIssues.correction: ∂/∂t spans (N)^{−u} T_x X when v|n̄, i.e. ∂/∂t = N^{−u}·(generator). Equivalently ω_x is N^u times a generator of the cotangent line. With the corrected (8.1) (see PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E16) this gives (x·x) = −u·ord_v(N), and hence Proposition (8.6) as printed.
sourceIssues.reason: When v|n̄ the kernel of φ is étale at p, and x lies on the fibral component through the cusp 0 = Cusp(1) (Prop. 3.1). Near that cusp the integral parameter is q′ = e^{2πiτ′}, τ′ = −1/(Nτ), attached to the Tate curve Tate(q′^N) with subgroup ⟨q′⟩. From η(−1/(Nτ′)) = (Nτ′/i)^{1/2}η(Nτ′) one gets ω = 2πiη⁴(τ)dτ = −N·η⁴(q′^N)dq′/q′. So ω vanishes to order ord_p(N) along that component: it is N times a generator. Equivalently, on the étale-kernel component the forgetful map (E→E′) ↦ E is inseparable (Frobenius), so ω = π_1^*ω_1 ≡ 0 mod p. The dual vector ∂/∂t is therefore N^{−1}·(generator) when u = 1; for u > 1 the normalisation ω = (g^{1/u}+…)dg/g raises this to N^{−u}. Conrad's Lemma 10.1 independently gives ord_{v,x}(Δ) = 6u·ord_v(N) in exactly this étale case, i.e. Δ(dq/q)^{⊗6} = ω^6 is N^6 times a generator. The printed (8.6) value −u r_𝒜(m) ord_p(N) is correct (Conrad Thm 10.4). It is obtained from the printed '(N)^u' only together with the literal (inverted) wording of (8.1), so the two misstatements cancel. (Also recorded by an earlier worker: new (the underlying fact is Conrad 2004, Lemma 10.1 and Theorem 10.4, which do not comment on GZ's sentence).)

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter III, §9, choice of the auxiliary prime q and the order S, p. 265 (inert case), and the ramified analogue (9.8), p. 266, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source chooses an auxiliary prime q satisfying (q/l) = (−p/l) at every prime l|D, and sets S = {α+βj: α∈𝔡^{-1}, β∈𝔡^{-1}𝔮^{-1}𝔫, α≡β mod O_𝔣}. In the ramified case it requires (q/p′) = (−1/p′) at each p′≠p dividing D, together with (−q/p) = −1.
sourceIssues.correction: For S (with the congruence α ≡ β) to be an order one needs −pq ≡ 1 (mod l) for every prime l|D, i.e. −pq ≡ 1 (mod D); in the ramified case one needs −q ≡ 1 (mod D/p). sourceIssues.correction: In (7.4), (8.5) and §9 the representative 𝔞 ∈ 𝒜 must be prime to p. For the congruences in (9.3) and (9.8) it must also be prime to 𝔡, or those congruences must be read modulo 𝔞O_𝔣. (7.3)(2) itself is fine for any 𝔞.

sourceIssues.reason: Each element has weight ½(1+ord_p Nb_−) = ½ord_p(pn) in (x·T_mx^σ)_v, and ⟨c,T_md^σ⟩_v = −2 log p (x·T_mx^σ)_v. Conrad 2004 §9 (Theorem 9.2, (9.9), Definition 9.5, Remark 9.3) gives a deformation-theoretic proof valid in all residue characteristics for non-elliptic x. sourceIssues.correction: γ = (a b; c d) ∈ SL₂(ℤ)
sourceIssues.reason: In odd weight 1, θ_𝒜|₁(−γ) = −θ_𝒜|₁γ, so the left side is not a function of the image of γ in PSL₂(ℤ). The right side also changes sign under γ ↦ −γ: ε_{D₁}(−1)ε_{D₂}(−1) = ε(−1) = −1 because exactly one of D₁, D₂ is negative, and c*d is unchanged. So the identity holds for every matrix of SL₂(ℤ) (either lift). This is what the proof uses ('an arbitrary element of SL₂(ℤ)') and what (2.2) states.

sourceIssues.correction: L^{(m)}(A/ℚ, 1) = m!·∏_α L′(f^α, 1). This holds under the standing assumption f|w_N = f: if the zeros are simple it is the Leibniz rule, and otherwise every L(f^α, s) vanishes to order at least 3 at s = 1 (Corollary (1.3)), so both sides are 0.
sourceIssues.reason: By (2.4) L(A/ℚ,s) = ∏_{α=1}^m L(f^α,s) with each factor vanishing to order 1 at s = 1. review.reason: Page image p. 313, line 2: 'L^{(m)}(A, s) = ∏_α L′(f^α, 1)'. By the Leibniz rule the m-th derivative at s = 1 of a product of m functions each vanishing there is m! times the product of their first derivatives (the multinomial coefficient m!/(1!)^m), and the left side must be evaluated at s = 1. The simple-zero proviso in the correction is not needed: under the standing assumption f|w_N = f, if one L(f^α, s) has a zero of order at least 3 at s = 1 then all do (Corollary (1.3)) and both sides vanish. Kind error (a false identity), affects nothing (the consequences are claimed only up to a non-zero rational factor). Proposed set sharpens the correction.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter V, §2, p. 310, definition of P_K, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source places the point in E(K) and claims that changing the Heegner point x affects it only by a sign.
sourceIssues.correction: Up to sign and the addition of a rational torsion point, P_K is independent of the choice of x
sourceIssues.reason: The 2^s·h Heegner points of discriminant D are permuted simply transitively by W × Gal(H/K) (Chap. II, p. 239; Chap. I, p. 227), so another choice is x' = w_Q(x^τ). Since w_Q acts on the f-part by the eigenvalue λ_Q = ±1, π∘w_Q − λ_Q π is a morphism X₀(N) → E pulling back ω to 0, hence constant, equal to π(w_Q(∞)): the image of a rational cusp, a torsion point of E(ℚ) by Manin–Drinfeld. So P'_K = λ_Q P_K + h·π(w_Q(∞)). This differs from ±P_K whenever P_K has infinite order and h·π(w_Q(∞)) ≠ 0. For instance N = 11, E = X₀(11), π(0) = (0) − (∞) has order 5, and any K with h_K prime to 5 and P_K non-torsion gives such a case. Heights, ranks and all conclusions of §2 are insensitive to torsion.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter V, §1, proof of Theorem (6.3) of Chap. I, p. 308, Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source completes {f} to f_1=f, f_2, …, f_d, a basis for S_2(Γ_0(N)), using normalized newforms and an oldform-space basis. It claims a decomposition into components with the transformation behavior of f_j: c_χ = Σ_{j=1}^d c_χ^{(j)}, satisfying T_m c_χ^{(j)} = a_m(f_j) c_χ^{(j)}.
sourceIssues.correction: Decompose only along f: by multiplicity one there is an idempotent e_f ∈ 𝕋⊗ℂ projecting onto the f-isotypical part. Write c_χ = e_f c_χ + (1 − e_f)c_χ with T_m e_f c_χ = a_m(f) e_f c_χ for all m; the two parts are orthogonal for <,> (T_m, (m,N) = 1, self-adjoint with different eigencharacters). The generating series of the second part is a form orthogonal to f, so (Σχ(𝒜)g_𝒜, f) = h^{−1}ĥ(c_{χ,f})(f,f) as claimed.
sourceIssues.reason: For an arbitrary basis of the oldspace, 'a_m(f_j)' is not an eigenvalue: for f_j = g(dz) with d > 1, a₁(f_j) = 0 while T₁ = 1, so the relation T_m c^{(j)} = a_m(f_j)c^{(j)} would force c^{(j)} = 0. Moreover the Hecke algebra 𝕋 of p. 306 (all T_m, including U_p for p | N) need not act semisimply on oldforms: for a weight-2 newform g of level M with p ∤ M and p³ | N, U_p acts on span{g(p^j z) : 0 ≤ j ≤ 3} by U_p g = a_p g − p g(pz), U_p g(p^j z) = g(p^{j−1}z) (j ≥ 1), with characteristic polynomial t²(t² − a_p t + p) and a one-dimensional kernel. So the stated decomposition with T_m c^{(j)} = a_m(f_j)c^{(j)} for all m cannot hold in general. Only the f-component is used, and f is new, so the conclusion stands with the idempotent argument of the correction (the form used by Gross–Kohnen–Zagier, Math. Ann. 278 (1987), p. 557).

review.reason: Page image p. 308: the quoted text is present. The printed decomposition fails for oldforms in two ways. For f_j = g(dz) with d > 1, a₁(f_j) = 0 while T₁ is the identity, so T_m c^{(j)} = a_m(f_j)c^{(j)} forces c^{(j)} = 0. And 𝕋 (generated by all T_m, p. 306) need not act semisimply on oldforms: for g a weight-2 newform of level M, p ∤ M and p³ | N, U_p on span{g(p^j z) : 0 ≤ j ≤ 3} (U_p g = a_p g − p g(pz), U_p g(p^j z) = g(p^{j−1}z)) has characteristic polynomial t²(t² − a_p t + p) and a one-dimensional kernel. The repair in the correction (an idempotent e_f of the algebra generated by the T_m, (m, N) = 1, strong multiplicity one, self-adjointness for the height pairing) is sound and is the form Gross–Kohnen–Zagier use for the same step (Math. Ann. 278, p. 557: 'a finite linear combination of Hecke operators which is the identity on f and 0 on its orthogonal complement'). S.-W. Zhang (Invent. Math. 130, §0.3) repeats the printed formalism in higher weight. The reason's example 'U_p on oldforms when p² | N' is imprecise: in weight 2 with p² ∥ N the old space is U_p-semisimple (from level M the eigenvalues are 0 and the two distinct roots of t² − a_p t + p; from level Mp they are a_p = ±1 and 0); non-semisimplicity needs p³ | N. Kind gap, affects nothing: acceptable (the conclusion stands; one could argue 'the proof'). Proposed set corrects the reason.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter II, §2, p. 241, last paragraph (the sentence leading to the display before (2.23)), Invent. Math. 84 (1986), published version (GDZ scan)
sourceIssues.printed: The source bases the following conclusion on the claim that T_m fixes every cusp.
sourceIssues.correction: Since T_m((∞)) = σ₁(m)(∞) and T_m((0)) = σ₁(m)(0) for (m, N) = 1, we have … (the displayed identity is unchanged). T_m does not fix the other cusps in general: it fixes every cusp for all m prime to N if and only if every f_d = (d, N/d) is at most 2, i.e. if and only if N is divisible neither by 9, nor by 16, nor by p² for a prime p ≥ 5.
sourceIssues.reason: For a cusp u/v in lowest terms with d = (v, N) and f = f_d, the Γ₀(N)-class is determined by d and the label (v/d)·u mod f (the corrected label of PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/E1). For a coset representative (a b; 0 δ) of Γ₀(N)\{γ ∈ R_N : det γ = m}, aδ = m, the image (au + bv)/(δv) reduces by g = gcd(au + bv, δv), which is prime to N; the new denominator has the same d, and since f | v the label becomes (m/g²)·(v/d)·u mod f. Taking the representative (m 0; 0 1) with m prime to v gives the factor m, which is not 1 mod f for suitable m once f ≥ 3. sourceIssues.reason: For an eigenform that is not new, (2.4) can fail with totally real coefficients: for N = Mp² and g a newform of level M, v = g − a_p(g)·g|V_p + p·g|V_{p²} is an eigenform of every T_m with U_p v = 0 (the matrix of U_p on g, g|V_p, g|V_{p²} has characteristic polynomial x(x² − a_p x + p) and kernel spanned by this v), its coefficients lie in M_g, but L(v, s) = L(g, s)·(1 − a_p p^{−s} + p^{1−2s}) while the Hecke quotient of J₀(N) attached to v is isogenous to A_g, whose L-function is ∏L(g^α, s).
